The Interpretation of His Words, glory be to Him and exalted are His names: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad (1)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the interpretation of the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "I am God, the Most Virtuous (anā Allāh afḍal)."

Those who said this:

14310- Sufyan narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sharik, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾, "I am God, the Most Virtuous."

14311- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His words: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾, "I am God, the Most Virtuous."

* *

Others said: it is the spelling-out (hijaʾ) of the letters of the name of God, blessed and exalted, which is "al-Musawwir" (the Fashioner).

Those who said this:

14312- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾, he said: it is the spelling-out of "al-Musawwir."

* *

Others said: it is one of the names of God, by which our Lord swore an oath.

Those who said this:

14313- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning his words: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾, "It is an oath which God swore, and it is one of the names of God."

* *

Others said: it is one of the names of the Qur'an.

Those who said this:

14314- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾, he said: "It is one of the names of the Qur'an."

14315- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

* *

Others said: they are disjointed letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf hijāʾ muqaṭṭaʿa).

* *

Others said: they are from the reckoning of the abjad (ḥisāb al-jumal).

* *

Others said: they are letters which contain many meanings, by which God indicated to His creatures His intention in that.

* *

Others said: they are the letters of the Greatest Name of God (ism Allāh al-aʿẓam).

* *

We have already mentioned all of that with its narrations, and the justification of each group that stated a view. As for the correct position in our view concerning this, with its proofs and evidences given earlier, that is sufficient so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See what has passed: 1:205–224. See also Maʿani al-Qurʾan by al-Farra' 1:368–370.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verses 2–3:

The exposition of the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿A Book that has been sent down to you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: this Qur'an, O Muhammad, is a Book that God has sent down to you.

* *

The word "al-Kitab" (the Book) is in the nominative case by way of interpretation: "This is a Book."

* *

The exposition of His words: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Says He, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So let your breast not be constrained, O Muhammad, from warning by it those to whom I have sent you to warn, and from conveying to those whom I have commanded you to convey it to; and do not doubt that it is from Me. Be patient in carrying out the command of God and in obeying Him in what He has charged you with and laid upon you of the burden of prophethood, just as the steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm) were patient, for God is with you.

* *

And "al-haraj" (constraint) means narrowness in the speech of the Arabs. We have already explained its meaning, with its evidences and proofs, in His words: ﴿a constricted, narrow breast﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 125], sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. [[See what has preceded, pp. 103–107.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said regarding this:

14316 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾, he said: "Do not be in doubt about it."

14317 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾, he said: "Doubt."

14318 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14319 – Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾, "doubt concerning it."

14320 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, the like of it.

14321 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾, he said: "As for 'al-haraj', it is doubt."

14322 – al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾, he said: "Doubt about the Qur'an."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What I have mentioned of interpretation from the people of interpretation is the meaning of what we have said regarding "al-haraj", for doubt about it does not occur except from constriction of the breast with it and lack of expansiveness to direct it to its proper direction, which is its correct direction. We chose to express it by the meaning of "constraint" because that is the predominant sense of it in the speech of the Arabs, as we have already explained.

* *

The exposition of His words: ﴿That you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: This is a Book that We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, that you may warn thereby those whom We have commanded you to warn, ﴿and as a reminder for the believers﴾ — and this is of the postponed (mu'akhkhar) which means the preposed (muqaddam). Its meaning is: "A Book sent down to you that you may warn thereby," and "a reminder for the believers," "so let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it."

If that is its meaning, then the position of His words ﴿and a reminder﴾ is in the accusative, in the sense: We sent down this Book to you that you may warn thereby and remind the believers thereby.

* *

If it were said that the meaning is: This is a Book sent down to you, so let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it, in warning by it and reminding the believers by it, that would be a statement whose correctness is not refuted.

When the meaning of the speech is directed to this aspect, then in His words ﴿and a reminder﴾ there are two grammatical possibilities:

One of them: the accusative, by way of agreement with the position of "li-tundhira bihi" (that you may warn thereby).

The other: the nominative, in coordination with "al-Kitab" (the Book), as if it were said: "Al-Mim. Sad. A Book sent down to you," and "a reminder for the believers." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 370.]]

* *

The exposition of His words: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as protectors. Little do you remember﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Says He, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people who worship idols and images: "Follow, O people, what has come to you from your Lord with the clear proofs and guidance, and act upon what your Lord has commanded you, and do not follow anything other than Him" — meaning: anything other than what your Lord has sent down to you. He says: Do not follow the command of your protectors who order you to associate others with God and to worship idols, for they will lead you astray and will not guide you.

* *

If someone says: How do you say "the meaning of the speech is: Say, follow," when the mention of "saying" is not present explicitly in the speech?

It is said: Although it is not explicitly mentioned, the speech contains an indication of it, namely His words: ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it, that you may warn thereby.﴾ In His words "that you may warn thereby" is the command to warn, and in the command to warn is the command to speak, since warning is speech. So the meaning of the speech is: Warn the people and say to them: "Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord."

If it were said that its meaning is: that you may warn thereby and remind the believers, so that you say to them, "Follow what has been sent down to you," that would not be refuted.

* *

Some of the grammarians said: His words ﴿Follow﴾ are an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the meaning is: "A Book sent down to you, so let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it; follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord." He holds that this is similar to the words of God: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [Surah al-Talaq: 1], since He began by addressing the Prophet ﷺ and then made the verb plural, as the command God gave His Prophet was a command to all of his community. Similarly, one says to a man who is singled out in address while the intended meaning is him and his followers or his clan and tribe: "Will you not fear God? Will you not be ashamed before God!" and similar speech. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 371, for this is his statement.]]

And although that is a possible aspect, the view we have chosen is more appropriate to the meaning of the speech, because of the evidence of the apparent sense that we described.

* *

As for His words ﴿Little do you remember﴾, He says: Little do you admonish yourselves and take heed, so that you return to the truth. [[See the explanation of "al-tadhakkur" above, vol. 11: 489, note 3, and the references there.]]
