Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 16:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His, may His praise be majestic, saying means: Iblis said to his Lord: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾, meaning: because You have misguided me, as follows:

14361 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾, meaning: "You have misguided me."

14362 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾, he said: "Because You have misguided me."

* *

Some of them interpreted His words ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾ as meaning: "because You have destroyed me," from their saying "ghawiya al-fasil yaghwa ghawan" (the young camel died of thirst/lack of milk), which is when it loses milk and dies, from the words of the poet: [[This is Mudrij al-Rih al-Jurmi, whose name is Amir ibn al-Majnun, as in al-Shi'r wa al-Shu'ara' p. 713, and in al-Wahshiyyat no. 380, and al-Aghani 3:115. In al-Ma'ani al-Kabir p. 1047 it appears as "Amir al-Majnun", the correct form being what is recorded here.]]

Bent in its middle, its young does not...
...neither milking it nor dying of thirst. [[Al-Ma'ani al-Kabir p. 1047; al-Makhassas 7:41, 180; Tahdhib Islah al-Mantiq 2:54; Lisan (gh-w-y). He describes a bow. Al-Tibrizi said in its commentary: "athna'uha" means its ends, the twisted parts. "Fasiluha" means the arrow, and "razza'uha" means it took something from it. He says: the young of this bow does not drink when it loses milk.]]

* *

The basic meaning of al-ighwa' in the speech of the Arabs is a man making something appear attractive to another, to the point of making it seem good to him, deceiving him. [[See the explanation of al-ghayy and al-ighwa' earlier, 5:416.]]

It has also been reported of some Tayy tribes that they say: "So-and-so became ghawiyan," meaning: he became ill. [[This report should be verified in the lexicographical books, for, to my knowledge, it is not mentioned in them.]]

* *

Some of them interpreted this as meaning an oath, as if its meaning in their view were: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path," just as one says: "By God, I will surely do such-and-such."

* *

Some of them interpreted this in the sense of recompense, as if its meaning in their view were: "Because You have led me astray, [or:] because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In this there is a clear proof against the error of the Qadariyyah, [[The Qadariyyah are those who deny divine decree and disbelieve in it. As for those who affirm the decree, who are the People of Truth, they are called "the People of Affirmation." See the indexes of terms and sects earlier.]] who claim that whoever disbelieves or believes does so because God has delegated the causes of that to him, [[Tafwid means ascribing the causes back to Him. See its explanation earlier, 1:162, note 3; 11:340; 12:92. It is the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah and their like.]] and that the cause by which the believer attains faith is the same cause by which the disbeliever attains disbelief. For if it were as they claim, the wicked one would have said: "Because You have guided me," since the cause of "leading astray" would be the cause of "guidance," and his report of being led astray would be a report of being guided. But since their causes differ, and the cause by which he went astray and perished was from God, he ascribed it to Him, saying: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾.

* *

Likewise Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, as related:

14363 - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Zayd ibn al-Habbab related to us, saying: Abu Mawdud related to us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "May God fight the Qadariyyah! Iblis knows more about God than they do!"

* *

As for His words ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾, He means: I will surely sit in wait for the children of Adam on "Your straight path," meaning: Your upright way, which is the true religion of God, namely Islam and its laws. [[See the explanation of "al-sirat al-mustaqim" earlier, p. 282, note 1, and the references there.]] The meaning of the speech is: I will surely turn the children of Adam away from worshipping and obeying You, and I will surely lead them astray as You have led me astray, and I will surely misguide them as You have misguided me.

This is as related from Sabrah ibn Abi al-Fakih: [[In the printed edition: "Sabrah ibn al-Fakih"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is correct. See the following note, p. 335, note 2.]]

14364 - That he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Indeed Satan sat in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat in wait for him on the path of Islam, saying: 'Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers?' But he disobeyed him and embraced Islam. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of emigration, saying: 'Will you emigrate and abandon your land and your sky? The emigrant is only like a horse on a tether?' [[Al-tawl (with kasra on ta' and fath on waw) is a long rope, one end of which is tied to a stake or something else, and the other to the horse's foreleg, so that it turns around it and grazes without running off. He means that emigration restrains him from moving about and roaming the earth, and returning to his land and sky; emigration's matter is grave, as you know.]] But he disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of jihad, which is striving with the self and wealth, saying: 'Will you fight and be killed, so that the woman is married and the wealth is divided?' He said: But he disobeyed him and strove." [[The report 14364: This is a report transmitted by the imams; Abu Ja'far mentioned it without its chain. "Sabrah ibn Abi al-Fakihah" (also written "Sabrah ibn Abi al-Fakih") was a Companion who settled in Kufa. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Usd al-Ghabah 2:260, al-Isabah (concerning his name), al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/188, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/295.

This report was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad in full, 3:483; al-Nasa'i 6:21, 22; al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh 2/2/188, 189; and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah 2:260. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah in his biography: "He has a hadith in al-Nasa'i with a good chain, though there is some disagreement in its chain," and then said: "Ibn Hibban declared it sound."]]

* *

It is also reported from Awn ibn Abd Allah regarding this:

14365 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Habbawayh Abu Yazid related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Awn ibn Abd Allah regarding ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾, he said: "The road to Makkah." [[Report 14365: "Habbawayh Abu Yazid" is so in the manuscript, but it is unpointed; in the printed edition it was "Hayawah Abu Yazid," changed without evidence.

Habbawayh Abu Yazid is Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi. He transmitted from Nafi' ibn Umar al-Jumahi, Amr ibn Abi Qays, and Nu'aym ibn Maysarah. Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Isfahani, Uthman and Abu Bakr the two sons of Shaybah, and Ibrahim ibn Musa transmitted from him. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "I hope he is truthful." He is biographed in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 1/1/212, and Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id in al-Mu'talif wa al-Mukhtalif p. 43, where it is written "Habbawayh" with a doubled ba' after the ha'.

It will also come in this chain as no. 14550.

Abd Allah ibn Bukayr al-Ghanawi al-Kufi transmitted from Muhammad ibn Suqah. He is not strong, though he was of the truthful; Ibn Adi mentioned rejected reports from him. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/16, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:26.]]

* *

What Awn said, although it is among God's straight paths, is not the whole path. Rather, the enemy of God informed that he would sit in wait for them on God's straight path, and did not specify any part of it over another. What is reported on this from the Messenger of God ﷺ is closer to the apparent sense of the revelation and more worthy of interpretation, because the wicked one spares no effort in diverting God's servants from everything that brings them nearer to God.

* *

In agreement with what we have said on this, the exegetes said regarding the meaning of "al-mustaqim" in this place.

Those who said so:

14366 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Your straight path﴾, he said: "The truth."

14367 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14368 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani related to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾: "The way of truth. Then I will surely lead them astray, except for a few."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The grammarians differed on this.

Some grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is: "I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path," just as one says "tawajjaha Makkah" (he turned toward Makkah), meaning "ila Makkah" (to Makkah), and as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

As if I, while striving to attain a bird
along with the star from the air of the sky, am swooping down.

meaning: "to attain a bird," so the "ba'" was dropped, as He said: ﴿Have you outrun the command of your Lord?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:150], meaning: "outrun from the command of your Lord."

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa said: the meaning, and God knows best, is: "I will surely sit in wait for them on their way, and in their way." He said: The dropping of the preposition in this manner is permissible, [[The "sifah" here means the preposition; see the indexes of terms earlier. It will come shortly with the meaning of "zarf" (adverb of place/time). See the following note.]] as you say: "I sat in wait for you at the edge of the road" and "on the edge of the road," because the road is, in meaning, a "sifah" [[The "sifah" here is the "zarf," as the Kufans also call it.]], so it admits what "today," "tonight," and "this year" admit when one says: "I will come to you tomorrow" and "I will come to you on tomorrow."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is, in my judgment, the more correct of the two opinions on this, because "sitting" requires a place in which one sits. Just as one says "qa'adtu fi makanika" (I sat in your place), one says "qa'adtu 'ala siratika" and "fi siratika" (I sat on your path / in your path), as the poet said: [[He is Sa'idah ibn Ju'yah al-Hudhali.]]

Pliant, its shaft shakes with the brandishing of the palm,
within it, as the fox ripples across the road.

[[Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 1:190; Sibawayh 1:16, 109; al-Khizanah 1:474, and others, from a long qasidah in which he describes his spear at its end; this verse describes a spear of Khatt wood. The Diwan's reading is "lidha," meaning the palm enjoys its brandishing. "Ya'sil" means it trembles. "Fihi" means in the brandishing. "'Asala al-tariqa al-tha'lab" means the fox undulated in its gait along the road. He likens the spear's shaking in the hand of the one brandishing it to strike, to the fox's undulating as it runs along the road.]]

The Arabs hardly say this with the names of towns: they do not say "jalasa Makkah" (he sat Makkah) or "qama Baghdad" (he stood Baghdad).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 17:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of His words ﴿I will come to them from before them﴾ is: from the direction of the Hereafter. ﴿And from behind them﴾ is: from the direction of this world. ﴿And from their right﴾ is: from the direction of truth. ﴿And from their left﴾ is: from the direction of falsehood.

Mention of those who said this:

14369- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾, he says: I will cast doubt upon them regarding their Hereafter. ﴿And from behind them﴾: I will make them desire their worldly life. ﴿And from their right﴾: I will confuse for them the matter of their religion. ﴿And from their left﴾: I will make sins appealing to them.

* *

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, through this same chain, an interpretation contrary to this one, namely:

14370- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾, meaning from the world. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the Hereafter. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of their good deeds. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of their evil deeds.

* *

And this report is confirmed by the other one which:

14371- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾, he said: As for "from before them", it is from their direction; as for "from behind them", it is the matter of their Hereafter; as for "from their right", it is from the direction of their good deeds; as for "from their left", it is from the direction of their evil deeds.

14372- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾, the verse: he came to them from before them and informed them that there is no resurrection, no Garden, and no Fire. "And from behind them": from the matter of the world; he adorned it for them and called them to it. "And from their right": from the direction of their good deeds; he held them back from them. "And from their left": he adorned for them the evil deeds and sins, called them to them and commanded them with them. He comes to you, son of Adam, from every direction, except that he does not come to you from above you; he cannot come between you and the mercy of God!

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of His words ﴿from before them﴾ is: from the direction of their worldly life, and ﴿from behind them﴾ is: from the direction of their Hereafter.

Mention of those who said this:

14373- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them﴾, he said: ﴿from before them﴾ is from the direction of their worldly life; ﴿and from behind them﴾ is from the direction of their Hereafter; ﴿and from their right﴾ is from the direction of their good deeds; ﴿and from their left﴾ is from the direction of their evil deeds.

14374- Ibn Wakî' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, regarding: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾, he said: ﴿from before them﴾ is from their worldly life; ﴿and from behind them﴾ is from their Hereafter; ﴿and from their right﴾ is from their good deeds; ﴿and from their left﴾ is from the direction of their evil deeds.

14375- Sufyan related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾, he said: from the direction of the world, adorning it for them. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the direction of the Hereafter, slowing them down from it. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of truth, turning them away from it. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of falsehood, making them desire it and adorning it for them.

14376- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾: as for ﴿from before them﴾, it is the world; I call them to it and make them desire it. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the Hereafter; I cast doubt upon it for them and put it far from them. ﴿And from their right﴾, meaning the truth: I cast doubt upon it for them. ﴿And from their left﴾, meaning falsehood: I make it light for them and make them desire it.

14377- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿from before them﴾: from their worldly life; I make them desire it. ﴿And from behind them﴾: their Hereafter; I make them disbelieve in it and make them abstain from it. ﴿And from their right﴾: their good deeds; I make them abstain from them. ﴿And from their left﴾: the evils of their deeds; I make them appealing to them.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: from where they see and from where they do not see.

Mention of those who said this:

14378- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: "from before them and from their right", he said: from where they see; ﴿and from behind them﴾ and ﴿from their left﴾: from where they do not see.

14379- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14380- Ibn Wakî' and Ibn Humayd related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, who said: We discussed in the presence of Mujahid His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾, and Mujahid said: It is as He said; he comes to them from before them, behind them, from their right and from their left. Ibn Humayd added, he said: "He comes to them from there."

14381- Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani related to us, saying: Mujahid said, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Asim.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: its meaning is: "Then I will come to them from all the directions of truth and falsehood, so I will turn them away from truth and beautify falsehood for them." This is because it follows His words: ﴿Surely I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾. He informs that he sits in wait for the children of Adam on the path which God commanded them to take, which is what we have described as the religion of God, the religion of truth. So he comes to them in that from every aspect: from the aspect God commanded them with, so he turns them away from it, and that is "from before them and from their right"; and from the aspect God forbade them, so he adorns it for them and calls them to it, and that is "from behind them and from their left."

* *

It was said: He did not say "from above them," because the mercy of God descends upon His servants from above them.

Mention of those who said this:

14382- Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam al-Misri related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾, and He did not say "from above them," because mercy descends from above them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ He means: And You will not find, my Lord, most of the children of Adam grateful to You for Your blessing which You bestowed upon them, such as Your honouring their father Adam with what You honoured him with, by having Your angels prostrate to him and by preferring him over me. And "their gratitude" to Him means their obedience to Him by acknowledging His oneness and following His command and prohibition.

* *

Ibn 'Abbas used to say concerning this:

14383- Al-Muthanna related to me with it, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾, he says: monotheists (muwahhidin).

The exegesis on His saying: ﴿Go forth from it, disgraced and banished﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may He be remembered, about His inflicting upon the wicked enemy of God what He inflicted upon him of His vengeance and curse, and His expulsion of him from His Garden, when he disobeyed Him, opposed His command, and answered Him with a reply he had no right to make. He says: God said to him at that point: ﴿Go forth from it﴾, that is, from the Garden, ﴿disgraced and banished﴾, meaning: reproached.

* *

"Al-dha'm" means blame. It is said of it: "dha'amahu yadh'amuhu dh'aman, fa-huwa madhu'um," and some drop the hamza, saying: "dhimtuhu adhimuhu dhaymAN wa-dhaman." "Al-dha'm" and "al-dhaym" are more emphatic in blame than "al-dhamm." Some of them recited this line: [[It is al-Harith ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi.]]

"I kept company with you when my eye was veiled, but when it cleared I cut myself off, blaming it (adhimuha)."

[[The line, its explanation and its sources have passed, and in a different narration earlier: 1:265.]]

Most narrators recite it as "alumuha" (I blame it).

* *

As for "al-madhur": it is the one who is driven away. It is said: "dahara-hu yadhharuhu dahran wa-duhuran," when he drives him away and expels him, and from it is their saying: "idhhar 'anka al-shaytan" (drive away from you Satan). [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1:212.]]

* *

Those in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

14384 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth from it, disgraced and banished﴾, he says: Go forth from it, cursed and exiled.

14385 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "mad'uman," detested.

14386 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth from it disgraced﴾, he says: small and exiled.

14387 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth from it, disgraced and banished﴾: as for "mad'uman," exiled; as for "madhurran," driven away.

14388 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿disgraced﴾, he said: exiled; ﴿banished﴾, he said: driven away.

14389 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth from it disgraced﴾, he said: exiled. And "al-madhur," he said: the diminished.

14390 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Yunus and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Go forth from it disgraced﴾, he said: exiled.

14391 – Abu 'Amr al-Qurqsani 'Uthman ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, who asked Ibn 'Abbas about ﴿Go forth from it disgraced and banished﴾, he said: detested. The matter is made more problematic in that I found Abu Ja'far in his History mentioning a chain from a teacher called "'Uthman ibn Yahya," in which the text reads: "'Uthman ibn Yahya narrated to me, from 'Uthman al-Qurqsani, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us," placing a man called "'Uthman al-Qurqsani" between "'Uthman ibn Yahya" and "Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna." This is what I found; perhaps I will gather what allows me to determine its correctness or error.]]

14392 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth from it disgraced and banished﴾, and said: We do not know "al-madhu'um" and "al-madhmum" except as one word, but there are letters that are shortened. The poet has said to 'Amir: "O 'Amm," and to al-Harith: "O Har," [[In the printed edition: "but there is shortening, and the Arabs said to 'Amir..." with a gap in the text. In the manuscript: "but these are shortened letters. The poet has said..." with a gap. The printer changed what is in the manuscript without honesty. An example of apocope in "al-Harith" is Zuhayr's words: "O Har, I will surely not let you be struck by a calamity that neither commoner nor king has encountered before me."]] and the Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs.

= ﴿lest you become among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: lest you become among those who opposed the command of their Lord and did what was not theirs to do.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So Satan whispered to them both to reveal to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿So he whispered to them﴾, He means: he whispered to them both. That whispering was his saying to them: ﴿Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become of the eternal [ones]﴾, and his swearing to them to that effect.

* *

It has also been said: "He whispered to them," and the meaning is what I have mentioned, as it is said: "gharidtu ilayhi" (I was weary of it, longed for it), meaning: "ishtaqtu ilayhi" (I longed for him), but what is intended is: "gharidtu min hā'ulā' ilayhi" (I was weary of these people toward him). [[In the printed edition: "kama qila: 'aradtu lahu', bi-ma'na: istabantu ilayhi" (as it is said: "I presented myself to him," meaning: "I became clear to him"), which differs completely from the manuscript, giving us meaningless drivel. The manuscript reads: "kama qila: 'aradtu ilayhi bi-ma'na: ishtaqtu ilayhi" (as it is said: "I presented myself toward him," meaning: "I longed for him"), and the correct reading is what I have established here.

His saying: "gharidtu ilayhi," meaning "ishtaqtu ilayhi," and "innama ta'ni: gharidtu min hā'ulā' ilayhi," appears to be the very words of al-Akhfash in explaining the verse of Ibn Harmah:

Who is a sincere messenger who will convey from me to 'Ulayyah, other than the words of a liar?

That I have been weary toward the harmony of her face, [as] the weariness of a lover toward the absent beloved.

His saying: "tanasuf wajhiha" means the beauties of her face which are equal to one another in beauty. Al-Akhfash said: "Its explanation: I was weary of these people toward him, because the Arabs connect all these particles with the verb." Al-Akhfash means that they say: "gharida gharadan" when one is impatient, anxious and bored; so when "ila" is added with the verb, its meaning becomes: he was impatient with this, struggling and longing for that.

The point of citation is that "al-waswasah" is the hidden sound of the inner speech of the soul, so Iblis conveyed what had stirred in his own soul to them both; therefore "al-lam" and "ila" were attached to "al-waswasah." But Abu Ja'far has here merged the discussion in a condensed manner.]] So the meaning of that is likewise.

So Satan whispered to them from his own soul, with falsehood in speech, in order to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts, as Ru'bah said:

"He whispered, calling upon the Lord of the daybreak, sincerely..."

[[From his Diwan, p. 108; Lisan al-'Arab (w-s-s). This is a line from his long rajaz poem, of which many verses have passed. This line is from verses describing a hidden hunter, watching for wild asses in order to strike one of them. He says: when he sensed the game and wanted to shoot it, he whispered to himself a prayer, fearing failure and hoping for success.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech: Iblis drew Adam and Hawwa' toward him and cast to them both: "Your Lord has only forbidden you to eat the fruit of this tree, unless you become angels or become of the eternal" — in order to reveal to them what God had concealed from them of their nakedness, covering it with the veil which He had drawn over them.

* *

Wahb ibn Munabbih used to say concerning the veil with which God had covered them:

14393 — Ḥawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Ibn Munabbih, concerning His saying: ﴿So their private parts became apparent to them﴾, he said: there was a light upon them, so their private parts were not seen.

[[Report 14393: Ḥawthara ibn Muhammad ibn Qudayd al-Minqari, Abu al-Azhar al-Warraq; Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Ṣā'id and others narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim, 1/2/283.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And he said: Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, unless you become angels or become of the eternal ones﴾ (20)

Abu Ja'far said: His praise be exalted says: Satan said to Adam and his wife Hawwa': "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree — that you eat its fruit — lest you become angels."

* *

The "la" has been dropped from the speech, because of what appears from it, as it was dropped from His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [Surat an-Nisa': 176]. The meaning: Allah makes clear to you that you not go astray.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra claimed that the meaning of the speech is: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, out of aversion that you become angels," as it is said: "iyyaka an taf'al" (beware that you do), meaning "karahiyata an taf'al" (out of aversion that you do).

* *

"Or that you become of the eternal ones" — in the Garden, remaining in it forever, so that you do not die. [[See the explanation of "al-khulud" in the earlier linguistic indexes (kh-l-d).]]

* *

The reading is with a fatḥah on the "lam," meaning: angels from among the angels.

* *

It is also related from Ibn 'Abbas:

14394 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: 'Isa al-A'ma narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to read: "illa an takunā malikayn," with a kasrah on the "lam."

* *

And from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir:

14395 — Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: Ya'la ibn Hakim narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, that he read it: "malikayn," with a kasrah on the "lam."

* *

It seems that Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya directed the interpretation of the speech toward the meaning that Satan said to them: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, unless you become kings among the kings" — and that they took as their basis in this the saying of God in another place: ﴿He said: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Surat Ta-Ha: 120].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading which I do not permit reciting otherwise is the reading upon which the reciters of the metropolitan cities agree, which is: with a fatḥah on the "lam" of "malakayn," meaning: two angels, from among the angels, because of what has already preceded in our explanation that whatever is widely transmitted among the reciters of Islam, that is the correct reading, and it is not permissible to oppose it.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors."﴾ (7:21)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿and he swore to them both﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, means: he swore an oath to them, just as He said elsewhere: ﴿Swear to one another by God that we will surely attack him by night﴾ (Surah an-Naml: 49), meaning: swear to one another by God. And just as Khalid ibn Zuhayr, the cousin of Abu Dhu'ayb, said:[[Found in the printed edition and the manuscript as "Khalid ibn Zuhayr, the paternal uncle of Abu Dhu'ayb." I have found no one who said this; rather, what they have said is that Khalid ibn Zuhayr al-Hudhali was the son of Abu Dhu'ayb's sister, or his nephew, or the cousin of Abu Dhu'ayb. The apparent correct wording is therefore what I have written. See Khizanat al-Adab 2: 320, 321; 3: 597, 598, 647, 648.]]

*"And he swore to her by God, earnestly, that you are sweeter to me than honey when its comb is taken."*[[Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 1: 158, from his poems exchanged with Abu Dhu'ayb concerning the woman who was the lover of ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Malik. Abu Dhu'ayb had been her messenger to him, but when ʿAbd ʿAmr grew old, Abu Dhu'ayb schemed against him, took her from him and became her lover. Abu Dhu'ayb then became angry with her, and his messenger to this woman became his cousin Khalid ibn Zuhayr, who did to him what he himself had done to ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Malik: he took the woman from him and became her lover. Abu Dhu'ayb became angry with him and with her. When she came to apologise to him, he said: "You want me to gather you and Khalid? Can two swords be sheathed in one scabbard, woe to you?"

"O Khalid, you have not honoured the close kinship, so as to guard me in my absence or in what you reveal.
Her eyes and neck called you to her, and you leaned toward her as a lover leans deliberately."

Then he said to Khalid: "Khalid kept my secret through nights when his soul followed the straight path in all its affairs.
But when youth and its errancy overcame him, while in the soul there was temptation and sin from him..."

He turned his head away from me and inclined his affection to the coquettish charms of a lady whom he used to visit long ago.

Khalid replied in verses: "Do not be distressed at a custom you yourself began, for the first to be content with a custom is the one who follows it.
Indeed what you claim about the one among us, and its like, is in you too, but I see you wronging her.
You rescued her from ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Malik, while you were the choicest and purest of his soul...
He lingers long with her to bring her back, but far off from him are her mansions and palaces..."

"And he swore to her by God..." [verse incomplete in the source]

*Al-Sulwa* is honey; "shara al-ʿasal yashuruhu" means he took it from its place in the hive.]]

meaning: he swore to them both by God, just as the poet A'sha of Banu Tha'laba said:

*"Two foster-brothers of the same milk, sharing the breast of one mother, swore by the black and dark (night), an oath that we shall never be separated."*[[From his Diwan, p. 150; al-Lisan (ʿawad) (saham), from a qasida of which many verses have passed. I mentioned this verse in explaining an earlier verse (10: 451, note 1). "Al-asham" means that which inclines to blackness; "ʿawad" refers to future time, meaning "forever." Scholars differed on the meaning of "bi-asham dajin" and the swearing by it. Some said it meant the night. Others said it meant the blackness of the nipple of his mother's breast. It was also said it meant the womb and its darkness. It was said it meant blood, because of its blackness, into which the hand is dipped at a covenant.]]

meaning: they swore an oath together.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors﴾, that is: I am among those who give you sincere counsel in what I advise you, and in ordering you to eat from the fruit of the tree you were forbidden to eat from, and in my informing you of what I tell you: that if you eat it, you will become angels or among the immortals. As related:

14396. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors"﴾: he swore to them both by God until he deceived them, and the believer may be deceived by God. He said: "I was created before you both, and I know more than you both, so follow me and I will guide you." And some scholars used to say: "Whoever deceives us by God, we are deceived."

On the exegesis of His words: ﴿So he lured them with deception. And when they tasted the tree, their shameful parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿So he lured them with deception﴾, He means: he deceived them with delusion.

It is said of this: "So-and-so never ceased luring so-and-so with deception," meaning he never ceased deceiving him with delusion and speaking to him with false embellished speech. [[See the explanation of "al-ghurur" (delusion) above, p. 123, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

= ﴿And when they tasted the tree﴾, he says: when Adam and Eve tasted the fruit of the tree, meaning they ate of it. [[See the explanation of "dhaqa" (tasted) above, p. 209, footnote 1, and the references.]] = ﴿Their shameful parts became apparent to them﴾, he says: their shameful parts were uncovered for them, because God had stripped them of the clothing with which He had clothed them before the sin and the transgression. He divested them of it because of the wrong they committed and the disobedience they engaged in. [[See the explanation of "bada" (became apparent) above, vol. 5, p. 582 / vol. 9, p. 350. And the explanation of "al-sau'ah" (shameful part) above, vol. 10, p. 229, and what will come later, p. 361, footnote 3.]] = ﴿And they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾, he says: they set about and began binding over themselves some leaves of the Garden, so as to cover their shameful parts, as follows:

14397. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾: he said, "They began taking from the leaves of the Garden and placing them over their shameful parts."

14398. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Adam was like a tall palm tree, very long, whose fruit is out of reach for the one who wants to pick it, with abundant hair on his head. When he committed the sin, his private part became visible to him, though he had not been seeing it. So he ran off fleeing, and a tree came in his way and caught him by his hair. He said to it, 'Release me!' It said, 'I will not release you!' So his Lord called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said, 'No, but I was ashamed before You.'" [[The report 14398: "al-Hajjaj" is Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, who has been mentioned many times. "Abu Bakr" is Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, mentioned under numbers 597, 8376, 13054; he is weak and not trustworthy. This report was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 3:458, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as a mawquf (ending with a Companion) report, not marfu' (traced to the Prophet). Ibn Kathir then said: "Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through several chains from al-Hasan, from Abu Ka'b, as marfu', but the mawquf is sounder in its chain." That is as he said. It will come later as number 14403, through the chain of Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, as mawquf.]]

14399. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna and Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan, from Imarah, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The tree which God forbade Adam and his wife was the ear of wheat. When they ate from it, their shameful parts became apparent to them. What covered their shameful parts was their fingernails. They began binding over themselves some leaves of the Garden, leaves of the fig tree, joining some of them to others. Adam then fled turning away through the Garden, and a tree of the Garden seized his head, and it called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, but I was ashamed before You, O Lord!' He said: 'Did you not have in what I gave you of the Garden and permitted you from it a sufficient alternative to what I forbade you?' He said: 'Yes, O Lord, but by Your might, I did not reckon that anyone would swear by You falsely.' He said: That is the saying of God: ﴿And he swore to them, 'Indeed I am to you among the sincere advisors.'﴾ He said: 'By My might, I will certainly bring you down to the earth, and you will not obtain livelihood except with toil.' He said: So he was brought down from the Garden, and they used to eat in it abundantly, and they were brought down into a place of abundant food and drink. He was taught the craft of iron, and was commanded to cultivate, so he cultivated and sowed, then irrigated, until when it reached harvest, he reaped it, then threshed it, then winnowed it, then ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate it. He did not swallow it until what God willed of it had been swallowed." [[The report 14399: "al-Hasan ibn Imarah ibn al-Mudrib al-Bajali" was in charge of judgeship in Baghdad during the reign of al-Mansur. Ahmad said: "Abandoned in narration, his narrations are rejected, his narrations are fabricated, and his hadith is not written down." The matter concerning him is even more severe than this. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/300, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/27. In the printed edition it read "from al-Hasan, from Imarah," which is a plain error; the correct reading is what is established from the manuscript, as in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir 3:459. In the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir: "fa-lam yablugh'hu hatta balagha..." all with dotted letters; what is in the manuscript is undotted, and I believe it is the correct reading matching the context.]]

14400. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying ﴿yakhsifan﴾: he said: "They patch, like the patching of a garment."

14401. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "They patch over themselves from the leaves, like the patching of a garment."

14402. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿So when they tasted the tree, their shameful parts became apparent to them﴾, and they had not been seeing them before that = ﴿And they began to fasten over themselves﴾, the verse.

14403. ... He said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: that Adam, peace be upon him, was a tall man, like a tall palm tree, with abundant hair on his head. When he fell into what he fell into of the sin, his private part became visible to him at that moment, though he had not been seeing it. So he ran away fleeing in the Garden, and a tree of the trees of the Garden caught his head. He said to it, "Release me!" It said, "I will not release you!" So his Lord called out to him: "O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?" He said, "My Lord, I was ashamed before You." [[The report 14403: See the commentary on the preceding report, number 14398. This is the mawquf report, and its chain is sounder than that marfu' one.]]

14404. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾, he said: "Leaves of the fig tree."

14405. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾, he said: "Leaves of the fig tree."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Hassam ibn Mishak, from Qatadah = and Abu Bakr, from other than Qatadah = who said: "Adam's clothing in the Garden was entirely of nails [of light], and when he fell into the sin, it was stripped from him and his private part became visible." = Abu Bakr said: Others than Qatadah said: "﴿And they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾," he said: "Leaves of the fig tree." [[The report 14406: "Hassam ibn Mishak ibn Zalim ibn Shaytan al-Azdi," weak, grossly erroneous and mistaken. It was mentioned under number 11720. He said: "The clothing of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, was light upon their private parts; this one's private part was not seen by that one, nor that one's by this one. * *

On the exegesis of His words: ﴿And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and tell you that Satan is a manifest enemy to you?"﴾ (22)

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says: And their Lord called out to Adam and Eve: "Did I not forbid you from eating the fruit of that tree whose fruit you ate, and inform you that Iblis is a manifest enemy to you?" = He says: He has made clear his enmity toward you by refusing to prostrate to Adam out of envy and rebellion. [[See the explanation of "mubin" (manifest) above, in the language indexes under (b-y-n).]] As follows:

14409. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding his saying: ﴿And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and tell you that Satan is a manifest enemy to you?"﴾: "Why did you eat it when I had forbidden you from it?" He said: "O Lord, Eve gave me to eat!" He said to Eve: "Why did you give him to eat?" She said: "The serpent commanded me!" He said to the serpent: "Why did you command her?" It said: "Iblis commanded me!" He said: "Cursed and banished! As for you, O Eve, just as you stained the tree [with blood], you will be stained every month. As for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs, so you will walk on your face, and whoever meets you will crush your head. Go down, some of you enemies to others." [[The report 14409: This narration was previously given in full with this chain under number 752, with slight variation in its wording. See its takhrij there.]]

14410. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it was said to him: 'Why did you eat from the tree I forbade you?' He said: 'Eve commanded me!' It said: 'Then I have made it so that she will not bear except with hardship, and will not give birth except with hardship.' Eve then wailed, and it was said to her: 'The wailing is upon you and upon your offspring.'" [[("Ranat al-mar'ah tarannu rannatan": the woman wailed, meaning she cried out and screamed from sorrow and distress. And "al-rinnah": the sorrowful cry at weeping.)]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 23:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about Adam and Eve in their reply to Him, their acknowledgment against themselves of the sin, and their asking Him for forgiveness and mercy from Him, in contrast to the reply of the accursed Iblis to Him.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves"﴾ is that Adam and Eve said to their Lord: "O our Lord, we have done wrong to ourselves by harming them through disobedience to You and opposing Your command, and by obeying our enemy and Your enemy in what we were not permitted to obey him in, namely eating from the tree You forbade us to eat from." [[The text here reads thus in the manuscript and the printed edition; the correct reading is probably: "we committed wrong against ourselves". See the explanation of "dhulm" in the language indexes under (ظلم).]] ﴿And if You do not forgive us﴾, meaning: if You do not cover over our sin, concealing it for us and leaving our disgrace by it unexposed through Your punishment of us for it [[See the explanation of "maghfirah" in the language indexes under (غفر).]] "and have mercy upon us", by Your kindness toward us and Your leaving off seizing us for it [[See the explanation of "rahmah" in the language indexes under (رحم).]] ﴿we will surely be among the losers﴾, meaning: we will surely be among the perished.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-khasir" (the loser) earlier, with its evidence and the transmitted reports concerning it, in a way that suffices and makes repeating it unnecessary here. [[See the explanation of "al-khusarah" (loss) earlier, p. 315, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

14411. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Adam, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, what do You think, if I repent and seek Your forgiveness?" He said: "Then I will admit you to the Garden." As for Iblis, he did not ask for repentance, but asked for respite, and each of them was given what he asked for.

14412. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us﴾, the verse, that he said: They are the words which Adam received from his Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 24:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Go down, some of you being enemies to others. And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about what He did with Iblis and his offspring, and with Adam and his offspring, and with the serpent.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Adam, Eve, Iblis and the serpent: "Go down from the heaven to the earth, some of you being enemies to others," as:

14413 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Talhah narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Go down, some of you being enemies to others﴾, he said: He cursed the serpent, cut off its legs, left it to walk on its belly, and made its sustenance from the dust. And they were sent down to the earth: Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent. [[The report 14413: "'Amr ibn Talhah" is "'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad," attributed to his grandfather. He has occurred hundreds of times in this chain and others: "'Amr ibn Hammad, from Asbat." It was previously mentioned under no. 755.]]

14414 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Abu 'Awanah, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿Go down, some of you being enemies to others﴾, he said: Adam, Eve, and the serpent. [[The report 14414 was previously mentioned under no. 754.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾, [[See the explanation of the similar verse previously: 1:535-541.]] He says: "And for you, O Adam and Eve, and Iblis and the serpent, on the earth is a settlement you will settle in, and a bed you will spread out," as:

14415 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾, he said: It is His saying: ﴿Who made the earth a bed for you﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 22]. [[The report 14415 was previously mentioned under no. 765. In the printed and manuscript editions here it read: "huwa alladhi ja'ala..." with an added "huwa", which is a slip of the copyist.]]

* *

And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this, that:

14416 - I was told, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾, he said: The graves. [[The report 14416: see what was previously mentioned under no. 767, with a different chain.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is that it should be said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed Adam, Eve, Iblis and the serpent, when they were sent down to the earth, that they are enemies to one another, and that for them therein is a dwelling place in which they settle. He did not restrict it to saying that they have a dwelling place therein during their lifetime rather than after their death; rather, He spoke of it in general terms, that for them therein is a dwelling place. So it applies in its generality, just as God's report covers it: they have a dwelling place therein during their lives upon its surface, and after their deaths within its belly, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?﴾ [Surah al-Mursalat: 25-26].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And provision for a time﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: "And for you therein is provision," which you enjoy until the cessation of this world; and that is the "time" He mentioned, as:

14417 - I was told, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, who said: Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And provision for a time﴾, he said: Until the Day of Resurrection and until the cessation of this world.

* *

And "al-hin" itself means a time, though its extent is unspecified [[See the explanation of "al-hin" previously: 1:540; it was not mentioned there in the explanation of the similar verse.]], as evidenced by the saying of the poet: [[He is Jarir.]]

"And what is your insolence after forbearance and religious devotion... while gray hair has overtaken you, a time that is no time."

[[The Diwan: 586; Sibawayh 1:358; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:212; al-Khizanah 2:94; and others. It is the opening of an ode in satire of al-Farazdaq. The Diwan and Sibawayh read: "ma bal jahlika ba'da al-hilmi wal-dini". After it: "For the young women there is a union that I will not sever... on their promise, with breaking and turning." "Indeed I fear the slanderers' belief about us, or that a rover might say to separation: 'Go away.'" "Al-mirah" (with a kasra on the mim): frivolity, pride and swaggering, which is from the madness of youth and self-conceit. The Diwan's reading appears to be the correct one. Sibawayh cited it as evidence for disregarding "la" and annexing the first "hin" to the second "hin," saying: "It is only hin hin, and 'la' is like 'ma' when it is disregarded." Abu Ja'far's source for this is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:212, who gave the verse as it is quoted here, though the printed Majaz reads "wa-ma mizaguka" with a zayn, which I believe is a typographical error.]]

That is, a time that is not a time.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 25:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Therein you shall live, and therein you shall die, and from it you shall be brought forth."﴾ (25)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: God said to those whom He had caused to descend from His heavens to His earth: ﴿Therein you shall live﴾, meaning: on the earth you shall live, that is, you will dwell there during the days of your lives. ﴿And therein you shall die﴾, meaning: on the earth your death will occur. ﴿And from it you shall be brought forth﴾, meaning: from the earth your Lord will bring you forth and gather you to Him for the resurrection, alive.

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Glorified is His praise, speaking to the ignorant among the Arabs who used to go naked while circumambulating (the Ka'bah), following the command of Satan and abandoning obedience to God. He made them aware of how they had been deceived by his delusion toward them, until he gained power over them and stripped them of the covering of God with which He had blessed them, so that he exposed their private parts and displayed them to one another, even though God had graciously enabled them to cover them. He had led them along his course regarding their parents Adam and Eve, whom he had lured by deception until he stripped them of the covering of God which He had bestowed upon them, until he exposed their private parts to them and left them naked: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing﴾, meaning by sending it down to them: that He created it for them and provided it to them. And "clothing" (libas) is what they wear of garments. ﴿To conceal your private parts﴾, meaning: to cover your nakedness from your eyes. And "private parts" (sawat) is used as a euphemism for nakedness ('awrat).

* *

Its singular is "sawah", which is on the pattern "fa'lah" from "al-su'" (evil), and it was called "sawah" because its exposure from the body distresses its owner, as the poet said: [I do not know who said it.]

They tore open the collar of their young woman... they did not mind the sawat of the man.

[Al-Kamil 1:165, Sharh al-Hamasah 1:117, Lisan (rajul), and others. Before the verse: "Every neighbor remained pleased with himself... other than my neighbors, the Banu Jabalah."

Their version: "they did not mind the sanctity (hurmah) of the man." By his saying "the collar of their young woman" he alluded to her nakedness and genitals. He used the masculine "rajul" and made the woman "rajulah".]

* *

Those interpreting the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

14418 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿clothing to conceal your private parts﴾, he said: Some people among the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, and none of them would wear a garment in which he had circumambulated.

14419 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

14420 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani related to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment﴾, he said: Four verses were revealed concerning Quraysh. In the Jahiliyyah they used to circumambulate the House only naked.

14421 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from 'Awf, who said: I heard Ma'bad al-Juhani say regarding His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment﴾, he said: The clothing is what you wear.

14422 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts﴾, he said: Quraysh used to circumambulate naked, and none of them would wear a garment in which he had circumambulated. Indeed, some people among the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked.

14423 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Sahl ibn Yusuf related to us, from 'Awf, from Ma'bad al-Juhani: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts﴾, he said: The clothing that conceals your private parts is your garments (labus) these. [Labus means garments, and it is masculine; if you take it to mean "garments" you may make it feminine. In the printed edition it read "hadha labusukum", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]

14424 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿clothing to conceal your private parts﴾, he said: They are garments.

14425 - al-Harith related to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, saying: Someone who heard 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr say related to me: "Clothing" means garments.

14426 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿We have certainly sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts﴾, he said: It means the garments of a man that he wears.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿and finery﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

The reading of the majority of the reciters of the regional cities is ﴿wariyshan﴾ (and finery), without an alif.

It is also reported from Zirr ibn Hubaysh and al-Hasan al-Basri that they both recited it as "wariyashan" (and finery, with an alif).

14427. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Aban al-'Attar, who said: 'Asim narrated to us that Zirr ibn Hubaysh recited it as "wariyashan".

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter is the reading of the one who recited ﴿wariyshan﴾ without an alif, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it.

It has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ a report whose chain is open to scrutiny, that he recited it as "wariyashan". [[This report will come with its chain under number 14446.]]

As for the one who recited it as "wariyashan", it is possible that he intended by it the plural of "al-rish" (feathers, plumage), just as "al-dhi'b" (the wolf) is pluralized as "dhi'ab" and "al-bi'r" (the well) as "bi'ar".

It is also possible that he intended it as a verbal noun (masdar), from the saying of the speaker: "Allah rashahu yarishuhu riyashan wa rishan" (God clothed him/enriched him, he clothes/enriches him, with riyash and rish). [[He here intended to make "rishan" a verbal noun with a kasra on the "ra'", as is clear in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Quran 1:375, and for this reason I have vocalised it so. What the lexicographers have stated is that the verbal noun "rishan" is with a fatha then a sukun.]] Just as one says: "labisahu yalbasuhu libasan wa libsan" (he wore it, he wears it, wearing and wear). Some of them recited the following verse: [[It is Humayd ibn Thawr al-Hilali.]]

"When they uncovered the clothing from him, they wiped him
with the fingertips of a tender child, adorning the thicket, tattooed."

[[In his Diwan: 14; also Ma'ani al-Quran of al-Farra' 1:375, al-Lisan (labisa, tafl), al-Mukhassas 4:35, and others. This verse is from a long qasida of his in his Diwan, which I consider to be out of order, and this verse is among those that are out of order. It describes the man, and he said about him (as in the Diwan, verse no. 37), after the slave-girls had adorned him: "The craftswomen attended to him, and matched with him the horses until he was about to neigh." Then he said after no. 40: "You would think, when they hung the embroidery, a steed walking with lofty gaze and bridled." And he said before the verse (both in the Diwan order: 32, 33): "They adorned him with wool until, if it were said to him, 'Come, come forward!' he would advance." The howdah had become like a horse with its adornment, splendour and saddle. His words "When they uncovered the clothing from him" refer to the howdah. "Wiped him" refers to the slave-girls who made it, decorated and embellished it. "Tifl" (with fatha and sukun) is the soft finger; he meant: wiped him with the fingertips of a tender child's fingers, making "tifl" a substitute for "al-bunan" (fingers). "Ghayl" (with fatha and sukun) is the full, lush forearm. "Mawshsham" means bearing tattoos, which was an adornment of the Jahiliyya that Islam abolished, and God curse the one who makes them, whether man or woman.]]
with a kasra on the "lam" in "al-libs".

"Al-riyash," in the speech of the Arabs, is household goods and whatever appears of garments and possessions that are worn or stuffed, such as bedding or coverings.

"Al-rish" is, among them, only property and wealth. They sometimes use it of garments and clothing apart from the rest of wealth. They say: "He gave him a saddle with its rish" and "a camel-saddle with its rish," meaning with its clothing and equipment. They say: "He is fine in the rish of garments," and "riyash" may be used of abundance and comfortable living.

Abu Ja'far said: Commentators have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that "riyash" means property:

14428. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿wariyshan﴾, he said: wealth.

14429. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿wariyshan﴾, he said: wealth.

14430. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14431. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "wariyashan", he said: As for "riyashan", it is the wealth of property. [[Since the second reading "riyash" has come in these reports, I leave it as it is and do not change it to our reading.]]

14432. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani narrated to us, saying: One who heard 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr say to me: "al-riyash" is wealth.

14433. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "wariyashan", he means: wealth.

Those who said: it is clothing and comfortable living.

14434. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "wariyashan", he said: "riyash" is clothing, living and bounty.

14435. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Awf, from Ma'bad al-Juhani: "wariyashan", he said: "riyash" is livelihood.

14436. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Ma'bad al-Juhani said: "wariyashan", he said: it is livelihood.

Others said: "al-rish" is beauty.

Those who said that:

14437. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "wariyashan", he said: "al-rish" is beauty.

Abu Ja'far said: Commentators have differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: "libas al-taqwa" (the garment of God-consciousness) is faith.

Those who said that:

14438. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, it is faith.

14439. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, faith.

14440. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, faith.

Others said: it is modesty.

Those who said that:

14441. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Awf, from Ma'bad al-Juhani regarding His words: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, which God mentioned in the Qur'an, is modesty.

14442. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Ma'bad al-Juhani said, and mentioned the like of it.

14443. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from 'Awf, from Ma'bad, similarly.

Others said: it is righteous deed.

Those who said that:

14444. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the garment of taqwa, that is better﴾, he said: the garment of taqwa is righteous deed.

Others said: rather, it is good bearing.

Those who said that:

14445. Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from ... ibn 'Amr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, he said: good bearing in the face. [[Report 14445: In this chain in the manuscript it reads "from al-Dana ibn 'Amr", a word whose reading I did not know, so I placed dots in its place; in the printed edition it was "al-Zaba' ibn 'Amr", and I do not know from where this name came!! I found in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:462: "al-Dayyal ibn 'Amr", and this too; I did not know what it would be.
"Muhammad ibn Musa": I could not identify who he is.]]

14446. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Arqam, from al-Hasan who said: I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan on the pulpit of the Messenger of God ﷺ, wearing a Quhistani shirt with its button undone. [[The "Quhistani shirt" is ascribed to Quhistan, a land adjoining the regions of Herat and Nishapur, to which a kind of garment is ascribed.]] I heard him order the killing of dogs and forbid playing with pigeons, then he said: O people, fear God regarding these inner secrets, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one ever does a secret deed except that God clothes him with the cloak of openness, [[Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, quoting this place from al-Tabari, says: "No one hides a secret except that God clothes it with its cloak openly," and I do not know from where this difference came; in the printed edition it is "his cloak", and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript.]] if good then good, and if evil then evil." Then he recited this verse: "wariyashan" (not reading it as ﴿wariyshan﴾) = ﴿and the garment of taqwa, that is better; that is among the signs of God﴾, and he said: good bearing.

[[Report 14446: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj al-Razi al-Tahhan, already mentioned under numbers 230, 1614, 10314. "Ishaq ibn Isma'il" perhaps is "Ishaq ibn li-Isma'il al-Razi", Abu Yazid, Hubawayh. Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/212.
"Sulayman ibn Arqam", Abu Mu'adh. Very weak, abandoned in hadith, mentioned under number 4923. Because of the weakness of Sulayman ibn Arqam, Abu Ja'far said previously on p. 363, note 1, that there is open scrutiny in the chain of this report.
Ibn Kathir narrated this report in his tafsir 3:462, 463, and weakened it, then said: "The imams al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and al-Bukhari in the Book of Adab have related sound reports from al-Hasan that he heard the commander of the believers 'Uthman ibn 'Affan order the killing of dogs and the slaughter of pigeons on Friday on the pulpit." I say: Ahmad's report is in the Musnad, number 521, and al-Bukhari's report is in al-Adab al-Mufrad pp. 332, 333, number 1301.]]

Others said: it is fear of God.

Those who said that:

14447. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd al-Madani narrated to us, saying: One who heard 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿libas al-taqwa﴾, is the fear of God.

Others said: ﴿libas al-taqwa﴾ in these places is covering the nakedness.

Those who said that:

14448. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿and the garment of taqwa﴾, one who is mindful of God covers his nakedness, that is "the garment of taqwa".

The readers differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the readers of Mecca, Kufa and Basra recited: ﴿wa-libasu al-taqwa dhalika khayr﴾, with the "wa-libasu" in the nominative.

The majority of the readers of Medina recited: "wa-libasa al-taqwa", with "al-libas" in the accusative, and this is the reading of some of the readers of Kufa.

As for one who put "wa-libasa" in the accusative, he made it accusative by conjunction with "al-rish", meaning: We have indeed sent down upon you clothing that covers your private parts and riyash, and We have sent down the garment of taqwa.

As for the nominative, the grammarians of Arabic differ regarding the case that makes "al-libas" nominative.

One of the grammarians of Basra said: it is nominative as a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in His words: ﴿that is better﴾. But some grammarians refuted him in this, saying: This is an error, because no returning pronoun refers back to "al-libas" in the sentence, so that "al-libas" would be a subject with "dhalika khayr" as its predicate.

One of the grammarians of Kufa said: ﴿wa-libas﴾ is nominative by its being a predicate of: "wa-libasu al-taqwa khayr" (and the garment of taqwa is better), and "dhalika" is its attribute.

Abu Ja'far said: This view is, in my opinion, more correct regarding the case-marking of "al-libas", because there is no way to make it nominative except that it be nominative by "khayr", and when it is nominative by "khayr" there is no way except to make "al-libas" a qualifier, not that it refers back to "al-libas" through the mention in His words: ﴿that is better﴾, so that "khayr" would be nominative by "dhalika" and "dhalika" would be by it.

Since this is so, the meaning of the speech, when "libas al-taqwa" is nominative, is: and the garment of taqwa, that which you have known, is better for you, O children of Adam, than the clothing garments which cover your private parts, and than the riyash which We sent down to you; so put it on.

As for the interpretation of one who recited it in the accusative, it is: "O children of Adam, We have indeed sent down upon you clothing that covers your private parts and riyash and the garment of taqwa"; this which We sent down upon you of the clothing that covers your nakedness, and the riyash, and the garment of taqwa is better for you than nakedness and stripping of clothes during your circumambulation of the House. So fear God, put on what God has provided you of riyash, and do not obey Satan by stripping and baring yourselves of clothes, for that is mockery and deception from him against you, as he did to your parents Adam and Eve, deceiving them until he stripped them of the garment of God which He had clothed them with by their obedience to Him, in eating what God had forbidden them to eat from the fruit of the tree whose fruit they disobeyed Him by eating.

Abu Ja'far said: This reading is, in my opinion, the more correct of the two readings, I mean the accusative of His words "wa-libasa al-taqwa", because its meaning in interpretation is sound as I have explained, and because God began the report about His sending down of the clothing that covers our nakedness and the riyash, as a rebuke to the polytheists who used to strip during their circumambulation of the House, and who commanded them to take their clothes and cover themselves with them in every state, together with faith in Him and following His obedience; and He informs them that all of that is better than everything they were upon of their disbelief in God and their nakedness, not that He informed them that some of what was sent down to them is better than some.

What confirms the soundness of what we have said in this matter is the verses after this verse, namely His words: "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts," and what follows of verses up to His words: "and that you say about God what you do not know." For He, great is His praise, in all of that commands taking adornment from clothing, using garments and abandoning stripping and nakedness, and faith in Him, following His command and acting by His obedience, and forbids associating others with Him and following the command of Satan, emphasising in all of that what He has summarised in His words: "O children of Adam, We have indeed sent down upon you clothing that covers your private parts and riyash, and the garment of taqwa, that is better."

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings regarding the interpretation of His words "and the garment of taqwa" is the souls' perception of the fear of God, in refraining from what God has forbidden of His disobedience and acting upon what He has commanded of His obedience. This encompasses faith, righteous deed, modesty, fear of God and good bearing, for whoever fears God is a believer in Him, acts upon what He has commanded, is fearful of Him, watches Him, and is shy before Him in what He dislikes from His servants. Whoever is like this, the signs of goodness appear in him, so his bearing and his conduct are good, and the radiance and light of faith are seen upon him.

We have said that by "the garment of taqwa" is meant the perception of the soul and heart, because "libas" is only the wearing of what is worn and the covering of what is clothed, or covering the body or part of it with it. Whoever wears something and covers himself with it, until his person or its trace is seen upon him, is "wearing" it. For this reason, He, great is His praise, made men a garment for women and women a garment for them, and made the night a garment for His servants. [[The first witness is the verse in Surat al-Baqara 2:187: "They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them." The second witness is the verse in Surat al-Naba' 78:10: "And We made the night a garment."]]

The discussion of one who interpreted it with the meaning we have mentioned, when "wa-libasu al-taqwa" is recited in the nominative.

[14449] Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿And the garment of God-consciousness﴾: it is faith. ﴿That is better﴾: he says, that is better than the finery and clothing which conceals your private parts.

[14450] Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And the garment of God-consciousness﴾. He said: The garment of God-consciousness is better, and it is faith.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿That is of the signs of God, perhaps they will remember﴾
