Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: That which I have mentioned to you, O people, that I sent down to you, of clothing and finery, is among the proofs and evidences of God by which He makes known to those who disbelieve the correctness of God's oneness and the error of what they persist in of misguidance. ﴿Perhaps they will remember﴾: His glory says: I made that a proof for them of what I have described, so that they may remember and take heed, and turn back to the truth and abandon falsehood, as a mercy from Me to My servants. [[See the entry on "ayah" (sign) in the previous lexical indices (a-y-y), and the entry on "yadhkuru" (remember) in them (dh-k-r).]]

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words: ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping off from them their clothing to show them their private parts.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O children of Adam, let not Satan deceive you so that he exposes your private parts to people through your obedience to him when he tests you, just as he did to your parents Adam and Eve when he tested them, so they obeyed him and disobeyed their Lord. He removed them from the Garden by means of the deception and trickery he caused them, and he stripped from them the clothing that he had put on them, so as to show them their private parts by uncovering their nakedness and displaying it to their eyes after it had been concealed.

* *

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of "fitnah" (temptation, trial) is testing and trying, which is sufficient without repeating it. [See the explanation of "fitnah" above, vol. 11: 388, footnote 1, and the references there.]

* *

The interpreters have differed concerning the nature of the "libas" (clothing) that God, may His majesty be exalted, said He stripped from our parents.

Some of them said: It was fingernails.

Mention of those whose statements were not mentioned earlier in this book regarding this:

14451- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾: He said: The clothing of every animal from it, and the clothing of man is the fingernail; so repentance reached Adam at his fingernail — or he said: his fingernails.

14452- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from Nadr Abu Umar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: His fingernails were left upon him as adornment and benefit, regarding His words: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾. [Note on the chain: "Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani" is "Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hamani," mentioned earlier under nos. 718 and 7863. "Nadr, Abu Umar" is "al-Nadr ibn Abd al-Rahman," Abu Umar al-Kharraz, also mentioned under nos. 718 and 10373; the printed edition had "Nasr ibn Umar," differing from the manuscript, which reads "Nasr Abi Umar," undotted.]

14453- Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir narrated to us, saying: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn informed us, from Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾, who said: Their clothing was the fingernail; when they committed the sin, it was stripped from them, and the fingernails were left as a reminder and adornment.

14454- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hamani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾, who said: His clothing was the fingernail, and his repentance ended at his fingernails.

* *

Others said: Their clothing was light.

Mention of those who said that:

14455- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾: the light.

14456- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, who said: Amr narrated to us, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say regarding His words: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing to show them their private parts﴾: The clothing of Adam and Eve was light upon their private parts; this one could not see the nakedness of that one, nor that one the nakedness of this one.

* *

Others said: God only meant by His words ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾ that He divested them of the piety of God.

Mention of those who said that:

14457- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Mutalib ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾: He said: Piety. [Note on the narrator: Mutalib ibn Ziyad ibn Abi Zuhayr al-Thaqafi; Ibn Sa'd said he was very weak in hadith; Ibn Adi said he had good and strange narrations and that he had seen nothing objectionable in him; Abu Hatim said his hadith is written but not used as proof.]

14458- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾: He said: Piety.

14459- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hamani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in interpreting this, in my opinion, is to say that God, may He be exalted, warned His servants that Satan should tempt them as he tempted their parents Adam and Eve, and that he should strip them of the garment of God which He sent down to them, just as He stripped their parents of their clothing. "Libas" used absolutely in speech, without addition to anything, in the common usage of people, is what the wearer puts on of various types of covering, or covers his body or part of it.

Since that is so, the truth is to say that what God related about Adam and Eve regarding the clothing that Satan stripped from them was part of what they used to cover their bodies and their nakedness.

It may be that it was fingernails; it may be that it was light; it may be something else. We have no report by which any of these is established as proof, so there is no statement on this more correct than saying as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿He stripped from them their clothing﴾.

* *

God, may His praise be exalted, attributed to Iblis the expulsion of Adam and Eve from the Garden and the stripping of their clothing from them, although God Himself is the one who did that to them as punishment for their disobedience to Him, since what came from them in that was due to Satan making it easy for them through his guile and deception. So it is sometimes attributed to him, and sometimes to God by His doing that to them.

* *

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: By this God, may His praise be exalted, means: Indeed, Satan sees you, he and... [the "ha" in "innahu" refers to Satan], and "qabilahu," meaning his kind and species from which he is, is one... [the word "jil" (kind, race) denotes each category of people or nation; it is said: "the Turks are a jil, the Chinese a jil, the Arabs a jil, the Romans a jil," meaning each people distinguished by a language, from whose gathering arises a nation and category of people known and described.] — namely the jinn, as:

1445(60)- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you﴾: He said: The jinn and the devils.

1445(61)- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you﴾: "Qabilahu" — his offspring.

* *

As for His words: ﴿from where you do not see them﴾, He means: from where you, O people, do not see Satan and his tribe. ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾, He means: We have made the devils helpers of the disbelievers who do not affirm God's oneness nor believe His messengers.

**The interpretation of His words (Exalted is He):** ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾ (7:28)

Abu Ja'far said: It has been mentioned that the meaning of "indecency" (al-fahisha) in this place [[See the explanation of "al-fahisha" and "al-fahsha" in the preceding discussion: p. 218, note 1, and the references there.]] is:

14462. Ali ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Kindi related to me, saying: Abu Muhyat related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."﴾ He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, saying, "We circumambulate as our mothers bore us." The woman would place upon her private part a *nisah* [[*Al-qubul* (with two dammas): the private parts of a woman and a man. *Al-nisah*: a wide strip of plaited leather placed on the chest of a camel.]] or something similar, and she would say:

*Today some of it or all of it appears,*
*But what appears of it, I do not make lawful.*
[[Athar 14462: "Abu Muhyat" is Yahya ibn Ya'la ibn Harmala al-Taymi, a trustworthy narrator. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/311, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/196.

The report's takhrij (sourcing) will come in Takhrij al-Athar: 14503–14506.]]

* * *

14463. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it"﴾ He said: Their indecency was that they circumambulated the House naked.

14464. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Mufaddal, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

14464. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Imran ibn Uyayna related to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi, regarding ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it"﴾ He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked.

14465. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."﴾ He said: A tribe of the Arabs from the people of Yemen used to circumambulate the House naked. When it was said to them, "Why do you do this?" they would say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."

14466. Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And when they commit an indecency﴾ He said: Their circumambulation of the House naked.

14467. Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it"﴾ He said: Concerning the circumambulation of the *Hums* in clothing, while others circumambulated naked. [[*Al-Hums*, plural of *Ahmas*, are the Quraysh, because of their strictness in their religion. For a detailed explanation of this, see above, 3:557, note 1, and report no. 3832, where it is stated: "the religion of Quraysh."]]

14468. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it"﴾ He said: Their women used to circumambulate the House naked. That is the indecency upon which they found their fathers: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency"﴾, the verse.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement, then, is: When those who do not believe in Allah, those whom Allah has made the devils their allies, commit an ugly act, which is "indecency"—namely, their exposing themselves and stripping naked for circumambulation of the House—they are rebuked for the ugliness of what they did and are reproached for it, and they say, "We found our fathers doing the like of what we do; so we do as they used to do, follow their guidance, and adhere to their practice. And Allah has commanded us to it, so we follow His command in it."

Allah, mentioning His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say"—O Muhammad—to them: "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency," meaning: He does not command His creatures to ugly deeds and evil acts. "Do you say"—O people—"about Allah that which you do not know?" meaning: Do you claim, concerning Allah, that He has commanded you to strip and to remove clothing for circumambulation [[Thus it is in the printed edition and the manuscript: "atarun ruyun 'ala Allah" (do you claim concerning Allah). I incline toward the correct reading being "atazurun" (do you fabricate), i.e., "do you utter falsehood and lies."]] while you do not know that He has commanded you to that?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 29:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice, and set your faces upright at every place of prostration, and call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted One says to His Prophet: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these people who claim that God commanded them to indecency, lying against God: My Lord did not command what you say. Rather, ﴿My Lord has commanded justice﴾, meaning: equity (al-qist, the term discussed earlier, see p. 224, note 4, and the references there), as:

14469. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice﴾, meaning equity.

14470. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice﴾; and justice (al-qist) is equity.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: turn your faces wherever you are in prayer toward the Ka'bah.

Those who said this:

14471. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾: toward the Ka'bah wherever you pray, in the church and elsewhere.

14472. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾, he said: When you pray, face the Ka'bah, in your churches and elsewhere.

14473. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾: it is "the place of prostration" (al-masjid), the Ka'bah.

14474. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dharr, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾, he said: The Ka'bah, wherever you are.

14475. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾, he said: Keep them upright toward the qibla, this qibla which God has commanded you.

* *

Others said: Rather, He meant by it: make your prostration purely for God, apart from whatever else is worshipped as gods and rivals.

Those who said this:

14476. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾, he said: It is in sincerity, that you not call upon other than Him, and that you make the religion sincerely His.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two interpretations of the verse is what al-Rabi' said: namely, that the people were commanded to direct their prayers to their Lord, not to what is other than Him of idols and images, and to make their supplication to God sincere, without mukaa' and tasdiya. [(Mukaa') is whistling, and (tasdiya) is clapping. They used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling with their mouths and clapping with their hands.]

We said this is the more correct interpretation of the verse because God addressed this verse to a people of the polytheists of the Arabs, who were not people of churches and synagogues; churches and synagogues belonged only to the People of the Two Books. It is not reasonable to say to one who does not pray in a church or synagogue: "Turn your face to the Ka'bah in a church or synagogue."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His﴾, He says: act for your Lord, making your religion and obedience sincerely His, not mixing that with polytheism, and not making any partner in what you do for Him, [(Consult the explanation of (du'a', supplication) and (ikhlas, sincerity) in the language indexes under the roots (d-'-a) and (kh-l-s).] as:

14477. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿and call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His﴾, he said: that you make the religion, the supplication and the deed sincerely His, then turn toward the Sacred House.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return. A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error has become due﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return.﴾

Some of them said: its interpretation is: as He originated you wretched and happy, so you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:

14478. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return. A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error has become due﴾, he said: God, glory be to Him, originated the creation of the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, as His Majestic Praise said: ﴿He it is who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer﴾ [Surat al-Taghabun: 2], then He will restore them on the Day of Resurrection as He originated their creation, believers and disbelievers.

14479. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, who said: Our companions narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: The believer is raised as a believer, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

14480. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from a man, from Jabir, who said: They will be raised upon what they were upon: the believer upon his faith, and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy. [Report 14480: (Yahya ibn al-Dahhak ibn Yasar al-Bajali al-Razi) is trustworthy, one whose books were sound and who took knowledge well. Biographical entries in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/282, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/158.]

14481. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: They returned to His knowledge of them. Have you not heard God's words about them: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾? Have you not heard His words: ﴿A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error has become due﴾?

14482. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: They were returned to His knowledge of them.

14483. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Hammam al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b regarding His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: Whoever God originated the creation of in wretchedness reaches what God originated his creation upon, even if he acts by the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis acted by the deeds of the people of happiness, then he reaches what his creation was originated upon. And whoever was originated in happiness reaches what his creation was originated upon, even if he acts by the deeds of the people of wretchedness, just as the magicians acted by the deeds of the people of wretchedness, [(Meaning the magicians of Pharaoh, who believed in Moses, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet.)] then they reached what their creation was originated upon.

14484. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Waqa' ibn Iyas Abu Yazid, from Mujahid: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: The Muslim is raised as a Muslim, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever. [Report 14484: (Waqa' ibn Iyas al-Asadi al-Walibi), Abu Yazid, trustworthy but spoken of; Yahya ibn Sa'id said: "He was not one to be relied upon." Biographical entries in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/188, which mentions no criticism, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/49. In the manuscript it read "Warqa' ibn Iyas," and the correct form is that of the printed edition.]

14485. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Yazid, from Mujahid: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: The Muslim is raised as a Muslim, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever. [Report 14485: "Abu Yazid" is Waqa' ibn Iyas, discussed in the preceding note.]

14486. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Wadda narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: As it was decreed for you, so you will be.

14487. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, the like of it.

14488. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return. A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error has become due﴾, he says: As He originated you, so you will return, as We created you: a party rightly guided, and a party astray; thus you will return and come forth from the wombs of your mothers.

14489. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abi Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sufyan, from Jabir, that the Prophet ﷺ said: Every soul will be raised upon what it was upon. [Report 14489: "Abu Sufyan" is Talha ibn Nafi' al-Qurashi al-Wasiti, trustworthy, whom the group narrated from; he has appeared earlier under numbers 6654, 11517, 11518. He is the one who narrates from Jabir, and al-A'mash's transmission is from him. In both the printed and manuscript editions it read "from Sufyan, from Jabir," which is an undoubted error; the correct reading is as quoted from Tafsir al-Tabari in Ibn Kathir 3:466.

This report has a sound chain. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 17:210 by two routes from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, with the wording: "Every servant will be raised upon what he died upon." Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan 1414, no. 4230, by the route of Shurayk, from al-A'mash, with the wording: "People will be gathered upon their intentions."]

14490. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: As it was decreed for you, so you will be.

14491. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: The believer is raised as a believer, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

14492. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾: wretched and happy.

14493. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us by reading, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: as He created you when you were not anything, you will return after annihilation.

Those who said this:

14494. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: As He originated you when you were nothing, then gave you life, so He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life on the Day of Resurrection.

14495. Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: As He originated you in this world, so you will return on the Day of Resurrection alive.

14496. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: He originated their creation when they were nothing, then they departed, then He will restore them.

14497. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return. A party He has guided﴾, he says: As We created you the first time, so you will return.

14498. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾: He will give you life after your death.

14499. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, he said: As He created them first, so He will restore them last.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the statements in the interpretation of this, in truth, is the statement of the one who said: its meaning is: as God originated you as creatures after you were not anything, so you will return after your annihilation as a creation like it, and He will gather you until the Day of Resurrection. This is because God, exalted is His remembrance, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform the polytheists, people of ignorance, who do not believe in the return and do not affirm the Resurrection, of what is in this verse. He commanded him to call them to acknowledge that God will raise them on the Day of Resurrection, and reward whoever obeys Him, and punish whoever disobeys Him. So He said to him: Say to them: My Lord has commanded justice, and that you set your faces upright, and that you call upon Him making your religion sincerely His, and that you acknowledge that as He originated you, so you will return. Thus the mention of "that you acknowledge that" is omitted, just as the mention of "that" with "set upright" was omitted, since what was mentioned indicates what was omitted from it.

Since this is so, there is no sense in commanding one who denies resurrection after death to call to acknowledgment of the state by which those who are resurrected are raised. Rather, one is commanded to call to that only if he believes in resurrection. As for one who denies it, he is called first to acknowledge it, and then informed of the conditions of resurrection. Moreover, in the report transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ, which:

14500. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: People will be gathered naked, barefoot and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrahim ﷺ. Then he recited: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall restore it, a promise upon Us; indeed We shall do it﴾ [Surat al-Anbiya: 104].

14501. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

14502. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ stood among us to exhort, and said: O people, you will be gathered to God barefoot, naked and uncircumcised: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall restore it, a promise upon Us; indeed We shall do it﴾.

[Reports 14500–14502: (al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man al-Nakha'i) is trustworthy, previously cited under number 13622.

This report was narrated by al-Bukhari from Shu'ba, from al-Mughira, in his Sahih (Fath 8:332 / 11:331), in full; Muslim also narrated it in full in his Sahih 17:193–194 by the route of Shu'ba. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad in full and abridged, nos. 1950, 2027, by the route of Sufyan al-Thawri in abridged form, as al-Tabari also narrated it. He then narrated it in full by the route of Shu'ba, nos. 2096, 2281, 2282. al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan 4:117.

Abu Ja'far will narrate it with these chains again in what follows, in the commentary on Surat al-Anbiya, 17:80 (Bulaq).

"Ghurul" is the plural of "aghral," meaning one who is uncircumcised.]

* *

= [This completes the first discussion; the context is: "Moreover, in the report transmitted from the Messenger of God... what clarifies the correctness of the statement."] What clarifies the correctness of the statement we made regarding it, that its meaning is: that creation will return to God on the Day of Resurrection as living creatures, just as He originated them in this world as living creatures.

* *

It is said from this: "God originated the creation, He originates them" and "He caused them to originate, causing their origination" — two eloquent dialects, meaning: He created them.

* *

Then the Exalted One began a report about what preceded in His knowledge of His creation and what His decree has run concerning them. He said: God guided a party of them, so He granted them success in righteous deeds, and they are rightly guided; and error has become due upon a party of them, from the guidance and right direction, by their taking Satan as a guardian apart from God.

* *

When the interpretation is this, the first "party" is in the accusative by the governing of "guided" over it, and the second "party" by the occurrence of His words "has become due" upon a pronoun referred to in "upon them," as His Exalted Praise said: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and the wrongdoers—He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ [Surat al-Insan: 31; see the Qur'anic grammatical discussion in al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:376].

* *

As for one who directs the interpretation to mean: as He originated you in this world as two kinds, disbelievers and believers, so you will return in the Hereafter as two groups: a party guided, and a party upon whom error has become due = "a party" is in the accusative by His words "you will return," and the second is made a conjunction to it. We have already stated what we hold to be correct regarding it. [See the explanation of (firqa, party) earlier, 11:490, note 2, and the references there.]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided﴾ (30).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the party upon whom error has been decreed only went astray from the path of Allah and deviated from the straight target, by taking the devils as helpers and supporters instead of Allah, [[See the explanation of "wali" (ally) in the previous indices of language, under (w-l-y).]] out of ignorance of the error of what they were upon in this, rather, they did that while they thought they were upon guidance and truth, and that the correct course was what they had come to and adopted.

This is among the clearest proofs against the error of the one who claims that Allah does not punish anyone for a disobedience he commits or an error he holds to, unless he commits it after knowing the correct way of it, and so commits it out of defiance toward his Lord in it. For if that were the case, there would be no difference between the party of error, who went astray while thinking he was guided, and the party of guidance. And Allah has distinguished between their names and their rulings in this verse.[[See the explanation of "hasiba" (to think/suppose) in the previous volume 10: 478, note: 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.﴾ (7:31)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to those who strip naked while circling His Sacred House and expose their private parts there, from among the idolaters of the Arabs, and those among them who forbade themselves what God had not forbidden them of the lawful provision He gave them, seeking to appear righteous in their own eyes before their Lord: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment﴾, meaning clothing and garments, ﴿at every place of prayer, and eat﴾, meaning of the good things with which I have provided you and made lawful for you, ﴿and drink﴾, meaning of the lawful drinks, and do not forbid anything except what I have forbidden you in My Book or on the tongue of My Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

14503- Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Salamah, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that the women used to circumambulate the House naked, and in another place he said: without garments, except that a woman would place a rag over her private part, as is described, God willing, and she would say:

Today some of it or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful.

He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer.﴾ [[Narration 14503 – the hadith of Shu'bah from Salamah ibn Kuhayl; Abu Ja'far transmitted it by three routes, which I will cite in this place.

Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi al-Shaybani, Abu Zakariyya, trustworthy; passed as no. 7818; biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/137.

Khalid ibn al-Harith ibn Ubayd al-Hujaymi, trustworthy, firm, an imam. Passed as nos. 7507, 7818, 9878.

"Salamah" is Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who has passed several times.

"Muslim al-Batin" is Muslim ibn Imran, trustworthy; the collectors of the six books narrated from him.

This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 18:162, through the route of Ghundar, from Shu'bah (and it comes below as no. 14506).

Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:319, 320 through the route of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, in similar form, but he said: "This verse was revealed: Say, who has forbidden the adornment of God." Then al-Hakim said: "It is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi concurred.]]

14504- Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to circumambulate naked, the men by day and the women by night, and a woman would say:

Today some of it or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful.

So God said: ﴿Take your adornment.﴾ [[Narration 14504 – a repetition of the preceding report, whose takhrij is given there.]]

14505- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾, he said: the garments.

14506- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ghundar and Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl who said: I heard Muslim al-Batin narrate, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas who said: A woman used to circumambulate the House naked – Ghundar said: "and she was naked" – he said. Wahb said: A woman would circumambulate the House having exposed her chest and what is beyond it – Ghundar said: and she would say: "Who will lend me a tiwaf [[The word "tiwaf" (with a kasra on the ta') means: a garment they used to take for circumambulation. Al-Nawawi said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to circumambulate naked, throwing their garments down and leaving them lying on the ground, never taking them back, letting them be trampled underfoot until they wore out; this was called al-liqa'. Until Islam came, and God commanded the covering of the private parts, saying: 'Take your adornment at every place of prayer,' and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'No one who is naked should circumambulate the House.'" It is also reported as "tiwaf" (with a fatha on the ta'), and they explained it as "one who has circumambulation," by eliding the modified noun.]]?" – she places it over her private part and says:

Today some of it or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful.

So God revealed: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer.﴾ [[Narration 14506 – a repetition of the two preceding reports 14503 and 14504, whose takhrij was given at the first of them. This is the wording of Muslim's hadith.]]

14507- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer.﴾ He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to wear their garments and not go naked.

14508- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ the verse. He said: Men used to circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them with adornment. "Adornment" is clothing, which covers the nakedness, and what is beyond that of fine cloth and goods; so they were commanded to take their adornment at every place of prayer.

14509- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Al-Muharibi and Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata: ﴿Take your adornment﴾, he said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were commanded to wear their garments.

14510- Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata, in similar form.

14511- Amr narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Ata regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ "Wear your garments."

14512- Yaqub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: Some people used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were forbidden from that.

14513- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were commanded to wear garments.

14514- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: Whatever covers the nakedness, even a cloak.

14515- Amr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id, Abu Asim and Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: Whatever covers your nakedness, even a cloak.

14516- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ concerning the Quraysh, for their leaving garments aside during circumambulation.

14517- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, in similar form.

14518- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: The garments.

14519- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Nafi', from Ibn Tawus, from his father: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: The shamlah is part of the adornment. [[The "shamlah" (with a fatha and then a sukun) is a cloak less than a qatifah; it is so named because it wraps around the body. From this is the prohibition by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in prayer of "ishtimal al-samma'," which is to wrap oneself in a garment so as to cover the whole body, without raising one side of it so that there is an opening through which the hand could come out.]]

14520- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Tawus: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: The garments.

14521- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Suwayd and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, and a woman circumambulated the House while naked and said:

Today some of it or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful.

14522- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ he said: There was a tribe from the people of Yemen, and whenever one of them came as a pilgrim or umrah performer, he would say: "It is not fitting for me to circumambulate in a garment in which I have sinned," [[The "danas" in a garment means the stain of filth and the like, and figuratively in morals as well. By his words "in which I have sinned" he means: in which I committed what disgraces and blemishes through sins.]] and he would say: "Who will lend me a loincloth?" If he was able to obtain one, well and good; otherwise he circumambulated naked. So God revealed concerning it what you hear: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer.﴾

14523- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: God said: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ meaning: whatever covers the nakedness at every place of prayer.

14524- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: that the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except the Hums, Quraysh and their allies. Whoever came from among others would take off his garments and circumambulate in the garments of the Ahmas, for it was not lawful for him to wear his own garments. If he did not find anyone from the Hums to lend him, he would throw off his garments and circumambulate naked. If he circumambulated in his own garments, when he finished his circumambulation he would cast them off, forbidding them to himself, making them unlawful for him. Therefore God said: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer.﴾ [[For the explanation of "al-Hums" see what has passed, p. 378, note 1.]]

14525- And with it from Ma'mar, who said: Ibn Tawus said, from his father: The shamlah is part of the adornment. [[Narration 14525 – see narration no. 14519.]]

14526- I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prayer,﴾ the verse: There were people from Yemen and the Bedouins who, when they performed the Hajj to the House, circumambulated it naked at night, so God commanded them to wear their garments and not go naked in the mosque.

14527- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Take your adornment﴾, he said: Their adornment is their garments, which they used to cast aside at the House and go naked.

14528- And he narrated it to me again with its chain, from Ibn Zayd regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ He said: Whenever they came to the House and circumambulated it, their garments in which they circumambulated became forbidden to them. If they found someone to lend them garments, well and good; otherwise they circumambulated the House naked. So He said: ﴿Who has forbidden the adornment of God?﴾ He said: The garments of God which He brought forth for His servants, the verse.

* *

Likewise, as we have said, they also said regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive.﴾

Mention of those who said that:

14529- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas who said: God made lawful eating and drinking, so long as there is no extravagance (sarf) or arrogance (makhilah). [[Sarf (with two fathas) is extravagance and exceeding the measure. Makhilah (with a fatha on the mim and a kasra on the kha') is self-admiration and pride. The well-known hadith of Ibn Abbas: "Eat what you wish and wear what you wish, so long as two things do not reach you: extravagance and arrogance," narrated by al-Bukhari.]]

14530- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive,﴾ concerning food and drink.

14531- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Those who circumambulated the House naked used to forbid themselves the fat (wadak) for as long as they remained at the season. [[Wadak means the fat of meat and its oil extracted from it. The "mawsim" is the gathering place of people during the days of the Hajj.]] So God said to them: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive,﴾ meaning: do not be excessive in forbidding.

14532- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His saying: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive,﴾ he said: He commanded them to eat and drink from what God provided them.

14533- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿but do not be excessive,﴾ "Do not eat what is unlawful; that is excess."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not like the excessive,﴾ it means: Indeed God does not love those who transgress His limits, whether in the lawful or the unlawful, those who go to extremes in what God has made lawful or forbidden, by making the unlawful lawful and the lawful unlawful. [[See the explanation of "al-israf" above, p. 176, note 1, and the references there.]] Rather, He loves that what He has made lawful be made lawful and what He has forbidden be forbidden, and that is the justice He has commanded.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 32:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these ignorant people among the Arabs who go naked when circling the House, and who forbid themselves the good provision I have made lawful for them: Who, O people, has forbidden you the adornment of Allah which He created for His servants, that you should adorn yourselves with it and beautify yourselves with its clothing, and the lawful provision of Allah which He gave to His creatures for their food and drink? [[See the explanation of "adornment" above, p. 389 and following.

And the explanation of "good things" in the earlier linguistic indexes (under ṭ-y-b).]]

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the text) differed about what is meant by "the good things of provision," after agreeing that "adornment" means what we have stated.

Some of them said: "The good things of provision" in this place means meat, because they did not eat it while in the state of ihram.

Those who said this:

14534. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ He said: it is the fat. [[The "wadak" (fat) was explained earlier, p. 395, note 1.]]

14535. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ It is what they forbade themselves. He said: When they performed the Hajj or the 'umrah, they forbade themselves the sheep and what comes from it.

14536. And Yunus also told me this again, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse: He said: A people used to forbid what comes from the sheep, its milk, its fat and its meat. So Allah said: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ He said: And the adornment is of garments.

14537. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: When Allah sent Muhammad, He said: "This is My Prophet, this is My chosen one, follow his example (istannu bihi)." Take up his path (sanan) and his way. [[In the printed edition: "fi sunnatih" ("in his sunnah"). The reading in the manuscript is what is established here. "Sunan" (with two fatha vowels) means the way; one says: "Walk in your sunan," and "So-and-so kept to his sunan," meaning his way.]] Doors were not closed against him, and chamberlains (al-hajabah) were not set up between him and people. [[Al-hajabah is the plural of hajib, the one who stands between people and the ruler so that they cannot enter upon him.]] Large bowls (al-jifan) were not brought to him in the morning, nor returned with them in the evening. [[In the printed edition: "wa lam yughda 'alayhi bi'l-jabar," with a note that a copy reads "bi'l-jabab." In the manuscript: "bi'l-jaban," without dots, which is an error. The correct reading is what is established here, as it appears correctly in Hilyat al-Awliya' of Abu Nu'aym, 2:153. "Al-jifan" is the plural of "jafnah," the great food bowl. The text of Abu Nu'aym: "By Allah, he was not fed with large bowls, nor was he brought them in the evening," and it is the better reading.]] He used to sit on the ground, eat his food on the ground, lick his fingers, wear coarse clothing, ride a donkey, and carry a rider behind him. [[In the printed edition: "wa yirdifu 'abdahu," different from the manuscript. In Abu Nu'aym: "wa yirdif khalfahu," which has the same meaning as what al-Tabari narrated. That is, he would have someone ride behind him on the animal as a rider (radif).]] And he used to say: "Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me." Al-Hasan said: How many turn away from his sunnah and abandon it! Then certain wicked, sinful men (ʿulūj fusṣāq), who eat usury and embezzlement, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "thumma 'ulujan" without "inna," and the correct reading is from Hilyat al-Awliya'. "Al-ghulul" is embezzlement of the spoils, and theft from the booty.]] whom my Lord has made foolish and despised, claimed that there is no harm upon them in what they ate and drank, and they adorned these houses, interpreting this verse: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ But that was only for the allies of Satan, who made them a plaything for his belly and his private parts. [[That is, he made the verse, by the interpretation they gave it, a game to be played with, in order to open the door to every desire of their belly and their private parts.]] — from words that Sufyan did not memorize. [[The report 14537, which Sufyan did not memorize, was memorized by others. Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Hilyat al-Awliya' 2:153-154 by way of Muhammad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Zur'ah, from Malik ibn Isma'il, from Maslamah ibn Ja'far, from al-Hasan, with nearly this wording. It is a description worth memorizing, and an admonition offered to our tyrants in our time, among those who speak without knowledge or understanding in issuing false fatwas to people, which their devils have adorned for them.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it means what the pre-Islamic period (al-jahiliyyah) used to forbid of the baha'ir and the sawa'ib.

Those who said this:

14538. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants﴾ — it is what the people of the pre-Islamic period forbade themselves of their property: the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and the haam.

14539. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ He said: The people of the pre-Islamic period used to forbid things that Allah had made lawful, of garments and other things. And this is the word of Allah: ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it lawful and unlawful?﴾ [Surah Yunus: 59], and this is it. So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those whom I commanded you to say to: ﴿Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ when they were unable to answer and did not know what to reply to you: The adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of His provision, are for those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger and followed what was sent down to you from your Lord, in this world; and although those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and opposed the command of their Lord share them in it in this world, it is purely theirs on the Day of Resurrection, and no one who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and opposed the command of their Lord will share it with them on that day. [[See the explanation of "khalisah" (purely) earlier, 2:365 / 12:148, 149.]]

* *

The exegetes said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

14540. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: The Muslims shared with the disbelievers in the good things; they ate of the good of their food, wore the finest of their clothing, married the righteous of their women, and were purified by them on the Day of Resurrection.

14541. And al-Muthanna told me this again, with the same chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world﴾ — meaning: the Muslims share with the polytheists in the good things in the life of this world; then Allah makes the good things purely for those who believe in the Hereafter, and the polytheists have no share in them.

14542. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision? Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — meaning: Say: it is in the Hereafter purely for those who believed in Me in this world, no one shares it with them in the Hereafter. [[The printed edition omitted "fi'l-akhirah" ("in the Hereafter") at the end of this sentence.]] That is because adornment in this world is for all the children of Adam, so Allah made it purely for His allies in the Hereafter.

14543. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: My father told us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: The Jews and Christians share it with you in this world, and it is purely for those who believe on the Day of Resurrection.

14544. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — purely for the believers in the Hereafter, the disbelievers do not share it with them. As for this world, they have shared it with them.

14545. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — whoever acted upon faith in this world, Allah's honor will be purely his on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever abandoned faith in this world will come before his Lord with no excuse.

14546. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world﴾ — the polytheists share it with them = ﴿purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ for those who believe.

14547. I was told, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision? Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: The polytheists share with the believers in this world in clothing, food and drink, and on the Day of Resurrection the clothing, food and drink will be purely for the believers, and the polytheists have no share in any of that.

14548. Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The believer and the disbeliever both obtain from this world, and the best of the Hereafter is purely for the believers, and the disbeliever has no share in it.

14549. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: This is for the believers on the Day of Resurrection, the people of disbelief do not share it with them, though they share it with them in this world. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will have no share in it, neither little nor much.

* *

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said on this matter the following:

14550. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, and Hubaywah al-Razi Abu Yazid, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: They benefit from it in this world, and its sin does not follow them. [[Report 14550: Isma'il ibn Aban al-Warraq al-Azdi, Abu Ishaq, was a Shi'i, reliable and truthful in narration. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/347, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/160.

Hubaywah al-Razi, Abu Yazid, whose biography has already passed as number 14365.]]

* *

The readers (qurra') differed regarding the reading of His word "khalisah" (purely).

Some of the readers of Madinah read it "khalisatun" (purely), in the nominative, meaning: Say: it is purely for those who believe.

* *

The majority of the readers of the regions (sa'ir qurra' al-amsar) read it: ﴿khalisatan﴾ in the accusative, as a circumstantial (hal) from "lahum" (for them), and its verb was omitted, being satisfied with what the apparent meaning indicates, as I have described in the interpretation of the speech: the meaning is: Say: it is for those who believe in the life of this world shared, and it is purely theirs in the Hereafter. Whoever recites with the accusative makes the predicate of "hiya" (it) His words: ﴿for those who believe﴾ [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:376, 377.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites in the accusative, because the Arabs prefer the accusative for a verb-like element when it comes after the noun and the adjective, [[Here "the verb" means the verbal noun (masdar). "The noun" means the derived noun. "The adjective" means the prepositional phrase and the adverbial expression. See the index of terms. Abu Ja'far has already stated, at 2:365, that "khalisah" is a masdar like "al-'afiyah."]] although the nominative is permissible, but that is more common in their speech.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know﴾ (32)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as I have shown you what is obligatory upon you regarding clothing and adornment, and the lawful and unlawful among foods and drinks, and distinguished that for you, O people, so I make clear all My proofs and arguments, and the signs of My lawful and unlawful and My rulings, for a people who know what is made clear to them, and understand what is distinguished for them. [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) earlier, p. 237, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "ayah" (sign) earlier in the linguistic index (a-y-y).]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin, and oppression without right﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who strip off their clothes to circle the House, and who forbid the eating of the good things Allah has made lawful for them from His provision: O people, Allah has not forbidden what you forbid, rather He has made that lawful for His believing servants and made it good for them. My Lord has only forbidden the ugly things = and they are "indecencies" (al-fawahish) [[See the explanation of "indecency" (fahishah) earlier, p. 377, note 2, and the references there.]] = "what is apparent of them," so it is public; "and what is hidden," of them, so it is secret, in concealment. [[See the explanation of "apparent" (zahara) and "hidden" (batana) earlier, p. 218, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been related from Mujahid regarding this:

14551. Al-Harith told me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told me, saying: Abu Sa'd told us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words: ﴿what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ — he said: "What is apparent of them" is the circumambulation of the people of the pre-Islamic period naked; "and what is hidden" is fornication.

* *

I have already mentioned the disagreement of the exegetes regarding the interpretation of this with narrations earlier, so I disliked repeating it. [[See what passed above, p. 218, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

As for "sin" (al-ithm), it is disobedience; and "oppression" (al-bagh), is to overpower people.

* *

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, together with sin and oppression against people.

* *

The exegetes said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

14552. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and sin and oppression﴾ — as for "sin," it is disobedience; and "oppression," is that one oppresses people without right.

14553. Al-Harith told me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Abu Sa'd told us, saying: I heard Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin and oppression﴾ — he said: He forbade "sin," which means all the acts of disobedience; and He informed that the oppressor's oppression falls back upon himself. [[In the manuscript: "an ikhtafa baghyuhu 'ala nafsihi" ("that his oppression is confined to himself"), which is unreadable; what is in the printed edition is closer to correct.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 33–34:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ (33).

Abu Ja'far said: His majestic praise says: "My Lord has only forbidden indecencies and associating partners with Him, that you worship alongside Allah a god other than Him." ﴿For which He has sent down no authority﴾ means: your Lord has forbidden you to make partners with Him in His worship, for something for which He has given you no proof or evidence in associating it with Him in worship, and "authority" (sultan) here [[See the explanation of "sultan" above, 11:490, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ means: and that you say that Allah commanded you to strip naked and go bare for circumambulation of the House, and forbade you to eat these livestock which you have forbidden, set free, and made into bahira, sa'iba, wasila and ham, and other things, while you do not know that Allah forbade them, or commanded them, or permitted them, so that you attribute to Allah their prohibition, their forbidding, and the command concerning them. For that is what Allah has forbidden you, rather than what you claim Allah has forbidden, or what you say Allah has commanded you, out of ignorance of the reality of what you say and attribute to Allah.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And for every nation there is a term; so when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ (34).

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says, threatening the polytheists, of whom He informed that when they committed an indecency they would say: "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah commanded us to do it" [[In the printed edition: "threatening the polytheists"; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is closer to the context.]] and as a warning from Him to them for their lies against Him, and for their persistence in associating partners with Him and remaining in their disbelief, and as a reminder to them of what befell the likes of those nations who were before them: ﴿And for every nation there is a term﴾ means: for every group that gathered to deny the messengers of Allah, [[See the explanation of "ummah" above, p. 37, footnote 2, and the references there.]] and rejected their advice, and associated partners with Allah, while their Lord followed up His proofs against them, there is a "term" (ajal), meaning: a time for the punishments to descend upon them and for the retributions to fall on them for their polytheism [[See the explanation of "ajal" above, p. 117, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿So when their term comes﴾ means: when the time that Allah appointed for their destruction and the descent of punishment upon them arrives ﴿they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ means: they will not be delayed by remaining in the world, nor will they be given enjoyment of life in it beyond the time of their destruction and the moment the term of their annihilation arrives, [[In the printed edition: "they are given enjoyment"; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] not even an hour of the hours of time. ﴿Nor can they advance it﴾ means: nor will they advance beyond the time that Allah has set for them as the time of destruction.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 35:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs, then whoever fears God and makes amends, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, is informing His creation of what He has prepared for His party, the people of His obedience and of belief in Him and His Messenger, and what He has prepared for the party of Satan, his allies, and those who disbelieve in Him and His messengers. ﴿O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you﴾ means: if My messengers whom I send to you come to you, calling you to obey Me and to submit to My command and My prohibition, ﴿from among you﴾ means: from your own selves and from your clans and tribes. ﴿Relating to you My signs﴾ means: they recite to you the verses of My Book and make known to you My proofs and signs confirming the truth of what they have brought you from Me, and the reality of what they have called you to of My Oneness. [See the explanation of "qass" (relating) above, pp. 120, 307, and the explanation of "ayah" (sign) above in the lexical indices under (ayy).] ﴿Then whoever fears God and makes amends﴾ means: whoever among you believes in what My messengers have brought him, of what has been related to him of My signs, and confirms it, and fears God, being mindful of Him by acting on what He has commanded him and refraining from what He has forbidden him through the tongue of His Messenger. ﴿And makes amends﴾ means: and rectifies his deeds which were corrupt before that, through the disobedience of God, by abstaining from them. [("Tahawwub min ithmih") means: refraining from sin on his part, i.e., leaving sin and guarding against it. See also the explanation of "aslaha" (made amends) above in the lexical indices under (slh).] ﴿There shall be no fear for them﴾ means: there shall be no fear for them on the Day of Resurrection of God's punishment when they come before Him. ﴿Nor shall they grieve﴾ means: over what they have missed of their worldly life which they abandoned, and their desires which they avoided, in compliance with God's prohibition of them, when they witness of God's honour what they will witness there. [See the explanation of "there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve" in its parallels above, under (khawf) (hazn) in the lexical indices.]

3554 (sic: 14554) - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Hisham Abu 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Hayyaj related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad related to us, from Abu Sayyar al-Sulami, who said: Indeed God placed Adam and his offspring in His palm and said: ﴿O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, relating to them My signs, then whoever fears God and makes amends, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ Then He looked at the messengers and said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed I am Knowing of what you do. And indeed this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 51-52.] Then He scattered them. [[The report 14554: This is an ambiguous chain which I have not been able to identify. Abu Sayyar al-Sulami: I do not know who he is, and so I could not determine who he is; nor 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, nor Hayyaj. The report was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:82, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.]]

* *

If someone says: What is the answer (jawab) to His saying: ﴿If there come to you messengers from among you﴾? It is said: The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah) have differed regarding this.

Some of them said: The answer is implied, indicated by what appears of the speech, and that is His saying: ﴿then whoever fears God and makes amends﴾. This is because when He said: ﴿then whoever fears God and makes amends﴾, it is as if He said: "then obey them."

* *

Others among them said: The answer is "then whoever fears God," because its meaning is: "then whoever among you fears God and makes amends." He said: What indicates that this is so is the partitioning of the speech, and in the partitioning there is sufficiency from the mention of "from among you."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and waxed proud against them, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (36)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His Majesty says: As for those who denied the revelations I sent to them through My messengers, who rejected My Oneness, disbelieved in what My messengers brought, and waxed proud against accepting My proofs and evidences, ﴿then those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾. That is, they will remain in the Fire of Hell, never to emerge from it. [[See the explanation of the terms of this verse in the earlier lexical indices.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 37:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His mention be exalted, says: Who is more wrong in deed, more ignorant in speech, and further astray from truth and rightness [[See the explanation of "al-zulm" (injustice) in the linguistic indexes of what has preceded.]] = ﴿than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: one who fabricates falsehood about Allah, so that when he commits an abomination he says, "Allah has commanded us to it" [[See the explanation of "iftara" (invent) in what has preceded, p. 189, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿or denies His signs﴾, meaning: or denies His proofs and indicators that point to His oneness and to the prophethood of His prophets, rejecting their reality and disputing their validity = ﴿Those﴾, meaning: whoever does that, who invents lies against Allah and denies His signs = ﴿will receive their portion of what is written﴾, meaning: their share of what Allah has decreed for them in the Preserved Tablet will reach them. [[See the explanation of "nala" (to receive) in what has preceded, 3:20 and 6:587. And the explanation of "nasib" (portion) in what has preceded, p. 131, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the nature of that "portion" which they have in "the Book," and what it is.

Some of them said: It is the punishment of Allah which He has prepared for those who disbelieve in Him.

Those who said this:

14555 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Marwan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, i.e., of the punishment.

14556 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, the same.

14557 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what has been written for them of punishment.

14558 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from Kathir ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: of the punishment.

14559 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from Abu Sahl, from al-Hasan, he said: of the punishment.

14560 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from a man, from al-Hasan, he said: of the punishment.

* *

And others said: The meaning of that is: those will receive their portion of what has already been decreed for them of misery and happiness.

Those who said this:

14561 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Sa'id: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: of wretchedness and happiness.

14562 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, like the wretched and the blessed. [[Meaning, like His saying in [Surah Hud: 105]: "Among them are the wretched and the blessed."]]

14563 - Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Mujahid say: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: it is what has preceded.

14564 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, what has been written for them of wretchedness and happiness.

14565 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿will receive their portion of what is written﴾, what has been written upon them of wretchedness and happiness, like the wretched and the blessed.

14566 - ... narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, of wretchedness and happiness.

14567 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr and Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Amr, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what has already preceded from the Book.

14568 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiyya: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what has preceded for them in the Book.
