14569 - ... narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿Those will receive their portion﴾, he said: of wretchedness and happiness.

14570 - ... narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: what has been decreed or determined for them.

14571 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿will receive their portion of what is written﴾, what was written for them of deeds will reach them.

14572 - Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Bakr al-Tawil, from Mujahid regarding the word of Allah: (Those will receive their portion of what is written), he said: people who do deeds that they must do. [[The report 14572: Isma'il ibn Sumay' al-Hanafi, passed as no. 4791, 4793. And "Bakr al-Tawil" appears to be "Bakr ibn Yazid al-Tawil al-Himsi," who narrated from Abu Hurayra al-Himsi, and from whom Abu Sa'id al-Shajj narrated; he is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/394.]]

* *

And others said: The meaning of that is: those will receive their portion of their book which was written for them or against them, by their deeds which they did in the world, good or evil.

Those who said this:

14573 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he says: their portion of deeds; whoever does good is recompensed for it, and whoever does evil is recompensed for it.

14574 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: of the rulings of the Book, according to the measure of their deeds.

14575 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: their portion in the Hereafter of the deeds they did and sent forward.

14576 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, i.e., their deeds, the evil deeds they did and sent forward.

14577 - Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: my father said: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, Qatada claimed: of their deeds which they did.

14578 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he says: their portion of deeds will reach them. If one of them does a portion of good, he is recompensed with good, and if he does evil, he is recompensed in its like.

* *

And others said: The meaning of that is: their portion of what they were promised in the Book of good or evil will reach them.

Those who said this:

14579 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: of good and evil.

14580 - ... said: Zayd narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: what they were promised.

14581 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what they were promised.

14582 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what they were promised therein of good or evil.

14583 - ... said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Layth, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what they were promised, its like.

14584 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: what they were promised therein of good or evil.

14585 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what they were promised therein.

14586 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what they were promised of good or evil.

14587 - Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Amr, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding the word of Allah: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: what has preceded for them of the Book will reach them.

* *

And others said: The meaning of that is: those will receive their portion of the Book which Allah wrote against the one who invented lies about Him.

Those who said this:

14588 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he says: what was written against them will reach them. He says: it has been written for whoever invents lies against Allah that his face will be blackened.

* *

And others said: The meaning of that is: those will receive their portion of what was written for them of provision, lifespan and deeds.

Those who said this:

14589 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, of what was written for them of provision.

14590 - ... said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'a, from Abu Sakhr, from al-Qurazi: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: their deeds, their provision and their lifespan.

14591 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾, he said: of deeds, provisions and lifespans. So when this is exhausted, Our messengers come to them to take them in death, and they have finished all these things.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred of these sayings to me as correct is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: those will receive their portion of what is written, of good and evil, provision, deeds and term in this world. This is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿until, when Our messengers come to them to take them, they say: "Where is what you used to call upon besides Allah?"﴾, and by following that with His saying, He made clear that: ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is written﴾ refers to what was decreed for them in this world to reach them, because He has informed that this reaches them until the time their messengers come to seize their souls. If that were their portion of the Book, or what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter, it would not be limited by reaching them until the coming of Allah's messengers for their death, because Allah's messengers do not come to them for death in the Hereafter, and their punishment in the Hereafter has no end or termination, for Allah has decreed upon them eternity in it. Thus it is evident that its meaning is what we have chosen to say.

* *

The discussion of His saying: ﴿until, when Our messengers come to them to take them, they say: "Where is what you used to call upon besides Allah?" They say: "They have strayed from us," and they will testify against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾ (37)

Abu Ja'far said: May His mention be exalted, by His saying: ﴿until, when Our messengers came to them﴾, He means: until Our messengers came to them. May His mention be exalted, says: These who invented lies against Allah or denied the signs of their Lord will receive their allotted portions which Allah wrote for them and which was foreknown to Him for them, of provision, deeds, term, good and evil in this world, until Our messengers come to them to seize their souls. So when Our messengers come to them, meaning the Angel of Death and his troops = ﴿to take them﴾, meaning: to complete their count from this world to the Hereafter [[See the explanation of "al-tawaffi" (taking in full) in what has preceded: 11:409, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿they say: "Where is what you used to call upon besides Allah?"﴾, meaning: the messengers say: where are those whom you used to call upon as protectors besides Allah and worship, who do not repel from you what has come to you of Allah's command, He who is your Creator and their Creator, and what great affliction has descended upon your courtyard? And will they not come to your aid from the distress you are in, so that they rescue you from it? Then the wretched ones answered them and said: "They have strayed from us, our protectors whom we used to call upon besides Allah." By His saying: ﴿They have strayed﴾, they mean: they departed and took other than our path, and abandoned us in our time of need for them, so they did not benefit us. [[See the explanation of "al-dalal" (straying) in what has preceded in the linguistic indexes (d-l-l).]] Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: And the people then testified against themselves that they had been disbelievers in Allah, denying His oneness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 38:

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿He will say, "Enter among nations that have passed away before you, of jinn and humankind, into the Fire. Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from God, may His praise be exalted, concerning what He will say to those who slandered Him and denied His signs on the Day of Resurrection. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He will say to them when they come before Him on the Day of Resurrection, "Enter, you who slandered your Lord and denied His messengers, in groups of your like[[See the explanation of "ummah" above, p. 405, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿that have passed away before you﴾, meaning: that have gone on before you [[See the explanation of "khalā" above, 3:100, 128; 4:289; 7:228.]] ﴿"of jinn and humankind into the Fire"﴾. The meaning is: Enter among nations that are in the Fire, which passed away before you, of jinn and humankind. By "nations" (umam) he means the factions and the people of the disbelieving religious communities. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says that every time a group of the people of one religion enters the Fire, it curses ("laʿanat," i.e. curses) its sister, meaning: the other group of the people of its own religion, disavowing it. [[See the explanation of "al-la'n" (cursing) above, 10:489, note 1.]]

By "sister" he means brotherhood in religion and creed. It was said "its sister" and not "its brother" because by "nation" he meant a group, so it is as if it were said: every time a nation enters, it curses another nation of the people of its religion and faith. [[See al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:378.]]

* *

Those who interpret (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said this:

14592. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾, he said: Every time a people of one religion enters, they curse their companions in that religion. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "kullama dakhalat ahl milla" (every time entered a people of one religion), and the correct reading is what I have established.]] The polytheists curse the polytheists, the Jews curse the Jews, the Christians curse the Christians, the Sabians curse the Sabians, and the Magians curse the Magians; the later one curses the earlier one.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿until, when they have gathered together therein all﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: until, when the nations have gathered together in the Fire, all of them, meaning they have assembled in it.

* *

It is said: "qad iddarakū" and "tadarakū" when they have assembled. [[See Abu Ubaydah, Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:214, where the text has a fine addition: "It is said: tadarak li 'alayhi shay'," meaning something gathered for me with him. The "t" is assimilated into the "d," so the "d" is doubled.]]

* *

He says: the earlier ones among the people of the disbelieving religions and the later ones among them have gathered in it.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿The last of them will say to the first of them, "Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment from the Fire." He will say, "For each there is a double, but you do not know."﴾ (38)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may His praise be exalted, about the dialogue of the factions of the disbelieving religions in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When the people of the disbelieving religions have gathered in the Fire and assembled, the last group of each religion that entered the Fire, who in the world came after an earlier group that preceded them and was for them a predecessor and a leader in error and disbelief, will say to the first of them, those who were before them in the world, "Our Lord, these led us astray from Your way, called us to worship other than You, and made the obedience to Satan attractive to us. So give them today a double punishment from Your punishment, in addition to ours," as:

14593. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "The last of them" (qalat ukhrahum), those who were at the end of time, "to the first of them" (li-ula-hum), those who established that religion for them: ﴿"Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a punishment, double, from the Fire."﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿He will say, "For each there is a double, but you do not know."﴾, this is a report from God about His answer to them. He says: God says to those who call upon Him and say, "Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment from the Fire": For all of you, the first and the last, and the followers and those followed, there is a "double," meaning the punishment is repeated upon them.

* *

And "the double of a thing" is its equal once more.

* *

Mujahid used to say about this what follows:

14594. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words: ﴿"a double punishment from the Fire." He said, "For each there is a double."﴾ He said: "Multiplied."

14595. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Among those who interpret, those who said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said this:

14596. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who said: God's words ﴿"For each double"﴾ refer to the first, and for the last there is a double.

14597. Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: someone other than one [narrator] told me, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud), concerning ﴿"a double from the Fire"﴾, he said: vipers.

14598. al-Harith told me, he said: Abd al-Aziz told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abd Allah, concerning ﴿"so give them a double punishment from the Fire"﴾, he said: serpents and vipers.

* *

It has been said that in the speech of the Arabs, "al-mudaʿaf" (the doubled) is what is two-fold, and "al-mudaʿaf" (the multiplied) is what is more than that. [[In the printed edition: "al-ḍaʿf, fi kalam al-ʿarab" (the double, in the speech of the Arabs), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿"but you do not know"﴾, He says: but you, O assembly of the people of the Fire, do not know the measure of what God has prepared for you of punishment, and therefore the disbelieving nation asks for a double of it for its first sister.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 39:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no advantage over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Glorified is His praise, He means: the first of every nation and religion who preceded in this world will say to their last, those who came after them and innovated after their time in it, following their path and adopting their practice: ﴿So you had no advantage over us﴾, for you know what punishment of God, glorified is His praise, befell us for our disobedience to Him and our disbelief in His signs, after the messengers and warners came to us and to you with that. [[In the printed edition: "and we disbelieved in it, and the messengers came to us and to you with that," while in the manuscript: "and we disbelieved in it, what came to us and to you," and this is not sound; its correct form, God willing, is what I have established, as the context of the preceding verses indicates. I have inferred this from the interpretation of the preceding verses.]] So will you repent to obedience to God [[In the printed edition: "have you desisted," while in the manuscript: "have you asm," and this is the correct reading of it; I added the fa' at the beginning of "hal" because the context of the speech requires it.]] and refrain from your error and misguidance? Thus the argument of the people was concluded, they were refuted, and they could not find an answer, so they would not say: "We were preferred over you when we took heed from you, so we believed in God and affirmed His messengers." [[In the printed edition: "that we took heed from you," and in the manuscript: "when we took heed from you," and the correct form is what I have established.]] God said to all of them: Taste, all of you, O disbelievers, the punishment of Hell, [[See the interpretation of: "taste the punishment" above, 11:420, note 1, and the references there.]] for what you used to earn in the world of sins and disobediences, and commit of wrongs and crimes. [[See the interpretation of "earning" above, p. 286, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

Those who expounded the interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

14599 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard Imran, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no advantage over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ He said: He says: "What is your superiority over us, when what was done to us has been made clear to you, and you were warned?"

14600 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no advantage over us"﴾: "You have gone astray just as we went astray."

* *

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

14601 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿So you had no advantage over us﴾: "From lightening of the punishment."

14602 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿So you had no advantage over us﴾: "From lightening."

* *

The view that we have mentioned from Mujahid is a view that has no meaning, because the statement of those who say: "So you had no advantage over us" to those to whom it is said, is only a rebuke from them for what had preceded from them before that state, as the use of "kana" (was) in the speech indicates. Had it been a rebuke to them for their saying that they said to their Lord: "Give them a double punishment from the Fire," the rebuke would have been to say: "So what advantage do you have over us in lightening the punishment for you, when you have suffered from the punishment what we have suffered," and it would not have said: "So you had no advantage over us."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 40 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, those who denied Our proofs and evidences, not believing in them, and did not follow Our messengers [[See the explanation of "al-ayah" (sign) in the earlier lexical indexes, under the root ʾ-y-y.]] = ﴿and were arrogant toward them﴾, meaning: they showed pride in not affirming them, and disdained to follow them and submit to them out of arrogance [[See the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) earlier, vol. 11, p. 540.]] = "the gates of heaven will not be opened for them": for their spirits when they leave their bodies. = "the gates of heaven", and no word or deed of theirs ascends to God during their lives, because their deeds are wicked. Only the good word and the righteous deed are raised, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Surah Fatir: 10].

* * *

Then the exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: the gates of heaven will not be opened for the spirits of these disbelievers.

Those who said this:

13603 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ya'la narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: By it he meant the disbelievers; that heaven is not opened for their spirits, but it is opened for the spirits of the believers.

14604 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The heaven is opened for the spirit of the believer, and it is not opened for the spirit of the disbeliever.

14605 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: When the spirit of the disbeliever is taken, the angels of the earth strike it until it rises to the heaven. When it reaches the lowest heaven, the angels of heaven strike it and it descends; the angels of the earth strike it and it rises; when it reaches the lowest heaven, the angels of the lowest heaven strike it and it descends down to the lowest of the earths. And if he is a believer, his spirit is breathed out [[In the printed edition: "his spirit is taken", but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] and the gates of heaven are opened for him. He does not pass by an angel without that angel greeting him and saluting him, until he reaches God, and He gives him what he asks. Then God says: Return the spirit of My servant to the earth, for I created his body from dust, and to dust it returns, and from it it comes forth.

* * *

Others said: the meaning of that is that no righteous deed or supplication to God ascends for them.

Those who said this:

14606 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. No word or deed ascends for them.

14607 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He means: nothing of their deeds ascends to God.

14608 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He says: It will not be opened for any good they do.

14609 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: No speech and no deed ascends for them.

14610 – Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: No deed or supplication rises for them. [[The report 14610: Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi, a teacher of al-Tabari, I have not found a biography for him; it also occurred earlier as no. 12198.]]

14611 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: No deed or supplication rises for them.

14612 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Sa'id: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: No righteous deed or supplication is raised for them.

* * *

Others said: the meaning is: the gates of heaven are not opened for their spirits nor for their deeds.

Those who said this:

14613 – al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij: ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. He said: For their spirits nor for their deeds.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: We have chosen what we have chosen in the interpretation of this because of the generality of God's report, may His praise be exalted, that the gates of heaven will not be opened for them. He did not specify the report as opening for them in any respect; so it is according to what God's report encompasses, that they are not opened for them in anything. This is supported by the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confirming what we have said about it, namely:

14614 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara': that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the seizing of the spirit of the wicked person, and that it ascends with it to heaven. He said: They ascend with it, and they do not pass by any assembly of angels without saying: "What is this wicked spirit?" They say: "So-and-so," using the most odious of the names by which he used to be called in the world, until they reach with it the heaven, and they ask for it to be opened, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of God recited: ﴿The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter the Garden until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. [[Report 14614: al-Minhal is al-Minhal ibn 'Amr al-Asadi, trustworthy; my brother Ahmad's authentication of him is noted in the Musnad under nos. 714, and below nos. 337 and 799. Zadhan is Abu 'Abd Allah, also called Abu 'Umar, al-Kufi al-Darir, a trustworthy Successor, previously mentioned as nos. 9508, 13017, 13018. This report, in abbreviated form, is transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad 4:287, 288, by two routes, and 297, all through al-A'mash from al-Minhal. He also transmits it 4:295, 296, by two routes: one through 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from Yunus ibn Khabbab from al-Minhal, and the other through Abu al-Rabi' from Hammad ibn Zayd from Yunus ibn Khabbab. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi transmits it in his Musnad p. 102, in full, through Abu 'Awanah from al-A'mash. Abu Dawud transmits it in his Sunan 3:289, no. 3212, abridged, and in full 4:330, no. 4753. al-Hakim transmits it in al-Mustadrak 1:37–40, through several routes, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), for both relied on al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and Zadhan ibn 'Amr, and Zadhan Abu 'Umar al-Kindi. In this hadith are many benefits for the People of the Sunnah and a suppression of the innovators, and the two did not transmit it in full." Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 3:473, 474, and said: "Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah transmitted it through several routes from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr," and then he quoted Ahmad's version from the Musnad. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:83, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad ibn al-Sarri, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his book on the punishment of the grave.]]

14615 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The dead person is attended by the angels. If he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come forth, O good soul, which was in a good body; come forth praiseworthy, and rejoice in rest and sweet fragrance, and a Lord not angry.'" He said: They keep saying this until it is brought up to heaven, and its opening is requested, and it is asked: "Who is this?" They say: "So-and-so." It is said: "Welcome to the good soul which was in the good body. Enter, praiseworthy, and rejoice in rest and a Lord not angry," and it is said this until it reaches the heaven in which God is. But if he is an evil man, he says: "Come forth, O evil soul, which was in an evil body; come forth blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water and dark liquid, and other kinds of similar torment," and they keep saying this until it comes out. Then it is brought up to heaven, and its opening is requested, and it is asked: "Who is this?" They say: "So-and-so." They say: "No welcome to the evil soul which was in the evil body. Return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you," [[In the printed edition: "will not be opened for you", but in the manuscript: "were not opened" without "for you"; I have kept what is in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir. In Ibn Majah: "will not be opened for you".]] so it is sent between heaven and earth, and then it returns to the grave. [[Reports 14615 and 14616: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn Umayyah al-Thaqafi, Abu Bahr al-Bakrawi, weak and spoken of; Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written down but not used as evidence." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/264. Ibn Abi Dhi'b is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Dhi'b, trustworthy and a memorizer, previously no. 2995. Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata' al-Qurashi al-'Amiri is trustworthy; the group transmitted from him. Sa'id ibn Yasar Abu al-Hubab al-Madani is a trustworthy Successor whose trustworthiness is not disputed; the group transmitted from him. This report is sound, and was transmitted from Ibn Abi Dhi'b by someone other than 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman. A chain without weakness will come in the following report. This report was transmitted by Ibn Majah, p. 1423, no. 4262. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 3:475 and attributed it to Ahmad and al-Nasa'i. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:83, and added attribution to Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th. The report 14616 is a sound chain for the preceding report.]]

14616 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly. [[Ibn Abi Fudayk is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Muslim ibn Abi Fudayk, trustworthy; the group transmitted from him. Previously nos. 4319, 9482, 9876.]]

* * *

The readers differed concerning the reading of this.

The common reading of the people of Kufa was: "lā yufattaḥu lahum abwābu al-samā'" with the ya' in "yufattaḥu" and the tā' lightened, meaning: they will not be opened for them all at once, in one opening.

* * *

Some Medinan and some Kufan readers read: ﴿lā tufattaḥu﴾ with the tā' and the second tā' doubled, meaning: they will not be opened for them door after door, and thing after thing.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this, in my judgment, is that it should be said: both are well-known readings, and both are sound in meaning. For the spirits of the disbelievers are not opened for them, nor their wicked deeds, by the gates of heaven all at once, nor time after time, door after door. So both meanings are sound. Likewise the ya' and the tā' in "yufattaḥu" and "tufattaḥu," because the ya' is according to the verb with a singular subject, and the tā' because "al-abwāb" (the doors) is a plural, so it is reported with the form of the plural.

[[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:378, 379.]]

* * *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they will not enter the Garden until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals﴾ (40).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Nor will those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them enter the Garden which God has prepared for His believing friends forever, just as the camel will never pass through the eye of the needle. That is the hole of the needle.

* * *

Every hole in an eye, a nose, or other things, the Arabs call "samm," and its plural "sumum," and "simam" is the plural of "samm" meaning the deadly poison, which is more famous and more eloquent than "sumum." For the plural of "samm" meaning the hole, it is more eloquent. Both are widely used among the Arabs. It may be said of one of the holes, "sumum" (the holes), "samm" and "summ" with the s vowelled with fatha or damma. And from "samm" meaning hole is the verse of al-Farazdaq:

So I relieved his "sammihi" until he breathed,
And I said to him: Do not fear anything behind you.

[[Diwan: 895; al-Naqa'id: 169; and Lisan (s-m-m). This is from the beginning of a qasidah in which he satirized Jarir, and supported al-Bu'aith and satirized him together. The cause of the satire between Jarir and al-Farazdaq was that al-Bu'aith al-Mujashi's camels were stolen by some people from Banu Yarbu', from the kin of Jarir. Al-Bu'aith sought them until he found them in their hands, and let his tongue loose against Banu Yarbu', and Jarir confronted him and satirized him, and the evil broke out for al-Bu'aith. Then al-Farazdaq went shortly after to support him, and said this qasidah satirizing Jarir, supporting and satirizing al-Bu'aith. He says to al-Bu'aith: "Ibn Hamra' al-'Ijan called me, and he did not find himself delayed from answering his call..." then "fa-naffastu 'an sammihi..." "naffasa 'anhu" means: relieved him of his distress when Jarir pressed on him, and rescued him from under his weight, so he was able to breathe. His words "do not fear anything behind you" mean: do not fear while you are a shield for you and you are behind me, sheltered by my tongue and my satire of Jarir. As for the words of Abu 'Ubaydah, "that is, do not fear anything coming upon you from behind," there is nothing to it in my view. In the printed edition it read: "shay'an warā'anā" which did not properly read the manuscript.]]

He means by "sammihi": the two holes of his nose.

* * *

As for "al-khiyat" (needle), it is "al-mikhyat," and it is the needle. It has been said: "khiyat" and "mikhyat," as it is said: "qina'" and "miqna'," "izar" and "mi'zar," "qiram" and "miqram," "lihaf" and "milhaf."

As for the readers of all the regions, they read His words: ﴿fī sammi al-khiyāt﴾ with the s vowelled with fatha, and they agreed on reading "al-jamal" (the camel) with fatha on the jim and the mim, and lightening that.

* * *

As for Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, it is reported from them that they read it: "al-jumm'al" (al-Jumull), with damma on the jim and doubling of the mim, with a disagreement on that from Sa'id and Ibn 'Abbas.

* * *

As for those who read it with fatha in both letters and lightening, they directed its interpretation to the well-known "jamal" (camel), and so they explained it.

Those who said this:

14617 – Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, regarding His words: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. He said: The camel is the son of the she-camel, or: the mate of the she-camel.

14618 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. He said: "The camel" is the mate of the she-camel.

14619 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, the same.

14620 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "The camel" is the mate of the she-camel.

14621 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, the same.

14622 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "The camel" is the one that stands in the "mirbad." [[Al-mirbad (with kasra and sukun) is the place where camels are confined; it is said: "rabada al-ibil rabdan," meaning he confined them. It is also said "mirbad al-ghanam" (for sheep). It is from this that "Mirbad al-Basrah" was named, because it was the place of the camel market.]]

14623 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. He said: until the beast passes through the hole of the needle. [["Khurt al-ibrah" (with damma or fatha on the kha', and sukun on the ra') is its hole. In the printed edition it read "fī kharq," which is correct; the manuscript looks like it could be read either way.]]

14624 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Hushaym, from 'Abbad ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan, who said: It is the camel! When they pressed him, he said: It is the "ashtar." [["Ashtar," which is the camel, in Persian.]]

14625 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan, the same.

14626 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Yahya, who said: al-Hasan used to read it: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. He said: Some of them went to ask him, and he said: "Ashtar, ashtar." [["Ashtar," which is the camel, in Persian.]]

1462​7. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu al-Nu'man 'Arim told us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd told us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾: "The camel is that which has four legs."

1462​8. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Husayn, or Husayn, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning His saying ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾: "The she-camel's mate, meaning the camel."

1462​9. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, from al-Dahhak, that he used to recite ﴿al-jamal﴾, and it is that which has four legs.

1463​0. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Abu Tumaylah told us, from 'Ubayd, from al-Dahhak: ﴿until the camel passes﴾, which has four legs.

1463​1. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab told us, from Qurrah, from al-Hasan: ﴿until the camel passes﴾, he said: "The one in al-Mirbad."

1463​2. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he used to recite: "ḥattā yalija al-jamalu al-aṣfaru" (until the yellow camel passes).

1463​3. Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym told us, saying: 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Makhariq told us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾, he said: "The camel is the son of the she-camel" — or "the mate of the she-camel."

* *

As for those who differed from this reading, they disagreed.

Two narrations are transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas on this matter. The first agrees with this reading and this interpretation.

The narration to this effect from him:

1463​4. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾, and "the camel" means "the one with legs."

* *

It is mentioned that Ibn Mas'ud also said this.

1463​5. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾, and it is the great camel, which does not enter the hole of a needle, because it is larger than it.

* *

The other narration is what follows:

1463​6. Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i told me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi" (until the jummal passes through the eye of a needle), he said: "It is the qal's of the ship." [((al-Qals)) (with a fatha on the qaf and sukun on the lam): a thick, large rope made of palm fiber or leaves, one of the ropes of ships.]

1463​7. 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil told me, saying: Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il told us, from Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Handhalah al-Sadusi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi," meaning the thick rope. I mentioned this to al-Hasan, and he recited: ﴿until the camel passes﴾. 'Abd al-A'la said: Abu Ghassan said: Khalid said: "It means the camel [al-ba'ir]."

1463​8. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Fudayl, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited: "al-jummalu" with a doubled mim, and said: "It is the rope of the ship."

1463​9. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Hushaym, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-jammal": the ropes of ships.

1464​0. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, from Ibn Mubarak, from Handhalah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi," he said: "The thick rope."

1464​1. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi," he said: "It is the rope that is on the ship."

* *

Also, there is disagreement on this matter from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Two narrations are transmitted from him. The first is like what we mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas: with a damma on the jim and a doubled mim.

The narration to this effect from him:

1464​2. 'Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz told us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Husayn al-Mu'allim told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited it: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu," meaning the qulus of ships, meaning the thick ropes. [((al-Qulus)) is the plural of ((qals)); see the note above.]

* *

The other of the two is with a damma on the jim and a light mim.

The narration to this effect from him:

1464​3. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: 'Amr told us, from Salim ibn 'Ajlan al-Aftas, who said: I recited to my father: "ḥattā yalija al-jummala," and he said: "ḥattā yalija al-jumalu," lightly, it is the rope of the ship. This is how Sa'id ibn Jubayr taught it to me.

* *

As for 'Ikrimah, he used to recite it: "al-jummalu," with a damma on the jim and a doubled mim, and he interpreted it as follows:

1464​4. Ibn Wakf told me, saying: Abu Tumaylah told us, from 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, who said: I heard 'Ikrimah recite "al-jummalu" with doubling, and he said: "It is the rope by which one climbs up to the palm trees."

1464​5. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Ka'b ibn Farrukh told us, saying: Qatadah told us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His saying: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi," he said: "The thick rope in the eye of the needle." [The report 14645: Ka'b ibn Farrukh, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Basri, is trustworthy. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/162. It will come later at no. 14650.]

1464​6. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "ḥattā yalija al-jummalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi," he said: "The rope of the ship in the eye of the needle."

1464​7. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: I heard Mujahid say: "The rope is one of the ropes of ships."

* *

It seems that whoever recited it with a light mim and a damma on the jim, as we mentioned from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, took it as a pattern like "al-Surad" and "al-Ju'al," and directed it toward a collection of ropes, gathered as "juml," just as "al-Zulmah" is gathered as "zulam" and "al-Khurbah" as "kharab."

* *

Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to deny the doubling of the mim and would say: The narrator only meant "al-Jumal" with lightness, but the listener did not understand this from him, so he doubled it.

* *

1464​8. It was related to me from al-Farra', from al-Kisa'i, that he said: "What he narrated from Ibn 'Abbas was non-Arabic (a'jami)."

* *

As for whoever doubled the mim and put a damma on the jim, he directed it to a single noun, meaning the rope or the thick thread.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is that upon which the readers of the major cities (al-amsar) agree, namely: ﴿ḥattā yalija al-jamalu fī sammi al-khiyāṭi﴾, with a fatha on the jim and the mim of "al-jamal," and light (unstressed) mim, and a fatha on the sin of "al-samm," because it is the widely transmitted recitation among the readers of the cities, and it is not permissible to oppose what the proof has come with, agreed upon in recitation.

Likewise is the fatha on the sin in His saying ﴿sammi al-khiyāṭ﴾.

* *

Since the correct recitation is this, the interpretation of the statement is: "And they will not enter the Garden until the camel passes" — "walaj" means entering, from the saying "Fulan walaja al-dar yalijuhu walujan," meaning: entered [[See the explanation of "al-walaj" earlier, 6:302, which contains further sources.]] — "the camel into the eye of the needle," which is its hole

﴿And thus do We recompense the criminals﴾, meaning: And thus do We reward those who committed crimes in this world with the painful punishment from Allah in the Hereafter, which they deserved. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" and "al-ijram" earlier in the linguistic indexes (jaza, jarm).]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿sam al-khiyāṭ﴾.

Those who said this:

1464​9. Ibn Wakf told us, saying: Abu Usamah, Ibn Mahdi and Suwayd al-Kalbi told us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Yahya ibn 'Atiq, who said: I asked al-Hasan about His saying ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of a needle﴾, and he said: "The hole of the needle." [[The report 14649: Suwayd al-Kalbi — it was said of him: "He used to invert chains and put weak texts on sound chains!!" Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Ma'in and al-'Ijli deemed him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/149, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/239. Yahya ibn 'Atiq al-Tufawi al-Basri is trustworthy, and he was scrupulous and proficient. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/295, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/176.]]

1465​0. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Ka'b ibn Farrukh told us, saying: Qatadah told us, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿in the eye of a needle﴾, he said: "The hole of the needle." [[The report 14650: Ka'b ibn Farrukh, passed at no. 14645.]]

1465​1. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, the same.

1465​2. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿in the eye of a needle﴾, he said: "The hole of the needle."

1465​3. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿in the eye of a needle﴾, meaning: "The hole of the needle."

1465​4. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿in the eye of a needle﴾, he said: "In its hole."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 41:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell, and over them coverings. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ (7:41)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them = ﴿a bed of Hell﴾.

* *

= That is what they spread out to sit and recline upon, like the bedding that is laid out and the carpet that is spread. [[See the explanation of "al-mihad" above: 4:246 / 6:229 / 7:494.]]

* *

= ﴿And over them coverings﴾.

* *

It is the plural of "ghashiyah," and it refers to that which covers them and envelops them from above.

* *

The meaning of the statement is: For them there is a bed of Hell beneath them, consisting of mattresses, and over them there are quilts from it, and they are between these.

* *

The interpreters have said similar things.

Mention of those who said that:

14655 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿For them a bed of Hell﴾, he said: "The bedding." = ﴿And over them coverings﴾, he said: "The quilts."

14656 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak: ﴿For them a bed of Hell and over them coverings﴾, he said: "al-mihad" are the bedspreads, and "al-ghawashi" are the quilts.

14657 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿For them a bed of Hell and over them coverings﴾. As for "al-mihad," it is like the form of bedding = and "al-ghawashi," they cover them from above.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, He means: Thus do We reward and requite those who wrong themselves, bringing upon themselves the wrath of Allah that they cannot bear, by their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His prophets. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" and "al-zulm" above in the language indexes under (jaza) and (zalama).]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 42:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds—We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity; those are the companions of Paradise, therein they will abide forever.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acknowledged what came to them from Allah's revelation, His sending down, and the laws of His religion, did what Allah commanded them, obeying Him, and avoided what He forbade them [[See the explanation of "al-salihat" (the righteous deeds) in the lexical indices previously mentioned (root ṣ-l-ḥ).]] = ﴿We do not burden any soul except with what it can bear﴾, meaning: We do not burden any soul with deeds except what it is able to bear, so there is no hardship in it [[See the explanation of "taklif" (obligation) and "wus" (capacity) previously mentioned, p. 225, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿those﴾, meaning: these who believed and did righteous deeds = ﴿are the companions of Paradise﴾, meaning: they are the people of Paradise, who truly belong to it, and not others who disbelieved in Allah and did evil [[See the explanation of "ashab al-jannah" (companions of Paradise) in the lexical indices previously mentioned (root ṣ-ḥ-b).]] = ﴿therein they will abide forever﴾, meaning [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fihā khālidūn" without "hum", but I have retained the text of the recitation.]]: they will remain in Paradise, their staying there is everlasting, they will not leave it, and its blessings will not be taken from them [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "wa lā yuslabūna ni'matahum", but the context requires what I have retained.]] [[See the explanation of "al-khuld" (eternity) in the lexical indices previously mentioned (root kh-l-d).]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; rivers flow beneath them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We will remove from the breasts of these people whom He described, and whom He informed are the companions of Paradise, whatever hatred, rancor, and enmity there was between some of them and others in the world. Then, when He admits them to Paradise, He places them on couches facing one another, and none of them envies another for anything Allah has specially granted to some of them and favored them with of His honor, while the rivers of Paradise flow beneath them. [[al-Ghamr (with a kasra and sukun) and al-ghamr (with two fatḥas): the rancor that overwhelms the heart.]]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14658. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾, he said: enmity.

14659. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾, he said: they are the ihan (grudges).

14660. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Isra'il Abu Musa, from al-Hasan, from 'Ali, who said: By Allah, it was revealed about us, the people of Badr: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, as brothers, on couches facing one another﴾ [Surah al-Hijr: 47].

14661. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Isra'il, who said: I heard him say: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: By Allah, it was revealed about us, the people of Badr: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, as brothers, on couches facing one another﴾.

14662. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Indeed I hope that I, 'Uthman, Talha, and al-Zubayr are among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾, may Allah be pleased with them.

14663. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; rivers flow beneath them﴾, he said: When the people of Paradise are driven to Paradise and arrive, they find at its gate a tree, at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They drink from one of them, and whatever resentment is in their breasts is removed; this is "the pure drink." They wash in the other, and "the radiance of bliss" flows over them, so their hair will never become disheveled nor their bodies soiled after that.

14664. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, who said: The people of Paradise will be detained before Paradise until judgment is passed between some of them and others, so that when they enter Paradise, none of them will demand from another even the paring of a fingernail that he wronged him by. And the people of the Fire will be detained before the Fire until judgment is passed between some of them and others, so that when they enter the Fire, none of them will demand from another even the paring of a fingernail that he wronged him by. [[The narration 14664: al-Jurayri is Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Jurayri, mentioned previously under no. 196. Abu Nadrah is al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, who narrated from 'Ali, mentioned previously under no. 6337.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 43:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this. And we would not have been [able] to be guided if not for that Allah guided us."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: And those whom He described, who believed and did righteous deeds, will say when they enter Paradise and see the honour Allah has bestowed upon them, and the torment of humiliation from which He has averted them, with which the people of the Fire were afflicted because of their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His messengers: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this﴾, meaning: Praise be to Allah, who enabled us to do the deed which earned us this that we are in, of Allah's honour and bounty, and the averting of His punishment from us. ﴿And we would not have been [able] to be guided if not for that Allah guided us﴾, meaning: We would not have been rightly guided to that, had Allah not guided us to it and enabled us by His grace and bounty, as:

14665 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from [Abu Sa'id], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every person of the Fire sees his place in Paradise, and they say, 'If only Allah had guided us!' and that becomes a regret for them. And every person of Paradise sees his place in the Fire, and they say, 'Had Allah not guided us!' This is their gratitude."

[Note on the chain: In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "from Abu Sa'id", meaning Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. It is evidently an error, as I did not find the report in the hadith of Abu Sa'id, and because this report is well known from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:85, saying: "al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir in Dhikr al-Mawt, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah," and he gave the report. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 3:477, saying: "al-Nasa'i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah," and he gave the report. al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 10:399, saying: "From Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said," and he gave the report in a similar form through two routes, then said: "All of it was narrated by Ahmad, and the narrators of the first route are the narrators of the authentic collections." I did not find its place in the Musnad. All of this makes it nearly certain that "from Abu Sa'id" in the printed edition and manuscript is an error, and that the correct reading is "from Abu Hurayrah," which is why I have placed it between brackets.]

14666 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating from 'Asim ibn Damrah, from 'Ali, who said: 'Umar mentioned something I do not remember, then mentioned Paradise and said: They enter, and there is a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. He said: They wash in one of them, and the radiance of bliss flows over them, so their hair does not become disheveled and their skin does not become dusty. And they drink from the other, and every impurity, filth and harm in their bellies is expelled. [Note: The printed edition reads "filth, dirt, or something in their bellies," while the manuscript reads "aws," unpointed with a ṭ above it indicating doubt and error. I have adopted the correct reading from Ibn al-Qayyim's Hadi al-Arwah and al-Durr al-Manthur.] He said: Then the gate of Paradise will be opened for them, and it will be said to them: ﴿Peace be upon you; you have become good, so enter it to abide eternally﴾. He said: The young boys (wildan) will meet them and surround them as a close relative (hamim) who has returned from his absence is surrounded. [Note: al-Hamim is the close relative whom one loves and is concerned for.] Then they will come to their wives and give them good news, naming them by their names and their fathers' names. The wives will say: "You saw him!" He said: Joy will overwhelm them, and they will come until they stand at the threshold of the door. [Note: Uskufat al-bab (with a damma on the hamza, sukun on the sin, damma on the kaf, followed by a shaddah-ed fatha fa') is the step of the door upon which one treads.] He said: They will come and enter, and the foundation of their houses will be of jundal pearls; there will be palaces of yellow, green, red and every colour, raised couches, arranged cups, aligned cushions, and spread carpets. Were it not that Allah had decreed them, their sight would be snatched away by what they see in them. [Note: Iltamaʿa al-shay' means he snatched it away and took it. Iltama'a basaruhu (passive) means his sight was snatched and stolen so that he can hardly see. It is similarly said iltama'a lawnuhu, meaning it departed and changed.] Then they will embrace their wives, sit on the couches, and say: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this, and we would not have been [able] to be guided had Allah not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth﴾, to the end of the verse. [Note: 'Asim ibn Damrah al-Sulami: Ibn Sa'd, Ibn al-Madini and al-'Ijli deemed him reliable, and al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him." But al-Jawzajani and Ibn 'Adi declared him weak, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: "He had poor memory and frequent errors, though his condition was better than al-A'war." He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/345, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:3.

Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned this report at length in Hadi al-Arwah (I'lam al-Muwaqqi'in) 1:233, saying: "'Adi ibn al-Ja'd said in al-Ja'diyyat: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah, from 'Ali, who said," and there is no mention of "'Umar" in it.

I then found that Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) narrated it in his tafsir (24:24, Bulaq edition) by the route of Mujahid ibn Musa, from Yazid, from Shuraik ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah, from 'Ali, in a similar form. Then he narrated it again by the route of Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali, in a similar form.

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 5:342, attributing it to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Jannah, al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah, and he did not attribute it to Ibn Jarir. He gave it in full.

Ibn Kathir gave it in his tafsir 7:273, from the tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, in a similar form.

None of these contains the mention of "'Umar," so the phrase "qala dhikr 'Umar, li-shay' la ahfazuhu" is extremely strange; I do not know its meaning nor what distortion is in it, unless it is: "qala Ghundar, li-shay' la ahfazuhu," and Ghundar is Muhammad ibn Ja'far, the narrator from Shu'bah, so the phrase "qala Ghundar" would be the words of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna. And Allah knows best.]

* * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth, and they will be called out: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾ (43)

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says, informing about those who believed and did righteous deeds, that they will say upon entering Paradise and seeing the honour of Allah which He has bestowed upon them, and that the enemies of Allah in the Fire will say, (namely) "By Allah, the messengers of our Lord came to us in this world, and to these who are in the Fire, with the truth, from the reports of the promise of Allah to the people of His obedience and faith in Him and His messengers, and His threat to the people of His disobedience and disbelief in Him."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will be called out: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾, its meaning is: a caller called out to those whose description Allah has given, and informed about what He has prepared for them of His honour: "O these, this is that Paradise which My messengers told you about in the world, which Allah has bequeathed to you in place of those who denied His messengers, because of your belief in them and your obedience to your Lord." And that is the meaning of His saying: ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

* * *

The people of interpretation said things in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

14667 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿And they will be called out: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾, he said: There is no disbeliever or believer except that he has a place in Paradise and the Fire. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and they enter their places, Paradise is raised for the people of the Fire, and they look at their places in it. It is said to them: "These are your places, had you acted in obedience to Allah." Then it is said: "O people of Paradise, inherit them for what you used to do," and the places of the people of Paradise are divided among them.

14668 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Sa'd Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, [from Sa'id ibn Bukayr], from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr, regarding: ﴿And they will be called out: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾, he said: It is called out: "Be healthy and never fall ill, abide and never die, and enjoy and never be miserable." [Note: The narrator Amr ibn Sa'd Abu Dawud al-Hafari is reliable. He appeared earlier as no. 863, and he narrates from Sufyan al-Thawri, but here it reads "Sa'id ibn Bukayr." As for "Sa'id ibn Bukayr," it reads "Sa'd ibn Bakr" in the printed edition, and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. I do not know who he is, or what it is a distortion of. "al-Aghurr" is Abu Muslim al-Madani, who narrated from Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id, and both had jointly freed him. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from him, a reliable Successor. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/44, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/308. This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 17:174, by the route of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), at length, in a similar form. It will come abbreviated in the next one.]

14669 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr, from Abu Sa'id, regarding: ﴿And they will be called out: "This is Paradise"﴾, to the end of the verse, he said: A caller calls out: "For you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill, ever." [Note: This is an abridgement of Muslim's hadith (17:174) mentioned in the previous footnote.]

* * *

The grammarians differed regarding the "an" that comes with "tilkum."

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is the heavy "anna," lightened, with its noun omitted, and it cannot be taken as the light one, because a noun follows it, and the light one is not followed by nouns. And a poet has said: [Note: He is al-A'sha.]

In a company like Indian swords, who have known that every one who goes barefoot and wears shoes is perishing.

[Note: Diwan: 45; Sibawayh 1:282, 440, 480; 2:123; Amali Ibn al-Shajari 2:2; al-Insaf: 89; al-Khizanah 3:547; 4:356; Sharh Shawahid al-'Ayni (in the margin of al-Khizanah) 2:287, and others.

This verse was recited by Sibawayh, and the grammarians followed him in their books. It is a verse compiled from two verses. al-A'sha says in his famous qasidah: "If you see us barefoot, having no sandals, indeed we are thus, whoever goes barefoot and whoever wears shoes..." (the verses follow in the original, and are given here as transliterated in the Arabic source).]

Another said: [Note: I did not know who said it.]

I associate with him, and I know that both of us are eager for what displeases his companion.

[Note: Sibawayh 1:440; al-Insaf of Ibn al-Anbari: 89, 183; Amali Ibn al-Shajari 1:188, and others. "Ukashiruhu" means: I laugh with him.]

He said: Its meaning is: that it is "kilana" (both of us). He said: It is like His saying: ﴿an qad wajadna﴾ in the place of "ay"; and His saying: ﴿an aqimu﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 13]. The "an" that governs verbs is not this, because you say: "ghaza'ani an qama" and "an dhahaba," and it falls upon verbs, even though it does not govern them. And in the Book of Allah: ﴿wa-ntalaqa al-mala' minhum ani mshu﴾ [Surat Sad: 6], that is: "walk."

* * *

Some of the people of Kufa rejected this statement, saying: It is not permissible that with "an" in this place there is a hidden "ha'" (pronoun), because "an" entered the speech to shield what follows it. He said: This "an" that is with "tilkum" is the circle in which falls what resembles narration, not the wording of narration, such as: "I called out that you are standing," and "anna Zayd qa'im," and "an qumta," so it follows the whole speech, and "an" is made a shield, because the calling falls upon what follows it, and what follows "an" is left intact as what follows "qawl" is left intact. Do you not see that you say: "I said: Zayd is standing," and "I said: he stood," so whatever speech you wish follows it? So when calling carried the meaning of "thinking" and what resembles "saying," what follows "an" was left intact, and "an" entered as a shield. He said: As for "ay," it does not come after "an"; "ay" cannot be the answer of the speech, and "an" suffices for the noun.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes." Then a crier will announce between them: "The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ (7:44)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire after they have entered it: "O people of the Fire, we have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true in this world through the tongues of His messengers, namely the reward for faith in Him and in them, and for obedience to Him. Have you found what our Lord promised you through their tongues, namely the punishment for disbelief in Him and for disobeying Him?" [[See the explanation of "companions of Paradise" and "companions of the Fire" in the earlier lexical indexes under (ṣ-ḥ-b).]] The people of the Fire will answer them: "Yes, indeed, we have found what our Lord promised to be true," as related in:

14670 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes."﴾ He said: The people of Paradise found what they had been promised of reward, and the people of the Fire found what they had been promised of punishment.

14671 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"﴾ That is because Allah promised the people of Paradise bliss, honor, and every good that people know or do not know, and He promised the people of the Fire every disgrace and punishment that people know or do not know. This is His saying: ﴿And other punishments of similar kind, in pairs﴾ [Surah Sad: 58]. He said: So the companions of Paradise call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They say, "Yes." Meaning: of disgrace, humiliation, and punishment. The people of Paradise said: "Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true, of bliss and honor." ﴿Then a crier will announce between them that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.﴾

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes."﴾

The majority of reciters from Madina, Kufa, and Basra recited it: ﴿قَالُوا نَعَمْ﴾ with a fatha on the 'ain of "نَعَمْ".

* *

It is related from some of the Kufans that he recited "قَالُوا نَعِمْ" with a kasra on the 'ain, and he recited a line of verse from the Banu Kalb:

Na'im, when he says it, is from him a confirmed thing... and 'asa is not disappointed from him, nor is qamin.

[[I did not find this line, nor did I know its author. "Qamin" means worthy. The meaning: if he says to you, "Perhaps what you ask will be," or "You are worthy of attaining what you seek," then that is from him an execution of what you ask and a realization of what you seek.

In the printed edition it read "wa la tajī'u 'asā" which differs from the manuscript, and the manuscript reading is correct, because he said that a promise with "na'am" is confirmed, and with something less than it in promise is also confirmed, and the one who asks it of him is not disappointed.]]

with a kasra on "نعم".

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in our view is ﴿نَعَمْ﴾ with a fatha on the 'ain, because it is the widely transmitted recitation among the reciters of the regions, and the well-known usage among the Arabs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then a crier will announce between them﴾, meaning: a caller calls out and an announcer announces among them, ﴿that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: the anger, wrath, and punishment of Allah upon those who disbelieved in Him. [[See the explanation of "al-la'na" (curse) in what preceded, p. 416, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

We have already explained the discussion of "anna" when it accompanies speech that resembles reported speech without being explicit reported speech: the Arabs sometimes make it emphatic (shaddada), and the verb falls upon it so they open it, and sometimes they lighten it, and the verb governs it so they put it in the accusative, and its governance is nullified over the noun that follows it. That was explained earlier, sufficiently to avoid repeating it in this place.

* *

Since that is so, whether "anna" is read with shadda or without it makes no difference, since the meaning of the speech is one regardless of which reading the reciter uses, and both are well-known recitations among the reciters of the regions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 45:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who bar (people) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, means: the caller (al-mu'adhdhin) between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire will say: "Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers," those who disbelieved in Allah and barred (others) from His way [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" (barring) earlier, 10:565, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, meaning: they seek to corrupt the way of Allah, which is His religion [[See the explanation of "the way of Allah" earlier in the lexical indexes (s-b-l).]] = "to alter it and change it from the uprightness with which Allah made it" [[See the explanation of "baghā" (seeking/desiring) earlier, p. 286, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they deny the Resurrection of the Hour, and the Raising, and the reward and punishment therein.

* *

The Arabs say of inclination in religion and in a path: "iwaj" with a kasra on the "ayn" (ʿiwaj). And of a man's inclination toward a thing and his leaning upon it, they say: "‘āja ilayhi yaʿūju ʿiyājan wa-ʿawaj­an wa-ʿiwajan," with a kasra or a fatha on the "ayn," as the poet said: [[I did not identify the one who said it.]]

*Qifā nasʾal manāzila Āl Layla … ʿalā ʿiwajin ilayhā wa-inthināʾ*
("Halt, let us ask the dwelling-places of the family of Layla … of bending toward them and turning back.") [[Lisan al-Arab (ʿ-w-j); its reading: *matā ʿiwajun ilayhā wa-inthinā'*. In the printed edition: "*qifā nabki*" ("halt, let us weep"), which is a misreading of the manuscript by the editor; the correct reading is what is recorded here, as also in the Lisan.]]

Al-Farra' mentioned that Abu al-Jarrah recited it to him with a kasra on the "ayn" of "ʿiwaj." As for what is a natural feature in a person, it is said of it: "ʿawaj of his shin (ʿawaj sāquhu)," with a fatha on the "ayn."

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And between them is a veil, and upon the heights (al-A'raf) are men who recognize each by his mark﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "And between them is a veil," may He be glorified, He means that between Paradise and Hellfire there is a veil, that is, a barrier. It is the wall that God, exalted is He, mentioned when He said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate. Its inner side will contain mercy, and its outer side will be facing torment﴾ [al-Hadid: 13]. And it is "al-A'raf" (the heights) of which God says: ﴿And upon the heights are men﴾, as such.

14671. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached me from Mujahid, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a veil between Paradise and Hellfire.

14672. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And between them is a veil﴾, and it is "the wall," and it is "al-A'raf."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And upon the heights are men﴾, "al-A'raf" is a plural whose singular is "'urf." Among the Arabs, every elevated part of the ground is an "'urf." The crest of a rooster is called "'urf" only because it is raised above the rest of its body. From this is the saying of al-Shammakh ibn Dirar:
