*And they stood on elevations, rising, as if they were*
*spears planted by a rider, facing the direction of the wind.*

[Note: his Diwan (p. 53), Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda (1:215). The variant in his Diwan and elsewhere is: "And they stood by al-yafa', as if they were..." This verse is from the end of the poem describing wild asses, after they returned from their long, wondrous journey in search of water, led by the male ass. He describes it and them, saying:

*A protector of their flanks, whom no sound frightens,*
*nor the hunter who pursues the wild beasts.*
*And he stood above the rise, the rise of a dove,*
*his hoof visible in the level of the earth.*
*And they stood wandering among the highlands...*

"Tughalli al-hums" means the wild asses rubbing against one another. He describes the leanness of the wild asses, as if they were spears leaning, facing the blowing winds. In the printed edition it read "Ta'ala," which is an error. In the manuscript it reads thus: "Wa-tallat bi-a'raf ta'ala ka'annaha rimah wajhahu rakiz," and the correct reading is what has been recorded.] He means by his saying "bi-a'raf" (on the heights): on elevations of the ground. From this is the saying of another [poet]: [Note: I do not know who said it.]

*Every compact of flesh, sturdy-limbed, tall,*
*like the mountain standing upon the heights.*

[Note: Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda (1:215); al-Lisan (n-w-f). "Al-kinaz" means one whose flesh is compact and strong. "Al-niyaf" means tall; he describes a camel. "Al-'alam" means the mountain.]

* *

Al-Suddi used to say: "Al-A'raf" was only named a'raf because its companions recognize the people.

14673. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me this same report, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

14674. Sufyan ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, who heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "Al-A'raf" is the elevated thing.

14675. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say the like.

14676. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" are walls like the crest of a rooster.

14677. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like.

14678. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a veil between Paradise and Hellfire, a wall that has a gate. [Abu Musa said: 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid narrated to me, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "Al-A'raf" is a mound between Paradise and Hellfire, upon which some people of sins are held between Paradise and Hellfire.]

14679. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a veil between Paradise and Hellfire, a wall with a gate.

14680. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire.

14681. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire.

14682. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying, ﴿And upon the heights are men﴾, that by al-A'raf he meant the wall which God mentioned in the Qur'an, [Note: this is the one mentioned in the verse of Surat al-Hadid: 13, and what was mentioned above in the earlier reports] and it is between Paradise and Hellfire.

14683. al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a wall that has a crest like the rooster's crest.

14684. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire.

14685. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "Al-A'raf" is the wall between Paradise and Hellfire.

* *

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the description of the men of whom God, may He be glorified, informed that they are upon al-A'raf, and what the cause was for which they came to be there.

Some of them said: They are a people from the children of Adam whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, so they were placed there until God decides concerning them what He wills; then He admits them to Paradise by the bounty of His mercy toward them.

Mention of those who said this:

14686. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, who said: al-Sha'bi said: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman sent for me, and with him was Abu al-Zinad 'Abdullah ibn Dhakwan, client of Quraysh. The two of them mentioned something about the companions of al-A'raf that was not as they had said. So I said to them: "If you wish, I will inform you of what Hudhayfa mentioned." They said: "Go on!" So I said: "Hudhayfa mentioned the companions of al-A'raf and said: They are a people whose good deeds carried them past the Fire, and whose bad deeds fell short of bringing them to Paradise. When their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say: 'Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.' While they are in that state, your Lord, blessed and exalted, looks down upon them and says: 'Go and enter Paradise, for I have forgiven you.'" [Note: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab al-'Adawi, who was called "al-A'raj." 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz appointed him over Kufa, and Abu al-Zinad was his secretary. He is trustworthy; the collection of hadith scholars narrated from him; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/15), and in Nasab Quraysh (363). Abu al-Zinad, 'Abdullah ibn Dhakwan, client of Quraysh, has passed as No. 11813.]

14687. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Hudhayfa, that he was asked about the companions of al-A'raf. He said: They are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, so their bad deeds fell short of bringing them to Paradise, and their good deeds failed to carry them beyond the Fire. He said: So they were made to stand there upon the wall until God decides concerning them.

14688. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir and 'Imran ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from Husayn, from 'Amir, from Hudhayfa, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people who had sins and good deeds; their sins fell short of bringing them to Paradise, and their good deeds carried them beyond the Fire. So they remain thus until God judges between His creatures, and His command takes effect concerning them.

14689. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, from Hudhayfa, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; He says: "Enter Paradise by My grace and My forgiveness; no fear shall be upon you today, nor shall you grieve."

14690. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from 'Amir, from Hudhayfa, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds carried them past the Fire, and whose bad deeds fell short of bringing them to Paradise.

14691. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, while narrating it from Ibn Mas'ud: People will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one enters Paradise, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one enters the Fire. Then he recited God's saying: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful. And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 8–9]. Then he said: Indeed the scale is tipped by the weight of a grain and goes down. He said: Whoever's good deeds and bad deeds are equal is among the companions of al-A'raf. They will stand upon the Sirat (bridge). Then they will recognize the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. When they look toward the people of Paradise, they call out: "Peace be upon you." And when they turn their eyes to their left and look at the companions of the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-A'raf: 47], and they seek refuge in God from their abodes. He said: As for the companions of good deeds, they are given a light by which they walk before them and on their right. Every servant and every female servant will be given a light on that day. When they reach the Sirat, God takes away the light of every hypocrite man and woman. When the people of Paradise see what the hypocrites suffer, [Note: in the manuscript: "fa-lamma ra'aw ahl al-Jannah," which is permissible] they say: "Our Lord, complete for us our light." As for the companions of al-A'raf, the light was in their hands and was not taken from their hands. It is then that God says: ﴿They have not entered it, while they hope﴾ [al-A'raf: 46], and so the hope was entry. He said: Ibn Mas'ud then said: Indeed, when a servant does a good deed, ten are written for him by it, and when he does a bad deed, only one is written. Then he says: Destroyed is the one whose singles overcome his tens. [Note: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not to be relied upon. Ghundar said: "He was our imam, and he used to lie." He has passed as Nos. 597, 8376, 13054, 14398. Ghundar said: "He was our imam, and he used to lie." Passed as Nos. 597, 8376, 13054, 14398. "Al-wuhdan," with a damma on the waw, is the plural of "wahid" (one). "Al-a'shar" is the plural of "'ashr" (ten).]

14692. Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: 'Isa al-Hannat informed me, from al-Sha'bi, from Hudhayfa, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people who had deeds by which God rescued them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise; they have recognized the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. [Note: al-Walid ibn Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni, Abu Hammam, the teacher of al-Tabari; they spoke about him, and Ibn Mu'in said: "There is no harm in him; he is not one who lies." Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written but not relied upon." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/7). 'Isa al-Hannat is 'Isa ibn Abi 'Isa al-Hannat al-Ghifari, and he is 'Isa ibn Maysara, weak, unsteady in hadith, whose hadith is not written. He was a "khabbat" (tailor), then he left that and became a "hannat" (grain seller), then he left that and began selling thread. Ibn Sa'd said: "He used to say: I am a khabbat, a hannat, a khayyat (tailor); each I have practiced." In the printed edition here it read "al-Khayyat," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript, though what is in the printed edition would be correct. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/289).]

14693. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; their good deeds do not exceed their bad deeds, nor do their bad deeds exceed their good deeds.

14694. Ibn Wakī' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire, and the companions of al-A'raf are in that place, until when God wills to pardon them, they are taken to a river called "al-Hayat" (Life), whose banks are reeds of gold, adorned with pearls, its soil musk. They plunge into it until their complexions are made right, and a white mark appears on their necks by which they are recognized. When their complexions are made right, the Merciful brings them and says: "Wish for whatever you desire!" He said: They wish, until their wishes run out, and He says to them: "What you have wished for is yours, and the like of it seventy times!" So they enter Paradise, with a white mark on their necks by which they are recognized; they are called "the paupers of Paradise." [Note: He will narrate it as a statement of a companion, 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, in the following report. Ibn Kathir said after mentioning both reports: "And from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith's own words, and this is more sound" (al-Tafsir 3:482). "Qusb al-dhahab" means tubes of gold, hollow and elongated. In the printed edition here and what follows it reads "qadb" with a dad.]

14695. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Mujahid, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are commanded to a river called "al-Hayat," whose soil is wars (a yellow dye) and saffron, and whose banks are reeds of pearl = He said: I think he said: adorned with pearls = He said: They wash in it, and a white mark appears on their necks. It is said to them: "Wish!" It is said to them: "What you wished is yours, and seventy times over!" And they are the paupers of the people of Paradise.

14696. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Mujahid, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: The companions of al-A'raf, they are led to a river called "al-Hayat," whose banks are reeds of gold = Sufyan said: I think he said: adorned with pearls = He said: They wash in it once, and a white mark appears on their necks. Then they return and wash, and they increase. Every time they wash, they grow whiter. It is said to them: "Wish for whatever you want!" So they wish for what they will, and it is said to them: "What you wished is yours, and seventy times over!" He said: They are the paupers of the people of Paradise.

14697. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi, from Hudhayfa, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. They are upon a wall between Paradise and Hellfire: ﴿They have not entered it, while they hope﴾.

14698. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "Al-A'raf" is between Paradise and Hellfire, where some people are held because of their deeds. And he used to say: They are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; their good deeds do not exceed their bad deeds, nor do their bad deeds exceed their good deeds.

14699. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal.

14700. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal.

14701. ... And he said: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The companions of al-A'raf: their deeds are equal.

14702. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The companions of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they were made to stand there upon the wall.

١٤٧٠٢- حدثنا ابن حميد قال، حدثنا جرير، عن منصور، عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت، عن سفيع، أو سميع = قال أبو جعفر: كذا وجدت في كتاب سفيع [[في المخطوطة: ((كتابي)) ثم ضرب على ((بي)) ، وكتب بعدها ((ب)) ، وأخشى أن يكون الذي ضرب عليه الناسخ هو الصواب.]] =، عن أبي علقمة قال: أصحاب الأعراف، قوم استوت حسناتهم وسيئاتهم. [[الأثر: ١٤٧٠٢ - ((سفيع)) ، لم أجد من ذكره.
وأما ((سميع)) الراوي عن ابن عباس، فهو ((سميع الزيات)) ((أبو صالح)) ، ثقة مترجم في الكبير ٢ /٢ / ١٩٠، وابن أبي حاتم ٢ / ١ / ٣٠٥.]]
* *
وقال آخرون: كانوا قتلوا في سبيل الله عصاة لآبائهم في الدنيا.
ذكر من قال ذلك:
١٤٧٠٣- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا يحيى بن يمان، عن أبي مسعر، عن شرحبيل بن سعد قال: هم قوم خرجوا في الغزو بغير إذن آبائهم.
١٤٧٠٤ - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح قال، حدثني الليث قال، حدثني خالد، عن سعيد، عن يحيى بن شبل: أن رجلا من بني النضير أخبره، عن رجل من بني هلال: أن أباه أخبره: أنه سأل رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ) عن أصحاب الأعراف فقال: هم قوم غزوا في سبيل الله عصاةً لآبائهم، فقتلوا، فأعتقهم الله من النار بقتلهم في سبيله، وحُبسوا عن الجنة بمعصية آبائهم، فهم آخر من يدخل الجنة. [[الأثر: ١٤٧٠٤ - ((يحيى بن شبل)) ، ((مولى بني هاشم)) لم أعرف حاله، ترجم له ابن أبي حاتم ٤ / ٢ / ١٥٧، ولم يذكر فيه جرحًا، والبخاري في الكبير ٤ / ٢ / ٢٨٢، وذكره في التهذيب إلحاقًا فقال: ((ولهم بن شبل شيخ آخر مدني، أقدم من هذا، يروي عنه أبو معشر حديثًا في أصحاب الأعراف))
واقتصر البخاري على أنه يروي عنه سعيد بن أبي هلال. وأما ابن أبي حاتم، فذكر أنه روى عن ((عمر بن عبد الرحمن المزني، وعن جده بن حسين (؟؟) عن علي رضي الله عنه)) ثم قال: ((روى عنه سعيد بن أبي هلال، وعبد العزيز بن عبد الله بن أبي سلمة، وأبو معشر، وموسى بن عبيدة الربذي، وابن أبي سبرة)) .
وزادنا أبو جعفر في الأثر التالي أنه ((مولى بني هاشم)) ، ولم أجد لذلك ذكرًا في الكتب التي بأيدينا.
وهذا خبر ضعيف، لما فيه من المجاهيل، ولأن ((أبا معشر)) نفسه، قد تكلموا فيه، وضعفوه. وانظر التعليق على الأثر التالي، ففيه التخريج.]]
١٤٧٠٥ - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا يزيد بن هارون، عن أبي معشر، عن يحيى بن شبل مولى بني هاشم، عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه قال: سئل رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ) عن أصحاب الأعراف، فقال: قوم قتلوا في سبيل الله بمعصية آبائهم، فمنعهم قتلهم في سبيل الله عن النار، ومنعتهم معصية آبائهم أن يدخلوا الجنة. [[الأثر: ١٤٧٠٥ - ((يحيى بن شبل، مولى بني هاشم)) ، انظر الأثر السالف.
و ((محمد بن عبد الرحمن المزني)) ، لم أجد له ترجمة مفردة، ويقال أيضًا ((عمر بن الرحمن المزني)) ، ويقال: ((عمرو بن عبد الرحمن)) ، إن صلح ما في ترجمة أبيه في أسد الغابة.
وأبوه ((عبد الرحمن المزني)) ، ويقال ((عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الرحمن)) ، وقال ابن عبد البر في الاستيعاب: ((وقد قيل: اسم أبيه محمد، وهو الصواب إن شاء الله)) .
وترجم له ابن عبد البر في الاستيعاب: ٣٩٩، وابن الأثير في أسد الغابة في موضعين ٣: ٣٠٧، ٣٢٢، وابن حجر في الإصابة في موضعين: في ((عبد الرحمن بن أبي الهلالي)) وفي ((عبد الرحمن المزني)) ، ولم يشر إلى ذلك في واحدة من الترجمتين، وهو عجيب!! واختلفوا في تسمية ولده، فقال ابن حجر: ((والد عمر، ويقال: والد محمد)) ، وقال ابن عبد البر: ((وله ولد آخر يقال له: ((عبد الرحمن)) . أما ابن الأثير، ففيه أن ولده ((عمرو)) ، وأن كنية ((عبد الرحمن المزني)) هو ((أبو عمرو)) .
وأما قوله في الأثر السالف: ((أن رجلا من بني النضير)) ، فهكذا جاء في المخطوطة والمطبوعة، وفي المراجع الأخرى: ((أن رجلا من بني نضر)) ، ولا أدري أهو بالضاد المعجمة أم الصاد المهملة. وأما ((عن رجل من بني هلال)) فكأنه يعني من ((بني هلال بن رئاب)) من ((بني عمرو بن أد)) ، وهم مزينة، ومن بني هلال بن رئاب ((إياس بن معاوية المزني)) القاضي المشهور. انظر جمهرة الأنساب لابن حزم: ١٩٢. ويدل على ذلك أن ابن حجر ترجم له في ((عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الرحمن الهلالي)) وفي ((عبد الرحمن المزني)) ، وذكر فيهما حديثه في الأعراف.
وهذا الخبر ذكروه جميعًا من طرق مختلفة، وكلها مضطرب، وقد جمع الكلام فيه الحافظ ابن حجر في الإصابة في الموضعين، ولكنه لم يستوفه.
ومهما يكن من شيء، فهو حديث ضعيف لضعف أبي معشر، ولما يحيط به من الجهالة كما أسلفت في التعليق على الأثر السالف.]]
* *
وقال آخرون: بل هم قوم صالحون فقهاء علماء.
ذكر من قال ذلك:
١٤٧٠٦- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبي، عن سفيان، عن خصيف، عن مجاهد قال: أصحاب الأعراف، قوم صالحون فقهاء علماء.
* *
وقال آخرون: بل هم ملائكة وليسوا ببني آدم.
ذكر من قال ذلك:
١٤٧٠٧- حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال، حدثنا ابن علية، عن أبي مجلز قوله: ﴿وبينهما حجاب وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: هم رجال من الملائكة، يعرفون أهل الجنة وأهل النار، قال: ﴿ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم﴾ ، إلى قوله: ﴿ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين﴾ ، قال: فنادى أصحاب الأعراف رجالا في النار يعرفونهم بسيماهم: ﴿ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون. أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة﴾ ، قال: فهذا حين دخل أهل الجنة الجنة: ﴿ادخلوا الجنة لا خوف عليكم ولا أنتم تحزنون﴾ .
١٤٧٠٨- حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى قال، حدثنا المعتمر قال، سمعت عمران قال: قلت لأبي مجلز: يقول الله: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال﴾ ، وتزعم أنتَ أنهم الملائكة؟ قال فقال: إنهم ذكور، وليسوا بإناث.
١٤٧٠٩- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا جرير، عن سليمان التيمي، عن أبي مجلز: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال﴾ ، قال: رجال من الملائكة، يعرفون الفريقين جميعًا بسيماهم، أهل النار وأهل الجنة، وهذا قبل أن يدخل أهل الجنة الجنة.
١٤٧١٠- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا محمد بن أبي عدي، عن التيمي، عن أبي مجلز، بنحوه.
١٤٧١١-. . . . وقال، حدثنا يحيى بن يمان، عن سفيان، عن التيمي، عن أبي مجلز قال: أصحاب الأعراف، الملائكة.
١٤٧١٢- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا يعلى بن أسد قال، حدثنا خالد قال، أخبرنا التيمي، عن أبي مجلز: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال﴾ ، قال: هم الملائكة.
١٤٧١٣- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبي، عن عمران بن حدير، عن أبي مجلز: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال﴾ ، قال: هم الملائكة. قلت: يا أبا مجلز، يقول الله تبارك وتعالى: "رجال"، وأنت تقول: ملائكة؟ قال: إنهم ذُكران ليسوا بإناث.
١٤٧١٤- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا الحجاج قال، حدثنا حماد، عن عمران بن حدير، عن أبي مجلز في قوله: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: الملائكة. قال قلت: يقول الله "رجال"؟ قال: الملائكة ذكور. [[في المخطوطة: ((الملائكة)) دون صفتهم ((ذكور)) ، كأنه قطع الكلام بالإثبات. وإن كان يخشى أيضًا أن يكون الناسخ أسقط ما ثبت في المطبوعة.]]
* *
قال أبو جعفر: والصواب من القول في أصحاب الأعراف أن يقال كما قال الله جل ثناؤه فيهم: هم رجال يعرفون كلا من أهل الجنة وأهل النار بسيماهم، ولا خبر عن رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ) يصح سنده، ولا أنه متفق على تأويلها، ولا إجماع من الأمة على أنهم ملائكة.
فإذ كان ذلك كذلك، وكان ذلك لا يدرك قياسًا، وكان المتعارف بين أهل لسان العرب أن "الرجال" اسم يجمع ذكور بني آدم دون إناثهم ودون سائر الخلق غيرهم، كان بيِّنًا أن ما قاله أبو مجلز من أنهم ملائكة، قولٌ لا معنى له، وأن الصحيح من القول في ذلك ما قاله سائر أهل التأويل غيره. هذا مع مَنْ قال بخلافه من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ)، ومع ما روي عن رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ) في ذلك من الأخبار، وإن كان في أسانيدها ما فيها، وقد:-
١٤٧١٥- حدثني القاسم قال، حدثني الحسين قال، حدثني جرير عن عمارة بن القعقاع، عن أبي زرعة بن عمرو بن جرير قال، سئل رسول الله ﷺ (ﷺ) عن أصحاب الأعراف فقال: "هم آخر مَنْ يفصل بينهم من العباد، وإذا فرغ ربُّ العالمين من فصله بين العباد قال: أنتم قوم أخرجتكم حسناتكم من النار، ولم تدخلكم الجنة، وأنتم عُتَقائي، فارعوا من الجنة حيث شئتم. [[الأثر: ١٤٧١٥ - ((عمارة بن القعقاع بن شبرمة الضبي، روى له الجماعة، مضى برقم: ١٤٢٠٣، ١٤٢٠٩.
و ((أبو زرعة بن عمرو بن جرير بن عبد الله البجلي)) ، ثقة، روى له الجماعة مضى كثيرًا، آخرها أيضًا رقم: ١٤٢٠٣، ١٤٢٠٩. وكان في المطبوعة والمخطوطة: ((أبو زرعة، عن عمرو بن جرير)) ، وهو خطأ.
وهذا خبر مرسل حسن، خرجه السيوطي في الدر المنثور ٣: ٨٧، وزاد إلى ابن المنذر. ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره ٣: ٤٨٢.]]
* *
القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ كُلا بِسِيمَاهُمْ وَنَادَوْا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ (٤٦) ﴾
قال أبو جعفر: يقول تعالى ذكره: وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون أهل الجنة بسيماهم، وذلك بياض وجوههم، ونضرةُ النعيم عليها = ويعرفون أهل النار كذلك بسيماهم، وذلك سواد وجوههم، وزرقة أعينهم، فإذا رأوا أهل الجنة نادوهم: "سلام عليكم".
* *
وبنحو ما قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل.
ذكر من قال ذلك:
١٤٧١٦- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح قال، حدثني معاوية، عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: يعرفون أهل النار بسواد الوجوه، وأهل الجنة ببياض الوجوه.
١٤٧١٧ - حدثني محمد بن سعد قال، حدثني أبي قال، حدثني عمي قال، حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: أنزلهم الله بتلك المنزلة، ليعرفوا من في الجنة والنار، وليعرفوا أهل النار بسواد الوجوه، ويتعوَّذوا بالله أن يجعلهم مع القوم الظالمين، وهم في ذلك يحيّون أهل الجنة بالسلام، لم يدخلوها، وهم يطمعون أن يدخلوها، وهم داخلوها إن شاء الله.
١٤٧١٨ - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم قال، حدثنا عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: بسواد الوجوه، وزُرقة العيون.
١٤٧١٩- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو حذيفة قال، حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، الكفار بسواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون، وسيما أهل الجنة مبيَضَّة وجوههم.
١٤٧٢٠- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال، حدثنا هشيم، عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس قال: أصحاب الأعراف إذا رأوا أصحاب الجنة عرَفوهم ببياض الوجوه، وإذا رأوا أصحاب النار عرفوهم بسواد الوجوه.
١٤٧٢١- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا سويد بن نصر قال، أخبرنا ابن المبارك، عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس قال: إن أصحاب الأعراف رجال كانت لهم ذنوبٌ عِظام، وكان حَسْمُ أمرهم لله، فأقيموا ذلك المقام، إذا نظروا إلى أهل النار عرفوهم بسواد الوجوه، فقالوا: ﴿ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين﴾ ، وإذا نظروا إلى أهل الجنة عرفوهم ببياض الوجوه، فذلك قوله: ﴿ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ .
١٤٧٢٢- حدثت عن الحسين بن الفرج قال، سمعت أبا معاذ قال، حدثنا عبيد بن سليمان قال، سمعت الضحاك في قوله: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، زعموا أن أصحاب الأعراف رجال من أهل الذنوب، أصابوا ذنوبًا، وكان حَسْم أمرهم لله، فجعلهم الله على الأعراف. فإذا نظروا إلى أهل النار عرفوهم بسواد الوجوه، فتعوذوا بالله من النار. وإذا نظروا إلى أهل الجنة نادوهم: "أن سلام عليكم"، قال الله: ﴿لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ . قال: وهذا قول ابن عباس.
١٤٧٢٣- حدثني محمد بن الحسين قال، حدثنا أحمد بن المفضل قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي: ﴿يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، يعرفون الناس بسيماهم، يعرفون أهل النار بسواد وجوههم، وأهل الجنة ببياض وجوههم.
١٤٧٢٤- حدثنا بشر بن معاذ قال، حدثنا يزيد بن زريع قال، حدثنا سعيد، عن قتادة قوله: ﴿يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، يعرفون أهل النار بسواد وجوههم، وأهل الجنة ببياض وجوههم.
١٤٧٢٥- حدثني يونس قال، أخبرنا ابن وهب قال، قال ابن زيد في قوله: ﴿وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: أهل الجنة بسيماهم. بيض الوجوه = وأهل النار بسيماهم، سود الوجوه. قال: وقوله ﴿يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: أصحاب الجنة وأصحاب النار = "ونادوا أصحاب الجنة"، قال: حين رأوا وجوههم قد ابيضت.
١٤٧٢٦- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا المحاربي، عن جويبر، عن الضحاك: ﴿يعرفون كلا بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: بسواد الوجوه.
١٤٧٢٧- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا يحيى بن يمان، عن مبارك، عن الحسن: ﴿بسيماهم﴾ ، قال: بسواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون.
* *
و"السيماء"، العلامة الدالة على الشيء، في كلام العرب. وأصله من "السِّمَة"، نقلت واوها التي هي فاء الفعل، إلى موضع العين، كما يقال: "اضمحلّ" و"امضحلّ". وذكر سماعًا عن بعض بني عقيل: "هي أرض خامة"، يعني "وَخِمة". ومنه قولهم: "له جاه عند الناس"، بمعنى "وجه"، نقلت واوه إلى موضع عين الفعل. [[انظر ((جاه)) فيما سلف ٦: ٤١٥.]] وفيها لغات ثلاث: "سيما" مقصورة، و"سيماء"، ممدودة، و"سيمياء"، بزيادة ياء أخرى بعد الميم فيها، ومدها، على مثال "الكبرياء"، [[انظر تفسير ((سيما)) فيما سلف ٥: ٥٩٤ - ٥٩٧ /٧: ١٨٩، ١٩٠.]] كما قال الشاعر: [[هو أسيد بن عنقاء الفزاري.]]
غُلامٌ رَمَاهُ الله بِالحُسْنِ إذْ رَمَى ... لَهُ سِيمِيَاءُ لا تَشُقُّ عَلَى البَصَرْ [[سلف البيت وتخريجه فيما سلف ٥: ٥٩٥ /٧: ١٨٩.]]
* *
وأما قوله: ﴿ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ ، أي: حلت عليهم أمنة الله من عقابه وأليم عذابه. [[انظر تفسير ((سلام)) فيما سلف ص: ١١٤، تعليق: ١، والمراجع هناك.]]
* *
واختلف أهل التأويل في المعنيّ بقوله: ﴿لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ .
فقال بعضهم: هذا خبر من الله عن أهل الأعراف: أنهم قالوا لأهل الجنة ما قالوا قبل دخول أصحاب الأعراف، غير أنهم قالوه وهم يطمعون في دخولها.
ذكر من قال ذلك:
١٤٧٢٨- حدثني محمد بن الحسين قال، حدثنا أحمد بن مفضل قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي قال: أهل الأعراف يعرفون الناسَ، فإذا مرُّوا عليهم بزُمْرة يُذْهب بها إلى الجنة قالوا: "سلام عليكم". يقول الله لأهل الأعراف: لم يدخلوها، وهم يطمعون أن يدخلوها.
١٤٧٢٩- حدثني محمد بن عبد الأعلى قال، حدثنا محمد بن ثور، عن معمر قال، تلا الحسن: ﴿لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ ، قال: والله ما جعل ذلك الطمع في قلوبهم، إلا لكرامة يريدها بهم.
١٤٧٣٠- حدثنا بشر قال، حدثنا يزيد قال، حدثنا سعيد، عن قتادة قوله: ﴿لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون﴾ ، قال: أنبأكم الله بمكانهم من الطمع.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 46 (part 3 of 3):

14731 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, while narrating this from Ibn Mas'ud: As for the People of the Heights (ashab al-a'raf), the light was in their hands, and it was taken from their hands [[In the printed edition: "ma intazaa" (what was taken), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]. God says: ﴿They have not entered it, while they yearn (to enter it)﴾. He said: "In entering it." Ibn 'Abbas said: "So God admitted the People of the Heights into Paradise."

14732 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah and 'Ata', regarding ﴿They have not entered it, while they yearn (to enter it)﴾, both of them said: "In entering it."

* *

Others said: What is meant by this is the people of Paradise, and that the People of the Heights say to them before they enter Paradise: "Peace be upon you," while the people of Paradise yearn to enter it, and have not yet entered it.

Mention of those who said this:

14733 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: WakI' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding ﴿And they call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, while they yearn (to enter it)﴾: He said: "The angels, who recognize both groups by their marks. And this is before the people of Paradise enter Paradise; the People of the Heights call out to the companions of the Garden: 'Peace be upon you,' while they have not entered it, yearning to enter it."

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words:** ﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ (7:47)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He means: "And when the eyes of the companions of al-A'raf (the Heights) are turned toward the companions of the Fire," that is, facing them and confronting them, "and they see the disfigurement Allah has inflicted on them," ﴿they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people,"﴾ who wronged themselves, earning for themselves Your wrath, which brought them the punishment they are in.

14734: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "And when they pass by them," that is, by the companions of al-A'raf, "by a group being led to the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾"

14735: al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The companions of al-A'raf, when they look at the people of the Fire and recognize them, say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾"

14736: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Makin, from his brother, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾, he said: "Their faces are made to face the Fire, and when they see the people of Paradise, that leaves them."

[[The narration: 14736. "Abu Makin" is "Nuh ibn Rabi'ah al-Ansari," previously cited under nos. 9742–9839. Waki' would err in saying that "Abu Makin" is "Nuh ibn Aban," brother of "al-Hakam ibn Aban," and they pointed out this error. See the biography of Nuh ibn Rabi'ah in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/482.

And his brother, i.e., Waki': "al-Hakam ibn Aban al-Adani," who narrates from Tawus and Ikrimah, a trustworthy (thiqah) narrator, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/334, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/113.]]

14737: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, regarding His words ﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾, said: "They see their faces blackened and their eyes bluish," ﴿and they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, saying: "Of what use to you were your hoarding and your arrogance?"﴾ [7:48]

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men﴾ from the people of the earth; ﴿whom they recognize by their marks﴾, the marks of the people of the Fire; ﴿saying: "Of what use to you was your hoarding"﴾, what you used to gather of wealth and numbers in the world; ﴿"and your arrogance?"﴾ means: your arrogance which you used to display in it [[See the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) above, 11:540 / 12:421.]], as related:

14738 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then there passed by them – meaning by the companions of the Heights – some people of the tyrants whom they recognized by their marks. He said: He says: The companions of the Heights said: ﴿"Of what use to you was your hoarding, and your arrogance?"﴾.

14739 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men﴾, he said: In the Fire. ﴿"whom they recognize by their marks," "Of what use to you was your hoarding, and your arrogance?"﴾ – and your arrogance. [[In the printed edition: "...your gathering and your arrogance and your being arrogant", and it is so in the manuscript, except that above "wa-takabburukum" there is the letter (m) indicating it is placed before its position; I returned it to the original, which is correct.]]

14740 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, saying: "Of what use to you were your hoarding and your arrogance?"﴾ He said: This is when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, ﴿"Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?"﴾ – the verse. I said to Abu Mijlaz: From Ibn 'Abbas? He said: No, rather from someone else.

14741 – Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks﴾, he said: The angels call out to men in the Fire whom they recognize by their marks: ﴿"Of what use to you was your hoarding and your arrogance? Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?"﴾, he said: This is when the people of Paradise enter Paradise: ﴿"Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve."﴾

14742 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks﴾: "The men" are great ones of the people of the world. He said: By this attribute the people of the Heights recognized the people of Paradise from the people of the Fire, and this is mentioned when the leader of the people of good and the leader of the people of evil depart on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Ibn Zayd also said, concerning His words: ﴿"Of what use to you was your hoarding and your arrogance?"﴾: "Over the people of obedience to Allah."

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words:** ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy? "Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve"﴾ (7:49).

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the referents of this speech.

Some of them said: This is the speech of God to the people of the Fire, rebuking them for what they had said in the world, addressed to the people of the A'raf (the Heights), when He admits the companions of the A'raf into the Garden.

Mention of those who said this:

14743. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The companions of the A'raf are men who had great sins, and whose affair was left to God. They stand on the A'raf, and when they look at the people of the Garden, they hope to enter it, and when they look at the people of the Fire, they seek refuge in God from it. So they were admitted into the Garden." This is His saying, exalted is He: "Are these the ones of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy?", meaning the companions of the A'raf. "Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve."

14744. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "God admitted the companions of the A'raf into the Garden, by His saying: 'Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.'"

14745. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: God said to the people of arrogance and wealth: "Are these the ones of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy?", meaning the companions of the A'raf. "Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve."

14746. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Are these" — the weak ones — "the ones of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy? Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve." He said: Hudhayfa said: "The companions of the A'raf are a people whose deeds were balanced, so their good deeds fell short of bringing them into the Garden, and their evil deeds fell short of bringing them into the Fire. So they were placed on the A'raf, recognising people by their marks. When judgment was passed among the servants, they were permitted to seek intercession, so they came to Adam, peace be upon him, and said: 'O Adam, you are our father; intercede for us with your Lord!' He said: 'Do you know anyone whom God created with His own hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, whose mercy preceded His wrath, and to whom the angels prostrated, other than me?' They said: 'No!' He said: 'I did not do in regard to it what is enough for me to intercede for you [[In the printed edition: "the mercy of God preceded His wrath"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]... [[Kunh (كنه) of a thing means its measure, limit, end and reality. He means: I did not do anything that would raise me to the rank of intercession for you. The printed edition has "ma 'alimtu" (I did not know); I have kept the manuscript reading. Ibn Kathir, quoting this passage, has "ma 'alimtu kunhahu ma astatee'" (I did not know its reality, what I am able to do), and the correct reading is that of the Tabari manuscript.]] But go to my son Ibraham!' They come to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and ask him to intercede for them with his Lord. He says: 'Do you know anyone whom God took as a close friend (khalil), or whom his people burned in the fire for God's sake, other than me?' They say: 'No!' He says: 'I did not do in regard to it what is enough for me to intercede for you [[In the printed edition here too: "ma 'alimtu"; I have kept the manuscript. The manuscript reads "ma 'amiltu fihi ma astatee'" (I did not do in regard to it what I am able to), with "kunh" probably omitted by the copyist.]]... But go to my son Musa!' They come to Musa, peace be upon him, and he says: 'Do you know anyone whom God spoke to directly (kallamahu taklimā) and brought near as a confidant (najiyyā), other than me?' They say: 'No!' He says: 'I did not do in regard to it what is enough for me to intercede for you... But go to Isa!' They come to him and say: 'Intercede for us with your Lord!' He says: 'Do you know anyone whom God created without a father, other than me?' They say: 'No!' He says: 'Do you know anyone who used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life by God's permission, other than me?' He said: They say: 'No!' He says: 'I am the one who disputes on behalf of himself (hajjīj nafsi). I did not do in regard to it what is enough for me to intercede for you [[In the printed edition: "ma 'alimtu kunh ma astatee'"; I have kept the manuscript, as I noted in the two previous notes.]]... But go to Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ)!' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'They come to me, and I strike my hand upon my chest and say: "I am for it!" Then I walk until I stand before the Throne, and I praise my Lord, and He opens to me praise such as no hearer has ever heard before. Then I prostrate, and it is said to me: "O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and you shall be given, intercede and your intercession shall be accepted!" So I raise my head and say: "My Lord, my community!" It is said: "They are yours." No prophet sent and no angel brought near will remain but that he will envy me that day for this station, which is the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud).' He said: 'I bring them to the gate of the Garden, and I ask for it to be opened, and it is opened for me and for them. They are taken to a river called "the River of Life" (nahr al-Hayawan) [[In the printed edition: "nahr al-Hayat" (River of Life); I have kept the manuscript, which agrees with Ibn Kathir.]], whose banks are of gold reeds (qasab) encrusted with pearls [[Al-qasab are hollow elongated tubes of jewel, gold or silver. In the printed edition, as noted earlier (p. 455, note 1), it is written with a "d" (qadab); I have kept the manuscript and other sources.]], its soil is musk and its pebbles are rubies. They wash in it, and the colours of the people of the Garden and the scent of the people of the Garden return to them [[In the manuscript: "wa rih" without "ahl al-Jannah". The printed edition has "wa rihuhum"; I have kept what Ibn Kathir has, vol. 3, p. 485, quoting this place of Tabari's tafsir.]], and they become like shining stars, and white marks remain on their chests by which they are recognised; they are called "the poor of the people of the Garden" (masakin ahl al-Jannah).'

14747. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "God admitted them after the companions of the Garden, by His saying: 'Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve,' meaning the companions of the A'raf." This is the saying of Ibn Abbas.

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech according to this interpretation which we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas, and from those whose statements we have mentioned, is: God said to the people of arrogance against acknowledging the oneness of God and submitting to His obedience and the obedience of His messengers, who gathered wealth in the world out of rivalry and ostentation: "O tyrants who were in the world, are these the weak ones, of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy?" He said: "I have forgiven them, and I have shown them mercy by My grace and My mercy. Enter, O companions of the A'raf, the Garden; no fear shall be upon you from any punishment thereafter by which you would be punished for the sins and crimes you committed in the world, nor shall you grieve over anything that escaped you in your worldly life." [[In the printed edition: "O tyrants who were in the world" with an added "alladhina" (who); this is not in the manuscript, which is the correct reading.]]

\* \*

Abu Mijlaz said: Rather, this speech is a report from God of what the angels said to the people of the Fire, after they had entered the Fire, reproaching them for what they used to say in the world to the believers whom God would admit into His Garden on the Day of Resurrection. As for His saying: "Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve," it is a report from God of His command to the people of the Garden to enter it.

14748. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, who said: The angels called to men in the Fire whom they recognised by their marks: "Did not your multitude avail you, nor what you were proud of? * Are these the ones of whom you swore that God would not grant them any mercy?" He said: "This is the time when the people of the Garden enter the Garden: 'Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 50:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided for you." They will say: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the appeal of the people of the Fire to the people of Paradise, when the great calamity of intense thirst and hunger descends upon them, as a punishment from Allah for what they had done in the world of abandoning the obedience of Allah and failing to pay what was obligatory upon them in the world regarding their wealth, namely the rights of the needy in zakat and charity.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out﴾, after they have entered it, ﴿to the companions of Paradise﴾, after they have settled in it, ﴿that﴾, O people of Paradise, ﴿pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾, that is: feed us from what Allah has provided for you of food, as:

14749 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿that pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾, he said: "Of the food."

1475 0 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿that pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾: "They will ask them for food and ask them for drink."

* *

= So the people of Paradise answered them: Indeed, Allah has forbidden water and food to those who denied His Oneness and disbelieved His messengers in the world.

* *

The "ha" and "mim" in His saying ﴿Allah has forbidden them both﴾ refer to "the water" and to "what" (ma) in His saying ﴿or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to this.

Those who said so:

1475 1 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman al-Thaqafi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾, he said: A man calls to his brother or his father, saying: "I have been burned, pour some water upon me!" It is said to them: "Answer them!" And they say: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."

1475 2 - And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Uthman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾, he said: A man calls his brother: "O my brother, I have been burned, so help me!" He says: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers." [[The report 14752: "Ibn Dukayn" is al-Fadl ibn Dukayn al-Taymi, who has passed several times, among them: 2554, 3035, 8535.]]

1475 3 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿They said: Indeed Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers﴾: "The food of the people of Paradise and their drink."

The discussion of His saying: ﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life deceived; so today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day, and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ (7:51)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God about what the people of Paradise say to the disbelievers.

His exalted remembrance says: the people of Paradise answer the people of the Fire, "Indeed God has forbidden them to the disbelievers," those who disbelieved in God and His messengers, who took their religion, which God had commanded them, as amusement and play, meaning: mockery and play. [[See the explanation of "al-lahw" (amusement) above, 11:441. And the explanation of "al-la'ib" (play) above, 11:441, note 2, and the references there.]]

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this:

14754 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abd Allah told us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "those who took their religion as amusement and play," the verse, he said: That is because when they were called to faith they mocked and ridiculed the one who called them to it, deceived by God.

* *

"And the worldly life deceived them," meaning: the immediate things they were in of life, ease and comfort deceived them away from taking their share of the Hereafter, until death came to them. [[See the explanation of "al-ghurur" (deception) above, p. 351, note 1, and the references there.]] God, His praise be great, says: "So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day," meaning: on this day, which is the Day of Resurrection, "We forget them," meaning: We leave them in the manifest punishment, hungry and thirsty, without food or drink, just as they left action for the meeting of this their day, and rejected preparing for it by wearying their bodies in obedience to God.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of His saying "We forget them" with its evidence earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "al-nisyan" (forgetting) above, 11:357, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

14755 - Ibn Waki' told us, he said: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid: "So today We forget them," he said: They are forgotten in the punishment.

14756 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So today We forget them," he said: We leave them as they left the meeting of this their day.

14757 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "We forget them," he said: We leave them in the Fire.

14758 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day," he said: We leave them without mercy, as they left off working for the meeting of this their day.

14759 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day," the verse, he said: God forgets them of good, and does not forget them of evil.

14760 - Al-Harith told me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, he said: Abu Sa'd told us, he said: I heard Mujahid concerning His saying: "So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day," he said: We delay them in the Fire.

* *

As for His saying: "and as they used to deny Our signs," its meaning is: "today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day," and as they used to deny Our signs.

* *

The "mā" in His saying "and as they used to" is coordinated with the "mā" in His saying "as they forgot."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the speech is: Today We leave them in the punishment, just as they left action in the world for the meeting of God on the Day of Resurrection, and just as they used to deny the signs of God, which are His proofs that He argued against them with, from the prophets, messengers, books, and other things. [[See the explanation of "al-ayah" (sign) in the earlier language indices (a-y-y).]]

"Yujhadun" (they used to deny): they lied and did not believe anything of that. [[See the explanation of "al-jahd" (denial) above, 11:334.]]

The Interpretation of His words: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We had detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾ (7:52)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Swear, O Muhammad, that We have certainly brought these disbelievers a Book, meaning the Qur'an which He sent down to you. That is: We have certainly sent down to them this Qur'an, detailed and clarified, in which the truth is distinguished from falsehood. "With knowledge" means: with Our knowledge of the truth of what has been detailed in it, and of the falsehood from which it distinguishes between it and the truth [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) above, p. 402, footnote 1, and the references there.]]. "A guidance and a mercy" means: We have made it clear so that a people who affirm it, and what it contains of God's commands and prohibitions, His reports, and His promise and threat, may be guided by it and shown mercy, and He rescues them by it from misguidance to guidance.

This verse is connected to His words: ﴿A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no constriction in your breast about it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ (7:2), "And We had certainly brought them a Book which We had detailed with knowledge."

* *

"Guidance" (hudan) is in the accusative case as a circumstantial qualifier (qat') relating to the pronoun "hu" in His words "fassalnahu" (We had detailed it). [["Qat'" here means the accusative of circumstance (hal); see the glossary of terms.] If it were put in the accusative as a verbal object of "fassalnahu" [[That is, in the accusative as an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq) not from its own verb, as if he had said: "We detailed it with detailing," so the meaning would be: "We detailed the Book in that manner" — this would also be correct.]], the meaning would also be sound.

If it were read "hudan wa rahmatin" (in the genitive for "rahmah"), it would be eloquent in its grammatical construction, and the genitive of that would be by agreement with "al-Kitab" (the Book). [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 380.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 53:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Do they await only its interpretation? The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "Do they await only its interpretation?" Do these polytheists, who deny the signs of Allah and reject meeting Him, await anything "but its interpretation" — that is, but what their affair will come to: their coming upon the punishment of Allah, their burning in His hellfire, and the like of what Allah has threatened them with.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "ta'wil" (interpretation, outcome) earlier, with its evidence, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [See the explanation of "ta'wil" above: 6:199–206 / 8:506.]

* *

Those who engage in ta'wil (exegesis) said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

14761 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Do they await only its interpretation," meaning: its reward. "The day its interpretation comes," meaning: its reward.

14762 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Do they await only its interpretation, the day its interpretation comes," he said: "Its interpretation" — its consequence.

14763 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Do they await only its interpretation," he said: its recompense. "The day its interpretation comes," he said: its recompense.

14764 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14765 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Do they await only its interpretation" — as for "its interpretation," its outcomes, such as the battle of Badr, and the Resurrection, and what was promised in it of a promise.

14766 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying: "Do they await only its interpretation? The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, 'The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth'": from its interpretation, a matter continues to occur after another, until its interpretation is completed on the Day of Resurrection. In that was revealed: "Do they await only its interpretation," when Allah, blessed and exalted, rewards His allies and His enemies with the reward of their deeds. On that day those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth," the verse.

14767 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Do they await only its interpretation, the day its interpretation comes," he said: the Day of Resurrection.

14768 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "The day its interpretation comes," he said: the day its reality comes. He recited the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 100]. He said: this is its realization. And he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿and none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 7], and said: none knows its reality and when it will come except Allah, exalted.

* *

As for His saying: "The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say," its meaning is: the day there comes what their affair will come to of the punishment of Allah, "those who had forgotten it before will say," meaning: those who neglected and abandoned what they were commanded to do of the deeds that would save them from what their affair would come to on that day of punishment, from before that in the world, "Indeed the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth." The wretched ones swore, when they witnessed the calamity and the punishment descended upon them, that the messengers of Allah who came to them with warning and conveyed to them the message from Allah had indeed advised them and told them the truth from Allah, but that was when belief would no longer benefit them. And the abundance of talk and speculation does not save them from the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment.

* *

Those who engage in ta'wil said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

14769 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Those who had forgotten it before will say, 'The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.'" As for "those who had forgotten it," they abandoned it; so when they saw what their prophets had promised them, they became certain and said: "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth."

14770 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Those who had forgotten it will say," he said: they turned away from it.

14771 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then do we have any intercessors who will intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we may do other than what we used to do?﴾ [Surah Al-A'raf: 53]. They have lost their souls, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them.

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, about these polytheists whose description He has given: that when the wrath of Allah descends upon them, and they arrive at His painful punishment, and witness the interpretation of what the messengers of Allah had promised them, they will say: "Do we have any friends or allies today who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that their intercession saves us from what has befallen us of the evil of our deeds in the world?" [See the explanation of "intercession" above: 11:547, note 1, and the references there.] "Or could we be returned to the world once more, so that we may act there in a way that pleases Him and wins back His favour from ourselves?" ["A'taba min nafsihi" means he gave him the reproach-reconciliation, i.e. satisfaction, and returned to being pleased.] The wretched ones said this word there, because they had in the world taken for themselves intercessors who would intercede for them in their needs, so they recall that at a time when they have neither friendship nor intercession.

Allah, may His praise be great and His names be sanctified, says: "They have lost their souls" [See the explanation of "loss" above: p. 357, note 3, and the references there], meaning: they were defrauded of their portion, by selling what has no worth — the everlasting bliss of the Hereafter — for the base, perishing goods of this world. "And what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them," meaning: they were delivered over to the punishment of Allah, and their allies who were worshipped besides Allah went astray from them, and they had claimed falsely and fabrication that those were their lords besides Allah. [See the explanation of "fabrication" above: p. 408, note 2, and the references there.]

14772 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: "They have lost their souls," he said: they sold them for loss.

* *

As for His saying "or could we be returned" being raised rather than put in the accusative as a conjunction with "so that they may intercede for us," this is because the meaning is: "Do we have any intercessors who will intercede for us?" or "could we be returned, so that we may do other than what we used to do?" And it is not intended as a conjunction with His saying "so that they may intercede for us."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 54:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [each] seeking the other rapidly﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Indeed, your master and the one who sets your affairs right, O people, is the one worthy of worship, to whom all worship is due [[See the explanation of "al-Rabb" (the Lord) above, 1:142–143 / 12:286.]], "who created the heavens and the earth in six days," and these are Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, as follows:

14773 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid, who said: The beginning of creation was the Throne, the water, and the wind; the earth was created from the water; and the beginning of creation was on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and the creation was completed on Friday; and the Jews adopted Judaism on Saturday. And one day of the six days is like a thousand years of what you count.

* *

"Then He established Himself above the Throne."

* *

We have already mentioned the meaning of "istiwa'" (establishing/settling) and the differences of people concerning it, earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary [[See the explanation of "al-istiwa'" above, 1:428–431.]].

* *

As for His saying: "He covers the night with the day, [each] seeking the other rapidly," He means: He brings the night over the day and clothes it with it, until its freshness and light are gone [[See the explanation of "al-ghashawa" (covering) above, 1:265–266.]] — "seeking it": He means the night seeks the day — "rapidly," meaning: swiftly.

* *

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

14774 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "seeking it rapidly," he said: swiftly.

14775 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "He covers the night with the day, seeking it rapidly," he said: He covers the night over the day with its light, and it seeks it swiftly until it overtakes it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars [are] subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (54).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, and the sun, the moon, and the stars, all by His command. He commanded them and they obeyed His command. Unquestionably, to Allah belongs all creation and the command that is not opposed and not refused, apart from everything else, and apart from what the polytheists worshipped of gods and idols that neither harm nor benefit, neither create nor command. Blessed is Allah, our Worshipped One, to whom all worship is due, Lord of the worlds [[See the explanation of "tabaraka" (blessed) above, p. 238, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "Rabb" above, p. 482, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-'alamin" in the language indexes above (under "'alima").]].

14776 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Ansari narrated to me, from 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Shami, from his father, who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Whoever does not praise Allah for the good deed he has done, and praises himself, his gratitude becomes little and his deed is nullified. And whoever claims that Allah has given His servants some of the command, has disbelieved in what Allah revealed to His prophets, based on His saying: "Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds." [[The report 14776: "'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Ansari" — this is how it appears here in the manuscript and the printed edition, and this is how Hafiz Ibn Hajar transmitted it from this place in the tafsir in the biography of (Abu 'Abd al-'Aziz) in al-Isaba, and Ibn Kathir transmitted it so in his tafsir, 3:489.

But what the biographical works agree on, and the other chains that Hafiz Ibn Hajar transmitted in another place in al-Isaba, is that he is: "'Abd al-Ghafur ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz," and his kunya is given as "Abu al-Sabah," and he is attributed as "al-Wasiti." He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 4:43–44, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/55, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:142. He is weak and his hadith is rejected; al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Du'afa'.

His father is "'Abd al-'Aziz al-Shami," and I found no mention of him except within these chains.

His father who had companionship is said to be named "Sa'id al-Shami," and he is biographed under this name in al-Isaba, with the kunya "Abu 'Abd al-'Aziz," and he is also biographed in the chapter of kunyas in al-Isaba, and in Usd al-Ghaba 5:247.

This report was transmitted by Hafiz Ibn Hajar in both places of the biographies of "Abu 'Abd al-'Aziz" and "Sa'id," and by Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghaba 5:247, Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 3:489, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:92.

It is a weak report with a lost chain. As for "Baqiyya ibn al-Walid," Ibn al-Mubarak said: "He was truthful, but he would write from whoever came and went." Ahmad said: "If he narrates from people who are not known, do not accept him." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He would narrate from the weak a hundred hadiths before he narrated from the trustworthy." Abu Zur'a said: "Baqiyya is astonishing! If he narrates from the trustworthy, he is trustworthy." He mentioned the statement of Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned above, then said: "Ibn al-Mubarak was right." Then he said: "This applies to the trustworthy; but as for the unknown, he narrates from people who are not known and not precisely verified."]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, Verse 55:

Discussion of the ta'wil (interpretation) of His words: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.﴾ (7:55)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: O people, call upon your Lord alone, sincerely devoting your supplication to Him, apart from what you call upon besides Him of gods and idols. "Humbly" means in humility and submission to His obedience. [See the explanation of "tadarru'" (humbility) earlier, 11:355, 414.] "And secretly" means with the humility of your hearts and the sincerity of your certainty in His oneness, between you and Him, not openly and ostentatiously, while your hearts are not certain of His oneness and lordship, as the people of hypocrisy and deception toward Allah and His Messenger do. [See the explanation of "khufyah" (secretly) earlier, 11:414.] As follows:

14777 - He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: A man would have gathered the Qur'an while his neighbor did not perceive it. A man would have understood much jurisprudence while people did not perceive it. A man would pray a long prayer in his house while visitors were with him, and they would not perceive it. We have indeed known people who had no deed on earth that they could do in secret which would become public, ever! The Muslims used to strive in supplication, and no voice of theirs was heard, except a whisper between them and their Lord. That is because Allah says: "Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly." And Allah mentioned a righteous servant and approved of his action, saying: ﴿When he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾ (19:3).

14778 - He related to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Jarir related to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was on a campaign, [This campaign was the Battle of Khaybar.] and they ascended a valley, shouting takbir and tahlil and raising their voices. He said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves; you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent! You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and near, and He is with you." [The report 14778: al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih (al-Fath 7:363), and Muslim in his Sahih 17:25 by this route, in full.

His words "be gentle with yourselves" mean: be kind to yourselves and lower your voices. In the manuscript it reads "All-Hearing, near, I am with you," without dots, and I have adopted what is in the two Sahihs. In the printed edition, what is in the manuscript was omitted, and it did not add the "He is" that I have added.]

14779 - He related to us al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly," he said: "Secretly."

* *

As for His words: "Indeed, He does not like transgressors," their meaning is: Indeed your Lord does not like those who transgress, exceeding the limit He set for His servants in their supplication and in their asking of their Lord, and raising their voices beyond the limit He set for them in calling upon Him and asking Him, and in other matters. [See the explanation of "i'tida'" (transgression) in the earlier language indexes under (ʿ-d-w).] As follows:

14780 - He related to me Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, who said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from 'Alqamah, from Abu Mijlaz regarding: "Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like transgressors," he said: "Not asking for the ranks of the Prophets, peace be upon them."

14781 - He related to me al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed, He does not like transgressors," in supplication or otherwise. Ibn Jurayj said: Indeed, among supplication is transgression: raising the voice, shouting and yelling in supplication is disliked, and humility and submission are commanded.

**Commentary on the words of God (Qur'an 7:56):** *"And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order, and call upon Him in fear and in hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good."*

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning of His words, "And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order," is: do not associate partners with Allah on the earth, and do not disobey Him in it. That is the corruption in it.

* *

We have already mentioned the narrations on this in what preceded, and explained its meaning with its evidences. [[See the explanation of "corruption on the earth" earlier, 1:287, 416, and other places, the last of which is 10:461, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

As for "after it has been set in order," it means: after Allah has set it in order for the people of His obedience, by sending among them messengers as callers to the truth and by clarifying His proofs to them. [[See the explanation of "setting in order" (işlah) in the language indexes earlier, under the root ṣ-l-ḥ.]]

As for "and call upon Him in fear and in hope," it means: devote your supplication and your deeds sincerely to Him, and do not associate with Him in your deeds anything other than Him, whether gods, idols or other things. Let whatever comes from you in this be out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. Whoever calls upon Him in other than this manner is among the deniers in the Hereafter, because one who does not fear the punishment of Allah and does not hope for His reward does not care what he commits of matters that displease Allah and that He does not approve of.

As for "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good," His words mean: the reward of Allah which He has promised to the doers of good for their goodness in this world is near to them, and that is His mercy. [[See the explanation of "mercy" (raḥma) in the language indexes earlier, under the root r-ḥ-m, and the explanation of "goodness" (iḥsān) earlier, under the root ḥ-s-n.]] For between them and their arrival at that, through His mercy and what He has prepared for them of honor, there is nothing but the separation of their souls from their bodies.

* *

For this reason of meaning, the word "near" (qarīb) is given the masculine form, though it is a predicate of "mercy" (raḥma), which is feminine. This is because what is intended is nearness in time, not nearness of kinship. When times are used in this sense as predicates of nouns, the Arabs treat them as adverbs of state: they keep them in the singular form with the singular, dual and plural alike, and they use the masculine form with the feminine. They say: "The honor of Allah is far from so-and-so" and "She is near to so-and-so," just as they say: "Hind is near to us," "The two Hinds are near to us," and "The Hinds are near to us," because the meaning is: she is in a place near to us. When they omit the place and make "near" a substitute for it, they make it masculine and singular even in the plural, just as the place was masculine and singular in the plural. But when they make it feminine, they give it the dual form with the dual and the plural form with the plural, saying: "She is near to us," and "The two of them are near to us [feminine dual]," as ʿUrwa [ibn al-Ward] said: [[This is how it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition, but the correct attribution is ʿUrwa ibn Ḥizām, as you will see in the sourcing. It seems to be a slip and an addition by the copyist, for Abu Ja'far followed al-Farra' in all of this in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, and al-Farra' mentioned only "ʿUrwa," so the copyist mistakenly added "ibn al-Ward."]]

*"In the evening, when ʿAfrāʾ is not near to you, and she draws close, nor is ʿAfrāʾ far from you…"*

[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', 1:381, as cited by Abu Ja'far, who quotes him. The verse is in the Diwan of ʿUrwa ibn Ḥizām, and in Tazyin al-Aswaq 1:84, and al-Bakri in his commentary on al-Amali: 401, from his poetry; the correct recitation with the letter bāʾ is: "In the evening, when ʿAfrāʾ is not far from you, and she forgets, nor is ʿAfrāʾ near to you…"

*"And indeed, a numbness overcomes me at the remembrance of you, a spell whose crawling is between my skin and my bones."*]]

So he made "near" (qarība) feminine, and "far" (baʿīd) masculine, as I described. If "near" (qarīb) were from "kinship" (qarāba) in lineage, it would only be feminine with a feminine noun and plural with a plural. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:381, and Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu ʿUbayda 1:216, 217.]]

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: "Near" (qarīb), which is a qualifier of "mercy," is masculine, like the Arabs' saying: "a violent wind" (rīḥ kharīq), "a new cloak" (mulḥafa jadīd), and "a sheep of six years" (shāt sadīs). [["Rīḥ kharīq" means violent, and it was said: gentle and easy. The opposite.]] He said: And if you wish, you may say: the interpretation of "mercy" here is rain and the like, and therefore it is masculine, as He said: ﴿And if a group of you believed﴾ [Qur'an 7:87], so He made it masculine, because He meant people. And if you wish, you may treat it like some feminine nouns that they use in the masculine, as the poet said: [[ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn al-Ṭāʾī.]]

*"Nor a land that has sprouted green after its sprouting…"*

[[This verse and its sourcing have passed earlier, 1:432, and I forgot to mention there that it will come again in this place of the commentary, and then in 18:118 (Bulaq). Its first half is: "Nor a cloud that has poured forth its rain…"]]

* *

Some of the people of Arabic language have rejected this view and held that if it is permissible to make "near" (qarīb) masculine by directing "mercy" to the sense of rain, then it would follow that one may say: "Hind stood up" (hind qāma), directing "Hind," a woman, to the sense of "a person."
