14816. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Abu Musa said: "I came to the land of Thamud and measured the watering-place of the she-camel, and I found it to be sixty cubits."

14817. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar; and Ismail ibn Umayyah informed me of something similar, meaning similar to the narration of Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by the grave of Abu Righal. They said: "And who was Abu Righal?" He said: "He was Abu Thaqif. He was in the Sanctuary (al-haram) when Allah destroyed his people. The sanctuary of Allah protected him from the punishment of Allah. But when he left it, he was struck by what struck his people, and he was buried here, and a golden branch was buried with him." He said: "So the people rushed toward it, searching for it, until they extracted that branch."

= And al-Hasan said: "The she-camel had a day for them and they had a day, so it harmed them." [[The report: 14823. This is another chain for the report no. 14818. As for the last statement of al-Hasan al-Basri, I do not know who said it.]]

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by al-Hijr, he said: "Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, lest there befall you what befell them!" Then he said: "This is the Valley of al-Nafar!" ["The Valley of al-Nafar" apparently means the nine men of Thamud who used to spread corruption in the land and not reform, and who conspired together to kill Salih (peace be upon him), so Allah destroyed them.] Then he covered his head and hastened his pace until he crossed the valley. [[The report: 14823. This report of al-Zuhri was transmitted by al-Bukhari in several places in his Sahih (al-Fath 6:270) by way of Muhammad ibn Muqatil, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, from his father Abd Allah ibn Umar. Then he transmitted it again by way of Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar. Then he transmitted it (al-Fath 8:95) by way of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar.
Muslim also transmitted it in his Sahih (18:111) by way of Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar.
Neither of their narrations mentions "the Valley of al-Nafar."
In the manuscript and the printed edition it read: "then he raised his head," which is undoubtedly a distortion; the correct reading is what I have established from the narration of al-Bukhari (al-Fath 8:95). "Qanna'a ra'sahu" means he covered it with a qina' (a head covering). In the other narration of al-Bukhari (al-Fath 6:270): "then he covered himself with his cloak while he was on the mount."
As for his words "ajaza al-wadi," they mean he crossed it and left it behind him.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾, He means: Do not touch the she-camel of Allah by hamstringing her or slaughtering her = ﴿lest a painful punishment seize you﴾, meaning: painful. [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) earlier: 11:370, note 1, and the references there.]] [[See the explanation of "alim" (painful) earlier in the language indexes (root alif-lam-mim).]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 74:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of ʿĀd and settled you in the land, taking for yourselves palaces in its plains and carving out the mountains as houses. So remember the bounties of Allah, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾ (7:74).

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah, mentioning the words of Ṣāliḥ to his people as an admonisher to them, says: "Remember, O people, the favour of Allah upon you," ﴿when He made you successors﴾, meaning: you succeed ʿĀd in the land after their destruction.

* *

"Khulafāʾ" is the plural of "khalīfa." The plural "khulafāʾ" (successors) is the form of "faʿlāʾ," which is normally the plural of "faʿīl," as "shuraka̓" (partners) is the plural of "sharīk," "ʿulamāʾ" (scholars) is the plural of "ʿalīm," and "ḥulamāʾ" (forbearing ones) is the plural of "ḥalīm." This is because the "khalīfa" was treated as referring to a man, so that its singular was thought of as "khalīf," and then the plural "khulafāʾ" was formed. But if "khalīfa" were pluralized as a counterpart to "karīma," "ḥalīla," and "raghība," it would be said "khalāʾif," as one says "karāʾim," "ḥalāʾil," and "raghāʾib," since these are attributes of females. "Khalīfa" was pluralized in both of the two ways that the Qur'an came with, because it was pluralized once according to its wording and once according to its meaning. [[See the explanation of "khalīfa" above, 1:449–453 / 12:288, 505, and what is not mentioned there is completed here.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and settled you in the land﴾, He means: He lodged you in the land, and made for you therein dwellings and mates. [[See the explanation of "bawwa'a" above, p. 4:164.]] ﴿Taking for yourselves palaces in its plains and carving out the mountains as houses﴾: he mentions that they used to hew out the rock as dwellings, as:

14823 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿and carving out the mountains as houses﴾: they used to hollow out houses in the mountains.

* *

His saying: ﴿So remember the bounties of Allah﴾ means: remember the favour of Allah which He has bestowed upon you. [[See the explanation of "al-ālāʾ" above, p. 506. In the printed edition it read "allatī anʿamahā," and I have kept what is in the manuscript; I do not know why the editor altered such a thing.]] ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾.

* *

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

14824 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾: he said, do not travel on the earth causing mischief.

* *

I have already explained the meaning of this with its evidences and the disagreement of those who differ concerning it, in what has passed, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See the explanation of "ʿathā" above, 2:123–124 / 5:499, and the explanation of "corruption on the earth" above, p. 487, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 75–76:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?" They said: "Indeed we are believers in that with which he has been sent."﴾ (75) ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed we are disbelievers in that which you believe in."﴾ (76)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said﴾, he means: the group of those among the people of Salih who were arrogant toward following Salih and believing in God and in him [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the chiefs, the notables) above: 5:291 / 12:499, 503.

And the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) above: 11:540 / 12:421, 467.]] = ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾, meaning: to the lowly among the followers of Salih and the believers in him from among them, apart from their people of rank and nobility = ﴿Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?﴾, sent by God to us and to you. Those among the lowly who believed in Salih said: Indeed we are believers in what God sent Salih with of truth and guidance, meaning: we confirm and acknowledge that it is from God, and that God commanded it, and that Salih called us to it on the command of God = ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾, on the command of God and the command of His messenger Salih = ﴿Indeed we﴾, O people (﴿in that which you believed in﴾), meaning: you affirmed in it, from the prophethood of Salih, and that what he brought is truth from God = ﴿are disbelievers﴾, meaning: we are deniers and rejecters, we do not affirm it nor acknowledge it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 75–76:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?" They said: "Indeed we are believers in that with which he has been sent."﴾ (75) ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed we are disbelievers in that which you believe in."﴾ (76)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said﴾, he means: the group of those among the people of Salih who were arrogant toward following Salih and believing in God and in him [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the chiefs, the notables) above: 5:291 / 12:499, 503.

And the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) above: 11:540 / 12:421, 467.]] = ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾, meaning: to the lowly among the followers of Salih and the believers in him from among them, apart from their people of rank and nobility = ﴿Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?﴾, sent by God to us and to you. Those among the lowly who believed in Salih said: Indeed we are believers in what God sent Salih with of truth and guidance, meaning: we confirm and acknowledge that it is from God, and that God commanded it, and that Salih called us to it on the command of God = ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾, on the command of God and the command of His messenger Salih = ﴿Indeed we﴾, O people (﴿in that which you believed in﴾), meaning: you affirmed in it, from the prophethood of Salih, and that what he brought is truth from God = ﴿are disbelievers﴾, meaning: we are deniers and rejecters, we do not affirm it nor acknowledge it.

The commentary on His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ (7:77)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Thamud hamstrung the she-camel that God had made for them as a sign= ﴿and defied the command of their Lord﴾, meaning: they were arrogant and tyrannical, refusing to follow God, and exalted themselves above the truth, as follows:

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿wa-'taw﴾ (and defied), "they rose up against the truth, [and] did not see [it]." [[In the printed edition: "they do not see it," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

14825: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿'Ataw 'an amri rabbihim﴾, "they rose up in falsehood."

14826: Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿and defied the command of their Lord﴾, he said: "They defied in falsehood and abandoned the truth."

14827: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: ﴿and defied the command of their Lord﴾, he said: "They rose up in falsehood."

* *

This derives from their saying: "a tyrannical rebel (jabbar 'at)," when he is haughty in his tyranny.

* *

= ﴿and said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with"﴾, meaning: they said: "Bring us, O Salih, what you threaten us with of God's punishment and vengeance," hastening the punishment= ﴿if you are indeed one of the messengers﴾, meaning: if you are truly a messenger of God to us, for God gives victory to His messengers over their enemies, so let that come upon them quickly as they hastened it, Exalted is His praise, says: ﴿So the quake seized them, and they awoke in their homes lying prostrate﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 78:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes in the morning﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The earthquake seized those who hamstrung the she-camel from Thamud, ﴿the earthquake﴾, which is the Cry.

* *

And "al-rajfah" (the earthquake), the form "fa'lah" (intensive noun), comes from the saying of the speaker: "rajafa bi-fulan kadhā yarjufu rajfan" (he shook so-and-so with such-and-such), which is when he shakes and unsettles him, as al-Akhtal said:

"When the white hair of age makes me yearn for youth, I tremble like the eagle, while man is broken down."[[His Diwan: 146, from a fine qasida of his which he composed in praise of Yazid ibn Mu'awiya, in which he mentioned youth in a wondrous manner, having seen the coquettes turn away from him because of it. He says after it:

Perhaps youth for me is in a station one day, and the swaying, tender-waisted women lead me on.

O how little good the coquettes are; how they turned away from him! His drink is a trickle, and among them a scant pouring.

They turned away from a grey-haired man whose head showed white; from him, when they saw him, they shrink back.

They used to know from me a fine smile and a parting of hair the clusters of curls had uncovered.

So they still take from me some acquaintance, and they show affection, neither stingy nor generous.

My covenant was new, then it was made worthless, and a covenant that is followed by what is in it, is to be recited.

They say: You are no husband to be led, nor is the youth that has passed returned.

Is there a return for the youth that has passed? Or is there a cure that restores the white hair?

The white hair will not return to youths, and they will not find the equal of youth, as long as the branch puts forth leaves.

Indeed youth is praised for its brightness, while white hair is turned away from and repelled.

These are verses filled with feeling, sorrow and regret, so memorize them.]] What is meant by "al-rajfah" here is the Cry that shook and stirred them to destruction, because Thamud perished by the Cry, as the people of knowledge have mentioned.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation said.

Those who said that:

14828 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: "al-rajfah", he said: the Cry.

14829 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

14830 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, and it is the Cry.

14831 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, from Mujahid: ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, he said: the Cry.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and they became prostrate in their homes in the morning﴾, means: those whom God destroyed from Thamud became in the morning ﴿in their homes﴾, meaning in their land in which they perished, and their town.

* *

For this reason he used the singular "dar" (home) and did not pluralize it, saying "fi duurihim" (in their homes). It is permissible that it was meant to be the plural "dur", but the singular was applied to the whole collectively, as it is said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr: 1-2].

* *

And His saying: ﴿jathimin﴾ (prostrate) means: fallen, struck down, not moving, because there were no spirits in them, having perished. The Arabs say of one who crouches on his knee: "jathim", and from it is the saying of Jarir:

"I recognized the trench, and I recognized from it the pot-supports like the crouching black stones."

[[His Diwan: 507, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 218, from his qasida in praise of Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik, of which a line has passed previously 1: 170.

He says before it: "I stood at the abodes, and what we mentioned of them is like a dwelling between Talah and al-Nazim."

And "al-muntana" is the shallow trench around the tent. "Mataya al-qidr" are its hearth-stones, the pot rests on them so they are its mount. And he likened them to the crouching black stones, because of their blackness from the soot of the fire.

In the manuscript it read: "'arafat al-sa'a", unpointed, and an error; its correct form is what is in the printed edition.]]

* *

And in accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation said.

Those who said that:

14832 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and they became prostrate in their homes in the morning﴾, he said: dead.

The discourse on His words: ﴿So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisers."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Salih turned away from them when they sought to hasten the punishment and hamstrung the she-camel of God, departing from their land and leaving them in their midst. [[See the explanation of "tawalla" (turned away) above, 10:575, note 1, and the references there.]] This was because God, may He be exalted and remembered, had revealed to him: "I will destroy them after three [days]." [[In the printed edition: "after three" (ba'da thalatha); the correct reading, beyond doubt, is what I have recorded from the manuscript.]]

It has been said: No nation perished while its prophet was still among it. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the Meanings of the Qur'an), 1:385.]]

So God, may His praise be exalted, informs of Salih's departure from among his people, who had transgressed against their Lord, when God wished to bring His punishment upon them. He says: ﴿So he turned away from them﴾ — Salih — ﴿and said﴾ to his people, Thamud: ﴿"I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord"﴾, and I have delivered to you what my Lord commanded me to deliver to you of His command and prohibition. [[See the explanation of "al-iblagh" (conveying) above: 10:575; 11:95; 12:504.]] ﴿"And advised you"﴾, in delivering the message of God to you, warning you of His might, since you persisted in your disbelief in Him and your worship of idols. ﴿"But you do not like advisers"﴾, those who counsel you concerning God, who forbid you to follow your desires and who turn you away from the lusts of your souls.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 80:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an abomination such as no one in all the worlds has committed before you?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And indeed We sent Lot."

* *

If it were said that its meaning is: "And mention Lot, O Muhammad, ﴿when he said to his people﴾," it would be a valid view, since there is no connecting word in the speech as there is in the mention of ʿAd and Thamud [i.e., the word "sent" is not present in the phrasing as it is for them].

* *

As for His words ﴿when he said to his people﴾, meaning: when he said to his people of Sodom, to whom Lot had been sent: ﴿"Do you commit the abomination?"﴾ Their abomination, for which God punished them, was their practice of approaching males [[See the explanation of "al-fahisha" above: p. 402, note 2, and the references there.]], ﴿"such as no one in all the worlds has committed before you"﴾, meaning: no one among the worlds has preceded you in committing this abomination. This is like what was reported:

14833 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, regarding His words ﴿"such as no one in all the worlds has committed before you"﴾, he said: "A male was never seen mounting a male until the people of Lot."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 81:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed limits.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His mention, informs about Lut (Lot), that he said to his people, rebuking them for their deed: "Indeed you, O people, approach men in their backsides out of your own desire for that, instead of what Allah has permitted and made lawful for you of women." ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed limits﴾ means: indeed you are a people who commit what Allah has forbidden you, and disobey Him by this deed of yours.

* *

That is the "israf" (exceeding limits) in this context. [[See the explanation of "israf" previously, p. 395, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And "shahwa" (desire) is a "fa'la" form, a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I desired this thing, I desire it, desire (shahwa)." From this is the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

*A disheveled man who longs for sleep; I said to him: "Set out!" when the stars turned away and stretched out.*

[[The first verse is in al-Lisan (under sh-h-y), and the reading in al-Lisan is "wa-isbakarrat" (and became straight).

And his saying "a disheveled man" means his traveling companion, whose journey lasted long on him, so his head became dusty and his hair scattered from neglecting oil. "The stars stretched out" means they extended, became straight, and hastened in their course. "Isbakarrat" has the same meaning.]]

*He rose dragging the cloak; had his soul been told, "Take it in your two palms!", it would have collapsed.* [["Kharrat" means fell, collapsed, and tumbled. In the printed edition it was "jarrat" with a jim, which is a clear error.]]

This second verse has a similar one in the poetry of al-Akhtal, who said:

*And a fair one, neither weak-hearted nor feeble in strength, we gave drink to when the first sparrows chirped.*

*I held back the cup from him, not slowly, through the night, until it growled at him and he growled back.*

*He rose dragging the cloak; had his soul, with his two palms, been able to ward off the heat of the wine, it would have collapsed.*

*He turned his back; had it been said, "Beware the sword!", his forelock would not have failed to bristle with fear.*

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 82:**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: The answer of the people of Lot to Lot, when he rebuked them for their vile deed and their practice of the foul act that God had forbidden them, was only that some of them said to others: "Expel Lot and his family from your town." This is why it says "expel them" in the plural, although the preceding mention was of Lot alone and not of others.

* *

It is also possible that the plural is meant to signify: "Expel Lot and those who follow his religion from your town." He mentioned only Lot at the beginning of the speech, without mentioning his followers, and then used the plural at the end of the speech, as in His words: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ (al-Talaq: 1).

* *

We have explained similar cases earlier, in a way that makes repeating them here unnecessary. [[See what has preceded, vol. 2, pp. 485–487, and elsewhere.]]

= As for ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, it means: Lot and those who followed him are people who keep themselves clear of what we do, namely having intercourse with men in their backsides. [[On the explanation of "taharrur" (purity/keeping oneself pure), see what has preceded, vol. 10, pp. 318, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said similarly to what we have said on this matter.

**Those who said this:**

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hani' ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "From the backsides of men and the backsides of women." [[The report: 14836 — Hani' ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i, saduq al-hadith (truthful in narration), passed as no. 13159 and 13965.]]

14834 — Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mujahid: ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, from the backsides of men and the backsides of women.

14835 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "They keep themselves pure from the backsides of men and women."

14836 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Imara informed us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "From the backsides of men and from the backsides of women."

14837 — Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "They refrain from sin (yataharrajun)."

14838 — Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, meaning: they found fault with them without a fault, and blamed them without a blame.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 83:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: When the people of Lut refused, despite Lut's rebuking them for the immorality they committed and his conveying to them the message of his Lord prohibiting it to them, they insisted only in their error, so We saved Lut and his family who believed in him, except his wife, for she was unfaithful to Lut and disbelieved in Allah.

* *

As for His words: ﴿among those who remained behind﴾, He means: among those who stayed behind.

* *

It has been said: ﴿among those who remained behind﴾ (al-ghabirin, masculine plural), and He did not say "al-ghabirat" (feminine plural), because it is intended that she was among those who remained with the men. When her mention was joined with the mention of the men, it was said: "among those who remained behind."  [Cf. Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:218, 219.]

* *

The verb from it is ghabara, yaghburu, ghuburan, and ghabran (the last verbal noun is vocalised with a fatha and then a sukun, but it does not appear in any lexicographical work; they mention only the first verbal noun), meaning to remain, as al-A'sha said:

He bit, with what the cattle left him of a maidservant, in the bygone time.

[Diwan: 106; Majaz al-Qur'an 1:219. From his qasida in which he satirised 'Alqamah and praised 'Amir, as I mentioned previously in the takhrij of verses that passed in the qasida. In the printed edition and Majaz al-Qur'an it reads "min ummihi" (from his mother), and I have kept what is in the Diwan. Abu 'Ubaydah said after the verse: "She had not been circumcised in the past, so she remained from the bygone time, i.e., the remaining. Do you not see that he said: 'And they had left from her a harm at the meeting, a complete rear'?" This is an ugly satire on the mother of 'Alqamah.]

And as another said: [He is Yazid ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As al-Thaqafi.]

My father, who conquered the lands with his sword, and humbled them for the Banu Aban of the bygone time.

[Khizanat al-Adab 1:55. Yazid was a noble and honoured man. His father al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As al-Thaqafi was one of the companions of the many conquests in Persia and elsewhere; likewise his paternal uncle 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, companion of the Messenger of Allah. Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi summoned him, appointed him over Fars, and when he came to take his letter of appointment, al-Hajjaj said to him: "O Yazid, recite some of your poetry to me," intending that he recite panegyric for him. He recited a qasida in which he boasted, saying: "My father, who conquered the lands with his sword, and humbled them for the Banu Aban of the bygone time. My father, who seized the white banner of the son of Kisra, fluttering like the eagle that swoops. When I boast, I boast without being a liar, a boast by which I crush the boasting of the boaster." Al-Hajjaj rose angrily, and Yazid left without bidding him farewell. Al-Hajjaj sent his chamberlain after him to retrieve the letter of appointment, saying to him: "Which is better for you, what your father bequeathed you, or this?" Yazid said: "Tell him: I inherited from my grandfather his glory and his deeds, and you inherited from your grandfather goats in al-Ta'if." Then he travelled and joined Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik while he was crown prince, and he took him in and made him among his intimates.

The author of Khizanat al-Adab related "li-bani al-zaman al-ghabir" (to the sons of the bygone time). As for the version of Ja'far, "li-bani Aban," he means his clan and kin, for his grandfather was "Abu al-'As ibn Bishr ibn 'Abd Dahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hammam ibn Aban ibn Yasar al-Thaqafi."

As for his words "My father, who seized the white banner of the son of Kisra," he means his father al-Hakam in the conquest of Fars and Istakhr in the year 23 AH. (See Tarikh al-Tabari 5:6 and Futuh al-Buldan: 393, 394.)]

He means: the remaining.

* *

If someone says: Was Lut's wife among those who were saved from the destruction by which the people of Lut were destroyed?

It is said: No, rather she was among those who perished.

If he says: How then is it said: ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾, when you have said that the meaning of "al-ghabir" is "the remaining"? It would then be necessary that she had remained?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have supposed. He only means by it: except his wife, she was among those who remained before the destruction, and the long-lived who had been overtaken by a great age and passed through a long time, until she became aged among the aged people, so she was among those who had remained a long age before the destruction of the people, and she perished with those of the people of Lut who perished when the punishment came upon them.

* *

It has also been said: The meaning of that is: among those who remained in the punishment of Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

14839 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara: 171; Surah al-Saffat: 135], in the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 84:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We rained down upon them a rain [of stones]. So see how was the end of the criminals﴾ (7:84).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We rained down upon the people of Lut, who denied Lut and did not believe in him, a rain of stones of sijjil with which We destroyed them. ﴿So see how was the end of the criminals﴾. He, majestic is His praise, says: So look, O Muhammad, at the end of these who denied Allah and His Messenger from the people of Lut, who committed the sins of Allah, indulged in obscenities, and made lawful what Allah had forbidden of men's backsides. How was it? And to what did it come? Was it anything other than ruin and destruction? Indeed, that, or its like, is the punishment that will be the end of those among your people who deny you and are arrogant toward faith in Allah and in your truthfulness, if they do not repent.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And to Midian We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you a clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive the people of their due, and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. That is best for you, if you are believers."﴾ (85)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted mention says: And We sent to the offspring of Midian. "Midian" refers to his descendants, Madyan ibn Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful. [[In the printed edition: "Madyan ibn Ibrahim." I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 159.]] As related:

14840 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq.

* *

If the matter is as he said, then "Midian" is a tribe like Tamim.

Ibn Ishaq also claimed that Shu'ayb, whom Allah mentioned that He sent to them, was from the offspring of this Midian, and that he was "Shu'ayb ibn Mikil ibn Yashjur." He said: His name in Syriac was "Bathrun." [[(2) In the manuscript: "Yathrub," without dots, with a ba. These are names I cannot now vocalize with certainty; see Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 167, and al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya 1: 185.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, according to what Ibn Ishaq said, is: And We had certainly sent to the offspring of Midian their brother Shu'ayb ibn Mikil, calling them to obey Allah, to desist at His command, and to abandon striving on the earth in corruption and turning away from His path. So Shu'ayb said to them: "O my people, worship Allah alone, with no partner. You have no god who deserves worship from you other than the God who created you, and in whose hand is your benefit and harm." ﴿There has certainly come to you a clear evidence from your Lord﴾, meaning: There has certainly come to you a sign and a proof from Allah of the reality of what I say and the truth of what I call you to. [[See the explanation of "bayyinah" in the earlier language indexes under (b-y-n).]] ﴿So give full measure and weight﴾, meaning: complete for the people their rights by the measure with which you measure, and by the weight with which you weigh. [[See the explanation of "giving full measure and weight" earlier, p. 224.]] ﴿And do not deprive the people of their due﴾, meaning: do not wrong the people in their rights, and do not diminish them.  [[See the explanation of "bakhs" earlier, 6: 56.]]

From this is their saying: "You consider her foolish, while she is deceitful" (bakhisah), meaning: unjust. [[This is a proverb. See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 83, 219; Amthal al-Maydani 1: 108; Jamharat al-Amthal: 68; and Lisan (b-kh-s). Their narration is: "wa-hiya bakhis," meaning: possessing bakhs, in the relative form. It is cited of one who feigns foolishness while having cunning. This is because a man of the Anbar clan of Amr ibn Tamim spoke with a woman and considered her foolish, unable to understand or to guard her wealth. He said to her: "Shall I not mix my wealth with yours?" He meant to mix them and then divide them, taking the good and leaving her the bad. When he did so and came to divide, she disputed with him, and he could not get free of her until he ransomed himself with what she wanted. When he was rebuked for deceiving the woman because of her weakness, he said: "You consider her foolish, while she is deceitful."]] Also the words of Allah: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 20], meaning by it: inferior.

* *

Those of the interpreters said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

14841 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not deprive the people of their due﴾, he said: do not wrong the people in their things.

14842 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And do not deprive the people of their due﴾, he said: do not wrong the people in their things.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾, meaning: do not work on Allah's earth with His disobedience, and with what you used to do before Allah sent His Prophet to you, of worshipping other than Allah, associating partners with Him, and depriving the people in measure and weight. [[See the explanation of "corruption on the earth" earlier, p. 542, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿After its reformation﴾, meaning: after Allah has reformed the earth by the sending of the Prophet ﷺ among you, forbidding you from what is not lawful for you and what Allah dislikes for you. [[See the explanation of "reformation" (islah) earlier under (s-l-h) in the language indexes.]] ﴿That is best for you﴾, meaning: this which I have mentioned to you and commanded you with, of sincerely worshipping Allah alone with no partner, giving people their rights in measure and weight, and abandoning corruption on the earth, is better for you in the immediate affairs of your worldly life and in the outcome of your Hereafter with Allah on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿If you are believers﴾, meaning: if you are truthful in what I say to you, and in conveying to you from Allah His command and His prohibition.

**Commentary on:** ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening [the believers] and turning away from the way of God those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He multiplied you. And look at how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ (7:86)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening﴾, he means: do not sit on every road, which is the *sirat* (path), threatening the believers with killing. [[See the explanation of *sirat* above, vol. 1, pp. 170–177, and then the language indexes under the root (s-r-t).]]

* *

It was reported that they used to sit on the road of anyone who intended to go to Shu'ayb and wanted to believe in him, and they would threaten and frighten him, saying, "He is a liar!"

Mention of those who said this:

14843 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿every path you threaten﴾: He said: They used to threaten whoever came to Shu'ayb and visited him, wanting to embrace Islam.

14844 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening﴾. The *sirat* is the road; they would frighten people from going to Shu'ayb.

14845 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening and turning away from the way of God﴾. He said: They used to sit on the road and inform whoever passed by them that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was a liar, so do not let him tempt you away from your religion.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿every path﴾, he said: road. ﴿You threaten﴾: every true way. [[In the printed edition, the phrase "he said: road" was omitted, and the rest of the sentence was altered to read "you threaten every true way," which badly corrupts the meaning! The correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

14846 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

14847 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening﴾: They used to sit on every road threatening the believers.

14848 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Qays, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening﴾: He said: the tax collectors.

'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Abu Hurayrah or someone else (Abu Ja'far al-Razi was uncertain), who said: The Prophet ﷺ came on the night of the Night Journey (*isra'*) to a piece of wood on the road; no garment passed by it without being torn, and nothing without being ripped. He said: "What is this, O Gabriel?" He said: "This is the likeness of people from your community who sit on the road and cut it off!" Then he recited: ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening and turning away﴾. [[The report 14853: this is an abridgement of a long report which Abu Ja'far will narrate with this same chain in his commentary on Surat al-Isra' (vol. 15, p. 6, Bulaq edition), where its takhrij will be given.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Abu al-'Aliyah are all trustworthy narrators (*thiqat*), and they have all appeared in various places.

Al-Haythami mentioned this report at length in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* (1:67–72) and said: "al-Bazzar narrated it and its narrators are reliable, except that al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, 'from Abu al-'Aliyah or someone else,' so its follower is unknown."

However, the wording of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) here and there indicates that Abu Ja'far al-Razi was uncertain whether it was from Abu Hurayrah or from another Companion, so perhaps what is in al-Bazzar's narration differs from what is in Abu Ja'far al-Tabari's narration.

al-Suyuti takhrij it at length in *al-Durr al-Manthur* (4:144) and attributed it to al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in *Kitab al-Salah*, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il*.]]

* *

This report which we have mentioned from Abu Hurayrah indicates that its meaning, according to Abu Hurayrah, was that the Prophet of God Shu'ayb only forbade his people, by his saying ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening﴾, from cutting the road, and that they were highwaymen.

* *

It has been said: ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening﴾. Had it been said outside the Qur'an, "Do not sit on every path," it would have been permissible and eloquent in speech. This is permissible because the road is not a specific known place, so it is allowed, just as it is permissible to say, "He sat for him in such-and-such a place, and on such-and-such a place, and in such-and-such a place."

* *

He said: ﴿threatening﴾, and did not say "*ta'idun*," because the Arabs do this with threats when they leave them vague and do not state them clearly. They say "*awadtuhu*" with an alif (*awadtuhu*, "I threatened him"), and "a threat was made by me against him" (*taqaddama minni ilayhi wa'id*). But when they specify what they threatened and state it clearly, they say "*wa'adtuhu khayran*" ("I promised him good") and "*wa'adtuhu sharran*" ("I promised him evil"), without an alif, just as His, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿The Fire God has promised it to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surat al-Hajj: 72].

* *

As for His saying ﴿and turning away from the way of God, those who believe in Him﴾, He means: you turn away from the way of God, and that is turning away from faith in God and from acting in obedience to Him. ﴿Those who believe in Him﴾: you turn away from the way of God those who believe in God and affirm His unity. ﴿And seek to make it crooked﴾: you seek, for whoever follows the way of God, believes in Him, and acts in obedience to Him, ﴿crookedness﴾, away from the straight and true path, toward deviation and misguidance. [[See the explanation of *al-sadd* above, p. 448, note 1, and its references there.]] [[See the explanation of *baghy* above, p. 448, note 3, and its references there.]] [[See the explanation of *al-'awaj* (crookedness) above, vol. 7, p. 54 / vol. 12, p. 448.]] As:

14849 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And turning away from the way of God﴾: He said: its people. ﴿And seeking to make it crooked﴾: you seek deviation in it.

14850 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

14851 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾: He said: you seek the way away from the truth, crooked.

14852 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And turning away from the way of God﴾, from Islam; you seek the way ﴿crooked﴾, destruction.

* *

His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and He multiplied you﴾: Shu'ayb reminds them of God's blessing upon them, that He multiplied their community after their number had been few, and that He raised them from humiliation and lowliness. He says to them: give thanks to God who has bestowed this blessing upon you, devote worship to Him alone, guard against His punishment by obedience, and beware of His vengeance by abandoning disobedience. ﴿And look at how was the end of the corrupters﴾: He says: consider what befell those nations before you when they transgressed against their Lord and disobeyed His messengers, of the punishments and vengeances, and how they found the outcome of their disobedience to Him. [[See the explanation of *al-'aqibah* (end, outcome) above, vol. 11, pp. 272–273 / vol. 12, p. 129.]] Did He not destroy some of them by drowning in the flood, some by stoning with stones, and some by the Cry?

* *

The word "*al-ifsad*" (corruption), in this place, means: disobedience to God. [[See the explanation of *al-ifsad* above, p. 556, note 1, and its references there.]]

The interpretation of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And if there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who have not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges﴾ (87).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿And if there is a group among you﴾, meaning: if there is a company among you and a faction [[See the explanation of "ṭā'ifah" above: 6:500 / 9:141 / 12:240.]] = ﴿who have believed﴾, meaning: who have affirmed the truth of that with which I have been sent, namely the sincere worship of Allah, the abandoning of His disobedience, and the refraining from wronging people and from cheating them in measures and weights, and so have followed me in that = ﴿and a group who have not believed﴾, meaning: and another company who did not affirm the truth of that and did not follow me in it = ﴿then be patient until Allah judges between us﴾, meaning: then wait steadfastly for the decisive judgment of Allah between us and you [[See the explanation of "ṣabr" (patience) above: 7:508, commentary note 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "ḥukm" (judgment) above: 9:175, 324, 462 / 11:413.]] = ﴿and He is the best of judges﴾, meaning: Allah is the best to decide and the most just to judge, for there is no inclination toward anyone in His judgment, nor any favoritism toward anyone.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 88:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said: "Even though we are unwilling?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: ﴿The chiefs of those who were arrogant said﴾, meaning by "al-mala'" (the chiefs, the leading group of men) [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" above, p. 542, footnote 2, and the references there.]] — and meaning by "those who were arrogant," those who showed pride against faith in God, and against submitting to His command and following His messenger Shu'ayb, when Shu'ayb warned them of God's punishment, by opposing their Lord's command and disbelieving in Him [[See the explanation of "istakbara" (to be arrogant) above, p. 542, footnote 2, and the references there.]] — ﴿"We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb,﴾ and those who follow you, believe you, and believe in what you have brought with you — ﴿from our town, or you will return to our religion﴾, meaning: you and they will surely return to our religion and to what we are upon [[See the explanation of "al-millah" (religion, creed) above, p. 282, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. Shu'ayb answered them, saying: ﴿"Even though we are unwilling?"﴾

The meaning of the speech is: Shu'ayb said to his people: "Will you expel us from your town, and bar us from the way of God, even though we are unwilling to do that?" Then the interrogative particle "alif" was placed before the conjunction "waw" in "wa-law" (and even if).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 89:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿We have indeed invented a lie against God if we return to your religion after God has rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it unless God, our Lord, wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In God we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders.﴾ (89)

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty says: Shu'ayb said to his people when they called him to return to their religion and enter it, and threatened to expel him and those who followed him from their town if he and they did not do so: ﴿We have indeed invented a lie against God﴾, meaning: we have fabricated a lie against God [[See the explanation of "iftira'" (fabrication) above, p. 481, note 6, and the references there.]] and spoken falsehood about Him, ﴿if we return to your religion﴾, meaning: if we turn back to it after God has rescued us from it by making us see its error and the correct guidance we are upon. ﴿It is not for us to return to it and adopt it as our religion, abandoning the truth we are upon.﴾ ﴿Unless God, our Lord, wills﴾, meaning: unless it has already been decreed in God's knowledge that we would return to it, so that God's decree would then take effect for us and His will would be carried out over us. ﴿Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾, meaning: the knowledge of our Lord encompasses all things and surrounds them, so nothing that has happened is hidden from Him, nor anything that will happen. [[See the explanation of "wasi'a" (encompassed) above, p. 207, note 1, and the references there.]] So if it has been decreed in His knowledge that we would return to your religion, and nothing that has happened or will happen is hidden from Him, then what He has foreknown must come to pass; otherwise we would not return to your religion. [[In the printed edition: "fa-la yakhfa" with a fa', and likewise in the manuscript, which is undotted; the correct reading is with a waw.]]

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said.

Those who said so:

14853. He told me, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said: He told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: He told us, Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿We have indeed invented a lie against God if we return to your religion after God has rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it unless God, our Lord, wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In God we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾: He says: It is not fitting for us to return to your shirk after God has rescued us from it, unless our Lord wills. God does not will shirk, but He says: unless God has known something, for He encompasses all things in knowledge.

* *

As for His words ﴿In God we have put our trust﴾, meaning: in God we rely in our affairs, and to Him we turn for support regarding what you threaten us with of your evil, O people, for He is sufficient for whoever puts his trust in Him. [[See the explanation of "tawakkul" (trust) above, vol. 7: 346; vol. 8: 566; vol. 10: 108, 184.]]

* *

Then, may God's blessings be upon him, he sought refuge with his Lord in supplication against his people, when he had despaired of their success and his hope had been cut off from their submitting to God in obedience and acknowledging His messengership, and he feared for himself and for those of his people who believed and followed him, from their wickedness, destruction and ruin, [[The context: "... bi-al-du'a' 'ala qawmihi ... bi-ta'jil al-niqma" (... by supplication against his people ... hastening the retribution).]] by hastening retribution. So he said: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾, meaning: judge between us and them by Your true judgement, in which there is no injustice, no partiality and no wrong, but is justice and truth. ﴿And You are the best of deciders﴾, meaning: the best of judges. [[See the explanation of "fath" (decision) above, vol. 2: 254; vol. 10: 405.]]

* *

Al-Farra' mentioned that the people of Oman call the judge "al-fatih" and "al-fattah." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', vol. 1: 385.]]

Others among the scholars of the Arabic language mentioned that it is from the dialect of Murad. [[This is Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an, vol. 1: 220-221.]] And he recited, for one of them, a line of verse, which is:

"Ala abligh Bani 'Usmin rasulan ... bi-anni 'an futahatikum ghaniyyun"
(Behold, let me convey to the Banu 'Usm a messenger: that I am independent of your judging.)

[[This line was cited earlier, vol. 2: 254, and I did not attribute it there to this place in Tafsir al-Tabari, so I have now specified it. It should be added that it is in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, vol. 1: 220-221. In the printed edition and the manuscript here it reads "fa-inni 'an fatahatikum," but the correct reading is what appeared earlier and what is in the manuscript there.]]

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of ta'wil have said.

Those who said so:

14854. He told us, Ibn Wakī', who said: He told us, my father, from Mis'ar, from Qatada, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I did not know what His words meant: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾, until I heard the daughter of Dhu Yazan say: "Come, let me decide [fatihak] with you," meaning: let me judge with you.

14855. He told me, al-Muthanna, who said: He told us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, who said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾, that he says: judge between us and our people.

14856. He told me, al-Muthanna, who said: He told us, Ibn Duka'in, who said: He told us, Mis'ar, who said: I heard Qatada say: Ibn 'Abbas said: I did not know what His words meant: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾, until I heard the daughter of Dhu Yazan say: "Come, let me decide with you."

14857. He told us, Bishr ibn Mu'adh, who said: He told us, Yazid, who said: He told us, Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿decide between us and our people with truth﴾, meaning: judge between us and our people with truth.

14858. He told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: He told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr, who said: He told us, Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿decide between us and our people with truth﴾: judge between us and our people with truth.

14859. He told me, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said: He told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: He told us, Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿decide between us﴾: he says, judge between us.

14860. He told us, al-Qasim, who said: He told us, al-Husayn, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Iftah" means "uhkum" (judge) between us and our people. And as for ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [al-Fath: 1], it means: We have given you a clear judgement.

14861. He told us, al-Qasim, who said: He told us, al-Husayn, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "iftah" means "iqdi" (judge).

14862. He told us, Ibn Bashshar, who said: He told us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: He told us, Mis'ar, from Qatada, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I did not know what ﴿decide between us and our people with truth﴾ meant, until I heard the daughter of Dhu Yazan say to her husband: "Go, let me decide with you."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said, "If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you would be losers."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The company of disbelieving men from the people of Shu'ayb said— and they are the "chiefs" [[See the explanation of "al-Mala'" (the chiefs, the notables) above, p. 561, footnote 22, and the references there.]]— those who denied the signs of God and called His Messenger a liar, and persisted in their error, to others among them: "If you follow Shu'ayb in what he says, and respond to what he calls you to, namely the affirmation of God's oneness and submission to His command and prohibition, and you acknowledge his prophethood—"; ﴿indeed you would then be losers﴾, meaning: you would be defrauded in your action, and in abandoning your religion in which you remain, for his religion to which he calls you; and you would be ruined by that action of yours. [[See the explanation of "al-Khasarah" (loss, ruin) above, p. 481, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes﴾ [7:91]

Abu Ja'far said: He means: the earthquake (al-rajfah) seized those among the people of Shu'ayb who disbelieved. I have already explained the meaning of "al-rajfah" earlier, and that it is the tremor that shakes [the earth] as a punishment from God. [[See the explanation of "al-rajfah" above, pp. 544–545.]]

* *

﴿And they became prostrate in their homes﴾, on their knees, dead and destroyed. [[See the explanation of "al-judum" (kneeling or lying prostrate) above, pp. 545–546.]]

* *

The nature of the punishment by which God destroyed them was as follows:

14863. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb﴾ [7:85]: He said: God sent Shu'ayb to Midian and to the companions of al-Aykah. "Al-Aykah" is a thicket of trees. Despite their disbelief, they used to cheat in measure and weight. He called them, but they denied him, and he said to them what God mentions in the Qur'an, and they answered him. When they became insolent and denied him, they asked him for the punishment. God opened for them a gate of Hell, and the heat from it destroyed them; neither shade nor water benefited them. Then He sent a cloud containing a pleasant wind, and they found the coolness and pleasantness of the wind. They called to one another: "The shade! Take shelter in it!" When they gathered beneath the cloud, men, women and children, it closed over them and destroyed them. This is His words: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾ [26:189].

14864. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The account of Shu'ayb and his people was as God mentions in the Qur'an. They were people who cheated people in their measures and weights, while disbelieving in God and denying their prophet. He called them to God and to worshipping Him, and to abandoning wronging people and cheating them in measure and weight. He spoke, giving them sincere advice, and he was truthful: ﴿I do not intend to oppose you by doing what I forbid you from. I only intend reform as far as I am able. My success is only through God; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn back﴾ [11:88]. Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ), according to what was related to me by Ya'qub ibn Abi Salamah, whenever he mentioned Shu'ayb, would say: "That is the orator of the prophets," because of the excellence of his argument with his people concerning what was intended against them. When they denied him and threatened him with stoning and expulsion from their land, and became insolent toward God, the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was a great day's punishment. It reached me that a man from the people of Midian, called Amr ibn Jalha', when he saw it, said:

O my people, Shu'ayb is a messenger, so leave aside
from you Sumayr and Imran ibn Shaddad.

I see a cloud, O my people, that has risen,
calling out with a voice over the hard land of the valley. [[In the printed edition: "I see a cloud" (ghaymah), which is also how it appears in Qisas al-Anbiya', but the manuscript has what I have recorded; "ghabyah" in al-Durr al-Manthur is an error, the correct reading is what I have recorded. "Al-ghabyah" (with a fatha on the ghayn and a sukun on the ba') is a violent burst of rain; it is said to be a light rain that is not heavy. Here he means by it a cloud containing a burst of rain. "Al-samanah" is a hard land with stones beside sand.]]

And indeed you will not see in it the forenoon of tomorrow
except al-Raqim walking between the high grounds. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "And indeed you, if you see" (wa-innakum in tarawa); the correct reading is what I have recorded. In Qisas al-Anbiya': "For he will not see in it"; in al-Durr al-Manthur: "For he does not see." The printed edition has "ma fiha illa al-Raqim ...", an addition that spoils the meter and is not in the manuscript, and is probably a printing error. "Al-anjad" is the plural of "najd," which is elevated land. "Al-duha'" with a fatha on the dad, extended, is like "al-duha" (with a damma on the dad), which is when the day has extended and nearly reached midday. The printed edition has "duha ghad."]]

"Samir" and "Imran" were their priests, and "al-Raqim" was their dog. [[The report: 14869 – al-Durr al-Manthur 3:103; Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi, p. 144.]]

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Abu Sahq," which is an obvious error.]], who said: It reached me, and God knows best, that God sent the heat upon them until it cooked them. Then He produced for them the shade like a black cloud. When they saw it, they rushed toward it, seeking relief from its coolness from the heat they were in. When they entered beneath it, it closed over them, and they all perished, while God saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by His mercy.

14865. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah al-Bajali related to me, saying: "Abu Jad," "Hawwaz," "Hutti," "Kalmun," "Sa'fas," and "Qarasht" are the names of the kings of Midian. Their king at the time of the Day of the Shade, in the time of Shu'ayb, was Kalmun. The sister of Kalmun wept for him, saying:

Kalmun, whose death has broken my pillar,
in the middle of the place of gathering,

the chief of the people, to whom death came as fire
in the midst of the shade.

They were made into fire upon them;
their dwelling became like what is dissolved. [[The report: 14871. I have not found anyone known by the kunyah "Abu 'Abdullah." However, Abu Ja'far narrated a report like this in his history, in the mention of these kings (1:99), with a chain that explains this chain, saying:

"Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl related to us, from Yahya ibn al-'Ala', from al-Qasim ibn Salman, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abjad, Hawwaz, Hutti, Kalman, Sa'fas and Qarasht were tyrannical kings..."

"Yahya ibn al-'Ala' al-Bajali," his kunyah is "Abu Salamah," and it is said "Abu 'Amr." I have not found his kunyah to be "Abu 'Abdullah," but the apparent [sense of] this chain suggests that "Abu 'Abdullah al-Bajali" is himself "Yahya ibn al-'Ala' al-Bajali," and God knows best.

As for "Yahya ibn al-'Ala' al-Bajali," Ahmad said: "A liar who fabricates hadith." He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/297), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/179).

This report was related by al-Baghawi (margin of Ibn Kathir's tafsir, 3:520) and Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi, p. 144, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Bajali, and in both of them it is "Kalman." I have added what is between the brackets from them, but I wrote it as its counterparts are written in the manuscript.

In al-Baghawi it is recorded: "Kalman has broken my pillar," and in Qisas al-Anbiya': "Kalman, I am destroyed in my pillar" [a difficult reading]; I do not know what this is!!]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb—it was as if they had never prospered therein. Those who denied Shu'ayb, they were the losers﴾ (7:92)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: So He destroyed those who denied Shu'ayb and did not believe in him, He annihilated them, and their town became desolate and empty of them. ﴿As if they had never prospered therein﴾ means: as if they had never dwelt there at all and had never lived in it at the time they perished.

* *

It is said: "Ghaniya fulan bi-makan kadha, fa-huwa yaghna bihi ghina wa ghuniyyan" [this second verbal noun "ghuniyyan" does not appear in any of the lexical sources; I have vocalized it with a damma on the ghayn, a kasra on the nun, and a shadda on the ya', on the pattern of "fu'ul," and so I deduced it. I do not know whether this is correct or not], meaning: he alighted at the place and was in it, as the poet said. [He is 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras.]

*Wa-laqad yaghna bi-ha jiranuki al-*
*mumsiku minki bi-'ahdin wa-wisal*

[His Diwan: 58; Mukhtarat Ibn al-Shajari 2:37; al-Khasa'is by Ibn Jinni 2:245 and al-Munsif by Ibn Jinni 1:66; al-Khizana 3:237. This is the splendid qasida in which he did not labor beyond what lay within his ability and capacity, without coercion or compulsion forcing him to it; he composed the entire qasida so that the final hemistich of each verse ends in the definite article "al-," as Ibn Jinni said in al-Khasa'is. Its opening is:
"O my two companions, halt and ask about the abode, the deserted dwelling of the people of al-Hilal,
Like the wearing away of a cloth, after you the rain has effaced its traces and the north wind's sweeping."
"And indeed your neighbors, who hold fast to you with bonds of covenant and union, have dwelt there"
He continued along this same path. In the printed edition it read "al-mustamsiku," which is a change from what is in the manuscript and from the transmitted version alike. His saying "al-mumsiku" means "al-mumsikun," and the nun was dropped because of the length of the phrase, not for idafa. The Arabs do this at times, as the Ansari said:
"Those who guard the honor of the tribe, no harm comes to them from behind us"
And al-Akhtal's saying:
"O sons of Kulayb, when my two paternal uncles killed the kings and unlocked the shackles"
See Sibawayh 1:95 and al-Munsif 1:67.]

And Ru'ba said:

*Wa-'ahdu maghni dimnatin bi-Dal'af'a* [His Diwan: 87. One verse of it has already passed earlier, 2:540, in praise of his people Banu Tamim, where he says:
"A dove came calling, and it is fitting for me to halt, a dove that called out to another dove with a cooing call,
It made Abu al-Sha'tha' and al-Sumayda' weep, and the covenant of the abode of the traces at Dal'af'a,
It perished, and its tent became scattered."
"Abu al-Sha'tha'" means himself. "Dal'af'a" is the name of a place.]

It is merely "mef'al" from "ghana."

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

14866 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿as if they had never prospered therein﴾: as if they had never lived, as if they had never enjoyed comfort.

14867 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿as if they had never prospered therein﴾, he said: as if they had never lived therein.

14868 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿as if they had never prospered therein﴾: as if they had never been there at all.

* *

As for His words ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, they were the losers﴾, He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: those who followed Shu'ayb were not the losers; rather, those who denied him were the losers, the perished. [See the explanation of "al-khusran" above, p. 565, note 2, and the references there.] For He, exalted is His praise, informed about them that those who denied Shu'ayb said to those who wanted to follow him: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, you will indeed then be losers﴾. So God refuted them by what He brought upon them of swift punishment. Then He said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): The followers of Shu'ayb did not lose; rather, when God's punishment came, those who denied Shu'ayb were the losers, not those who believed and affirmed him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 93:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how should I grieve over a disbelieving people?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His words, exalted is His mention, is: Shu'ayb turned his back on them, departing from among them when the punishment of God came upon them. [See the explanation of "tawalla" above, p. 546, note 2, and the references there.] And he said, when he was certain of the descent of God's vengeance upon his people who had denied him, out of grief for them: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord﴾, and I had delivered to you what He sent me with, namely warning you of His wrath for your persistence in disbelief in Him and the wrongdoing of people in their possessions [See the explanation of "al-balagh" above, p. 547, note 2, and the references there] ﴿and advised you﴾, by my commanding you to obey God and forbidding you to disobey Him. ﴿So how should I grieve﴾, meaning: How should I grieve over a people who denied the oneness of God and rejected His messenger, and feel sorrow at their destruction? [See the explanation of "al-asa" above, vol. 10, pp. 200, 475.]

* *

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14869. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So how should I grieve﴾, meaning: How should I be sorrowful?

14870. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So how should I grieve﴾, he says: How should I be sorrowful?

14871. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Grief befell Shu'ayb over his people, because of what he saw of God's vengeance upon them; then he consoled himself, as God related of him: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how should I grieve over a disbelieving people?﴾

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We sent not into any town a prophet but We seized its people with adversity and affliction, that haply they might humble themselves.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), informing him of His practice regarding the nations that passed before his community, and reminding those of Quraysh who disbelieved in him, so that they might desist from what they were persisting in of polytheism toward God and denial of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And We sent not into any town a prophet﴾ before you, ﴿but We seized its people with adversity and affliction﴾, and "adversity" (al-ba'sa') is distress, hardship of livelihood and its straitness, and "affliction" (al-darra') is harm and ill condition in the means of their worldly life. ﴿That haply they might humble themselves﴾, meaning: We did that so that they would humble themselves before their Lord, submit to Him, and turn back (to Him) [[See the explanation of "tadarru'" (humbling oneself) previously: 11:345, 414/ 12:485.]] by abandoning their disbelief and repenting of their denial of their prophets.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14872 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿We seized its people with adversity and affliction﴾, meaning: with poverty and hunger.

* *

We have already cited earlier the evidences for the soundness of what we have said regarding the meaning of "al-ba'sa'" and "al-darra'", which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See the explanation of "al-ba'sa'" previously: 3:349–353/ 4:288/ 11:354; and the explanation of "al-darra'" previously: 3:349–353/ 4:288/ 7:214/ 11:355.]]

* *

It was said: "yadda

rra'un" (yaḍḍarra'ūn), and the meaning is yatadarra'ūn (they humble themselves), but the "ta'" (ت) was assimilated into the "ḍād" (ض) because their places of articulation are close.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then We exchanged in place of the evil the good, until they multiplied and said, "Indeed, our fathers were touched by adversity and ease," so We seized them suddenly while they were not aware﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: ﴿Then We exchanged﴾ the people of the town whose people We seized with misfortune and hardship = ﴿in place of the evil﴾, which is the misfortune and hardship. He made that "evil" because it is what grieves people, = and "the good" does not grieve them, which is ease, bounty, and abundance in livelihood [[See the explanation of "al-darra'" (hardship) in the preceding footnote.

= And the explanation of "al-sarra'" (ease) earlier, 7:213.

= And the explanation of "al-sayyi'a" (evil) and "al-hasana" (good), earlier in the linguistic indices, roots (s-w-' ) and (h-s-n).

= And the explanation of "massa" (touched) earlier, p. 540, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿until they multiplied﴾, meaning: until they increased in number.

* *

Likewise, everything that increases is said of as "qad 'afa" [[See the explanation of "'afa" earlier, 3:370 / 4:343.]], as the poet said: [[He is Labid.]]

"But we cut the sword from them... among the sturdy, fat-rich, dense(?) shanks"
[[The verse has passed, with its takhrij and explanation, earlier, 4:343.]]

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14873. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿in place of the evil the good﴾, he said: in place of hardship, ease = ﴿until they multiplied﴾.

14874. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: ﴿in place of the evil the good﴾, he said: "the evil" is harm, and "the good" is ease, wealth, and children.

14875. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿in place of the evil the good﴾, he said: "the evil" is harm, and "the good" is good.

14876. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then We exchanged in place of the evil the good﴾, he said: in place of hardship, ease.

14877. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Then We exchanged in place of the evil the good until they multiplied﴾, he said: We exchanged in place of what they disliked what they loved in this world = ﴿until they multiplied﴾, from that punishment = ﴿and said, "Indeed, our fathers were touched by adversity and ease."﴾

* *

They differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿until they multiplied﴾.

Some of them said something similar to what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

14878. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: until they increased and their wealth increased.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: they gathered [wealth] (jammu). [["Jamma al-shay'" and "istajamma" mean it increased. "Mal jamm" means abundant wealth.]]

14879. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: their wealth and their children increased.

14880. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14881. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, until they increased.

14882. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: until they gathered [wealth] and increased.

14883. ... narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: until they gathered [wealth].

14884. ... narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, meaning: they gathered and increased.

14885. ... narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, he said: until their wealth and children increased.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, they increased as plants and feathers (al-rish) increase, [["Al-rish" (with a kasra on the ra') means goods and wealth.]] then He seized them at that moment suddenly while they were not aware.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: until they rejoiced.

Mention of those who said that:

14886. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿until they multiplied﴾, meaning: until they rejoiced in that.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Qatadah said regarding the meaning of "'afaw" is an interpretation for which there is no basis in the language of the Arabs, because "al-'afw" is not known to mean joy in anything of their speech, unless he meant: until they rejoiced in their multitude and the abundance of their wealth, in which case that would be a possible reading, though it is far-fetched.

* *
