As for His saying: ﴿and said, "Indeed, our fathers were touched by adversity and ease,"﴾ it is a report from God about these people whom He replaced the good with the evil in which they had been, as a means of gradual leading and testing: that they said, when He did that to them, "These are conditions that have befallen those before us from our fathers, and reached our forebears, and we are none other than their likes; what befell them of hardship in livelihoods will befall us, and ease in them," and it is "al-sarra'" (ease), because it gladdens its people.

And the foolish ones ignored the thankfulness due for God's blessing, and through their ignorance neglected the continuation of His favor by turning back to His obedience and hastening to desist from what He dislikes through repentance, until His command came upon them while they were not aware.

He, exalted is His majesty, says: ﴿So We seized them suddenly while they were not aware﴾, meaning: So We seized them with destruction and punishment unexpectedly, coming upon them unawares by its arrival, while they did not know nor realize that it would come to them; rather, they were denying that it would reach them, until they witnessed it and saw it.

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heavens and the earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.﴾ (96)

﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping?﴾ (97)

﴿Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ (98)

[The printed edition omitted the tafsir (exegesis) of these three verses, and the publisher did not point this out. It is also missing from the manuscript. The manuscript text runs on continuously with no blank space, so the scribe overlooked these three verses.

It seems this is an old lacuna. I do not know whether it originates with al-Tabari himself, with the copyist of the old manuscript from which our copy was transcribed, or with the copyist of the copy we have before us.

The evidence that it is an old gap is that I have not found anyone who transmitted anything from al-Tabari's reports on the exegesis of this verse. Ibn Kathir does not mention anything attributed to Ibn Jarir, nor does al-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur, nor al-Qurtubi, nor Abu Hayyan, nor anyone else who would be expected to transmit from Abu Ja'far. This nearly suggests that all the copies that reached them had this gap, and that none of them noticed it. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verses 99–100:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ (99)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says: Do they feel secure, O Muhammad, these who deny Allah and His Messenger and reject His signs, from Allah's gradual drawing them on (istidraj) through the blessings He has bestowed upon them in their worldly life, of bodily health and comfortable living, just as He drew on the peoples before them whose accounts He related to you? [[See the explanation of "al-makr" (plan/scheme) above, pp. 95, 97, note 1, and the references there.]] For none feels secure from the plan of Allah; that is, none is safe from that being a gradual drawing-on, while they persist in their disbelief and insist on their disobedience. ﴿Except the losing people﴾, and they are the ones who will be destroyed. [[See the explanation of "al-khusran" (losing/loss) above, p. 570, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people that, if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, and seal over their hearts so they do not hear?﴾ (100)

Abu Ja'far said: He says: Has it not become clear to those who are made successors in the earth after others before them have perished, who were its people, so that they followed their way, did their deeds, and rebelled against the command of their Lord? [[See the explanation of "hada" (to guide/make clear) in the lexical indexes above, root h-d-y.]] ﴿That if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins﴾: that is, if We willed, We could do to them as We did to those before them, seizing them for their sins and hastening Our punishment upon them as We hastened it upon those who came before them and inherited the earth from those before them, and destroy them for their sins. ﴿And seal over their hearts﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-tab'" (sealing) above, vol. 1: 258–261 / vol. 9: 364.]] that is, and We seal their hearts, ﴿so they do not hear﴾ admonition or reminder, the hearing of one who benefits from them.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

14887. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿awa lam yahd﴾: he said: it means "yubayyan" (is made clear).

14888. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14889. ... Narrated to us by 'Abdullah ibn Salih, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿awa lam yahd﴾: "awa lam yubayyan" (has it not been made clear).

14890. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Or has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people﴾: he says: has it not become clear to them?

14891. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people﴾: he says: has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people, meaning the polytheists.

14892. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people﴾: has We not made it clear to them, ﴿that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins﴾. He said: "al-huda" is the clarification by which he was sent as a guide to them, making things clear to them so that they might know. Without clarification, they would not know.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 101:

Concerning the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His saying: ﴿Those are the cities; We relate to you some of their news. And their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.﴾ (7:101)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: These cities that I have mentioned to you, O Muhammad, their affair and the affair of their people, meaning the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, and Shu'ayb, "We relate to you some of their news," so We inform you about them and about the reports of their people, and what happened to them and to the messengers of Allah who were sent to them [see the explanation of "al-qasas" (narratives) above, 12:406, footnote 1, and its references; and the explanation of "al-naba'" (news) above, 12:287, footnote 2, and its references], so that you may know that We give victory to Our messengers and to those who believe in the life of this world over Our enemies and the people who disbelieve in Us, and so that your deniers among your people may know the outcome of the affair of those who denied the messengers of Allah, and so that they may refrain from denying you and turn in repentance to the Oneness of Allah and obedience to Him. "And their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs": he says, the people of the cities that I have related to you the news of certainly were visited by their messengers "with clear proofs," meaning with arguments, the clear proofs [see the explanation of "al-bayyinat" (clear proofs) above in the lexical indexes under (bayn)]. "But they were not to believe in what they had denied before."

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: These polytheists whom We destroyed from the people of the cities were not going to believe, at the time of Our sending to them, in what they had denied before that, [in the printed edition: "bima kadhdhabu qabla dhalik" (in what they had denied before that), and in the manuscript: "bima yuhdithu qabla dhalik" (what they would invent before that); I deduce that the correct reading is what is recorded, because of his saying in the report he cited as evidence, "so they believed under compulsion"]. That refers to the day their covenant was taken, when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

14901 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "But they were not to believe in what they had denied before," he said: That is the day the covenant was taken from them, and they believed under compulsion.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: They were not going to believe at the coming of the messengers in what Allah's knowledge had already determined they would deny on the day He brought them forth from the backbone of Adam, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

14902 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "But they were not to believe in what they had denied before," he said: It was in His knowledge on the day they acknowledged Him with the covenant.

14903 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: It is incumbent upon the servants to take from knowledge what their Lord and the prophets have made apparent to them, and to leave aside the knowledge of what Allah has concealed from them, for His knowledge is effective in what has been and what will be. And concerning that He said: "And their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers." He said: His knowledge took effect concerning them, which of them would be obedient and which disobedient, when He created them in the time of Adam. And the confirmation of that is when He said to Noah: ﴿Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you; and there will be nations We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾ (11:48). And He said concerning that: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ (6:28). And concerning that He said: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ (17:15). And concerning that He said: ﴿So that mankind will not have an argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ (4:165). And there is no argument for anyone against Allah.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "But they were not to believe," even if We were to revive them after their destruction and they witnessed what they witnessed of the punishment of Allah, "in what they had denied before," meaning their destruction, as His saying, majestic is His praise, says: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ (6:28).

Mention of those who said that:

14904 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: "in what they had denied before," he said: Like His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: The most similar of these sayings to the interpretation of the verse and the most preferable to correctness is the saying we have mentioned from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Rabi'. That is because whoever Allah, blessed and exalted, has determined in His knowledge will not believe in Him, will never believe. And it had been determined in the knowledge of Allah, blessed and exalted, concerning those among the nations whose news is related in this surah who were destroyed, that they would never believe. So He, majestic is His praise, informed about them that they were not going to believe in what they were denying in His prior knowledge, before the coming of the messengers and at their coming to them. And if it were said that its interpretation is: "Then were these people who inherited the earth, O Muhammad, from the polytheists of your people, after its former inhabitants, who were there from 'Ad and Thamud, going to believe in what those who inherited it from them denied of the Oneness of Allah, His promise and His threat," it would have been a valid view and position, but I do not know of any speaker of it among those whose knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur'an is relied upon.

* *

As for what Mujahid said, that its meaning is: "If they were returned, they would not have believed," it is an interpretation for which there is no indication in the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor in any sound report from the Messenger. And if that is so, then what is more fitting to correctness is what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates.

* *

As for His saying: "Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers," He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as Allah sealed the hearts of those who disbelieved in their Lord and disobeyed His messengers from these nations whose news We have related to you, O Muhammad, in this surah, until the punishment of Allah came upon them and they perished by it, "Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers," those for whom it was written that they would never believe, from your people [see the explanation of "al-tab'" (sealing) above, 12:579, footnote 4, and its references].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 102:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And We found not for most of them any covenant; and indeed We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: We did not find for most of the people of these towns, whom We destroyed and whose account We related to you, O Muhammad, [any] "covenant" — meaning, [any] fulfilment of what We enjoined upon them: the affirmation of God's oneness, following His messengers, acting in obedience to Him, avoiding His disobedience, and abandoning the worship of idols and images.

* *

The "covenant" (ʿahd) is the charge (wasiyya), which we have already explained earlier in a manner sufficient to make its repetition unnecessary. [See the explanation of "ʿahd" above: 1:410, 557 / 2:279 / 3:20–24, 349 / 6:526.] ﴿And indeed We found most of them﴾ — meaning: We did not find most of them except as transgressors (fasiqun) against the obedience of their Lord, abandoning His covenant and His charge.

We have already explained the meaning of "fisq" (transgression) earlier. [See the explanation of "fisq" above: 12:195, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14905 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, blessed and exalted: "And indeed We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient," he said: "The past generations."

14906 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "And We found not for most of them any covenant," the verse, he said: "The past generations. And 'His covenant' is that which He took from the children of Adam in the loins of Adam, and they did not fulfil it."

14907 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-ʿAliya, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "And We found not for most of them any covenant," he said: "[It refers to] the covenant which He took in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him."

14908 – Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And We found not for most of them any covenant, and indeed We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient." That is because God only destroyed the towns because they had not preserved what He had charged them with.

The commentary on His words, "Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged themselves through them. So look how was the end of the corrupters" (7:103):

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then We sent Moses ibn Imran after Noah, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb.

* *

The "ha' and mim" in His words "from after them" refer to the prophets, peace be upon them, who were mentioned from the beginning of this surah up to this point.

* *

"With Our signs" means: with Our proofs and evidences [[See the explanation of "ayah" (sign) in the earlier lexical references under the root (ayy).]]. "To Pharaoh and his chiefs" means: to Pharaoh's company of men [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the chiefs) in the earlier discussion, 12:565, note 2, and the references there.]]. "But they wronged themselves through them" means: they disbelieved in them. The "ha' and alif" in His words "through them" refer to "the signs." The meaning is: they wronged themselves through Our signs with which We sent Moses to them. It is permissible to say "they wronged through them" in the sense of "they disbelieved in them," because wronging (zulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. I have already shown in earlier passages that this is its meaning, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary [[See the explanation of "zulm" (wronging) in the earlier lexical index under the root (z-l-m)]].

* *

Disbelief in the signs of God is placing them in other than their proper place and turning them away from the direction for which they were intended. "So look how was the end of the corrupters": His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, at how the end was for those who spread corruption in the land [[See the explanation of "al-'aqibah" (the end) in the earlier discussion, 12:560, note 1, and the references there; and the explanation of "al-fasad" (corruption) in the earlier discussion, 12:560, note 2, and the references there.]]. That means Pharaoh and his chiefs, when they wronged themselves by the signs of God that Moses, peace be upon him, brought them. Their end was that they were all drowned in the sea.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾ (7:104)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verses 105–106:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is fitting for me that I should not say about God except the truth. I have come to you with a clear sign from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel﴾ (105) ﴿[Pharaoh] said: If you have come with a sign, then bring it, if you are among the truthful﴾ (106).

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed over the reading of His saying: "Haqiq 'ala an la aqula 'ala Allah illa al-haqq" (it is fitting for me that I should not say about God except the truth).

A group of the reciters of Mecca, Medina, Basra and Kufa read it: ﴿haqiqun 'ala an la aqula﴾, with the "ya'" of "'ala" unstressed (without shaddah), meaning: "I am fitting (haqiq) to not say about God except the truth." They understood the meaning of "'ala" as the meaning of "ba'" (bi), as one says: "ramaytu bi al-qaws" (I shot with the bow) and "ramaytu 'ala al-qaws," and "ji'tu 'ala hal hasanah" (I came in a good state) and "ji'tu bi hal hasanah."
[See what has preceded in 11:317, footnote 1, and Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:386.]

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: when it is read thus, its meaning is: "haris 'ala an la aqula" (eager that I should not say), or "fa-haqqun an la aqula" (so it is right that I should not say). [Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:224. In the printed edition here it read: "harish 'ala an la aqula illa bi-haqq," and in the manuscript: "harish 'ala an la aqula bi-haqq la aqula," and both are errors; the correct text is from Majaz al-Qur'an, being the exact wording of his statement.]

* *

And a group of the people of Medina read it: "Haqiqun 'alayya alla aqula" (It is binding upon me that I should not say), meaning: "wajib 'alayya an la aqula" (it is obligatory upon me that I should not say), and "haqqun 'alayya an la aqula" (it is my right/duty that I should not say).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that both are well-known readings, close in meaning. Imams among the reciters have read each of them, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct in his recitation.

* *

As for His saying: "Qad ji'tukum bi-bayyinatin min rabbikum" (I have certainly come to you with a clear proof from your Lord), it means: Moses said to Pharaoh and his chiefs: I have come to you with a proof from your Lord, which bears witness, O people, to the truth of what I say and the truth of what I tell you concerning God's sending me to you as a messenger. So send with me the Children of Israel, O Pharaoh. Pharaoh said to him: "In kunta ji'ta bi-ayah" (if you have come with a sign), meaning: with a proof and a sign testifying to the truth of what you say, "fa'ti biha in kunta mina al-sadiqin" (then bring it, if you are among the truthful).

Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So he cast down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent (107). And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers (108).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His praise be exalted: "So Moses cast down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent," meaning a snake, "manifest" meaning that it was clear to whoever saw it that it was a snake. [Refer to the explanation of "manifest" in the earlier lexical indexes under (ب ي ن).]

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said regarding this.

14909 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "behold, it was a manifest serpent," he said: It turned into a great serpent. Another said: like a city.

14910 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: "behold, it was a manifest serpent," he said: behold, it was a serpent that nearly "yatasawwaruhu," meaning: nearly leapt upon him. [In the printed edition: "kadat" with the feminine in both places, and I have preserved what is in the manuscript. And "al-hayyah" (the serpent) has both masculine and feminine usage.]

14911 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "behold, it was a manifest serpent," and "al-thu'ban" is the male of serpents, its mouth open, its lower jaw set on the ground and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, then it turned toward Pharaoh to seize him. When he saw it, he was terrified of it, leapt up and defecated, which he had not done before, and cried: "O Moses, take it, and I believe in you, and I will send the Children of Israel with you!" So Moses took it, and it returned to being a staff.

14912 - 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "behold, it was a manifest serpent," he said: He cast the staff and it became a serpent; it placed its lower jaw at the bottom of the dome and its upper jaw at the top of the dome. [The "fuqm" (plural "fuqman") is the same as the "lahy" that I explained before.] When it wanted to seize him, Pharaoh said: "O Moses, take it!" So Moses took it in his hand, and it returned to being a staff as it was the first time.

When Pharaoh saw that it was heading toward him, he leapt from his throne, [meaning he threw himself down and fell from his throne] and sought help from Moses to restrain it from him, and he did so.

14914 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding his saying: "a manifest serpent," he said: the male serpent.

It charged at the people, and they fled, and twenty-five thousand of them died, some of them killing others, and Pharaoh stood up fleeing until he entered the house.

14917 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "behold, it was a manifest serpent," he said: the male serpent.

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying: "And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers," He says: he brought out his hand, and behold, it was white, shining to whoever among the people looked at it. [Refer to the explanation of "nazaa" in the earlier volume 12:437.]

* *

Moses, as it has been related to us, was dark-skinned, so Allah made his hand, when it turned, white without leprosy, as a sign for him and as proof of the truth of his saying: "Indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds." Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying: "And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers," He says: he brought out his hand, and behold, it was white, shining to whoever among the people looked at it. [Refer to the explanation of "nazaa" in the earlier volume 12:437.]

* *

Moses, as it has been related to us, was dark-skinned, so Allah made his hand, when it turned, white without leprosy, as a sign for him and as proof of the truth of his saying: "Indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds." Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

14918 - al-'Abbas narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He brought his hand out of his collar and saw it white without blemish, meaning without leprosy. Then he returned it to his sleeve, and it returned to its former color.

14919 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying: "white to the onlookers," he said: without leprosy.

14920 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers," he said: He drew his hand out of his collar, white without leprosy.

14921 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14922 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And he drew out his hand," he brought it out of his collar, "and behold, it was white to the onlookers."

14923 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His saying: "And he drew out his hand," he said: he drew his hand out of his collar, "and behold, it was white to the onlookers." Moses was dark-skinned, so he brought out his hand, and behold, it was white, whiter than milk, "without blemish," he said: without leprosy, as a sign for Pharaoh.

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿The chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said, "Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you advise?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty and majestic is He, says: The group of men from the people of Pharaoh and their nobles [[See the explanation of *al-mala'* (the chiefs) earlier, p. 12, note 2, and the references there.]] said, "Indeed, this is," meaning Musa, peace be upon him, "a knowing sorcerer," meaning that he deceives people's eyes through his trickery, so that the staff appears to them as a serpent, the wheat-colored (*adam*) appears white, and a thing appears other than what it is. From this it is said, "The rain *sahara* the earth" when it pours upon it, uprooting its plants from their roots and turning the earth upside down, so that it *yasharuhu* (bewitches it) *sahran*, and "the earth is *masjura*" (bewitched) when this happens to it. [[This explanation of the meaning of "the rain bewitched the earth" is very good and clarifies the meaning of the word. It is clearer than what appears in the lexicon books, so take note of it there.]] Thus the sorcery of the sorcerer is likened to this, because he makes the one he bewitches imagine that he sees a thing other than what it is. [[See the explanation of *al-sihr* (sorcery) earlier, 2:436–442 / 11:265.]] From this is the verse of Dhu al-Rummah describing the mirage:

*"And a bewitching one of the eyes from the deserts, its surfaces dancing with the tall (ones)"*

[[His Diwan: 591, and al-Lisan (*arm*), with this narration. The narration in the Diwan is: "And a bewitching one of the mirage from the deserts... dancing in its *asaqilihā* the *awrum*." And: "Death comes to the sandgrouse of the wilderness therein from thirst, and the breeze perishes in its sides." And: "Therein are deceptions, and there is no rain there, and phantoms that move and do not depart." This is extremely fine poetry! The narration here is that of Abu 'Ubaydah in *Majaz al-Qur'an*. The narration of Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' is *nawasiraha*. In the printed edition it read *nawashizaha* with a *zay*, but in the manuscript it is unpointed. *Al-Mawami* is the plural of *mawmah*, meaning a wide, smooth desert with no water and no companion. *Al-'Asaqil* is the plural of *'Asaqilah*, and *al-'Asaqil* is the plural of *'Asaqul*, meaning the patches of mirage that shine and glitter to the eye of the beholder. *Al-Awrum* is the plural of *Irm*, meaning landmarks; it is said they are the graves of 'Ad and Iram. The narration in his Diwan is *wasajirah* with a *jim*, meaning filled with mirage. He describes the mirage as it shakes and quivers, so one sees stones and landmarks rising in it and sinking, while it moves with them. As for Abu Ja'far's narration *"tarqusu fi nawashirihā"* (dancing in its *nawashir*), I have not found an explanation for it from any commentator on poetry or in the lexicon books. My opinion is that he means by it the mirage, as in "in its *'asaqil*," and that it derives from *nashr al-shay'* (spreading out a thing), meaning to stretch and extend it. Did he mean by it what stretches and spreads out of the mirage?]]

As for His words, ﴿knowing﴾, it means: a sorcerer who is knowing in sorcery [[See the explanation of *'alim* (knowing) earlier in the lexical indexes under (*'alima*).]]. ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land﴾, the land of Egypt, O assembly of the Copts, the sorcerers [[Thus it is in the manuscript, vocalized with a shadda on the *sin*: *al-sahara* (the sorcerers). If it were read as *bi-sihrihi* (by his sorcery), it would be a fine reading.]]. ﴿So what do you advise?﴾ Pharaoh said to the chiefs, "What do you order us to do about his matter? With what do you advise regarding it?"

* *

It has been said: "So what do you advise?" is a report about Pharaoh, though Pharaoh is not mentioned. Such a thing rarely occurs in speech, and it is similar to His words: ﴿The wife of the ruler said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful. That is so he will know that I did not betray him in his absence."﴾ [Yusuf: 51–52]. It is said that "That is so he will know that I did not betray him in his absence" is from the words of Yusuf, though Yusuf is not mentioned. Another example of this is when one says, "I said to Zayd, 'Stand,' for I am standing," and he means, "Zayd said, 'Indeed, I am standing.'" [[See the detailed treatment of this in al-Farra's *Ma'ani al-Qur'an*, 1:387.]]

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿They said: Put him off, and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers﴾ (7:111)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said to Pharaoh: "Put him off," that is, delay him.

* *

Some said: its meaning is: detain him.

* *

Al-irja' (postponement) in the speech of the Arabs means delay. It is said from it: "arjaytu hadha al-amr" and "arja'tuhu," meaning, "I delayed it." From it is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 51], meaning: you delay. The hamza is from the speech of some tribes of Qays, who say "arja'tu hadha al-amr," while dropping the hamza is from the dialect of Tamim and Asad, who say "arjaytuhu." [[The detailed attribution of dialects to their tribes is not found in any lexicon; it is an addition noted in its place there.]].

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The common readers of Medina and some Iraqis recited it: "arjihi," without hamza and with the "ha" vowelled with a kasra.

Some of the readers of Kufa recited it: "arjih," with the hamza dropped and the "ha" pronounced with sukun, according to the dialect of those who pause on the pronominal "ha" in connected speech when the preceding letter is vowelled, as the rajiz said: [[This is Duwayd ibn Zayd ibn Nahd al-Qudha'i, one of the long-lived.]]

"Time has afflicted me in leg and hand, swearing it will repair nothing without corrupting it,
So today it repairs and tomorrow it corrupts."
[[Tabaqat fuhul al-shu'ara': 28; al-Mu'ammarin: 20; and Amali al-Sharif 1: 137; al-Shi'r wa-al-shu'ara': 51; al-Mu'talif wa-al-mukhtalif: 114; Sharh shawahid al-Shafiya: 274; and many others. It is among ancient poetry, as Ibn Sallam said. The transmission of these verses differs greatly across all the sources, as I indicated in the commentary on Tabaqat Ibn Sallam. In the printed edition it read " alha 'ala al-dahr" and "fa-qasamahu la nusliha," which is a corrupt error; its correct form is in the manuscript and in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra'.]]

They do likewise with the feminine "ha," saying "hadhihi Talhah qad aqbalat" (this is Talhah, she has come), as the rajiz said: [[It is said he is Manzur ibn Hibba al-Asadi.]]

"When he saw that there was neither ease nor fullness, he turned to a tamarisk-bush on a dune and lay down."
[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 388; Islah al-mantiq: 108; Tahdhib Islah al-mantiq 1: 167; Sharh shawahid al-Shafiya: 274–276, 480. He describes a gazelle, and before it says: "O Lord of a leaping gazelle of the reddish kind..., the wolf drew itself together and gathered." Al-Tibrizi said in its commentary: "He describes a gazelle. Al-Abbaz is the one that leaps. Al-'Afr among gazelles are those whose colour is reddish. Taqabbada: he gathered his legs to pin the gazelle. Lamma ra'a anna la da'a, meaning the wolf, when he saw that he would not be sated by the gazelle nor overtake it, and that he had tired in pursuing it, he turned to a tamarisk and lay down beside it. Al-Artan is a kind of desert shrub, its singular being artah. Al-Haqf is the bent part of the sand."]]

And some of the Basran readers recited it: "arji'hu," with the hamza and the "ha" vowelled with a damma, according to the dialect of Qays mentioned above.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the recitations is the one most widely known and most eloquent in the speech of the Arabs, which is dropping the hamza and vowelling the "ha" with a kasra. Although the other is permissible, what we have chosen is the most eloquent of the dialects and the most common on the tongues of the eloquent Arabs.

* *

The exegetes differed regarding the interpretation of His words "arjih."

Some said: its meaning is: delay him.

Those who said this:

14924 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "arjih wa-akhahu," he said: delay him.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: detain him.

Those who said this:

14925 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "arjih wa-akhahu," that is: detain him and his brother.

* *

As for His words: "wa-arsil fi al-madd'in hashirin," he means: whoever gathers the sorcerers and brings them together to you. [[See the explanation of "al-hashr" above, 12:115, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It was said: they are the police.

Those who said this:

14926 - Abbas ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr related to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn 'Abbas: "wa-arsil fi al-madd'in hashirin," he said: the police.

14927 - Ibn Wakî' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from his father, from Mujahid: "wa-arsil fi al-madd'in hashirin," he said: the police.

14928 - He said: Humayd related to us, from Qays, from al-Suddi: "wa-arsil fi al-madd'in hashirin," he said: the police.

14929 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir related to us, from his father, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "fi al-madd'in hashirin," he said: the police.

14930 - 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham related to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "wa-arsil fi al-madd'in hashirin," he said: the police.

The discussion of His saying: ﴿They will bring you every skilled sorcerer﴾ ﴿And the sorcerers came to Pharaoh, saying, "Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about the counsel of the chiefs of Pharaoh's people to Pharaoh, that he should send heralds to the cities to gather every skilled sorcerer.

* *

There is an omission in the speech, which is left because the apparent wording indicates it, and it is: "So he sent heralds to the cities, who would gather the sorcerers."

* *

"And the sorcerers came to Pharaoh, saying, 'Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward'" means: indeed, there will be a reward for us from you for our victory over Musa [see the explanation of "al-ajr" in the earlier lexical indexes, root *a-j-r*], "if we are, O Pharaoh, the victors."

* *

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

14931 - Al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Regarding "So he sent heralds to the cities," he gathered for him every sorcerer who claimed knowledge. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: "With what does this sorcerer work?" They said: "He works with serpents." They said: "By Allah, there is no people on earth who work with sorcery, serpents, ropes and staffs more knowledgeable than us, so what is our reward if we overcome him?" He said to them: "You are my kin and my close relations, and I will do for you everything you desire."

14932 - Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Pharaoh said: "We will not contend with him" — meaning Musa — "except with one of his own kind." So he prepared scholars from the Children of Israel and sent them to a village in Egypt called "al-Farama," where they taught them sorcery as children are taught writing in the kuttab. He said: They taught them a great deal of sorcery. He said: Musa had promised Pharaoh an appointment, and when that appointment came, Pharaoh sent for them, and they came with their teacher. Pharaoh said to him: "What have you done?" He said: "I have taught them sorcery such that no sorcery of the people of the earth can withstand it, except that it be a matter from heaven, for they have no power against that. As for the sorcery of the people of the earth, it will not overcome them." When the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh: "Will there indeed be a reward for us if we are the victors?" He said: "Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near."

14933 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So Pharaoh sent heralds to the cities," and they gathered the sorcerers to him. "When the sorcerers came to Pharaoh, they said, 'Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors'" — meaning: a gift that will be given to us. "If we are the victors?" He said: "Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near."

14934 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Delay him and his brother, and send heralds to the cities* who will bring you every skilled sorcerer." That is, outnumber him with sorcerers, perhaps you will find among the sorcerers one who can bring the like of what he brought. Musa and Harun had gone out from his presence after he showed them of the authority of Allah what He showed them. [In the printed edition: "min sultanihi"; in the manuscript: "min sultan wa-ba'atha Fir'awn," the omission restored from the text of al-Tabari's History 1:210.] Pharaoh sent throughout his realm, and he did not leave in his dominion a sorcerer except that he was brought. It was mentioned to me, and Allah knows best, that he gathered for him fifteen thousand sorcerers. When they assembled before him, he gave them his command and said to them: "A sorcerer has come to us the like of whom we have never seen, and if you overcome him, I will honor you, elevate you, and bring you near above the people of my realm!" They said: "And will we have that if we overcome him?" He said: "Yes!" [Report 14934: this is part of a long report that Abu Ja'far narrated with this chain in his History 1:210.]

14935 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, who said: The sorcerers were seventy. Abu Ja'far said: I think he said: "a thousand." [Meaning "seventy thousand."]

14936 - He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mundhir, who said: The sorcerers were eighty thousand.

14937 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Khaythamah, from Abu Sawdah, from Ka'b, who said: The sorcerers of Pharaoh were twelve thousand.

14935 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, who said: The sorcerers were seventy. Abu Ja'far said: I think he said: "a thousand." [Meaning "seventy thousand."]

14936 - He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mundhir, who said: The sorcerers were eighty thousand.

14937 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Khaythamah, from Abu Sawdah, from Ka'b, who said: The sorcerers of Pharaoh were twelve thousand.

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿He said, "Yes, and you will indeed be among those brought near." They said, "O Moses, either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Mighty is His praise. He says: Pharaoh said to the magicians, when they said to him, "Will we have a reward from you if we overcome Moses?" He said, "Yes, you will have that, and you will indeed be among those whom I bring near and favour." "They said, 'O Moses'" means: the magicians said to Moses, "O Moses, choose either to throw your staff, or we will throw ours." For this reason "an" (that) was introduced with "imma" (either) in the speech, because it is in the position of a command to choose. So "an" is in the accusative position, given the meaning I have described, since the meaning of the speech is: choose that you throw, or that we throw. When speech with "imma" takes the form of a command, it must include "an", as when you say to a man, "Either you go, or you sit," meaning the command: go or sit. When it takes the form of a report, "an" is not included, as in His saying: ﴿And others are held in suspense for the command of God; either He will punish them, or He will turn to them in mercy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 106]. This is what is called *takhyir* (giving an option) [[His saying, "This is what is called takhyir," is the first ruling on the inclusion of "an" with "imma". As for what comes in the form of a report, such as "either He punishes them, or He turns to them," they call it *ibham* (indefiniteness). It would have been right for Abu Ja'far to put his saying "This is what is called takhyir" before his saying "When it takes the form of a report," to remove confusion from his speech.]] And likewise everything that takes the form of a report. "Imma" in all of these is vowelled with a kasra [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 389, 390; this is a very good discussion.]].

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿He said, "Throw!" And when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and produced a great magic.﴾ [7:116]

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Moses said to the magicians, ﴿"Throw"﴾ what you are going to throw! So the magicians threw what they had with them. When they threw it, ﴿"they bewitched the eyes of the people"﴾: they made the eyes of the people imagine, through the illusion and deceptions they produced, that the objects were moving. ﴿"And terrified them"﴾: they terrified the people with what they had bewitched in their eyes, until they feared the staffs and ropes, thinking them to be snakes. ﴿"And they produced"﴾, as God said, ﴿"a great magic"﴾: a great, large illusion, of the kind made by illusion and deception. (See the discussion of *sihr* (magic) above, p. 19, note 2, and the references there.)

Similar to this is what has been reported:

So they threw their ropes and staffs. There were some thirty-odd thousand men, and not one of them was without a rope and a staff. ﴿"When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them"﴾, meaning: they scattered them (*farraqu-hum*, with a shadda on the ra; they caused them *al-firq* (with fatha on the fa and ra), which is fear). ﴿So Moses sensed fear within himself﴾.

**On the interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And We revealed to Moses, "Throw down your staff," and behold, it swallowed up what they had falsely fabricated.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We revealed to Moses, "Throw down your staff," so he threw it down, and it became a serpent that swallowed up and gulped down what they had been conjuring up as falsehood and vanity.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 118:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿So the truth took place, and what they had been doing was nullified﴾ (7:118).

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The truth became manifest and clear to those who witnessed and were present regarding the matter of Musa, and that he was a messenger of God calling to the truth. **Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, Verse 123:**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation and meaning) of His words:** ﴿Pharaoh said, "You believed in Him before I gave you permission. Indeed, this is a scheme that you devised in the city, to drive its people out of it. But you will come to know."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Pharaoh said to the magicians when they believed in God, meaning they affirmed His Messenger Musa (peace be upon him), because of what they witnessed of the great power and authority of God: "You believed in Him," meaning: you affirmed Musa and acknowledged his prophethood. "Before I gave you permission," meaning: before I permitted you to believe in him. "Indeed, this," meaning: your affirmation of him and your acknowledgment of his prophethood, "is a scheme that you devised in the city," meaning: a deception by which you deceived the people of our city, [See the discussion of "al-makr" (scheming) above, 12:95 and 97:597.] "to drive them out of it." "But you will come to know," meaning: what I will do to you, and what punishment from me you will meet for this deed of yours.

* *

As for what their scheme consisted of:

14955 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik; and Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas; and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud; and from some of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): Musa and the chief of the magicians met, and Musa said to him: "Tell me, if I defeat you, will you believe in me and testify that what I have brought is true?" The magician said: "I will bring tomorrow a magic that no magic can overcome. By God, if you defeat me, I will indeed believe in you and testify that you are right!" Pharaoh was watching them. This is the meaning of Pharaoh's words: "Indeed, this is a scheme you devised in the city, when you two met, to conspire together so that you might drive its people out of it." [Report 14955: This is part of a long report, which Abu Ja'far related in his History, 1:213.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 124:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Surely I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all﴾ (7:124).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says, reporting the words of Pharaoh to the magicians when they believed in God and affirmed His messenger Moses: "Surely I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides." This means that he would cut off one of them, the right hand and the left foot, or cut off the left hand and the right foot, thus differing between the two limbs in the cutting. His differing between them in this way is "cutting on opposite sides." [[See the explanation of "cutting on opposite sides" above, vol. 10, p. 268.]]

* *

It is said that the first to institute this kind of cutting was Pharaoh, and his words "then I will crucify you all" were said by Pharaoh only because of what he saw of God's abandonment of him and Moses' (peace be upon him) victory over him and subjugation of him.

14956 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Hafari and Hubawiyah al-Razi narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "Surely I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all," he said: The first to crucify, and the first to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides, was Pharaoh. [[Report 14956 - "Hubawiyah al-Razi" is Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi, Abu Yazid; it has passed under numbers 14365 and 14550.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the verse: ﴿They said, "Indeed, to our Lord we will return. And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and take us in death as Muslims."﴾ (7:125–126)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: The magicians answered Pharaoh when he threatened them with cutting off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifying them: ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return﴾. By "return" (inqilab) they mean returning to Allah, going back to Him and arriving at Him. [See the explanation of "inqilab" above, p. 32, note 1, and the references there.]

And His saying: ﴿And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord﴾. It means: You do not hold anything against us, O Pharaoh, and you find no fault in us, except that we believed, that is, we affirmed the truth of, ﴿the signs of our Lord﴾, meaning the proofs, evidences and indications of our Lord that neither you nor anyone else can produce, apart from Allah, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. [See the explanation of "the sign" in the earlier lexical index, under the root (ʾ-y-y).] Then they turned to Allah, asking Him for patience under Pharaoh's punishment and for their souls to be taken while they are upon Islam. So they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾. By their words "pour" they mean: send down upon us a restraint that keeps us from disbelieving in You, [see the explanation of "pour upon us patience" above, vol. 5, p. 354, and the explanation of "patience" above, vol. 12, p. 561, note 1, and the references there] at the time of Pharaoh's torturing us. ﴿And take us in death as Muslims﴾: that is, take us to You upon Islam, the religion of Your friend Abraham (ﷺ), and not upon associating others with You. [See the explanation of "tawaffa" above, vol. 12, p. 415, note 1, and the references there.]

Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides﴾, that he killed them and crucified them, as Abdullah ibn Abbas said, when they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and take us in death as Muslims﴾. He said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: The magicians were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿And the magicians were thrown down prostrating﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at its end.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and take us in death as Muslims﴾, he said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at its end.

So they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾. By their words "pour" they mean: send down upon us a restraint that keeps us from disbelieving in You, [see the explanation of "pour upon us patience" above, vol. 5, p. 354, and the explanation of "patience" above, vol. 12, p. 561, note 1, and the references there] at the time of Pharaoh's torturing us. ﴿And take us in death as Muslims﴾: that is, take us to You upon Islam, the religion of Your friend Abraham (ﷺ), and not upon associating others with You. [See the explanation of "tawaffa" above, vol. 12, p. 415, note 1, and the references there.]

Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides﴾, that he killed them and crucified them, as Abdullah ibn Abbas said, when they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and take us in death as Muslims﴾. He said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: The magicians were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿And the magicians were thrown down prostrating﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at its end.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and take us in death as Muslims﴾, he said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at its end.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, "Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land and to abandon you and your gods?" He said, "We will kill their sons and spare their women, and we are certainly dominant over them."﴾ (7:127)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: A group of men from Pharaoh's people said to Pharaoh [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the chiefs/notables) earlier, p. 18, note 1, and the references there.]], "Will you leave Moses and his people, the Children of Israel [[See the explanation of "yadhar" (to leave/abandon) earlier, 12:136, note 3, and the references there.]]," ﴿to spread corruption in the land﴾, meaning: so that they may corrupt your servants and slaves against you in your land of Egypt [[See the explanation of "fasad fi'l-ard" (corruption in the land) earlier, p. 13, note 1, and the references there.]], ﴿and to abandon you and your gods﴾, meaning: "and abandon you," and abandon serving you, and the worship of you and your gods.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿and to abandon you and your gods﴾, there are two possible interpretations.

The first: "Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land, when he has abandoned you and abandoned the worship of you and your gods?" If the sentence is understood in this way, the accusative in ﴿wa-yadharaka﴾ is in the form of *al-sarf* [[*Al-sarf* is a grammatical term; its explanation was given earlier, 7:247, note 2, and the references there. See also al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:391.]], not coordinated with His saying "to spread corruption."

The second: "Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land, and to abandon you and your gods?" This is a rebuke from them to Pharaoh for leaving Moses to do these two things. If the sentence is understood in this way, the accusative in ﴿wa-yadharaka﴾ is coordinated with ﴿li-yufsidu﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: The first interpretation is the more correct of the two, namely that the accusative of ﴿wa-yadharaka﴾ is in the form of *al-sarf*, because the interpretation of the people of interpretation (*ta'wil*) came in this way.

* *

Furthermore, in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, *alladhi* [[Text reads: "al-ladhi" in the sense of the reading variant as given in the report below.]]:

14961 – Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us from Harun, who said: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿Wa-qad taraknaka an ya'budukum wa-alihatak﴾. [[See also al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:391.]]

* *

This is a clear indication that the accusative in that place is in the form of *al-sarf*.

* *

It is also reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he would read it: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-alihatak﴾, coordinating "wa-yadharaka" with His saying ﴿atadharu Musa﴾.

= It is as if he directed its interpretation to: "Will you leave Moses and his people, and abandon you and your gods, to spread corruption in the land?" It is possible that al-Hasan's reading means: "Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land, while he abandons you and your gods?" In that case, "yadharaka" is in the nominative, begun as a new sentence, and free of the influence of other words. [[In the printed edition, the phrase "and free of the influence of other words" is omitted, as though its meaning was not understood; the author intended its freedom from the governing particles that make it nominative, accusative or genitive. In the manuscript it reads "ila ibtida' al-kalam" and in the printed edition "ala ibta' al-kalam"; what is recorded here is the better reading.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿wa-alihatak﴾, the readers of the regional centres (*amsar*) read the alif in it with a fatha and with a long vowel (*madd*), meaning: "Moses has abandoned the worship of you and the worship of your gods which you worship."

* *

It is mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "He had a cow which he worshipped."

* *

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that they used to read it: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾ with a kasra on the alif, meaning: "and [he will] abandon you and your worship." [[See what preceded at 1:123–124 concerning the explanation of "al-ilaha," and the reports of Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid with their chains, and it will come under nos. 14966–14971.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading which we do not consider valid except that one is the reading upon which the readers of the regional centres agree, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

Mention of those who said that Pharaoh worshipped gods, according to the reading of the one who read: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-alihatak﴾.

14962 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-alihatak﴾ – "and his gods," as Ibn 'Abbas claimed, were cows. When they saw a beautiful cow he would order them to worship it. For this reason he brought out for them a calf and a cow.

14963 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan, who said: Pharaoh had an amulet (*jumana*) hanging on his chest, which he worshipped and prostrated to.

14964 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: "It has reached me that Pharaoh used to worship a god in secret," and he recited: "wa-yadharaka wa-alihatak."

14965 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, who said: Pharaoh had a god which he worshipped in secret.

* *

Mention of those who said: the meaning of that is "and [he will] abandon you and your worship," according to the reading of the one who read: ﴿wa-ilahatak﴾.

14966 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Hasan, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾, he said: "Pharaoh was only worshipped; he did not worship." [[Report 14966: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib is a reliable Successor (*tabi'i*). He was mentioned earlier under no. 2892. In the manuscript and printed edition here it reads "Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from al-Hasan," which is an error. The report has already appeared correctly with this chain under no. 143, and it will come correctly under no. 14971.]]

14967 – ... he said: my father narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾, and said: "and your worship," and he would say: "He was worshipped and did not worship." [[Report 14967: Nafi' ibn 'Umar, mentioned many times earlier. In the manuscript and printed edition it reads "from Nafi', from Ibn 'Amm," which is an error; the correct form is as given earlier under no. 142.]]

14968 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas his saying: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾, he said: "He abandons your worship."

14969 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to read: ﴿wa-ilahatak﴾, saying: "and your worship."

14970 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾, he said: "your worship."

14971 – Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he used to read: ﴿wa-yadharaka wa-ilahatak﴾, and said: "Pharaoh was only worshipped; he did not worship." [[Report 14971: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib; see the note on no. 14966.]]

* *

Some of them claimed that whoever reads "wa-ilahatak" intends roughly the meaning of the one who reads ﴿wa-alihatak﴾, except that he made it feminine while intending a single god, as if he meant: "wa-yadharaka wa-ilahuk," then he made "al-ilah" feminine and said "wa-ilahatak."

* *

Some of the Basrans mentioned that a Bedouin was asked about "al-ilaha," and he said: "It is an 'alama," meaning a sign (*'alam*), and he made "al-'alam" feminine, so that it was as if it were a thing set up to be worshipped. The daughter of 'Utayba ibn al-Harith al-Yarbu'i said: [[In the manuscript it reads: "Utayba ibn Shihab al-Yarbu'i," which is an error beyond doubt. In the printed edition it reads: "the daughter of 'Utayba ibn al-Harith al-Yarbu'i," which is correct, a correction by the editor of the first printed edition. The lineage is established by combining what is in the manuscript and the printed edition. She is said to be "Umma bint 'Utayba," and it is also said her name was "Mayya," and she is "Umm al-Banin." It is also said that the poem belongs to a female mourner of 'Utayba.]]

*We returned from al-La'ba' at evening, and hurried the goddess to return.* [[Sources: Balaghat al-nisa' 189; Mu'jam ma sta'jam 1156; Mu'jam al-buldan (al-La'ba'); Lisan al-'Arab (l-'-b; '-l-h), and many others. She is lamenting her father, who was killed on the day of Khuww, slain by the Banu Asad. After the line comes:*

*"Over one like Ibn Mayya, so wail for him, / rending the tunics of soft-skinned women."*

*"And my father 'Utayba was a tough warrior, who would not face (a foe) without taking his share, / A striker with both hands when the war is kindled; not timid, not cowardly."*

*Al-La'ba' lies between al-Rabadha and the land of Banu Sulaym, and it belongs to Fazara; it is said otherwise too. "Qasran" means in the evening. In the printed edition it reads "'asran," which is one of the variant readings of the line; what is in the manuscript is recorded here.]]

She means by "al-ilaha" in this place the sun. It is as if this interpreter, who gave this interpretation, directed "al-ilaha," when the feminine ending is added to it while meaning the singular of "al-alihah" (gods), toward the pattern of their adding the "ha'" in "walidati," "kawkabati," and "ma'ati" [[In the printed edition it reads "amati," which is an error; the correct reading is as in the manuscript.]], which is "ahlat dhak," and as the rajaz poet said: [[I have not identified its speaker.]]

*O Mudar the Red, you are my family,*
*and you are my refuge, and you are my back.*

He means: my back. [[Note: "mulajati" with the hamza softened; its original form is "mulaja'ti," and the taa' is also appended here, in the same way as the saying "mulaja'" — both forms together are evidence for what Abu Ja'far said.]]

* *

Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid have explained what they meant in this meaning in their reading of that as they read it, so there is no basis for the words of this speaker, given their own explanation of what they held regarding the meaning of that.

* *

As for His saying ﴿He said, "We will kill their sons"﴾, meaning: Pharaoh said, "We will kill their male sons from among the children of Israel," ﴿and spare their women﴾, meaning: and keep alive their females [[See the explanation of "al-istihya'" (sparing/keeping alive) earlier, 2:41–48.]], ﴿and we are certainly dominant over them﴾, meaning: and we are exalted over them by domination, that is, by the domination of kingship and authority. [[See the explanation of "al-qahr" (domination) earlier, 11:284, 408.]]

We have already shown that everything that is exalted over something by domination and overpowering, the Arabs say of it: "He is above it" (*huwa fawqahu*). [[See the explanation of "fawq" (above) earlier, 11:284, and the language indices under "fawq."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 128:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Moses said to his people, "Seek help in God and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the good outcome is for the righteous."﴾ (7:128)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Moses said to his people," meaning the Children of Israel, when Pharaoh had said to the chiefs of his people: "We will kill their sons and spare their women": ﴿Seek help in God﴾ against Pharaoh and his people in whatever befalls you of your affairs; "and be patient" over the hardships that have afflicted you in your own selves and your sons at the hands of Pharaoh. Now a group of the Children of Israel had followed Moses, concerning which:

14972 - Abd al-Karim narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the sorcerers believed, six hundred thousand of the Children of Israel followed Moses.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants﴾, He says: Indeed, the earth belongs to God; perhaps God will make you inherit it, if you are patient over the hardship that has befallen you in your own selves and your children at the hands of Pharaoh, and you seek reward for that and remain upright in rectitude, (inheriting) the land of Pharaoh and his people, by destroying them and making you successors in it, for God gives His earth as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾: He says: the praiseworthy outcome belongs to those who fear God and are mindful of Him, fearing Him by avoiding His disobedience and performing His obligations. [[See the explanation of "al-'Aqibah" above: p. 13, note 1, and the references there.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 129:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿They said: "We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us." He said: "It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you will act."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The people of Moses said to Moses, when he said to them, "Seek help in God and be patient": ﴿We were harmed﴾ by the killing of our sons; ﴿before you came to us﴾, meaning: before you came to us with the message of God to us, because Pharaoh used to kill their male children when the time of Moses drew near, as I have already explained earlier in this book of ours. [See what has preceded, 2:41–48.] As for His words, ﴿and after you came to us﴾, meaning: and after you came to us with the message of God, this is because when Pharaoh's sorcerers were defeated, and he said to the chiefs of his people what he said, he intended to renew the punishment upon them by killing their sons and sparing their women.

* *

It has also been said: the people of Moses said this to him when they feared that Pharaoh would overtake them while they were fleeing from him, and when the two hosts had come in sight of each other. They said to him: ﴿O Moses, we were harmed before you came to us﴾, they used to slaughter our sons and spare our women; ﴿and after you came to us﴾, today Pharaoh will overtake us and kill us.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have spoken in accordance with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

* *

14973 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿before you came to us﴾, before God sent you and after.

14974 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14974 – Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: When the two hosts came in sight of each other, the children of Israel looked and saw Pharaoh coming up behind them [("radifahum": following them)], they said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾, and they said: ﴿We were harmed before you came to us﴾, they used to slaughter our sons and spare our women; ﴿and after you came to us﴾, today Pharaoh will overtake us and kill us: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken.﴾ [The report 14974 is part of a long narration which Abu Ja'far divided among various places in his commentary, and he related it in his History 1:214.]

14975 – Abd al-Karim related to me, saying: Ibrahim related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses travelled with the children of Israel until they came upon the sea. They turned around and saw the dust of Pharaoh's beasts, and they said: "O Moses, we were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us. This sea is before us and this is Pharaoh with those who are with him!" He said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you will act.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿He said: "It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy"﴾, May His praise be exalted, means: Moses said to his people: Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy, Pharaoh and his people [see the explanation of "'asa" (perhaps) in what has preceded, 10:405, note 1, and the references there. Then see Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubaydah 1:225; and the explanation of "al-ihlak" (destruction) in the lexical indices under (halaka)]; ﴿and make you successors﴾, meaning: He will make you succeed them in their land after their destruction, so that you will not fear them or anyone else besides them [(2) see the explanation of "al-istikhlaf" (succession) in what has preceded, 12:126]; ﴿and see how you will act﴾, meaning: so your Lord will see what you do after them, of your hastening to obey Him and your reluctance toward it.

The Interpretation of His words: ﴿And We certainly afflicted the people of Pharaoh with years [of drought] and shortage of fruits, that they might remember﴾ [Qur'an 7:130]

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: We tested the people of Pharaoh and his followers in their state of misguidance, "with years," meaning with droughts, year after year, and famine.

* *

It is said of this: "The people became afflicted by drought (asnata al-qawm)," when they suffered drought.

* *

﴿And shortage of fruits﴾: He says: And We tested them, along with the droughts, by the loss of their fruits and produce, except for a little. ﴿That they might remember﴾: He says: as admonition for them and a reminder to them, so that they would desist from their misguidance and turn to their Lord in repentance. [[See the explanation of "al-tadhkira" in the previous lexical indexes under (dh-k-r)]] The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

14976 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿And We certainly afflicted the people of Pharaoh with years﴾, he said: the years of hunger.

14977 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the word of God: ﴿with years﴾, the calamity (al-ja'ihah) = ﴿and shortage of fruits﴾, other than that.

14978 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

14979 - al-Qasim ibn Dinar narrated to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Shaybân, from Abu Ishaq, from Raja' ibn Haywah regarding His words: ﴿and shortage of fruits﴾, he said: when a date palm bears only one date.

14980 - Ibn Waki' narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Raja' ibn Haywah, from Ka'b, who said: A time will come upon people when a date palm bears only one date.

14981 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Raja' ibn Haywah: ﴿and shortage of fruits﴾, he said: A time will come upon people when a date palm bears only one date.

14982 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And We certainly afflicted the people of Pharaoh with years﴾, God afflicted them with years, with hunger, year after year = ﴿and shortage of fruits﴾. As for "the years," that was among their desert dwellers and the people of their livestock; and as for "shortage of fruits," that was in their cities and villages.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 131:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours by right." And if evil struck them, they ascribed it to the ill omen of Moses and those with him.﴾ (131)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may He be exalted, means: when the people of Pharaoh received well-being, fertility, ease, and abundance of fruits, and saw what they loved in their worldly affairs [[See the explanation of "al-hasanah" (good) in the earlier lexical indices, under (h-s-n).]], ﴿they said, "This is ours by right"﴾, meaning: we are more deserving of it. ﴿And if evil struck them﴾, meaning drought, famine, and calamity [[See the explanation of "al-sayyi'ah" (evil) in the earlier lexical indices, under (s-w-'').]], ﴿they ascribed it to the ill omen of Moses and those with him﴾, meaning: they considered it an omen of misfortune and said: our shares of ease, fertility, and well-being have gone since Moses, peace be upon him, came to us.

* *

Those who held views similar to what we have said on this matter are the scholars of interpretation.

Mention of those who said so:

14983 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿But when good came to them﴾, well-being and ease; ﴿they said, "This is ours by right"﴾, we are more entitled to it; ﴿And if evil struck them﴾, affliction and punishment; ﴿they ascribed it to the ill omen﴾, they considered it an omen of misfortune from Moses.

14984 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with similar wording.

14985 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours by right." And if evil struck them, they ascribed it to the ill omen of Moses and those with him﴾: They said: "This has befallen us only because of you, O Moses, and those with you.
