We have seen no evil until we saw you!" And regarding His saying: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours by right"﴾, he said: the good is what they love. And when what they dislike came, they said: "This has befallen us only because of the ill omen of these wrongdoers!" The people of Salih said: ﴿We see an omen of ill in you and those with you﴾, and God said: ﴿Their omen is with God; rather, you are a people being tested﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 47]. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "innama tairukum" with the addition of "innama", which is an error; that is a different verse.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Surely their omen is with God, but most of them do not know﴾ (131)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may He be exalted, means: Surely the omen of the people of Pharaoh and others is nothing but with God, which means their shares of ease, fertility, and other shares of good and evil, ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ that this is so; and because of their ignorance of this, they used to ascribe their misfortunes to Moses and those with him.

* *

Those who held views similar to what we have said on this matter are the scholars of interpretation.

Mention of those who said so:

14986 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Surely their omen is with God﴾, he said: their calamities are with God. God said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

14987 - Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Surely their omen is with God﴾, he said: the matter is from God's decree.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 132 (part 1 of 3):**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will never believe you."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The family of Pharaoh said to Musa, "O Musa, whatever sign or proof you bring us," "to enchant us" means "to turn us away by it from the religion of Pharaoh in which we are," ﴿so we will never believe you﴾ means "so we will not, in this matter, confirm that you are right in what you call us to."

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of "sihr" (magic) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "al-sihr" above, p. 27, note 3, and the references there.]]

* * *

Ibn Zayd used to say, regarding the meaning of ﴿whatever sign you bring us﴾, about "ma" (whatever):

14988 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: [Ibn Wahb informed us], saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿whatever sign you bring us﴾: he said, "Indeed, what you bring us of a sign." This [reading] includes the additional "ma." [[The report 14988: the addition between the brackets is necessary; this is a circular chain (isnad dā'ir) found in the tafsir, the nearest instance of which is no. 14985. This is only an error of the copyist.]]

* * *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Then We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "al-tufan" (the flood). Some of them said: it is water.

Those who said this:

14989 – Ibn Waki' narrated to me, saying: Habwayh Abu Yazid narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa came with the signs, the first of the signs was the flood, so God sent the sky upon them. [[Report 14989: "Habwayh" – "Abu Yazid" is Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi; it occurred as nos. 14365, 14550, 14956. In the printed edition it was "Habwayh al-Razi," which is correct, but the editor misread the manuscript and changed it; the manuscript read "Habwayh Abu Mazid." The correct reading is what I have given.]]

14990 – Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Malik, who said: "al-tufan" is water.

14991 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "al-tufan" is water.

14992 – ... narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-tufan" is drowning.

14993 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "al-tufan" is water, and "al-ta'un" (plague) is death in every case. [[It is probably that the correct wording is: "and the plague is death in every case."]]

14994 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "al-tufan" is death in every case.

14995 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-tufan" is water.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it is death.

Those who said this:

14996 – Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: al-Minhal ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam ibn Maynā', from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The tufan is death." [[Report 14996: "al-Minhal ibn Khalifa al-'Ijli," Abu Qudama; he is subject to criticism. Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim declared him weak. al-Bukhari said: "Acceptable, but questionable"; and he said elsewhere: "His hadith is munkar" (rejected). Ibn Hibban said: "He used to be alone in transmitting rejected reports from well-known narrators." Translated from al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/12, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/357, and Mizan al-I'tidal 3:204. "al-Hajjaj" is al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'a, who has occurred many times. "al-Hakam ibn Maynā' al-Ansari" is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). Translated from al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/340, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/127. This report is recorded by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3:536 from this same place, and he said: "Likewise it was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Yahya ibn Yaman with this chain, and it is a gharib (strange) hadith." I say: he attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See the following report, no. 15000.]]

14997 – 'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I asked 'Ata': "What is the tufan?" He said: "Death." [[Report 14997: "'Abbas ibn Muhammad" is 'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Duri, the teacher of al-Tabari, occurring as no. 7701.]]

14998 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from someone who narrated to him, from Mujahid, who said: "al-tufan" is death.

14999 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, concerning ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, who said: death. Ibn Juraij said: And I asked 'Ata' about "al-tufan," and he said: death. Ibn Juraij said: And Mujahid said: Death in every case.

15000 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Khalifa, from Hajjaj, from a man, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "al-tufan is death." [[Report 15000: This is another chain for the report no. 14996, except that the narrator from 'A'isha is left unnamed there, and he is named as "al-Hakam ibn Maynā'" in that report. The takhrij of this report and the explanation of its weakness have already passed.]]

Others said: Rather, that was a command from God that swept over them.

Those who said this:

15001 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, who said: "The command of God, the tufan," then he recited ﴿Then there swept over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep﴾ [al-Qalam: 19].

* * *

Some people of knowledge of the Arabic language, from the people of Basra [[This is Abu 'Ubayda, in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:226.]], claimed that "al-tufan" is from the torrent: "al-ba'iq" and "al-dubash," which is the severe [flood]. [[al-Ba'iq" (with a damma on the ba'): is abundant, heavy rain that pours down with water, i.e., flows with a thick torrent. And "sayl dubash" (with a damma on the dal) is a great torrent that sweeps away everything with force.]] And [it is used for] death that is widespread, grievous, and swift. [[In the manuscript: "al-mutaba'" (the successive); in Majaz al-Qur'an: "al-mubalagh" (the extreme); and in the printed edition "al-mutatabi'" (the successive). I have preferred the text of Abu 'Ubayda.]]

* * *

Some said: It is abundant rain and wind.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: "al-tufan" is a verbal noun (masdar) like "al-rujhan" and "al-nuqsan," which has no plural.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is a plural, whose singular by analogy would be "al-tufana." [[This is al-Akhfash. Ibn Sida said: "al-Akhfash is trustworthy, and when a trustworthy person transmits something, accepting it is required."]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is what Ibn 'Abbas said, according to what Abu Zabyan narrated from him [[meaning report no. 15001]], that it was a command from God that swept over them. It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "The command of God swept over them, sweeping (yatufu) a tufan," just as it is said: "This thing diminished (naqasa) a diminution (nuqsan)." When this is so, it is permissible that what swept over them was a severe rain, and it is permissible that it was a grievous death. As evidence that heavy rain may also be called "tufan," there is the saying of Husayl ibn 'Urfuta [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-Hasan ibn 'Urfuta," which is an error. Abu Hatim said: "Husayn ibn 'Urfuta," which is also an error. See Nawadir Abi Zayd, 75, 77. He is Husayl ibn 'Urfuta al-Asadi, a pre-Islamic poet.]]:

"The newness of its signs was changed by the rending winds and the tufan of rain."

[[Nawadir Abi Zayd: 77; al-Wasata: 329; Lisan (twf). The line preceding it is: "The truth was not that the trace of a dwelling was stirring him, which had been effaced by the sirar." Abu Hatim said: "bi-l-sirar" with fatha on the sin and the ra. "al-Kharq" are the cuts (gusts) of wind; its singular is "kharqa." "Tufan al-matar" is its abundance. Al-Asma'i narrated "kharq" (meaning with damma on the kha' and the ra'). This is the exact text of what is in Nawadir Abi Zayd. "Kharq" (with two dammas) is the plural of "kharīq," which is a strong wind that blows and penetrates places.]]

And it is narrated as:

"The gusts of wind with the tufan of rain."

And the saying of al-Ra'i [[Lisan (nkth) (z'd). Perhaps it is from his poetry in which he praised 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan (see Khizanat al-Adab 3:288). "al-Nakã'ith" is the plural of "nakītha," which is the exertion of the soul's strength. It is said: "So-and-so is of severe nakītha," meaning of soul. It is also said: "His nakītha reached" (in the passive), meaning: his effort exhausted him. "Balagh fulan nakītha bi'īrihi" means: he pushed his camel's effort to the limit in travelling. "al-Zu'd" (with damma on the hamza or with sukun) means fright and fear. "Kharqā'" is an adjective for a she-camel, meaning the one that does not take care of the places of her legs because of her vigour. He describes her as sharp, as if she were mad, when the camels are weary, her strength remains and her surplus vigour persists.]]:

"She becomes, when the camels reach their nakã'ith, a wild she-camel frequented by the tufan and the zu'd."

And the saying of Abu al-Najm [[I did not find it elsewhere. "al-Sha'ayib" is the plural of "sha'ubub," which is a single burst of rain. It is said: "shaʾāʾib" is not said of rain unless there is hail in it.]]:

"A tufan has extended, and scattered its extent, for a month in showers, and for a month in hail."

* * *

As for "al-qummal" (lice), the people of interpretation differed about its meaning.

Some of them said: It is the weevil that emerges from wheat.

Those who said this:

15002 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-qummal" is the weevil that emerges from wheat.

15003 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id in similar words.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it is "al-dabā," which is small locusts that have no wings.

Those who said this:

15004 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā.

15005 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: al-dabā is al-qummal.

15006 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā.

15007 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā.

15008 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā, and they are the young of the locust.

15009 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā.

15010 – ... narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Qays, from someone he mentioned, from 'Ikrima, who said: "al-qummal" is the daughters of the locust.

15011 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-qummal" is al-dabā.

* * *

Others said: Rather, "al-qummal" is fleas.

Those who said this:

15012 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, and the lice﴾: he said: "Some people claim that the lice are fleas."

* * *

Some said: They are small black creatures.

Those who said this:

15013 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan say: "al-qummal" are small black creatures.

* * *

Some people of knowledge of the Arabic language, from the people of Basra, claimed [[This is Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:226.]] that "al-qummal," according to the Arabs, is "al-hamnan" – and "al-hamnan" is a kind of tick, whose singular is "hamnana," above the "qamqama." [[al-Qamqama" is the small ticks (plural of qurrād), which are at their first stage, small, scarcely seen because of their size; it is also a kind of lice that clings strongly to the roots of hair.]] And "al-qammal" is a plural, whose singular is "qamla," which is a creature resembling lice, which camels eat, as I have been told, and it is what al-A'sha meant in his saying: [[In the printed edition: "al-A'mash," which is a printing error.]]

"A people treating their sons with lice, and with chains, unbroken, and a door closed tight."

[[His Diwan: 154; Lisan (qml). From his ode which he said to Kisra when he demanded of the clan of Dubay'a (the Ash'a's kin) hostages, when al-Harith ibn Wa'la raided some of the countryside (al-sawad) and Kisra seized Qays ibn Mas'ud and whoever he found of Bakr, and began to imprison them. Al-A'sha said to him:

"Who will convey to Kisra, when he comes to him as a hostage, from me, his camels, torn-ears, scattered..."

"We have sworn that we will not give him any of our sons as hostages, for he would corrupt them as he corrupted men before."

"Until he gives you from his sons a hostage: Na'sh, and the Simak will take the Farqad as hostage from you."

He means: whoever conveys to Kisra from me, something that angers him, messages come to him from every direction: that we have sworn not to give him any of our sons as hostages, which he would take charge of corrupting, as he corrupted some men before, and he will not obtain that from us until stars of the heavens give him hostages from their companions. Then he said to him:

"We are not like those whom Iyad made their home at Takrit, preventing its grain from being harvested..."

"A people treating [their sons with lice]..."

"God has made our food from our wealth a provision that He has guaranteed us and which will never run out."

He means: We are not like Iyad, which gave you hostages, for they dwelt in Takrit watching what was harvested from the crops from year to year; they were ploughmen, who had become infested with lice, so their sons stood treating the lice, dragging chains to tie them to the threshing floors, and striving to lock their doors. As for us, God has made our camels our provision; their milk guarantees us food that never runs out, and we have removed from our necks the yoke of servitude to towns and cities, for the freedom of the desert, where we go out and return, and you have no authority over us. This is from the poetry of the free Arabs. "al-Ajd" (with two dammas) means: the strong, firmly bound. It is said: "a camel that is ajd," strong and firmly built. And "a camel mu'ajjada al-qurā" is like that. It is also said: "Praise be to God who strengthened me (ājadanī) after weakness," meaning: gave me strength. "al-Mu'sad" from "awṣada al-bāb" means he closed it and shut it tight, so it is "mūṣad" and "mu'sad" with hamza. Similarly is His saying, may He be remembered: ﴿indeed it is closed over them﴾ with hamza, meaning sealed tight.]]

Al-Farra' used to say: I have not heard anything about it. If it is not a plural, then its singular is "qāmil," like "sājid" and "rākiʿ" [[In the printed edition: "If it is not a plural," with the addition of "lam," which corrupts the sense; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]], and if it is a noun with the meaning of a plural, then its singular is "qamla." [[I did not find this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an at this place of the tafsir of the verse. See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:393, where he says: "al-qummal is al-dabā that has no wings," and he added nothing more.]]

* * *

**Mention of the states that befell the people of Pharaoh through the occurrence of these signs, and the reason for which God brought them upon them.**

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 132 (part 2 of 3):

15014 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Musa came to Fir'awn, he said to him: "Send the Children of Israel with me!" But he refused. So God sent upon them the *tufan* (the flood), which is rain, and it poured down on them some of it. They feared it was a punishment, so they said to Musa: "Call upon your Lord to remove the rain from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you" [[(3) In the printed edition: "Call upon your Lord, that if You remove the *rijz* from us, we will surely believe in you and surely send the Children of Israel with you," which differs from the manuscript, and the verse text is not written out (Surat al-A'raf: 134). The manuscript had what I have recorded, except that it wrote: "If the rain is removed from us, you will believe in him," and the correct wording is what I have given, God willing.]]. So he called upon his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. Then He made grow for them that year something that had not grown before: crops, fruit and pasture. They said: "This is what we used to wish for!" So God sent the locusts, and He set them upon the pasture. When they saw its effect on the pasture, they knew that the crops would not survive. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the locusts from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. They threshed the grain and gathered it into their houses [[(*Dās al-nās al-ḥabb*) means they threshed the grain. (*Aḥraza al-shay'*) means he gathered it, preserved it and guarded it from being taken.]]. They said: "We have secured it," so God sent upon them the *qummal* (the lice), which is the weevil that emerges from grain. A man would bring ten *ajriba* (sacks) to the mill, and not get back from them three *aqfiza* (measures). They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the lice from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. Then, while he was sitting with Fir'awn, he heard the croaking of a frog. He said to Fir'awn: "What do you and your people face from this?" He replied: "What could the scheming of this man possibly be!" They had not finished the evening before a man was sitting with frogs up to his chin, and when he wanted to speak, the frogs would leap into his mouth. They said to Musa: "Call upon your Lord to remove these frogs from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" [So He removed them from them, but they did not believe] [[What is between the brackets is not in the manuscript. In the manuscript at this point there is the letter (ṭ) between "Isra'il" and "fa-arsala," and another (ṭ) in the margin, indicating an error. What is in the printed edition is correct, God willing.]]. Then God sent upon them *al-dam* (the blood). Whatever they drew from rivers and wells, or what was in their vessels, they found to be fresh blood. They complained to Fir'awn, saying: "We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink!" He said: "He has indeed bewitched you!" They said: "How could he have bewitched us, when we find nothing in our vessels of water but fresh blood?" So they came to him and said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

15015 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Habwaya Abu Yazid narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When they feared drowning, Fir'awn said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove this rain from us, and we will believe in you." Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Humayd, from Ya'qub. [[The report 15015: Habwaya, Abu Yazid, is Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi. It has passed under numbers 14365, 14550, 14956, and 14989. In the printed edition here it reads "Habwaba al-Razi," and the correct form is from the manuscript and from the verification of this in the numbers I have mentioned above.]]

15016 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then God sent upon them, meaning upon the people of Fir'awn, the *tufan*, which is rain, and it drowned everything they had. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove it from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So God removed it from them, [[(1) In the printed edition: "So God removed it from them." I have kept what is in the manuscript and in the history.]] and their crops grew by it. They said: "We are not pleased that we were not rained upon." So God sent the locusts upon them, and they ate their crops. They asked Musa to call upon his Lord to remove it, and they would believe in Him. He called, and He removed it, but some of their crops remained. They said: "You have not kept faith, for some of our crops remain that are enough for us?" So God sent upon them the *daba* (the lice), which is the *qummal*, and it licked the whole earth [[(2) "The locust licked the plants" means when it eats them and leaves nothing of them. From this, the harsh years of drought are called *al-lawahis* (the licking years), because they lick everything.]]. It would enter between one's garment and skin and bite him. If someone had food, it would become full of lice. One of them would build a column with plaster and make it so slippery that nothing could climb it, and he would put his food on top of it. When he climbed up to eat it, he would find it full of lice. They were not afflicted with any calamity more severe than the lice, which is the *rijz* that God mentions in the Qur'an as having befallen them. They asked Musa to call upon his Lord to remove it from them, and they would believe in Him. When it was removed from them, they refused to believe. So God sent upon them the *dam* (blood). A Israelite and a Qibti (Egyptian) would come to draw water from the same source, and the Qibti's water would come out as blood, while the Israelite's water would come out as water. When this grew severe upon them, they asked Musa to remove it, and they would believe in Him. It was removed, but they refused to believe. That is when God says: ﴿Then when We removed the torment from them, behold, they broke their word﴾ [Al-Zukhruf: 50]. [[The report 15016: It is part of a long report narrated by Abu Ja'far in his *Tarikh* 1:211, 212.]]

15017 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, he said: God sent upon them water until they stood in it up to their feet. Then it was removed from them, but they did not believe. [[In the manuscript: "Then it was removed from them, but they did not benefit." I left what is in the printed edition as it is, because of his saying in another report: "but they did not believe either."]] Their lands became abundantly fertile, more than they had ever been. Then God sent upon them the locusts, which ate everything except a little, but they still did not believe. Then God sent the *qummal*, which is the *daba*, and which are the young of locusts, and they ate what remained of their crops, but they did not believe. Then He sent upon them the frogs, which entered their houses and fell into their vessels and bedding, but they did not believe. Then God sent upon them the blood, so that whenever one of them wanted to drink, that water turned to blood. God said: ﴿Clear signs, detailed﴾.

15018 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, until ﴿criminals﴾. He said: God sent upon them water until they stood in it up to their feet. They called upon Musa, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the evil that was coming upon them. Then their land produced. Then God sent upon them the locusts, which ate most of their crops and fruit. Then they called upon Musa, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the worst of what was coming upon them. God sent upon them the lice, this *daba* that you have seen, and it ate what the locusts had left of their crops, and licked it. They called upon Musa, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the worst of what was coming upon them. Then God sent upon them the frogs, until they filled their houses and courtyards. They called upon Musa, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the worst of what was coming upon them. So God sent upon them the blood, and they could not scoop anything from their water except red blood. It is mentioned that the enemy of God, Fir'awn, would bring together two men over a single vessel, a Qibti and an Israelite, and what was on the Israelite's side was water, while what was on the Qibti's side was blood. They called upon Musa, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, in nine signs: the years of drought, the shortage of fruits, and He showed them the hand of Musa (peace be upon him) and his staff.

15019 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, which is rain, until they feared destruction. They came to Musa and said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the rain from us, [that we believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the rain from them]" [[In the manuscript, what is between the brackets was omitted, and restoring it is necessary for the sense.]]. So God made their crops grow by it, and their lands became fertile by it. They said: "We do not like that we were not rained upon, by abandoning our religion. We will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you!" So God sent the locusts upon them, which quickly spread destruction to their fruits and crops. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord [to remove the locusts from us, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!]" [[What is between the brackets is not in the manuscript.]]. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them. Some remnants of their crops and livelihood remained, and they said: "What remains for us is enough for us, so we will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you." So God sent upon them the *qummal*, which is the *daba*, and it hunted down what the locusts had left, and they became distressed and felt destruction. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the *daba* from us, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the *daba* from them. They said: "We will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you!" So God sent upon them the frogs, which filled their houses with them, and they suffered from them a severe harm the like of which they had not suffered before. They would leap into their pots and spoil their food, and extinguish their fires. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the frogs from us, for we have suffered from them affliction and harm, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the frogs from them. They said: "We will not believe in you, nor send the Children of Israel with you!" So God sent upon them the blood, and they could eat nothing but blood, nor drink anything but blood. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the blood from us, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the blood from them. They said: "O Musa, we will not believe in you, nor send the Children of Israel with you!" So these were clear, detailed signs, one following another, so that God's proof would be established against them. Then God seized them for their sins and drowned them in the sea.

15020 - 'Abd al-Karim narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God sent upon the people of Fir'awn the signs: the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, clear detailed signs. He said: A man from the Children of Israel would ride in a boat with a man from the people of Fir'awn, and the Israelite would scoop up water, while the Pharaonic would scoop up blood. He said: The man from the people of Fir'awn would sleep on one side, and the lice and frogs would gather so heavily on him that he could not turn over onto the other side. They continued like this until God revealed to Musa: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."

15021 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa came to Fir'awn with the message, he refused to believe and to send the Children of Israel with him. He was arrogant and said: "I will not send the Children of Israel with you!" [[In the printed edition: "we will not send," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]. So God sent upon them the *tufan*, which is water. He rained upon them from the sky until they nearly perished, and everything from their lands was prevented. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord by the covenant He has with you. If You remove this from us, we will surely believe in you and surely send the Children of Israel with you!" So he called upon God, and He removed the rain from them. God made their crops grow for them, and by that rain brought every thing in their lands to life. They said: "By God, we do not like that we had not been rained upon by this rain, and it was better for us. We will not send the Children of Israel with you, and we will not believe in you, O Musa!" So God sent the locusts upon them, which ate most of their crops, and the locusts spread quickly in their destruction. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the locusts from us, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" So God removed the locusts from them. The locusts had left a remnant of their crops, and they said: "What remains of our crops is enough for us, so we will not abandon our religion, and we will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you!" So God sent upon them the *qummal*, and "*al-qummal*" is the *daba*, which is the locust that has no wings. It tracked down what remained of their crops, trees, and every plant they had. The *qummal* was more severe upon them than the locusts, and they could find no way to deal with the *qummal*, and they became distressed by it. They came to Musa and said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord to remove the *qummal* from us, for it has left us nothing. It has eaten what remained of our crops. If you remove the *qummal* from us, we will surely believe in you, and surely send the Children of Israel with you!" So God removed the *qummal* from them, but they broke their word and said: "We will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you!" So God sent the frogs upon them, and their houses were filled with them. No food or drink remained that did not have frogs in it. They suffered from them something they had not suffered before. They said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord. If You remove the *rijz* from us, we will surely believe in you and surely send the Children of Israel with you!" He said: So God removed it from them, but they did not keep their word. Then God revealed: ﴿But when We removed from them the torment until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word﴾, up to ﴿and they were heedless of them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 135–136].

15022 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Zayd, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The frogs were wild, but when God sent them upon the family of Fir'awn, they obeyed and complied. They began drowning themselves in the pots while they were boiling, and in the ovens while they were blazing. So God rewarded them for their good obedience with the coolness of water.

15023 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The enemy of God, meaning Fir'awn, returned defeated and bound when the magicians believed, but he refused to remain anything but in disbelief, and persisted in evil. So God followed up upon him with the signs, and seized him with the years of drought. He sent upon him the *tufan*, then the locusts, then the lice, then the frogs, then the blood, clear detailed signs. He sent the *tufan*, which is water, and it overflowed over the face of the earth and then stagnated. They could not plow or do anything, until they were afflicted with hunger. When this reached them, they said: "O Musa, call upon your Lord. If You remove the *rijz* from us, we will surely believe in you and surely send the Children of Israel with you!" Musa called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not keep any of their promises. So God sent the locusts upon them, and they ate the trees, so I have been told, until it would even eat the iron nails of the doors, until their houses and dwellings fell. They said what they had said before. He called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not keep any of their promises. So God sent the lice upon them. It was reported to me that Musa was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. He went to a great, crumbling sand dune [[(*Kathīb ahyal*) on the pattern of *af'al*: a loose heap whose sand does not hold until it collapses.]] and struck it with it, and the lice poured down upon them [[(*Inthāl al-turāb*) means the dust poured down, flowing from every direction.]], until they overwhelmed the houses and the food, and prevented them from sleeping and resting. When it had worn them out, they said to him what they had said. He called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not keep any of their promises. So God sent the frogs upon them, which filled the houses, the food, and the vessels, so that no one could uncover a garment, food, or vessel without finding frogs overwhelming it. When this had worn them out, they said to him what they had said, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not keep any of their promises. So God sent the blood upon them, and the waters of the family of Fir'awn became blood. They could not draw water from a well or a river, nor scoop anything from a vessel, without it turning into fresh blood. [[The report 15023: Abu Ja'far narrated this report in his *Tarikh* 1:215.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 132 (part 3 of 3):

15024 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that he was told that the woman from the family of Pharaoh used to come to a woman from the Children of Israel when thirst afflicted them, and say: "Give me to drink from your water!" So she would scoop for her from her jar, or pour for her from her waterskin, and it would turn into blood in the vessel. Indeed, she would say to her: "Put it in your mouth, then spit it into my mouth!" So she would take water into her mouth, and when she spat it into her (the Pharaonic woman's) mouth, it became blood. They remained in that for seven days. [[Narration 15024: Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) transmitted this report at length in his History, 1: 215, 216.]]

15025 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: The locusts would eat their crops and plants, the frogs would fall upon their bedding and food, and the blood would be in their houses, their clothes, their water and their food.

= He said: Shibl related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: When the Nile flowed with blood, the Israelite would draw pure water, while the Egyptian would draw blood; and they would share one vessel, so that the part nearest the Israelite was pure water and the part nearest the Egyptian was blood.

15026 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me: When Moses confronted Pharaoh with the four signs: the staff, the hand, the shortage of fruits, and the years = he said: "O Lord, this servant of Yours has exalted himself in the land, transgressed in the land, rebelled against me, exalted himself over You, and raised himself up with his people. Lord, seize Your servant with a punishment that You make a vengeance upon him and his people, and make it a warning to my people, and a sign for those after me among the nations that remain!" So God sent upon them the flood = and it is the water = and the houses of the Children of Israel and the houses of the Copts were intertwined and mixed together, one with another; so the houses of the Copts filled with water, until they stood in the water up to their collarbones; whoever sat down among them drowned. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "whoever was detained (min habas)", and the correct reading is what is established here.]] Not a drop entered the houses of the Children of Israel. So the Copts began calling out to Moses: "Pray to your Lord by what He has promised you! If you remove the plague from us, we will surely believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" He said: So they made a covenant with Moses, a pact by which he took their oaths, and the water seized them on Saturday, and it remained over them for seven days until the next Saturday. Moses prayed to his Lord, and the water was lifted from them, and their lands grew green from that water, and they remained a month in well-being. Then they denied and said: "This water was only a blessing upon us and a fertility for our lands; we do not wish that it had not been." = He said: Someone said to Ibn Abbas: "I asked Ibn Umar about the flood, and he said: 'I do not know, was it death or water?'" Ibn Abbas said: "Does Ibn Umar not read Surah al-Ankabut, when God mentioned the people of Noah and said: ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 14]? Tell me: if they had died, to whom did Moses, peace be upon him, bring the four signs after the flood?"

= He said: Moses said: "O Lord, Your servants have broken Your covenant and failed my promise. Lord, seize them with a punishment that You make a vengeance upon them, and a warning to my people, and a sign for those after them among the nations that remain!" He said: So God sent upon them the locusts, and they left them no leaf, no tree, no flower, and no fruit without devouring it, until they left no produce; and when they had consumed all the greens, they ate the wood, until they ate the doors and the roofs of the houses. The locusts were afflicted with hunger, so that they never became full, except that they did not enter the houses of the Children of Israel. So they cried out and shouted to Moses, and said: "O Moses, this time pray to your Lord by what He has promised you! If you remove the plague from us, we will surely believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!" They gave him the covenant and pledge of God, so he prayed to his Lord, and God removed the locusts from them after they had remained upon them seven days from Saturday to Saturday. Then they remained a month in well-being; then they returned to their denial and their rejection, and to their evil deeds. He said: Moses said: "O Lord, Your servants have broken my covenant and failed my appointment; so seize them with a punishment that You make a vengeance upon them, and a warning to my people, and a sign for those after me among the nations that remain!" So God sent upon them the lice = Abu Bakr said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan saying: Beside them was a reddish sand dune in a village of Egypt called "Ayn Shams", [[The sand dune "al-kathib al-a'far" here means the red one.]] so Moses walked to that dune and struck it with his staff, a single strike, and it became lice that crawled toward them = and they are small black creatures. The lice crawled upon them, and they took their hair, their skin, the lashes of their eyes and their eyebrows, and clung to their skins as if it were smallpox upon them; so they cried out and shouted to Moses: "We repent and will not return, so pray to your Lord for us!" He prayed to his Lord, and He removed the lice from them after they had remained upon them seven days from Saturday to Saturday. They remained a month in well-being, then they returned and said: "We were never more entitled to be certain that he is a sorcerer than we are today: he made the sand into creatures! By the might of Pharaoh, we will never believe him or follow him!" So they returned to their denial and rejection. Moses prayed against them and said: "O Lord, Your servants have broken my covenant and failed my promise, so seize them with a punishment that You make a vengeance upon them, and a warning to my people, and a sign for those after me among the nations that remain!" So God sent upon them the frogs; one of them would lie down, and the frogs would mount him and pile up upon him, until he could not turn to the other side, and when he opened his mouth to eat a morsel, the frog would get to his mouth before his morsel did; and no dough would be kneaded without the frogs being squashed into it [[In the printed edition: "tushdakhat" with sh and kh, which has no meaning here; in the manuscript it is undotted and this appears to be the correct reading. One says "sadaha al-shay'" when one spreads it on the ground or lays it down; "insadaha al-rajul" means he lay on his back and spread his legs. The phrase "tasaddaha" (with a doubled dal) is a sound Arabic form.]], and no pot would be cooked without being filled with frogs. So they were tormented by them with the most severe torment, and they complained to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: "This time we repent and will not return!" So he took their covenant and pledge. Then he prayed to his Lord, and God removed the frogs from them after they had remained upon them seven days from Saturday to Saturday. They remained a month in well-being, then they returned to their denial and rejection and said: "It has become clear to you his sorcery: he makes the dust into creatures and brings frogs without water!" So they harmed Moses, peace be upon him, and Moses said: "O Lord, Your servants have broken my covenant and failed my promise, so seize them with a punishment that makes it a punishment for them, and a warning to my people, and a sign for those after me among the nations that remain!" Then God afflicted them with blood, which spoiled their livelihoods, so that the Israelite and the Copt would come to the Nile to draw water; the Israelite would draw water and the Copt would draw blood. They would go to the jar, in which there was water, and the Israelite would get water in his vessel while the Copt got blood. [[al-Hubb (with a dammah on the h): the large jar in which water is kept.]]

15027 - Al-Harith related to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: Abu Sa'd related to us, he said: I heard Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, say: "Death." "And the locusts": he said: The locusts would eat their goods, their clothes, and the nails of their doors. "And the lice" is the dabba (a kind of locust-like insect), which God sent upon them after the locusts. He said: "And the frogs", which would fall into their food in their houses and into their drinks. [[Narration 15027: "Abu Sa'd al-Madani"; in the manuscript and printed edition it reads "Ibn Sa'd", which is an error; it is the chain that has occurred repeatedly, the nearest being no. 14916.]]

* *

Some of them said: The "blood" which God sent upon them was nosebleeds (ru'af).
Those who said that:

15028 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Khalid related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr related to us, he said: Zuhayr related to us, he said: Zayd ibn Aslam said: As for "the lice," then the lice; and as for "the blood," God sent upon them nosebleeds. [[Narration 15028: "Ahmad ibn Khalid" appears to be Ahmad ibn Khalid ibn Musa al-Wahbi, listed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/49; "Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr al-Asadi," who has occurred many times, the last being no. 7544; "Zuhayr" is Zuhayr ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, occurring as no. 5230, 6628.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Clear signs (ayat mufassalat)﴾, its meaning is: signs and indications of the truth of Moses' prophethood [[See the explanation of "ayah" in the language indexes, under the root (a-y-y)]] and the reality of what he called them to, "detailed (mufassalat)": they were distinguished from one another, so that some followed others and some came one after another. [[See also the explanation of "tafsil" in the earlier volume 12: 477, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this.
Those who said that:

15029 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "So there were clear signs, some following others, so that the proof would be God's against them; and God seized them for their sins and drowned them in the sea."

15030 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿Clear signs﴾: he said: one following another, so that God's proof would be against them, and then He would take vengeance upon them. The sign would remain among them from Saturday to Saturday and would be lifted from them for a month. God the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So We took vengeance upon them and drowned them in the sea﴾ [al-A'raf: 136] ... the verse.

15031 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿Clear signs (mufassalat)﴾: that is, one sign after another, one following another. [[Narration 15031: This is a fragment of the earlier report no. 15023, which Abu Ja'far removed from the main text and presented separately here. In the History, 1: 215, he related the report continuously, including this phrase of interpretation.]]

* *

Mujahid used to say, as reported from him, regarding the meaning of "mufassalat":

15032 - Al-Harith related to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: Abu Sa'd related to us, he said: I heard Mujahid say regarding "clear signs (mufassalat)": "Known (ma'lumat)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 133–134:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So they waxed proud, and they were a guilty people (133)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: So these people, upon whom God sent the signs and proofs mentioned in these verses, waxed proud against faith in God and in confirming His messenger Musa (ﷺ) and following what he called them to, and they exalted themselves against God and transgressed against Him [[See the explanation of "istikbar" (arrogance) above, 12:561, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿and they were a guilty people﴾, meaning: they were a people who committed what God hates of sins and wickedness, out of rebellion and defiance. [[See the explanation of "ijram" (guilt) above, 12:207, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when the punishment (rijz) fell upon them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you" (134)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: "And when the punishment fell upon them", that is, when the chastisement of God descended upon them and His wrath settled on them.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning that "rijz" (punishment) which God informed had fallen upon these people.

Some of them said: It was plague (ta'un).

Those who said so:

15033 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: And Musa commanded his people from the Children of Israel – and that was after the people of Pharaoh had come with the five signs: the flood and what God mentioned in this verse – but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with him. So he said: Let every man among you slaughter a ram, then let him dip his palm in its blood, then let him strike it upon his door! The Copts said to the Children of Israel: Why do you smear this blood upon your doors? They said: Indeed God is sending a punishment upon you, so we will be saved and you will perish. The Copts said: Does God recognize you only by these signs? They said: Thus our Prophet commanded us! So they awoke, and seventy thousand of the people of Pharaoh had been stabbed, and by evening they were not burying one another. Then Pharaoh said at that point: ﴿Pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us﴾, and it was the plague, ﴿we will surely believe in you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you﴾. So he prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them. Pharaoh was the first of them all to break his word, and he said to Musa: Go with the Children of Israel wherever you wish.

15034 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Huwayh al-Razi and Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr – Huwayh said, from Ibn Abbas – ﴿If you remove the punishment from us﴾: he said: It is the plague.

* *

Others said: It is the chastisement.

Those who said so:

15035 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The punishment (rijz)" is the chastisement.

15036 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15037 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Then when We removed from them the punishment﴾, that is, the chastisement.

15038 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, he said: the chastisement.

15039 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, he said: "The punishment" is the chastisement which God sent upon them of locusts, lice and other things, and they covenanted with Him for all of that, then they broke their covenant.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "rijz" earlier in this book, with its sufficient evidences so that we need not repeat them. [[See the explanation of "rijz" above, 2:116–118 / 12:521.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this place is to say that God, exalted is His remembrance, informed concerning Pharaoh and his people that when the punishment fell upon them – and it is the chastisement and the wrath of God upon them – they fled to Musa, asking him to pray to his Lord to remove it from them. It is possible that this "rijz" was the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, since all of that was a punishment upon them. And it is possible that this "rijz" was the plague, but God has not told us which of these it was, nor has any report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) been authentically transmitted about which it was, so that we would submit to it. So the correct course is to say concerning it as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, and not to go beyond that except with clarification on which the people of interpretation have no dispute, namely that when the chastisement and wrath of God descended upon them.

* *

= ﴿They said: O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you﴾, meaning: by what He has charged you and commanded you with. [[See the explanation of "ahd" (covenant) above, p. 10, note 2, and the references there.]] We have already explained the meaning of "ahd" earlier.

* *

= ﴿If you remove the punishment from us﴾, meaning: if you lift from us the chastisement we are in [[See the explanation of "kashf" (removal) above, 11:354.]] ﴿we will surely believe in you﴾, meaning: we will surely confirm what you have brought and called to, and we will surely affirm it for you = ﴿and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you﴾, meaning: we will surely let the Children of Israel go with you, and not prevent them from going wherever they wish.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 133–134:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So they waxed proud, and they were a guilty people (133)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: So these people, upon whom God sent the signs and proofs mentioned in these verses, waxed proud against faith in God and in confirming His messenger Musa (ﷺ) and following what he called them to, and they exalted themselves against God and transgressed against Him [[See the explanation of "istikbar" (arrogance) above, 12:561, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿and they were a guilty people﴾, meaning: they were a people who committed what God hates of sins and wickedness, out of rebellion and defiance. [[See the explanation of "ijram" (guilt) above, 12:207, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when the punishment (rijz) fell upon them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you" (134)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: "And when the punishment fell upon them", that is, when the chastisement of God descended upon them and His wrath settled on them.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning that "rijz" (punishment) which God informed had fallen upon these people.

Some of them said: It was plague (ta'un).

Those who said so:

15033 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: And Musa commanded his people from the Children of Israel – and that was after the people of Pharaoh had come with the five signs: the flood and what God mentioned in this verse – but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with him. So he said: Let every man among you slaughter a ram, then let him dip his palm in its blood, then let him strike it upon his door! The Copts said to the Children of Israel: Why do you smear this blood upon your doors? They said: Indeed God is sending a punishment upon you, so we will be saved and you will perish. The Copts said: Does God recognize you only by these signs? They said: Thus our Prophet commanded us! So they awoke, and seventy thousand of the people of Pharaoh had been stabbed, and by evening they were not burying one another. Then Pharaoh said at that point: ﴿Pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us﴾, and it was the plague, ﴿we will surely believe in you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you﴾. So he prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them. Pharaoh was the first of them all to break his word, and he said to Musa: Go with the Children of Israel wherever you wish.

15034 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Huwayh al-Razi and Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr – Huwayh said, from Ibn Abbas – ﴿If you remove the punishment from us﴾: he said: It is the plague.

* *

Others said: It is the chastisement.

Those who said so:

15035 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The punishment (rijz)" is the chastisement.

15036 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15037 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Then when We removed from them the punishment﴾, that is, the chastisement.

15038 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, he said: the chastisement.

15039 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, he said: "The punishment" is the chastisement which God sent upon them of locusts, lice and other things, and they covenanted with Him for all of that, then they broke their covenant.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "rijz" earlier in this book, with its sufficient evidences so that we need not repeat them. [[See the explanation of "rijz" above, 2:116–118 / 12:521.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this place is to say that God, exalted is His remembrance, informed concerning Pharaoh and his people that when the punishment fell upon them – and it is the chastisement and the wrath of God upon them – they fled to Musa, asking him to pray to his Lord to remove it from them. It is possible that this "rijz" was the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, since all of that was a punishment upon them. And it is possible that this "rijz" was the plague, but God has not told us which of these it was, nor has any report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) been authentically transmitted about which it was, so that we would submit to it. So the correct course is to say concerning it as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, and not to go beyond that except with clarification on which the people of interpretation have no dispute, namely that when the chastisement and wrath of God descended upon them.

* *

= ﴿They said: O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you﴾, meaning: by what He has charged you and commanded you with. [[See the explanation of "ahd" (covenant) above, p. 10, note 2, and the references there.]] We have already explained the meaning of "ahd" earlier.

* *

= ﴿If you remove the punishment from us﴾, meaning: if you lift from us the chastisement we are in [[See the explanation of "kashf" (removal) above, 11:354.]] ﴿we will surely believe in you﴾, meaning: we will surely confirm what you have brought and called to, and we will surely affirm it for you = ﴿and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you﴾, meaning: we will surely let the Children of Israel go with you, and not prevent them from going wherever they wish.

The discussion of His saying: ﴿So when We removed the punishment from them, until a term which they should reach, behold, they broke their word (135)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Musa called upon his Lord and He answered him. So when Allah lifted from them the punishment He had sent down upon them, ﴿until a term which they should reach﴾, that they might fully suffer the punishment of their days, which Allah had appointed for them as a term of life, until the time of their destruction [[See the explanation of "al-ajal" (term) above, 12:405, footnote 2, and the reference there.]], ﴿behold, they broke their word﴾, meaning: behold, they violated the covenants they had made with their Lord and with Musa, and persisted in their disbelief and error. The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

15040 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿until a term which they should reach﴾, he said: a fixed number of their days.

15041 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

15042 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when We removed from them the punishment until a term which they should reach, behold, they broke their word﴾, he said: what they had been given of covenants. And this is when Allah says: ﴿And We indeed seized the people of Pharaoh with years [of drought] and shortage of fruits, that they might remember﴾ [al-A'raf: 130], which is hunger.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ (7:136)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He means: when they broke their covenants, "We took retribution from them," meaning: We gained victory over them by bringing Our vengeance down upon them, and that was His punishment. "So We drowned them in the yam," which is the sea, as Dhu al-Rummah said:

Desert wastes and the darkness of night, as if they were
a sea whose shores the Romans babble along.[[Diwan: 576, from a lofty qasidah. This verse is from his description of a frightening wasteland. He says before it: Between the sides and the far-off ends... a waste whose traveller is struck with fear and is kept silent. Al-Rija means the direction. Al-Wasiyah is a wasteland joined to another terrifying wasteland, as if some of them enjoin the others with horrors. Khabituha is the one who travels through it, who can barely find his way. Yahma'* is a vague, featureless expanse in which a person can barely find his way. Makum means one whose mouth is tied shut, unable to speak from terror. Zajal al-jinn is their voice and their enchanted murmuring. Al-Aysham is a plant that rustles when the wind blows over it. Al-Haynum is the murmuring, a sound you hear but cannot understand; he says these sounds come to him from the right and the left. Al-Dawiyyah, or al-Dawiyah, is the wasteland in which the echo of a voice is heard because its edges are distant. This is superb poetry.]] And as the rajaz poet said: [[He is al-'Ajjaj.]]

like the lofty waves of the sea, which the sea has watered [[Diwan: 63; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 227. From an urjuzah in which he mentions Mas'ud ibn 'Amr al-'Ataki al-Azdi and what befell him and his people from Tamim, the kin of al-'Ajjaj. He says, mentioning Tamim and Khuzaymah and Qays 'Aylan, when their battalions and armies gathered: "They emerged when the multitude assembled, with a river whose waves are high." Like the lofty ones of the sea, which the sea has watered, and it has long coastlines and high-pitched expanses. In the printed edition it read "kamadih al-yamm", which is an error, as the editor did not read the manuscript well. The phrase "kabadhikh al-yamm" means the waves of the sea; "saqahu al-yamm" means the sea sustained it, so it remains ever in height and elevation. "Al-Ghatam" is the sea with abundant water and surging waves. "Asṭam al-bahr" is its gathering and its center, where part of it strikes another because of its abundance.]]

= ﴿because they denied Our signs﴾, He says: We did that to them because they denied Our proofs and the signs that We showed them [[See the explanation of "ayah" in the earlier glossary of terms under (ayy)]] = ﴿and were heedless of them﴾, He says: they were heedless of the vengeance We brought down upon them, unaware before it befell them that it would surely come upon them.

* *

The "ha' and alif" in His words "'anha" (of them) refers back to "the vengeance." But if someone said it refers back to "the signs," and directed the meaning to: "and they were turning away from them," making their turning away a heedlessness on their part because they did not accept them, that would also be a valid view. From "ghafalah" (heedlessness) one says: "ghafala al-rajul 'an kadha yaghfulu 'anhu ghaflatan wa ghufulan wa ghafalan." [[See the explanation of "ghaflah" in the earlier passages 2: 244, 316; 3: 127, 184; 9: 162, where this exposition was not given as it is here.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), Jami' al-Bayan, on surah 7, verse 137:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good promise of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been building﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: "And We caused to inherit the people whom Pharaoh and his people had been oppressing, slaughtering their sons, sparing their women, and enslaving and subjugating them, from the Children of Israel" [[See the explanation of "oppression" (al-istid'af) in what has preceded, 12:542.]]. "The eastern parts of the land" (mashāriq al-arḍ) is al-Shām (Syria), which is the area lying to its east. "And its western parts which We had blessed": He says, "in which We had placed lasting good for its people." [[See the explanation of "blessing" (al-barakah) in what has preceded in the lexical indexes, under the root b-r-k.]]

He, may His praise be exalted, said "We caused to inherit" because He gave that land to the Children of Israel after the destruction of the 'Amaliqah who had been in it.

* *

Those who expounded the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning His words "the eastern and western parts of the land."

Mention of those who said that:

15043 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahyā ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Isrā'īl, from Furāt al-Qazzāz, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words: ﴿And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾. He said: "The Shām."

15044 - al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Isrā'īl informed us, from Furāt al-Qazzāz, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan say, and he mentioned something similar.

15045 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Qabīṣah narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Furāt al-Qazzāz, from al-Ḥasan, "the land which We had blessed," he said: "The Shām."

15046 - Bishr ibn Mu'ādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words: ﴿And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾, he said: "It is the land of the Shām."

15047 - Muḥammad ibn 'Abd al-A'lā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatādah, concerning His words: ﴿the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾, he said: "The land in which He placed blessing: the Shām."

* *

Some grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) claimed that "the eastern and western parts of the land" is in the accusative by place (naṣb 'alā al-maḥall), meaning: "And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed in the eastern and western parts of the land," and that His words "We caused to inherit" fell upon His words "which We had blessed." [[By "falling," he means that it passed over to it, so it is its direct object.]]

This is a view with no meaning, because the Children of Israel were not oppressed in the days of Pharaoh by anyone other than Pharaoh and his people, and he had no authority except in Egypt. It is therefore impermissible, given that situation, to say: "those who were oppressed in the eastern and western parts of the land."

* *

If someone says: its meaning is "in the eastern parts of the land of Egypt and its western parts," then that is far from what is understood from the address, and it departs from the views of the people of interpretation and the scholars of tafsir.

* *

As for His words ﴿And the good promise of your Lord was fulfilled﴾, He says: the promise that God made to the Children of Israel was fulfilled in its entirety, as He had promised them, of establishing them in the land and granting them victory over their enemy Pharaoh. And "His good word" is His, may His praise be exalted, saying: ﴿And We wished to bestow favor upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and to establish them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them what they had been fearing﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 5-6].

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

15048 - Muḥammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abū 'Āṣim narrated to us, saying: 'Īsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning God's words: ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾, he said: "The people of Moses prevailed over Pharaoh," and "God's establishment of them in the land," and what He bequeathed to them of it. [[In the printed edition: "the prevalence of the people of Moses..." and then: "and what He bequeathed to them of it," with an added waw; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is perfectly sound.]]

15049 - al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making﴾, He says: We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been constructing of buildings and farms. ﴿And what they had been building﴾: He says, "and what they had been constructing of structures and palaces, and We removed them from all of that, and We ruined all of it."

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "ta'rīsh" (trellising/building) earlier, with its evidence. [[See the explanation of "ta'rīsh" in what has preceded, 12:156.]] The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

15050 - al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Mu'āwiyah narrated to me, from 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn 'Abbās, concerning His words: ﴿and what they had been building﴾, he said: "They build."

15051 - Muḥammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abū 'Āṣim narrated to us, from 'Īsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿ya'rishūn﴾, "they build houses and dwellings, however high they reached, and their vines were not trellised." [[In the printed edition: "not trellised" (ghayr ma'rūsh); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

15052 - al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

* *

The readers (al-qurrā') differed concerning the recitation of this.

The recitation of the majority of the readers of Ḥijāz and Iraq is ﴿يَعْرِشُونَ﴾ with a kasrah on the rā' (ya'rishūn), except for 'Āṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, who read it with a ḍammah on it (ya'rushūn).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These are two well-known dialectal forms among the Arabs; it is said: "'arasha ya'rishu and ya'rushu." When that is the case, whichever of the two the reader recites is correct, because the meanings of both agree, and both are known in the speech of the Arabs. Likewise, the Arabs do with the pattern "fa'ala," when they convert it to the future (the imperfect), sometimes putting a ḍammah on its 'ayn and sometimes a kasrah. However, the recitation I prefer more of the two is the kasrah on the rā', because of its fame among the common people, the large number of readers who use it, and because it is the more correct of the two dialects.

**On the interpretation of His words:** ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to idols of theirs. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."﴾ (7:138)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We parted the sea for the Children of Israel after the signs We had shown them and the lessons they had witnessed at the hands of God's Prophet Moses. Yet those signs did not restrain them, and those lessons and clear proofs did not admonish them, until they said, despite having seen proofs that should have made even the beasts take heed, when they passed by a people devoted to idols of theirs, meaning that they stood attending upon images of theirs that they worshipped besides God. [[See the explanation of "al-ukuf" (devotion/attendance) above, 3:41, 3:539, 3:540. "Al-mithl" (with two dammas) is the plural of "mithal" (with a kasra on the mim), which means a likeness or image, like "al-timthal" (statue).]] "Make for us," O Moses, "a god," meaning: an image we may worship and an idol we may take as a god, just as these people have idols they worship. Worship is not fitting for anything other than God, the One, the Subduer. Moses, upon him be God's blessings, said: Indeed, you, O people, are a people who are ignorant of the greatness of God and of the duty of His right over you, and you do not know that worship is not permissible for anything other than God, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.

* *

It is related from Ibn Jurayj concerning this:

15053 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me regarding ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to idols of theirs﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: "devoted to idols of theirs" – he said: they were images of cows. When the calf of the Samiri was made, it was made to appear to them as if it were from those cows, and that was the beginning of the affair of the calf. ﴿They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."﴾

* *

It was also said: The people who were devoted to their idols, whom God mentions in this verse, were a people from Lakhm.

Those who said this:

15054 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Abu al-'Awwam, from Qatadah regarding ﴿they came upon a people who were devoted to idols of theirs﴾, he said: "upon Lakhm." [[The report 15054: "Bishr ibn 'Amr" is al-Hakam ibn 'Uqbah al-Zuhrani al-Azdi, whom the whole group (of canonical compilers) narrated from; he appeared earlier under no. 3375. "al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl" – thus in the manuscript and the printed edition, but I think it is "al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari al-Waqifi," mentioned in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/212; he is one whose narrations are abandoned. "Abu al-'Awwam" is "Imran ibn Dawwar al-Qattan," who appeared earlier under no. 7503.]]

* *

It was also said: They were of the Canaanites whom Moses, upon him peace, was commanded to fight. And:

15055 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that Abu Waqid al-Laythi said: "We set out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) before Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree [[al-sidrah, its singular being "sidrah," is the jujube (nabq) tree.]]. We said: 'O Prophet of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat (a tree for hanging weapons) just as the disbelievers have a Dhat Anwat!' The disbelievers used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and devote themselves around it [[nata al-shay' yanutuhu nawtan means he hung it up. "Al-anwat" is what is hung on a howdah or other thing, and they are the hanging objects.]]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God is greatest! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Moses: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods.' Indeed, you will follow the ways of those who came before you."
