[[The report 15055: the report of Abu Waqid al-Laythi concerning "Dhat Anwat" is narrated by Abu Ja'far through four routes; this is the first of them, and it is a mursal report, because al-Zuhri did not attribute it (to a companion). Its takhrij will come in the one that follows.]]

15056 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, from Waqid al-Laythi who said: "We set out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) before Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree, and we said: 'O Prophet of God, make for us this a Dhat Anwat,' and he mentioned something similar." [[The report 15056: "Sinan ibn Abi Sinan" – al-Dili or al-Du'mi or al-Jadhari – a reliable Successor. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/163, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/252. This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 5:218 through 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, in similar wording.]]

15057 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), something similar. [[The report 15057: Ibn Ishaq narrated it in his Sirah 4:84, from "Abu Waqid al-Laythi, al-Harith ibn Malik, who said: We set out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Hunayn, and we were recently converted from disbelief." In the Halabi printed edition it reads "that al-Harith ibn Malik," with an added "that," which is a corrupt addition not found in the other copies.]]

15058 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: 'Aqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili informed me, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, that they went out from Mecca with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Hunayn. He said: The disbelievers had a lote tree where they devoted themselves, and they hung their weapons upon it, and it was called "Dhat Anwat." He said: We passed by a great green lote tree, and we said: "O Messenger of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat." He said: "You have spoken! By Him in whose hand my soul is, you have said what the people of Moses said: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods. He said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."' Indeed, these are the ways, and you will certainly follow the ways of those who came before you." [[The report 15058: "Ibn Salih" is 'Abdullah ibn Salih al-Juhani al-Misri, Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth ibn Sa'd. In the printed edition and manuscript the phrase [al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying] has been dropped; Abu Ja'far did not meet Abu Salih, and only narrates from him through al-Muthanna, as occurred earlier in its recurring isnad in the tafsir; the nearest is 15050: "al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us." Al-Bukhari narrated it directly from Abu Salih, as you will see, which establishes that "al-Muthanna narrated to me" has fallen from the isnad, so I added it. Compare this isnad with what preceded at 2350. "Al-Layth" is the Imam al-Layth ibn Sa'd. "'Aqil" is 'Aqil ibn Khalid al-Ayli, who appeared under nos. 19, 2350, a reliable, firm, authoritative transmitter. This report was narrated by Ahmad through Hajjaj, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, in similar wording; al-Bukhari narrated it in abridged form in his Tarikh 2/2/164, saying: "Abu Salih said to us: al-Layth narrated to me, 'Aqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Du'ali, then al-Jadhari, informed me, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'You will certainly follow the ways of those who came before you.'" Ahmad added another route for the report of Abu Waqid in his Musnad: the route of Malik ibn Anas, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan (Musnad no. 5:218). Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in his Musnad: 191, through Ibrahim ibn Sa'd al-Zuhri, from [al-Zuhri], from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, in similar wording; the Musnad omits "al-Zuhri" in brackets. al-Suyuti takhrij it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:114, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh. "Al-sunan" (with two fathas) means the path or way.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 139:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, these people—what they are engaged in will be destroyed, and what they have been doing is in vain.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning what Moses said to his people from the Children of Israel. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Moses said to them, "Indeed, these who are devoted to these idols—God will destroy what they are engaged in, its work and its corruption, and will cause them loss in it by requiting them for it with a humiliating punishment." "And what they have been doing is in vain"—that is, their worship of them—is nullified, because it will not benefit them when God's command comes and descends upon them, nor will it defend them against God's might when it befalls them, nor will it rescue them from His punishment when He punishes them on the Day of Resurrection. So it is in the sense of what has never been. [[In the printed edition: "غير نافع" (ghayr nafi'), and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript.]] [[See the explanation of "al-batil" in the earlier language indexes under (b-ṭ-l).]]

* *

Those interpreting the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

15059 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us. And Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us. Both of them said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, these—what they are engaged in will be destroyed﴾, he said: destroyed is what they are engaged in.

15060 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, these—what they are engaged in will be destroyed﴾, he said: loss.

15061 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, these—what they are engaged in will be destroyed, and what they have been doing is in vain﴾, he said: "This is all one, like the pattern of 'Forgiving, Merciful' and 'Pardoning, Forgiving.'" He said: The Arabs say, "Indeed he is truly wretched (al-ba'is) to be destroyed (mutabbar)," and "Indeed he is truly wretched to be lost (mukhassar)."

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿He said, "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ (7:140)

Abu Ja'far said: God Most High says: Moses said to his people, "Shall I seek for you, other than Allah, a god, and make for you an object of worship that you worship?" [[See the explanation of "baghā" (to seek/desire) above, vol. 12, p. 559, note 3, and the references there.]] — the One Who is your Creator, Who has preferred you over the worlds of your age and time? [[See the explanation of "al-'ālamīn" (the worlds) in the linguistic indexes above under the root ('-l-m).]] That is: "Shall I seek for you an object of worship that neither benefits you nor harms you, and that you worship, while you abandon the worship of the One Who has preferred you over all creation? Indeed, this from you is ignorance!"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 141:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with terrible torment, slaying your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty God says to the Jews of the Children of Israel who were living among the neighbours of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) [in Medina], "Remember, along with this statement of yours which you made to Moses after seeing the signs and lessons, and after the blessings that I bestowed upon you and the favours that preceded from Me to you, your deed of what you did: ﴿when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh﴾, and they were those who followed his path and method of disbelief in God from among his people [see the explanation of "al-Al" (family/people) above: 2:37; 3:222, n. 3; 6:326; 8:480]. ﴿who afflicted you with terrible torment﴾, meaning: when they subjected you to the most vile and evil torment. [See the explanation of "al-Sawm" (inflicting) above: 2:40.]"

* *

We have already explained earlier in this book what the torment that they inflicted upon them was, and its evil. [See above: 2:40, 41.]

* *

﴿slaying your sons﴾, meaning the males among their offspring. ﴿and sparing your women﴾, meaning: they let their females live. [See the explanation of "al-Istihya'" (sparing) above: 2:41-48; 13:41.] ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, meaning: and in their afflicting you with terrible torment there was a test from God for you and a great blessing. [See the explanation of "al-Bala'" (trial) above: 12:289, n. 2, and the references there. In the printed edition it read "wa-ta'ammud 'azim" (and a deliberate great [thing]), which has no meaning; the correct reading is what is adopted here, and see what has preceded in the interpretation of the similar verse at 2:48, 49, from which I deduced the correct reading.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, Verse 142:**

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time with his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: And We appointed Moses for Our communication (munajat) thirty nights. [[See the explanation of "al-mu'ada" (appointment) in what preceded, 2:58-60, in a similar verse.]] It has also been said that they were thirty nights of Dhu al-Qa'dah. = ﴿And completed them with ten﴾ means: and We completed the thirty nights with ten nights, to make forty nights.

* *

It has been said that the ten with which He completed them to forty were the ten of Dhu al-Hijjah.

Those who said this:

15062. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾. He said: Dhu al-Qa'dah and the ten of Dhu al-Hijjah.

15063. ... He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾. He said: Dhu al-Qa'dah and the ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. Concerning this, they differed. [[The report 15063: I have placed dots because it is an abridgment; the intent is that the opening of its chain is the opening of the chain before it. Such a thing has passed many times without my pointing it out, so I have chosen from now on to place dots as a notice of this. It is the narration of Sufyan ibn Wakī', from Jarir, as has passed many times with such a chain.]]

15064. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights﴾. He said: It is Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten from Dhu al-Hijjah. That is His saying: ﴿So the appointed time with his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾.

15065. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that the thirty nights with which Moses had promised his Lord were Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the ten of Dhu al-Hijjah with which God completed the forty.

15066. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights﴾. He said: Dhu al-Qa'dah. ﴿And completed them with ten﴾. He said: the ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said the like of it.

15067. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say concerning His saying: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾: Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten of Dhu al-Hijjah.

15068. ... He said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq: ﴿And completed them with ten﴾. He said: the ten of the Adha (sacrifice).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So the appointed time with his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾, it means: the time which God had appointed for Moses was completed as forty nights, and was fulfilled. [[See the explanation of "al-tamam" (completion) in what preceded, 3:17-18; 4:7; 12:62. And the explanation of "al-mithaq" (appointed time) in what preceded, 3:553-555.]] As:

15069. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿So the appointed time with his Lord was completed﴾. He said: the appointed time with his Lord reached forty nights.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Moses said to his brother Harun: Take my place among my people, and set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ (142)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: When he went forth to the appointment with his Lord, he said to his brother Harun: ﴿Take my place among my people﴾, meaning: be my successor among them until I return.

* *

It is said from this: "He succeeded him (khalafahu, yakhlufuhu), succession (khilafah)." [[See the explanation of "al-khilafah" (succession) in what preceded, 12:540-541, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

﴿And set things right﴾ means: and set them right by bringing them to obedience to God and His worship, as:

15070. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "And Moses said to his brother Harun: Take my place among my people, and set things right." And among his setting things right was that he would not let the calf be worshipped.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾, it means: do not take the path of those who cause corruption on the earth, by their disobedience to their Lord, and their assisting the people of sin in their disobedience to their Lord. Rather, take the path of those who obey their Lord. [[See the explanation of "ittaba'" (follow) and "al-fasad" (corruption) in what preceded, in the lexical indexes (under t-b-' and f-s-d).]]

* *

God's appointment with Moses, peace be upon him, took place after He had destroyed Pharaoh and delivered the Children of Israel from him, according to the people of knowledge, as:

15071. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: It says that this was after he had finished with Pharaoh and before the Mount (Tur). When God delivered Moses, peace be upon him, from the sea and drowned the family of Pharaoh, and he reached the good land, God sent down to them therein manna and quails, and his Lord commanded him to meet Him. When he wished to meet his Lord, he appointed Harun as successor over his people, and promised them that he would come to them after thirty nights, an appointment from Him, without the command of his Lord or His promise. So he set out to meet his Lord. When thirty nights were completed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said: Moses will not come to you, and nothing will set you right except a god you worship! Harun adjured them and said: Do not do this; wait this night of yours and this day of yours, and if he comes, well, and if not, do what you wish! They said: Yes! When they woke the next morning and did not see Moses, the Samiri returned to his words of yesterday. He said: And God added a further term after the term He had set between them, ten nights, [[In the printed edition: "bainahum 'ashran" (between them, ten); in the manuscript it is unpointed, and this is its correct form.]] so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. Harun then came and adjured them, except that they should wait that day also; if he came, well, and if not, do what you wish! Then the Samiri returned a third time with the same words to them, and Harun came and adjured them to wait. When they did not see...[[Report 15071: This is an incomplete report, as you see, and I have not found it anywhere else. The reason is that his words "when they did not see him" appear in the manuscript at the end of the left-hand page, and then after it comes: "Al-Qasim said," so it is clear that the copyist hurried, and dropped the completion of the report when he turned the page and began the following report after it.]]

15072. Al-Qasim said, Al-Husayn said, Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hudhali narrated to me, saying: The Samiri stood before Harun when Moses had set out, and said: O Prophet of God, on the day we went out from the Copts we borrowed a great deal of their finery of jewelry, and the troops who are with you have hastened to sell the jewelry and spend it. [[(3) In the printed edition: "wa inna al-dhina ma'aka" (and indeed those who are with you), omitting "al-jund" (the troops), because it was unpointed and he did not read it well.]] It was only a loan from the family of Pharaoh, and they are not alive for us to return it to them, and we do not know; perhaps your brother, the Prophet of God Moses, when he comes, will have an opinion about it: either he will offer it as an offering, and the fire will consume it, or he will give it to the poor rather than the rich! Harun said to him: What a fine opinion you have and what a fine thing you have said! So he commanded a herald, who proclaimed: Whoever has any of the jewelry of the family of Pharaoh, let him bring it to us! They brought it to him, and Harun said: O Samiri, you are most entitled to keep this treasure! So the Samiri took it. He was the enemy of God, the wicked one, a goldsmith, and he fashioned from it a calf, a body. Then he cast into its belly a handful of dust from the print of the hoof of Gabriel, peace be upon him, which he had seen in the sea. So it began to low, and it lowed only once. He said to the Children of Israel: Moses only went away for these thirty nights seeking this! ﴿This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:88]. Meaning: Moses, peace be upon him, forgot his Lord.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 143 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: When Moses came at the time We had appointed for Him to meet Us therein [[See the explanation of "al-Miqat" (the appointed time) earlier, p. 87, note 1, and the references there.]] = "and his Lord spoke to him," and conversed with him privately = "he said" (Moses said to his Lord) = ﴿"My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You."﴾ God said to him in reply: "﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain.﴾"

* *

The reason for Moses' request to his Lord to look upon Him was what follows:

15073. It was related to me by Musa ibn Harun, who said: Amr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When his Lord spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, he desired to look upon Him. He said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me." So the mountain was surrounded [by angels], [[This addition between the brackets is required by the context.]] and the angels were surrounded by fire, and the fire was surrounded by angels, and the angels were surrounded by fire. Then his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain.

15074. It was related to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾ [Maryam: 52], he said: One who met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ related to me that the Lord brought him close until he heard the scratching of the pen. [[Ṣarīf al-qalam (the scratching of the pen), al-bāb (the door) and al-nāb (the tooth), and the like: it is like al-ṣarīr, which is a prolonged, sharp sound.]] Then, out of longing for Him, he said: ﴿"My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain."﴾

15075. Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to me, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: When Moses, peace be upon him, delayed beyond the thirty [days], until he heard the speech of God, he longed to look upon Him, and said: ﴿"My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You!" He said: "You will not see Me."﴾ No human being is able to look upon Me in this world; whoever looks upon Me dies! He said: "My God, I have heard Your speech, and I have longed to look upon You; and to look upon You then die is dearer to me than to live without seeing You!" He said: "Look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me."

15076. Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abdullah related to us, who said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿"Show me Yourself, that I may look upon You,"﴾ he said: "Give me."

15077. Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Moses appointed Harun as his successor over the Children of Israel and said: "I am hastening to my Lord; so take my place among my people, and do not follow the way of the corrupters." Moses went out to his Lord, hastening to meet Him out of longing for Him, and Harun remained among the Children of Israel, and with him was the Samiri, who led them along the trail of Moses in order to catch up with him. When God spoke to Moses, he hoped to see Him, and asked his Lord to look upon Him. God said to Moses: "Indeed, you will not see Me, ﴿but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me﴾," and so on to the end of the verse. Ibn Ishaq said: This is what has reached us in the Book of God concerning the account of Moses when he sought to look upon his Lord. The People of the Book, and the people of the Torah, assert that there was for that an explanation, a story, many matters and a dialogue that did not come to us in the Book of God, and God knows best. =

Ibn Ishaq said, citing some of the early scholars of the traditions of the People of the Book: They find in the explanation of what is in their possession, from the account of Moses when he sought that from his Lord, that it was part of his speech to Him when he hoped to see Him and asked Him for that, and his Lord replied to him with what He replied: that Moses purified himself, purified his garments, and fasted for the meeting with his Lord. When he came to Mount Sinai, and God drew near to him in the cloud and spoke to him, he glorified Him, praised Him, magnified Him and sanctified Him, with humble supplication and sorrowful weeping. Then he began to extol Him, and said: "My Lord, how great You are, and how great is Your entire majesty! Of Your greatness is that nothing existed before You; You are the One, the Subduer. As if Your throne beneath Your greatness were a fire kindled for You, and You made a canopy [of light] before it, a canopy of light. [[The addition between the brackets is required by the context.]] How great You are, my Lord, and how great is Your kingdom! You placed between Yourself and Your angels a distance of five hundred years' journey. How great You are, my Lord, and how great is Your kingdom in Your dominion! When You wish to decree something among Your hosts that are in the heavens or those that are on the earth, and Your hosts that are in the sea, You send the wind from Your presence, which none of Your creation sees except You, if You will, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "You sent the wind." I have no doubt that the correct reading is what I have given, and it refers to what God, glorified is He, said in Surat Ghafir, 15: "Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, that he may warn of the Day of Meeting."]] and it enters into the belly of whomever You wish of Your prophets, and they convey what You desire to Your servants. [[In the printed edition: "for what You desired of Your servants"; in the manuscript: "what You desired." The correct reading is what I have given.]] No angel of Yours is able to bear any part of Your greatness, or of Your throne, nor hear Your voice. You have bestowed favour upon me, and magnified Your favour upon me, and You have been most gracious to me in every kindness! You magnified me among the nations of the earth, and magnified me before Your angels, and You made me hear Your voice, and You gave me Your speech, and bestowed upon me Your wisdom. If I count Your blessings, I cannot enumerate them; and if I wish to give You thanks, I cannot manage it. [[In the printed edition: "and if I wished to thank You, I could not do it"; in the manuscript: "and if I wish to thank You, I cannot manage it." The correct reading is what I have given.]] My Lord, I called upon You against Pharaoh with the great signs and severe punishment, and You struck the sea with my staff that was in my hand, and it split for me and for those with me! I called upon You when I crossed the sea, [[In the printed edition: "I crossed"; I have adopted the manuscript reading, which is also correct.]] and You drowned Your enemy and my enemy. I asked You for water for myself and my community, and You had me strike the rock with my staff that was in my hand, and from it You gave me and my community to drink. I asked You for food for my community, which no one before them had eaten, and You commanded me to call upon You from the east and from the west; I called upon You from the east of my community, and You gave them the manna from the east for myself, [[In the printed edition: "from the east for myself"; this is a garbled sentence whose correct form I do not know.]] and You brought them the quails from their west, by the sea; and I complained of the heat, and I called upon You, and You shaded them with clouds. I cannot bear to enumerate Your blessings upon me, nor count them; and if I wish to thank You for them, I cannot manage it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "I cannot manage it." The correct reading is what I have given.]] So I have come to You today, desiring, seeking, asking, humbly supplicating, that You give me what You have withheld from others. I beseech You, and I ask You, O Possessor of majesty, might and sovereignty, to show me Yourself, that I may look upon You, for I have longed to see Your face, which none of Your creation has seen!" The Lord of Might said to him: "Do you not perceive, O son of Imran, what you are saying? You have spoken words greater than all the rest of creation! No one who sees Me shall live, [[The phrase between these brackets I do not understand; it appears in the manuscript as: "In the heavens is My habitation, for they have grown too weak to bear My greatness, and on earth is My habitation, for it has grown too weak to contain My hosts." The remainder of the sentence is as in the printed edition. I am uncertain about its wording and have not been able to determine its corruption, so I have placed it between brackets. The entire report is confused in its wording, and I have not found it elsewhere. Therefore I have left it as it is, unless it is clearly an error.]] so I am not in one place to manifest Myself to an eye that looks upon Me." Moses said: "O Lord, to see You and die is dearer to me than not to see You and live." The Lord of Might said to him: "O son of Imran, you have spoken words greater than all the rest of creation: no one who sees Me shall live!" He said: "Lord, complete Your blessings upon me, complete Your favour upon me, and complete Your kindness upon me, through this that I have asked of You, not that I may see You and be taken, but I wish to see You so that my heart may be at rest." He said to him: "O son of Imran, no one shall see Me and live!" He said: "Moses, my Lord, complete Your blessings upon me, complete Your favour upon me, and complete Your kindness upon me, through this that I have asked of You, and then I shall die, [[In the printed edition: "this that I have asked of You, that I see You and die," with the addition made by analogy to the preceding phrase; I have adopted the manuscript reading.]] dearer to me than life!" Then the Merciful, who shows compassion to His creatures, said: "You have asked, O Moses, [and I will] [[This word between the brackets is as written in the manuscript; I do not know its reading. The printed edition omits it, alters what follows, and writes "and I have given you" in place of "I will give you."]] your request, if you are able to look upon Me. Go, take for yourself two tablets, then look at the great rock at the summit of the mountain; for what is behind it and below it is narrow, and cannot hold anything but your place of sitting, O son of Imran. Then look, for I shall descend to you, and My hosts, few and many." Moses did as his Lord commanded him; he hewed two tablets, then ascended the mountain with them, and sat upon the rock. When he had settled upon it, God commanded His hosts that are in the lowest heaven, saying: "Lay down your wings around the mountain." They heard what the Lord said, and they did His command. Then God sent the thunderbolts, the darkness and the cloud upon what was near the mountain where Moses was, four farsakhs in every direction. Then God commanded the angels of the lower world to pass by Moses, and they came forth before him, and passed by him flying like the nightingales, [[Al-nugar (pronounced with the first vowel a damma and the second a fatha): a kind of bird with red beaks and red jaw-roots; it is said among the people of Medina that it is the nightingale.]] their mouths pouring forth sanctification and glorification with mighty voices, like the sound of a violent thunder. Moses son of Imran, peace be upon him, said: "My Lord, I was independent of this; my eyes see nothing; their sight has gone because of the ray of light flaring from the angels of my Lord!" Then God commanded the angels of the second heaven: "Descend upon Moses and come forth before him!" So they descended, like lions, with a roaring of glorification and sanctification, [[Al-lajab (with a fatha on each of the two letters): the rising of voices and their mingling.]] and the weak servant, Ibn Imran, was terrified at what he saw and heard; every hair on his head and his skin stood on end. Then he said: "I repent of my request to You; will anything save me from this place in which I am?" The chief of the angels and their leader said to him: [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "the best of the angels." It seems that the correct reading is "the chief of the angels," as I have written, and "the best of the angels" appears in all the following places; in the last of them I have written the correct form "chief."]] "O Moses, be patient in what you have asked; a little of what you have seen is out of much!" Then God commanded the angels of the third heaven: "Descend upon Moses and come forth before him!" So they came forth like eagles, having a crashing, a trembling, and a mighty roar, [[In the printed edition: "nakhf"; in the manuscript: "qasf," undotted, and the correct reading of it is what I have given. "Al-qasf" and "al-qasif" are the sound of thunder and what resembles it.]] and their mouths pouring forth glorification and sanctification, like the roar of a mighty army, like the blaze of fire. [[In the printed edition: "aw ka-lahab," with the added "aw"; I have adopted the manuscript reading.]] Moses was terrified, his soul was despairing and he thought ill, [[In the printed edition: "his soul despaired and he thought ill"; I have adopted the manuscript reading, which is correct. It is said: "asiyat nafsuhu," meaning he was grieved. For the explanation of "sa'a zannuhu" see what has passed earlier, 3:585, note 1; its meaning is that evil suspicions overcame him.]] and he despaired of life. The chief of the angels and their leader said to him: "Stay where you are, O son of Imran, until you see what you cannot endure!" Then God commanded the angels of the fourth heaven: "Descend and come forth before Moses son of Imran!" So they came forward and descended upon him, resembling none of those who had passed by him before; their colours were like the blaze of fire, and the rest of their form like white snow, their voices loud in glorification and sanctification; none of the voices of those who had passed by him before came near to theirs. His knees knocked together, his heart trembled, and his weeping intensified. The chief of the angels and their leader said: "O son of Imran, be patient in what you have asked; a little of much you have seen!" Then God commanded the angels of the fifth heaven: "Descend and come forth before Moses!" So they descended upon him in seven colours, and Moses could not follow them with his gaze, nor had he seen their like, nor heard their voices, and his inner being was filled with fear, his grief intensified, and his weeping increased. The chief of the angels and their leader said to him: "O son of Imran, stay where you are until you see what you cannot endure!" Then God commanded the angels of the sixth heaven: "Descend upon My servant who asked to see Me, Moses son of Imran, and come forth before him!" So they descended upon him, each angel holding in his hand something like a tall palm tree of fire, brighter than the sun, and their garments were like the blaze of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, all the angels of the heavens who were before them responded to them, saying with the strength of their voices: "Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of Might, forever, He does not die." Each of them had four faces on his head. When Moses saw them, he raised his voice, glorifying with them as they glorified, weeping and saying: "My Lord, remember me, and do not forget Your servant; I do not know whether I will be delivered from what I am in; if I go out I shall be burnt, and if I remain I shall die!" The chief of the angels and their leader said to him [[See the previous note, p. 95, note 1.]]: "You are about to be filled inwardly, O son of Imran, your heart is about to be torn out, and your weeping is about to intensify; so be patient for what you sat to look upon, O son of Imran!" The mountain of Moses was a great mountain. God commanded that His throne be carried, and then said: "Pass before My servant, so that he may see Me, for a little of much he has seen!" The mountain was split open by the greatness of the Lord, and the light of the Throne of the Merciful covered the mountain of Moses, and the angels of the heavens raised their voices all together, so the mountain shook and crumbled, and every tree that was upon it; and the weak servant, Moses son of Imran, fell down upon his face in a swoon, his spirit not with him. Then God sent life by His mercy, and it covered him by His mercy, [[In the printed edition the word "the spirit" was dropped from the sentence.]] and He turned the rock upon which he was into something like a stomach, shaped like a dome, [[The same in the manuscript and the printed edition: "kal-mi'idah" (like a stomach). I do not know whether this is correct or not.]] so that Moses would not be burnt; and the spirit raised him up, as a mother raises her child when it has been struck down. He said: Then Moses rose, glorifying God and saying: "I believe that You are my Lord, and I affirm that no one sees You and lives; and whoever looks upon Your angels has his heart torn out. How great You are, my Lord, and how great are Your angels! You are the Lord of lords, the God of gods, and the King of kings; You command the hosts that are with You and they obey You, and You command the heavens and what is in them and they obey You; You are not too proud for that, and nothing is equal to You, and nothing stands before You. My Lord, I repent to You. Praise be to God, who has no partner. How great You are, and how exalted, O Lord of the worlds!"

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down in a swoon.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: When the Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, God made the mountain crumble, that is, level with the earth = ﴿and Moses fell down in a swoon,﴾ that is, he was unconscious. [[See the explanation of "al-sa'qah" (the thunderous stroke) earlier, 2:83, 84; 9:359.]]

* *

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

15078. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Anqazi related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding God's words: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble,﴾ he said: Only the size of the little finger of Him was manifested = ﴿He made it crumble,﴾ he said: into dust = ﴿and Moses fell down in a swoon,﴾ he said: unconscious.

15079. Musa related to us, who said: Amr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, who said: al-Suddi asserted, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: There was manifested of Him as much as the little finger, so the mountain was made to crumble, and Moses fell down in a swoon, and he remained in a swoon for as long as God willed.

15080. Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And Moses fell down in a swoon,﴾ he said: unconscious.

15081. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble,﴾ he said: part of it was broken upon another = ﴿and Moses fell down in a swoon,﴾ that is, dead.

15082. Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿and Moses fell down in a swoon,﴾ that is, dead.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 143 (part 2 of 2):

15083 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿crumbled﴾, he said: "Some of it crumbled upon the rest."

15084 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding His saying: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, he said: "The mountain sank into the earth until it reached the sea, and it keeps moving along with it."

15085 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali regarding: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, he said: "It was uprooted and went under the earth, and it does not appear until the Day of Resurrection."

15086 - Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Qarah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from a man, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He pointed with His finger and made it crumble." And Abu Isma'il showed us with his index finger. [[The report 15086: Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti, the teacher of al-Tabari, I have not found a biography for him. And "Qarah Abi 'Isa," I have not found a biography or any mention of him. This report was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, quoting from this place, and he only added: "This isnad contains an unnamed man who is not identified."]]

15087 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to me, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, he said, "like this with his finger," [[Here "qala" means: pointed.]] and the Prophet ﷺ placed the thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, "and the mountain sank." [[The report 15087: Hammad is Hammad ibn Salamah, who has passed many times. And Thabit is Thabit ibn Aslam al-Bunani, trustworthy, related from by the group; he has passed under numbers 2942 and 7030. This is an isnad whose narrators are trustworthy. This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his tafsir of the verse, through Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad, and then said: "This is a sound, strange hadith, which we only know from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah." Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 3:546, from this place in the tafsir of al-Tabari, but he wrote its isnad thus: "Hammad narrated to us, from Layth, from Anas," and then said: "This is how it occurred in this narration: 'Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Layth, from Anas,'" and that is not as he reported. For Thabit is in the manuscript and the printed edition: "Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas," and there is no "Layth" in it, so I do not know how this happened to the hafiz Ibn Kathir, nor from where? See the takhrij of the following report.]]

15088 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hudbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, and said: He placed the thumb close to the tip of his little finger, and said: "Then the mountain sank." Humayd then said to Thabit: "Do you say this?" He said: Thabit raised his hand and struck Humayd's chest, saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says it, and Anas says it, and I conceal it!" [[The report 15088: It is the lengthy version of the earlier report. Ibn Kathir narrated it in his tafsir 3:546-547, then said: "Thus it was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad: Abu al-Muthanna, Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik," then he mentioned the report in similar wording. Then he said: "Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his tafsir of this verse, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Hakam al-Warraq, from Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh." Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:320, through 'Affan ibn Muslim, from Hammad ibn Salamah, and through Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad, in similar wording to the hadith of Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad, and then said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Kathir said: "This isnad is sound, but it has a defect," after mentioning the report of Abu Ja'far. And "Humayd" mentioned in this report is "Humayd al-Tawil."]]

15089 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious﴾. That was because when the veil was lifted and the mountain saw the light, it became like one of the dakks (dakkat). [[(2) Perhaps the correct reading is "al-dakawat," as will come on p. 101, note 1.]]

15090 - al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Mujahid: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said: My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look at You. He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me.﴾ For it is greater than you and stronger in creation. ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾, he looked at the mountain, unable to contain himself, and the mountain began to crumble from its base. [[(1) Thus in the printed edition; in the manuscript it is also "ala adlihi," but with a shadda on the lam, so it seems to be read as "ala adhlihi," which is clearer in meaning than the one in the printed edition. It means that it humbled itself to the utmost humility and crumbled.]] When Musa saw what the mountain was doing, he fell down unconscious.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿dakkan﴾. The common reciters of the people of Madinah and Basra recited it: ﴿dakkan﴾, with a short vowel and tanwin, meaning: "Allah crumbled the mountain to pieces," i.e., broke it into fragments, and in support of the saying of Allah: ﴿Nay, when the earth is pounded to powder, pounded to powder﴾ [Surah al-Fajr: 21], and His saying: ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 14]. Some of them cited for this the verse of Humayd: [[Humayd is Humayd al-Arqat.]]

yadukku arkana al-jibali hazmuhu / takhtiru bil-bidi al-riqaqi buhmuhu

[[I have not found the two verses anywhere, but in Tarikh al-Tabari 7:41 there are verses of rajaz, and what is here seems to be part of them. In the printed edition here it read "hadmuhu," and the correct reading is what is given here; the manuscript is undotted, and there seems to be a plain ra rather than a dal. "Al-hazm" (with two fatha) and "al-hazim" is the sound of thunder resembling breaking, and similar is Ru'bah's description of a roaring army: "yurjifu anda' al-jibali hazmah"

"Takhtiru" means walks swaying, shaking its swords, pleased and proud of its strength and valor. "Al-buham," plural of "buhmah" (with a damma and sukun): the brave horseman about whom it is not known from where he may be approached, nor from where his killers may enter upon him, due to the intensity of his valor and alertness. "Al-bid al-riqaq": thin swords from the excellence of their polishing.]]

* *

And the common readers of Kufa recited it: "ja'alahu dakka'," with the mad and without the kasra and tanwin, like "hamra'" and "sawda'." Ikrimah was among those who recited it thus, and he would say regarding it:

15091 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Hazim, from Ikrimah who said: "Dakka'" from the "dakka'at." And he said: When Allah, blessed and exalted, looked at the mountain, it became a plain of dust. [[(1) Report 15091: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muhallab ibn Abi Sufrah al-Azdi, trustworthy, related from by the group; biography in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/82. And Yazid ibn Hazim ibn Yazid al-Azdi al-Jahdami, declared trustworthy by Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in, and he is the brother of Jarir ibn Hazim, older than him; biography in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/325, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/257. And his saying: "dakka' min al-dakka'at," "al-dakka'at" is the plural of "dakka'," which is a mound of mud that is not thick; they treated it as a noun due to its prevalence, like their saying: "there is no charity in the vegetables." In the printed edition it was: "it became a rock of dust," and in the manuscript: "sar sahra turaban," and this is the correct reading.]]

* *

The people of Arabic grammar differed regarding its meaning when recited thus.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The Arabs say: "naqah dakka'," meaning a she-camel without a hump. And he said: "al-jabal" is masculine, so it is not fitting that it be described thus, unless it means: "like a dakka'," deleting "like," and treating it as in: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82].

* *

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning of that is: he made the mountain into a dakka' land, then "the land" was deleted, and "the dakka'" was placed in its position, since it fulfilled its function.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿ja'alahu dakka'﴾, with the mad and without the kasra, due to the indication of the report which we narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, establishing its soundness. For it is narrated from him ﷺ that he said: "the mountain sank" [[(2) Meaning in the two reports No. 15087 and 15088]], and he did not say: "it crumbled to pieces" nor "it turned into dust." There is no doubt that when it sinks and disappears, the face of the earth is revealed, and it becomes like the she-camel whose hump has gone, and becomes a dakka' without a hump. As for when it crumbles, it is only that some of it breaks the rest and fragments, and it does not sink. As for "al-dakka'," it is a substitute for "al-ard" (the earth), and therefore it is feminine, as I have explained.

* *

So the meaning of the statement then is: "When His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, it sank, and in its place He made a dakka' land." We have explained the meaning of "al-sa'q" (swoon) with its evidences earlier, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [[(2) See the explanation of "al-sa'q" earlier: 2:83, 84 / 3:359.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then when he recovered, he said: Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers﴾ (143)

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: When his understanding returned to Musa, peace be upon him, from his faint, and that is the recovery from the swoon into which Musa ﷺ fell. "He said: Glory be to You," exalting You, O Lord, and absolving You that anyone should see You in this world and then live. "I have turned to You in repentance," from my request of You what I asked of You of seeing You. "And I am the first of the believers," in You among my people, that none should see You in this world and then die. [[(3) See the explanation of "subhan" earlier: 12:10, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Among those who said the like of what we have said regarding that were a group of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

15092 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His saying: "I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers," he said: There were believers before him, but he means: I am the first to believe that none of Your creation will see You until the Day of Resurrection.

15093 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: When Musa saw that and recovered, he knew that he had asked for a matter that was not fitting for him, so he said: "Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers." Abu al-'Aliyah said: He meant: I am the first to believe in You that none will see You before the Day of Resurrection.

15094 - 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And Musa fell down unconscious," so the angels passed by him while he was unconscious, and they said: "O son of the menstruating women, you have asked your Lord for a great matter!" When he recovered, he said: "Glory be to You, there is no god but You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers!" He said: I am the first to believe that none of Your creation will see You, meaning: in this world.

15095 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding his saying: "He said: Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers," meaning: I am the first to believe that nothing of Your creation will see You.

15096 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: "Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance," he said: From my request for the vision.

15097 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, from Mujahid: "He said: Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance," that I ask You for the vision.

15098 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from a man, from Mujahid: "Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance," that I ask You for the vision.

15099 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance," he said: I have turned to You from asking You for the vision.

* *

Others said: The meaning of His saying "and I am the first of the believers" is: the first of the believers in You from the Children of Israel.

Mention of those who said that:

15100 - al-Husayn ibn 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And I am the first of the believers," he said: the first to believe in You from the Children of Israel.

15101 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And I am the first of the believers," meaning: the first of the believers from the Children of Israel.

15102 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "And I am the first of the believers," I am the first of my people in faith.

15103 - Ibn Waki' and al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from a man, from Mujahid: "And I am the first of the believers," he says: the first of my people in faith.

15104 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And I am the first of the believers," he said: I am the first of my people in faith.

15105 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His saying: "And I am the first of the believers," he said: the first of my people to believe.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We chose the view we have chosen regarding His saying "and I am the first of the believers," over the view of the one who said its meaning is: "I am the first of the believers from the Children of Israel," because there were believers and prophets among the Children of Israel before him, including the children of Israel himself by his loins, and they were believers and prophets. For that reason we chose the view we stated earlier.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 144:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿He said, "O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His mention be exalted, says: God said to Moses, "O Moses, I have chosen you above the people," meaning: I have selected you over the people [[(1) See the explanation of "al-istifa' (choosing)" in what has preceded: 3:91, 96 / 5:312 / 6:326, 393.]] = "by My messages," to My creation, by which I sent you to them = "and by My speech," I spoke to you and conversed with you, apart from others of My creation. = "So take what I have given you," meaning: take what I have given you of My command and My prohibition, hold fast to it, and act upon it [ ... ] [[(2) In the printed edition: "and act upon it, meaning..." and in the manuscript: "and act upon it, your hands..." This has no meaning here; it appears to be a corruption of "bi-jidd" (earnestly) or something similar, but I have not been able to determine it, so I have left dots in brackets in its place. See the explanation of His saying in "Surat al-Baqarah": 63, "Take what We have given you with strength," vol. 2: 160, 161.]] = "and be among the grateful," to God for what He has given you of His messages and what He has singled you out for of private conversation [[(3) In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and what has been obtained by it of private conversation," and the correct reading is what I have adopted.]], by obeying Him in His command and His prohibition, and by hastening to His pleasure.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 145:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets, of everything, an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We wrote for Musa on his tablets.

* *

The definite article "al" was added to "al-alwah" (the tablets) in place of a possessive, as the poet said: [[(1) He is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani.]]

*and their minds are not unsound* [[(2) The line has already passed, with its takhrij and explanation, in volume 5, p. 160, note 3, but its place was not mentioned there, so let it be noted. The line, in the version quoted earlier, reads: "They have a disposition that time has not given to anyone else among people, so their minds are not unsound."]]

And as His, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿For indeed, Paradise is the refuge﴾ [Surah al-Nazi'at 79:41], meaning: it is his refuge. [[(3) See what has passed, volume 5, pp. 160–161.]]

* *

As for His words "of everything": it means, of reminder and warning of the greatness of God and the might of His dominion, "an admonition" for His people and for those commanded to act upon what was written on the tablets, "and a detailed explanation of everything": meaning, and a clarification of everything from God's command and prohibition. [[(4) See the explanation of "admonition" (maw'izah) in the lexical indices (root w-'-z) of what has passed.]] [[(5) See the explanation of "detailed explanation" (tafsil) in what has passed, p. 68, note 5, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

15106. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, or Sa'id ibn Jubayr (it is in the original of my book: from Sa'id ibn Jubayr), concerning God's words "and a detailed explanation of everything," he said: what they were commanded and what they were forbidden.

15107. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

15108. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything," from the lawful and the unlawful.

15109. Al-Harith told me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, he said: Abu Sa'd told us, he said: I heard Mujahid say concerning His words "and a detailed explanation of everything," he said: what they were commanded and what they were forbidden.

15110. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: "And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything." 'Atiyah [[(1) This is 'Atiyah al-'Awfi, and he is the great-grandfather of Muhammad ibn Sa'd. See the discussion of this chain at no. 305.]] said: Ibn 'Abbas informed me that Musa, peace be upon him, when death distressed him, "hastened" [[(2) In the printed edition, and in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:21, the text reads: "that Musa, peace be upon him, when death distressed him." The word I have written, "yantasilat" (hastened), is in the manuscript in a form that I could not match to a clear word; "hastened" is the closest in meaning. It is said: "insalata fi al-amr," when one bolts and hurries. It is said: "insalata ya'du," when one runs quickly. "Al-munsalit" is the one who hastens in anything. Al-Bukhari has related in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Angel of Death was sent to Musa, peace be upon him. When he came to him, Musa struck him, and he returned to his Lord, mighty and majestic, and said: You sent me to a servant who does not want to die, and so on. This seems to have happened because he disliked death and hated it, so he hastened when he saw him, saying what he said. This is what I have seen, and above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows. See the accounts of the death of Musa, peace be upon him, in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah 1:316–319.]] said: This is because of Adam! God had placed us in a dwelling of abode where we would not die, but Adam erred, so He sent us down here! God said to Musa: Shall I send Adam to you so that you can dispute with him? He said: Yes! When God sent Adam, Musa questioned him, and our father Adam, peace be upon them both, said: O Musa, you asked God to send me to you! Musa said: Had it not been for you, we would not be here! Adam said to him: Did God not give you, of everything, an admonition and a detailed explanation? Do you not know that no calamity befalls the earth or yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being? [[(1) This is a quotation woven into the verse of Surah al-Hadid 57:22.]] Musa said: Yes! So Adam overcame him in the argument, may God's blessings be upon them both. [[(2) The report 15110 is a very weak chain, as has passed in the explanation of its chain at no. 305. The argument between Adam and Musa, peace be upon them both, has been related by al-Bukhari and Muslim and all the books of Sunan. See the fine section gathered by Ibn Kathir in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah 1:81–85. It is said: "khasamahu, fa-khasamahu," meaning he overcame him in the dispute, which is argumentation.]]

15111. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil: that he heard Wahb say concerning His words: "And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything," he said: He wrote for him: Do not associate anything with Me, of the inhabitants of heaven or of the inhabitants of earth, for all of that is My creation. Do not swear by My name falsely, for whoever swears falsely by My name, I will not purify him. And honour your parents.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿So take hold of them with strength﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We said to Musa, when We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything: Take hold of the tablets with strength.

* *

The word "the tablets" is used as a report, and what is meant is what is in them.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "strength" (quwwah) in this place.

Some of them said: its meaning is with earnestness.

Those who said so:

15112. 'Abd al-Karim told me, he said: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn 'Uyaynah told us, he said: Abu Sa'd said, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So take hold of it with strength," he said: with earnestness.

10113 [sic]. Musa told me, he said: 'Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "So take hold of it with strength," he said: with earnestness and striving.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: take hold of it with obedience to God.

Those who said so:

15114. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd told us, he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, concerning His words: "So take hold of it with strength," he said: with obedience.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of this, with its evidence and the differences of the people of interpretation concerning it, in Surah al-Baqarah at His words: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:63], and that suffices so that it need not be repeated here. [[(1) See what has passed, volume 2, pp. 160–161.]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And command your people, they will take the best of it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We said to Musa: "And command your people," the Children of Israel, "they will take the best of it," meaning: they will act upon the best of what they find in it, as:

15115. Musa told me, he said: 'Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And command your people, they will take the best of it," the best of what they find in it.

15116. 'Abd al-Karim told me, he said: Ibrahim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Abu Sa'd told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And command your people, they will take the best of it," he said: Musa was commanded to take it with more firmness than he was commanded to ask of his people.

* *

If someone says: What is the meaning of His words "and command your people, they will take the best of it"? Was it one of their traits to leave out some of the good that is in it?

It is said: No. But in it there was a command and a prohibition, so God commanded them to act upon what He commanded them to do, and to leave what He forbade them. Acting upon what is commanded is better than acting upon what is forbidden.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Musa, when He wrote on the tablets of everything: Take hold of it with earnestness in acting upon what is in it and with striving, and command your people to take the best of what is in it, and forbid them from neglecting it, and from neglecting acting upon what is in it, and from associating anything with Me. For whoever among them or others associates anything with Me, I will show him in the Hereafter, when he comes to Me, "the abode of the defiantly disobedient" (dar al-fasiqin), and it is the Fire of God which He has prepared for His enemies. [[(1) See the explanation of "defiance" (fisq) in what has passed, p. 11, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

He only said "I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient" as one says to someone he is addressing: "Tomorrow I will show you where the state of one who opposes my command will end," as a threat and warning to whoever disobeys him and opposes his command. [[(2) In the printed edition it reads "on the basis of threat," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the pure correct reading.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have differed concerning the meaning of this.

Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

15117. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient," he said: their destination in the Hereafter.

15118. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

15119. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim told us, he said: Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: "I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient," he said: Hell.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: I will make you enter the land of Syria, and I will show you the dwellings of the disbelievers who are its inhabitants, from the tyrants and the Amalekites.

Those who said so:

15120. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient," their dwellings.

15121. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "the abode of the defiantly disobedient," he said: their dwellings.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: I will show you the abode of the people of Pharaoh, which is Egypt.

Those who said so:

................................................................................................

..............................................................................................

[[(1) Blank space in the manuscript of about five lines; in the margin of the manuscript, in red ink: "Lacuna, as in the original."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have chosen the view we have chosen in the interpretation of this, because what precedes His words, majestic is His praise, "I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient," is a command from God to Musa and his people to act upon what is in the Torah. So the most fitting of matters with God's wisdom is that this be concluded with a threat against whoever neglects it, falls short in acting for God, and turns away from His path, rather than with a report about what the report has already ceased to be about, or about what has not been mentioned.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant in the earth without right﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "I will remove from them understanding of the Book."

Mention of those who said this:

15122. Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr narrated to me, saying: I heard Ibn 'Uyaynah say concerning the words of God, "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant in the earth without right," that He says: "I will remove from them the understanding of the Qur'an, and I will turn them away from My signs." [[(2) The report: 15122 — Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar al-Ramadi, a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned earlier under numbers 10260 and 10521. And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr ibn Sulayman al-Khuza'i al-San'ani al-Khalanji, a trustworthy narrator (saduq). Al-Nasa'i, Abu Hatim and others narrated from him. His biography is in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/295.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation of Ibn 'Uyaynah indicates that, in his view, this statement was a threat from God to the people of disbelief in God among those to whom our Prophet ﷺ was sent, and not to the people of Musa, because the Qur'an was revealed only to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, not to Musa (peace be upon him).

* *

Others said concerning this: its meaning is: "I will turn them away from taking lessons from the proofs."

Mention of those who said this:

15123. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning "I will turn away from My signs": from the creation of the heavens and the earth and the signs within them; "I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking heed."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views, in our judgment, is that it be said: God informed that He will turn away from His signs, which are His proofs and indicators of the truth of what He commanded His servants and obligated upon them of obedience to Him in His oneness and justice, [[(1) In the printed edition: "ala haqiqati ma amara bihi 'ibadahu" — it was altered as its predecessors were. See what preceded, p. 68, note 4, and the references there.]] and other of His obligations. The heavens and the earth, and every existing thing of His creation, are among His signs, and the Qur'an too is among His signs. [[(2) See the explanation of "ayah" in the vocabulary indexes of what preceded (ayy).]] He has generally informed that He turns away from His signs those who are arrogant in the earth without right, and they are those upon whom the word of God has come true that they will not believe. So they are turned away from understanding all His signs and from taking lessons and remembrance from them. For if they were granted success in understanding some of that and guided to take a lesson from it, they would admonish themselves and turn in repentance to the truth; but that does not occur from them, because He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾, and there is no alteration of the words of God.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of right guidance, they will not take it as a way; and if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ (146)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if those who are arrogant in the earth without right see — "and their arrogance therein without right" means their tyranny therein and their haughtiness in refusing to believe in God and His Messenger and to submit to His command and prohibition, [[(1) See the explanation of "takabbur" (arrogance) above, p. 70, note 1, and the references there.]] while they are servants of God whom He nourishes with His bounty and whose provision He brings to them morning and evening — ﴿every sign﴾, that is: every proof of God's oneness and lordship, and every indication that worship is not fitting except to Him alone, to the exclusion of others — ﴿they will not believe in it﴾, that is: they will not affirm that sign as indicating what it proves; rather they say, "It is sorcery and lies." ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not take it as a way﴾, that is: if those described by this description see the path of guidance and rectitude which, if they travelled it, would save them from ruin and destruction and bring them to eternal bliss, they will not travel it nor take it for themselves as a way, out of their ignorance and bewilderment. [[(5) See the explanation of "al-sabil" (way) above in the vocabulary indexes (sabl), and of "al-rushd" (right guidance) above, 3:482 / 5:416 / 7:576.]] ﴿And if they see the way of error﴾, that is: if they see the path of destruction which, if they travel it, they go astray and perish.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-ghayy" (error) earlier, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. [[(6) See the explanation of "al-ghayy" above, 5:416 / 12:333.]]

﴿They will take it as a way﴾, that is: they will travel it and make it a path for themselves, because God has turned them away from His signs and sealed their hearts, so they do not prosper nor succeed. ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We turned them away from Our signs, so that they would not understand them and comprehend them, and so that they would not take lessons from them and remember and turn in repentance, as a punishment from Us for their denial of Our signs. ﴿And were heedless of them﴾, that is: they were heedless of Our signs and Our proofs which bear witness to the truth of what We commanded them and forbade them. ﴿Heedless﴾: they do not reflect upon them, they are unmindful of them, and they do not take lessons from them; so the word of our Lord became binding upon them, and they perished. [[(1) See the explanation of "al-ghaflah" (heedlessness) above, p. 75, note 4, and the references there.]]

* *

The readers differed regarding the reading of His words: "al-rushd."

The common readers of Madina, some of the Meccans and some of the Basrans read it: ﴿al-rushd﴾, with a damma on the "ra" and a sukun on the "shin."

* *

The common readers of Kufa and some of the Meccans read it: ﴿al-rashad﴾, with a fatha on the "ra" and the "shin."

* *

Then the scholars of the Arabic language differed regarding the meaning of this when its "ra" is vowelled with damma and its "shin" is unvowelled, and regarding the meaning when both are vowelled with fatha.

It is reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he used to say: its meaning, when its "ra" is vowelled with damma and its "shin" is unvowelled, is righteousness, as God said: ﴿If you perceive in them rushd (sound judgement)﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 6], meaning: righteousness. And thus he himself would read it. Its meaning when both its "ra" and "shin" are vowelled with fatha is: rectitude in religion, as the exalted One said: ﴿Will you teach me of what you have been taught as rashad (right guidance)?﴾ [Surat al-Kahf: 66], meaning: uprightness and correctness in religion. [[(2) Our reading and the reading of the Seven: "rushdan" (with damma on the "ra" and sukun on the "shin"); Abu 'Amr's reading among the Seven is as Abu Ja'far mentioned, and therefore he cited it for Abu 'Amr at this place. Abu Ja'far did not mention this reading in his explanation of the verse from Surat al-Kahf.]]

* *

Al-Kisa'i used to say: they are two dialects with one meaning, like "al-suqm" and "al-saqam" (sickness), and "al-huzn" and "al-hazan" (sorrow); and likewise "al-rushd" and "al-rashad."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my judgment, is to say: they are two readings widely transmitted among the readers of the cities, agreeing in meaning; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct in it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 147:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for these arrogant ones upon the earth without right, and every denier of God's proofs, His messengers and His signs, and everyone who rejects that He will be raised after death on the Day of Resurrection, and who denies the meeting with God in the Hereafter, their deeds have gone and become void, and their burdens have been acquired and established for them, because they worked for other than God and wearied themselves in what does not please God, so their deeds became a burden upon them. God, mighty is His praise, says: "Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?" meaning: will they be rewarded except with the reward of what they used to do? [[(1) In the printed edition: "will they receive except the reward of", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] So the reward of their deeds becomes eternal abiding in a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them, since their deeds were in obedience to Satan rather than to the Most Merciful. We seek refuge with God from His wrath. We have already explained the meaning of "ḥubūṭ" (nullification of deeds), "jazā'" (recompense) and "ākhirah" (the Hereafter) earlier, in a way that makes repeating them unnecessary. [[(2) See the explanation of "ḥubūṭ" earlier, vol. 11, p. 514, note 2, and the references there. For the explanation of "jazā'" and "ākhirah", see the language indices earlier under the roots (jazā) and (akhara).]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the people of Moses, after him, made from their ornaments a calf, a body that had a lowing sound. Did they not see that it does not speak to them and does not guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers﴾ (7:148).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, He says: The children of Israel, the people of Moses, took after Moses had departed from them, going forward to his Lord for His intimate conversation, and in fulfilment of the promise which his Lord had made to him, "from their ornaments a calf" (ʿijl), which is the young of a cow, and they worshipped it.
