القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿أَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَّا إِنْ هِيَ إِلا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغَافِرِينَ (١٥٥) ﴾
(On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? This is only Your trial: You lead astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers﴾ (7:155))

قال أبو جعفر: اختلف أهل التأويل في تأويل ذلك.
(Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding its interpretation.)

فقال بعضهم: معنى ذلك: أتهلك هؤلاء الذين أهلكتهم بما فعل السفهاء منا، أي: بعبادة من عبد العجل؟ قالوا: وكان الله إنما أهلكهم لأنهم كانوا ممن يَعبد العجل. وقال موسى ما قال، ولا علم عنده بما كان منهم من ذلك. [[(١) انظر تفسير ((السفهاء)) فيما سلف من فهارس اللغة (سفه) = وتفسير ((الهلاك)) فيما سلف (هلك) .]]
(Some of them said: The meaning is: Will You destroy these whom You destroyed for what the foolish among us did, that is, for worshipping those who worshipped the calf? They said: God destroyed them only because they were among those who worshipped the calf. Musa said what he said, but he had no knowledge of what they had done in that regard. [[(1) See the explanation of "as-sufaha'" (the foolish) earlier in the language index (s-f-h), and the explanation of "al-halak" (destruction) earlier (h-l-k).]]

ذكر من قال ذلك:
(Those who said this:)
١٥١٦٨- حدثنا موسى بن هارون قال، حدثنا عمرو قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي: "أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا"، فأوحى الله إلى موسى: إن هؤلاء السبعين ممن اتخذ العجلَ! فذلك حين يقول موسى: "إن هي إلا فتنتك تُضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء". [[(٢) الأثر: ١٥١٦٨ - مضى قديمًا برقم ٩٥٨ بتمامه، ومضى صدره قريبًا برقم: ١٥١٥٢]]
(15168: Musa ibn Harun told us, he said: 'Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?" God revealed to Musa: These seventy have taken the calf! So that is when Musa says: "This is only Your trial: You lead astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will." [[(2) The report 15168 passed long ago under number 958 in full, and its beginning passed recently under number 15152.]]

* *

وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: إن إهلاكك هؤلاء الذين أهلكتهم، هلاك لمن وراءهم من بني إسرائيل، إذا انصرفت إليهم وليسوا معي= و"السفهاء"، على هذا القول، كانوا المهلَكين الذين سألوا موسى أن يُرِيهم ربَّهم.
(Others said: The meaning is: Your destruction of these whom You destroyed is a destruction of those behind them from the Children of Israel, when I return to them and these are not with me. And "the foolish," according to this view, were those destroyed who asked Musa to show them their Lord.)

ذكر من قال ذلك:
(Those who said this:)
١٥١٦٩- حدثنا ابن حميد قال، حدثنا سلمة، عن ابن إسحاق قال: لما أخذت الرجفة السبعين فماتوا جميعًا، قام موسى يناشد ربّه ويدعوه ويرغب إليه، يقول: "رب لو شئتَ أهلكتهم من قبل وإيّاي"، قد سفهوا، أفتهلك من ورائي من بني إسرائيل بما فعل السفهاء منا؟ أي: إن هذا لهم هلاكٌ، قد اخترت منهم سبعين رجلا الخيِّر فالخيِّر، أرجع إليهم وليس معى رجل واحد! فما الذي يصدِّقونني به، أو يأمنونني عليه بعد هذا؟ [[الأثر: ١٥١٦٩ مضى قديما برقم ٩٥٧ بتمامه، ومضى قريبا بتمامه رقم: ١٥١٥٣.]]
(15169: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the quake seized the seventy and they all died, Musa stood beseeching his Lord, calling upon Him and turning to Him in desire, saying: "My Lord, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me too," they had acted foolishly. Will You destroy those behind me among the Children of Israel for what the foolish among us did? That is: this is a destruction for them. I had chosen from among them seventy men, the best and then the best. I return to them and not a single man is with me! What will they believe me about, or trust me with, after this? [[The report 15169 passed long ago under number 957 in full, and passed recently in full under number 15153.]]

* *

وقال آخرون في ذلك بما: -
(Others said about this, with what follows:)
١٥١٧٠- حدثني يونس قال، أخبرنا ابن وهب قال، قال ابن زيد في قوله: "أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا"، أتؤاخذنا وليس منا رجلٌ واحد تَرَك عبادتك، ولا استبدل بك غيرك؟
(15170: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?" Will You punish us when not one of us has abandoned Your worship or exchanged You for another?)

* *

قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين بتأويل الآية، قولُ من قال: إن موسى إنما حزن على هلاك السبعين بقوله: "أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا"، وأنّه إنما عنى ب"السفهاء" عبدةَ العجل. وذلك أنه محالٌ أن يكون موسى ﷺ كان تخيَّر من قومه لمسألة ربِّه ما أراه أن يسألَ لهم إلا الأفضل فالأفضل منهم، ومحالٌ أن يكون الأفضل كان عنده مَنْ أشرك في عبادة العجل واتخذَه دون الله إلهًا.
(Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of those who said that Musa grieved over the destruction of the seventy by his words "Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?", and that by "the foolish" he meant the worshippers of the calf. This is because it is impossible that Musa ﷺ had chosen from his people, for the request to his Lord, only the best of them, the best among them, and then that the best in his view were those who associated others in worshipping the calf and took it as a god besides God.)

* *

قال: فإن قال قائل: فجائز أن يكون موسى عليه السلام كان معتقدًا أن الله سبحانه يعاقب قومًا بذنوب غيرهم، فيقول: أتهلكنا بذنوب من عبد العجل، ونحن من ذلك برآء؟ قيل: جائز أن يكون معنى "الإهلاك" قبض الأرواح على غير وجه العقوبة، كما قال جل ثناؤه: ﴿إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ﴾ ، [سورة النساء: ١٧٦] = يعني: مات= فيقول: أتميتنا بما فعل السُّفهاء منَّا؟ [[انظر تفسير ((الهلاك)) فيما سلف ٩: ٣٠ / ١٠٤: ١٤٧، وفهارس اللغة (هلك) .]]
(He said: If someone says: Is it possible that Musa, peace be upon him, believed that God, glory be to Him, punishes a people for the sins of others, and so he says: "Will You destroy us for the sins of those who worshipped the calf, when we are innocent of that?" It is said: It is possible that the meaning of "destruction" is the taking of souls not by way of punishment, as His majestic praise says: ﴿If a man dies (halaka)﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:176], meaning: dies. So he says: Will You cause us to die for what the foolish among us did? [[See the explanation of "al-halak" (destruction) earlier, 9: 30 / 10: 147, and the language index (h-l-k).]]

* *

وأما قوله: "إن هي إلا فتنتك"، فإنه يقول جل ثناؤه: ما هذه الفعلة التي فعلَها قومي، من عبادتهم ما عبَدُوا دونك، إلا فتنة منك أصَابتهم= ويعني ب"الفتنة"، الابتلاء والاختبار [[(١) انظر تفسير ((الفتنة)) فيما سلف ١٢: ٣٧٣، تعليق: ١، والمراجع هناك.]] = يقول: ابتليتهم بها، ليتبين الذي يضلَّ عن الحق بعبادته إياه، والذي يهتدي بترك عبادته. وأضاف إضلالهم وهدايتهم إلى الله، إذ كان ما كان منهم من ذلك عن سببٍ منه جل ثناؤه.
(As for His words: "This is only Your trial," He, may His majestic praise be exalted, means: this act that my people did, in worshipping what they worshipped besides You, is only a trial from You that befell them — and by "trial" (fitna) is meant testing and examination [[(1) See the explanation of "fitna" earlier, 12: 373, note 1, and the references there.]] — that is, You tested them with it, so that it might become clear who goes astray from the truth by worshipping it, and who is guided by abandoning its worship. He attributed their leading astray and their guidance to God, since what occurred among them of that was from a cause from Him, may His majestic praise be exalted.)

* *

وبنحو ما قلنا في "الفتنة" قال جماعة من أهل التأويل.
(Several of the people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said about "fitna.")
ذكر من قال ذلك:
(Those who said this:)
١٥١٧١- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبى، عن أبي جعفر، عن الربيع، عن أبي العالية: ﴿إن هي إلا فتنتك"،﴾ قال: بليّتك.
(15171: Ibn WakI' told us, he said: My father told us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya: "This is only Your trial," he said: Your affliction.)

١٥١٧٢-.... قال، حدثنا حبويه الرازي، عن يعقوب، عن جعفر بن أبي المغيرة، عن سعيد بن جبير: "إلا فتنتك"،: إلا بليتك. [[(٢) الأثر: ١٥١٧٢ - ((حبويه الرازي)) هو: ((إسحق بن إسماعيل الرازي)) ((أبو يزيد)) ، مضى مرارًا، آخرها رقم ١٥٠١٥، والراوي عن حبويه هو ((ابن وكيع)) ، كما هو ظاهر، ولذلك وضعت نقطاً مكان اسمه، في هذا الموضع وما يشابهه من المواضع، حيث يختصر أبو جعفر شيخه من الإسناد.]]
(15172: ... he said: Habwayh al-Razi told us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Only Your trial": only Your affliction. [[(2) The report 15172: "Habwayh al-Razi" is Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi, Abu Yazid, who has passed many times, the last at number 15015. The narrator from Habwayh is Ibn WakI', as is clear, and for that reason I have placed dots in place of his name in this place and similar places, where Abu Ja'far abbreviates his teacher from the isnad (chain).]]

١٥١٧٣- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن سعد قال، أخبرنا أبو جعفر، [[(٣) في المطبعة والمخطوطة: ((أخبرنا ابن جعفر)) ، وهو خطأ ظاهر جداً، صوابه ما أثبت. وقد مضى هذا الإسناد وشبهه من رواية أبي جعفر الرازي عن الربيع، انظر ما سلف قريباً: ١٥١٧١.]] عن الربيع بن أنس: "إن هي إلا فتنتك"، قال: بليتك.
(15173: al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd told us, he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, [[(3) In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Ibn Ja'far informed us," which is an obvious and very great error; the correct reading is what I have written. This isnad and its like have passed through the narration of Abu Ja'far al-Razi from al-Rabi'; see above 15171.]] from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "This is only Your trial," he said: Your affliction.)

١٥١٧٤-.... قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح قال، حدثني معاوية بن صالح، عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: "إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء"، إن هو إلا عذابك تصيبُ به من تشاء، وتصرفه عمن تشاء. [[(٤) الأثر: ١٥١٧٤ - شيخ الطبري في هذا الإسناد، هو ((المثنى)) المذكور في الأثر قبله. وسأضع هذه النقط، حيث يختصر أبو جعفر شيخه، ثم لا أنبه إليه، ومعلوم أن المحذوف هو شيخه في الإسناد قبله.]]
(15174: ... he said: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "This is only Your trial: You lead astray by it whom You will," meaning: it is only Your punishment, with which You strike whom You will, and You turn it away from whom You will. [[(4) The teacher of al-Tabari in this isnad is "al-Muthanna" mentioned in the report before it. I will place these dots where Abu Ja'far abbreviates his teacher, and I will not point it out again; it is known that the omitted one is his teacher in the preceding isnad.]]

١٥١٧٥- حدثني يونس قال، أخبرنا ابن وهب قال، قال ابن زيد في قوله: "إن هي إلا فتنتك"، أنت فتنتهم.
(15175: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "This is only Your trial," You are their trial.)

* *

وقوله: "أنت ولينا"، يقول: أنت ناصرنا. [[(١) انظر تفسير ((ولى)) فيما سلف ١١: ٢٨٢، تعليق: ١، والمراجع هناك.]] = "فاغفر لنا"، يقول: فاستر علينا ذنوبَنا بتركك عقابَنا عليها= "وارحمنا"، تعطف علينا برحمتك= "وأنت خير الغافرين"، يقول: خير من صَفَح عن جُرم، وسَتر على ذنب. [[(٢) انظر تفسير ((المغفرة)) ، و ((الرحمة)) فيما سلف من فهارس اللغة (غفر) و (رحم) .]]
(As for His words: "You are our Protector" (waliyyuna), He means: You are our helper. [[(1) See the explanation of "wali" (protector) earlier, 11: 282, note 1, and the references there.]] "So forgive us" — He means: cover over our sins for us by Your not punishing us for them; "and have mercy upon us" — show compassion to us with Your mercy; "and You are the best of forgivers" — He means: the best of those who pardon an offence and conceal a sin. [[(2) See the explanation of "al-maghfira" (forgiveness) and "al-rahma" (mercy) earlier in the language indexes (gh-f-r) and (r-h-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 156:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And prescribe for us in this world a good [thing], and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, reporting the supplication of His Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, in which he said: "And prescribe for us," meaning: make us among those for whom You have prescribed "in this world a good [thing]," which means righteous deeds [[(3) See the explanation of "al-husna" (the good) in the earlier lexical indexes under (ḥ-s-n).]] "and in the Hereafter," meaning among those for whom You have prescribed forgiveness of their sins, as:

15176- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: "And prescribe for us in this world a good [thing]," he said: forgiveness.

* *

As for His words: "Indeed, we have turned back (hudna) to You," it means: indeed, we have repented to You. [[(4) See the explanation of "hada" in the earlier volume 12, p. 198, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said the same.

15178- He said: Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: we have repented to You.

15179-.... He said: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: we have repented to You.

15180-.... We have already explained the meaning of this with its evidences earlier, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. [[(4) See the explanation of "hada" in the earlier volume, p. 152, note 4, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He said: My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me, and pay the zakat, and those who believe in Our verses.﴾ (156)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: God said to Musa: this with which I struck your people from the earthquake, My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will of My creatures, just as I afflicted these whom I afflicted among your people with it [[(1) See the explanation of "al-isaba" in the earlier lexical indexes under (ṣ-w-b).]] "and My mercy encompasses all things," meaning: My mercy has embraced all of My creatures. [[(2) See the explanation of "wasi'a" in the earlier volume 12: 562, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its outward meaning is general, and its meaning is specific, and what is intended is: My mercy has encompassed those who believe in Me from the community of Muhammad ﷺ. They cited as evidence the statement that follows it, which is His words: "so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me," and so on.

Mention of those who said that:

15202- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salama al-Munqari narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that he recited: "And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me." He said: Allah made it for this community. [[(3) Report 15202: Abu Salama al-Munqari is Abu Salama al-Tabudhaki, Musa ibn Isma'il al-Munqari, their client. Al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud narrated from him, and the rest of the authors of the six books narrated from him through an intermediary. He is trustworthy and an imam. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/280, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/136.]]

15203- Abd al-Karim narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali said: When "And My mercy encompasses all things" was revealed, Iblis said: "I am among 'things'!" So Allah withdrew it from Iblis, and He said: "So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and pay the zakat and those who believe in Our verses." The Jews said: "We fear Allah, pay the zakat, and believe in the verses of our Lord!" So Allah withdrew it from the Jews and said: "Those who follow the Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet." He said: Allah withdrew it from Iblis and from the Jews, and made it for this community. [[(1) Report 15203: Abd al-Karim is Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham ibn Ziyad al-Qattan, a teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, mentioned under no. 892. Ibrahim ibn Bashshar al-Ramadi is trustworthy, mentioned under nos. 892 and 6321. Sufyan is Ibn Uyayna. Abu Bakr al-Hudhali is weak, mentioned several times, the last under no. 14690.]]

15204- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: When "And My mercy encompasses all things" was revealed, Iblis said: "I am among 'all things'!" God said: "So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and pay the zakat and those who believe in Our verses," and so on. The Jews said: "We too fear Allah and pay the zakat!" So God revealed: "Those who follow the Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet." He said: God withdrew it from Iblis and from the Jews, and made it for the community of Muhammad: "I will prescribe it for those of your people who fear Me."

15205- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things." Iblis said: "I am among that 'thing'!" So God revealed: "So I will prescribe it for those who fear" the disobedience of Allah, "and who believe in Our verses." The Jews and Christians coveted it, so God revealed a firm, clear condition, saying: "Those who follow the Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet," who is your Prophet, who was unlettered and did not write ﷺ.

15206- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha informed us, from Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And prescribe for us in this world a good [thing], and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You," he said: He did not give it, so He said: "My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me," up to His words: "the Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet." [[(1) Reports 15206 and 15207: Anas Abu al-Aryan al-Mujashi'i, without "ibn" between them, is biographed in al-Kabir 1/2/44 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/333, and neither indicates that he is "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan." In the manuscript in the first report it reads "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan" with "ibn," and in the second report in both places "Anas ibn al-Aryan" without "ibn," as I have recorded it; in the printed edition he has made it "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan" throughout, which is a blameworthy alteration without doubt. It appears the name was reported differently from Ibn Ulayya: once as "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan," then as "Anas Abi al-Aryan," as in the second of them, and al-Tabari mentioned the statement of Abd al-A'la to support this report from Ibn Ulayya. If this difference is confirmed from Ibn Uyayna, otherwise one of two things must be the case: either the correct form of the first report is "Anas Abi al-Aryan," and the second is "Anas Abi al-Aryan" and from Abd al-A'la "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan"; or the first from Ibn Uyayna is "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan," the second also "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan," and from Abd al-A'la "Anas ibn Abi al-Aryan." God knows best the correct form in all of this, and I have no preference.]]

15207- Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya and Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Khalid, from Anas Abi al-Aryan, said Abd al-A'la, from Anas Abi al-A'rjan, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: "And prescribe for us in this world a good [thing], and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You," he said: Musa was not given it, so He said: "My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it," to the end of the verse.

15208- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God had written in the tablets the mention of Muhammad and the mention of his community, what He had stored up for them with Him, what He had made easy for them in their religion, and what He had widened for them in what He made lawful for them. So He said: "My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me" = meaning: shirk = the verse.

* *

Others said: rather, it is general in this world and specific in the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

15209- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding His words: "And My mercy encompasses all things," they both said: It encompassed the righteous and the wicked in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection it is for those who are God-fearing exclusively.

* *

Others said: it is general, and it is repentance.

Mention of those who said that:

15210- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers. And prescribe for us in this world a good [thing], and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You," he said: Musa asked this, and God said: "My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will" = the punishment He mentioned = "and My mercy," repentance = "encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me." He said: So His mercy is the repentance which Musa, peace be upon him, asked for, which God prescribed for us.

* *

As for His words: "so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me," it means: so I will prescribe My mercy which encompasses all things. The meaning of "prescribe" in this place is: I will write in the tablet in which the Torah was written, "for those who fear Me," meaning: for the people who fear God and dread His punishment for disbelieving in Him and disobeying Him in His command and prohibition, so they perform His obligations and avoid His disobediences. [[(1) In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "al-ladhina yattaquna" without the lam; the correct form is what I have recorded.]] [[(2) See the explanation of "taqwa" in the earlier lexical indexes under (w-q-y).]]

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning by which God described these people as fearing Him. Some of them said: it is shirk.

Mention of those who said that:

15211- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me," meaning shirk.

* *

Others said: rather, it is all sins.

Mention of those who said that:

15212- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me," the disobediences of God.

* *

As for "zakat and paying it," we have explained its nature earlier, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. [[(1) See the explanation of "iita' al-zakat" in the earlier volume 1: 573-574, and what follows, in the lexical indexes under (z-k-w) and (a-t-y).]]

* *

It has been mentioned from Ibn Abbas regarding this place that he said the following:

15213- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "and who pay the zakat," he said: those who obey God and His Messenger.

* *

It seems that Ibn Abbas interpreted it to mean the practice of what purifies the soul and cleanses it of righteous deeds.

* *

As for His words: "and those who believe in Our verses," it means: for the people who give credence to and acknowledge Our signs and proofs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 157:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This statement is a clarification from God, may His praise be majestic, that those whom Moses, peace be upon him, was promised by his Lord that He would write mercy for them, the mercy which He described, may His praise be majestic, in His words: "And My mercy encompasses all things," are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is because no messenger of God is known to have been described with this attribute, meaning "the unlettered" (al-ummi), other than our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). And the narrations from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have come to this effect.

Mention of those who said this:

15214. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: 'Imran ibn 'Uyayna related to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So I will write it for those who fear God," he said: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

15215. ... He said: Zayd ibn Habbab related to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

15216. Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakic related to us, both said: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id regarding His words: "So I will write it for those who fear God," he said: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then Moses, peace be upon him, said: "Would that I had been created in the community of Muhammad!"

15217. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic related to us, both said: Jarir related to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "So I will write it for those who fear God," he said: those who follow Muhammad (ﷺ).

15218. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Nawf al-Himyari, he said: When Moses chose seventy men from his people for the appointed time of his Lord, God said to Moses: "I will make the earth for you a place of prostration and a purifier, and I will place tranquility (sakina) among you in your houses, and I will make you recite the Torah from the backs of your hearts" [in the printed edition: "from the backs of the hearts," with the plural "hearts," and what is in the manuscript is retained, which is entirely correct], "a man among you and a woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old will recite it." Moses said to his people: "Indeed God may make the earth for you a purifier and a place of prostration." They said: "We do not want to pray except in churches!" He said: "And He will place tranquility among you in your houses." They said: "We want only that it be as it was, in the ark!" He said: "And He will make you recite the Torah from the back of your hearts" [in the printed edition: "from the backs"; see the note above], "and a man among you and a woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old will recite it." They said: "We do not want to recite it except by looking!" So God said: "So I will write it for those who fear God and give zakat," up to His words: "those are the successful."

[Note: The narration 15218: "Nawf al-Himyari" is Nawf al-Bakali mentioned in the two following narrations 15219 and 15220, and he is "Nawf ibn Fudala al-Himyari al-Bakali al-Shami," who passed as no. 3965, 9446, 9456.]

15219. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Nawf al-Bakali, he said: When Moses set off with the delegation of the Children of Israel, God spoke to him, saying: "Indeed I have spread the earth for them as a purifier and places of prostration where they may pray wherever prayer reaches them, except at a latrine, a grave, or a bath; and I have placed tranquility in their hearts, and made them recite the Torah from the back of their tongues." He said: Moses mentioned that to the Children of Israel, and they said: "We cannot bear the tranquility in our hearts, so place it for us in an ark; and we will not recite the Torah except by looking, and we will not pray except in the church!" So God said: "So I will write it for those who fear God and give zakat," until He reached: "those are the successful." He said: Moses, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, make me their prophet!" He said: "Their prophet is one of them!" He said: "Lord, make me one of them!" He said: "You will not reach them!" He said: "O Lord, I brought You the delegation of the Children of Israel, and You made our delegation for others!" So God revealed: "And among the people of Moses is a community that guides by the truth and by it acts justly" [Surah al-A'raf: 159].

Nawf al-Bakali said: So praise God who preserved your absence and took your share for you, and made the delegation of the Children of Israel for you.

15220. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Nawf al-Bakali, similarly, except that he said: "Indeed I will send down to you the Torah which you will recite from the back of your tongues, your men, your women and your children." They said: "We will not pray except in a church," then he mentioned the rest of the narration similarly.

15221. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il related to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "So I will write it for those who fear God," he said: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). [Note: The narration 15221: "Ishaq ibn Isma'il" is Hubayya, Abu Yazid al-Razi, who passed shortly before as no. 15198, and is named here for the first time.]

15222. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "So I will write it for those who fear God," he said: these are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

15223. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, he said: When it was said: "So I will write it for those who fear God and give zakat, and those who believe in Our signs," the Jews and Christians coveted it, so God revealed a clear and firm condition, saying: "Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet," and he is your Prophet (ﷺ), who was unlettered and did not write. [Note: narration 15223 - see the earlier narration no. 15205.]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "the unlettered" previously, in a way that suffices without repeating it. [Note: see the explanation of "al-ummi" previously, 2: 257-259 / 3: 442 / 6: 281, 282, 522; then see nos. 5827, 1774, 6775.]

* *

As for His words: "whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel," the pronoun in His words "they find him" refers to "the Messenger," who is Muhammad (ﷺ), as in what follows:

15224. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet," this is Muhammad (ﷺ).

15225. Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar related to us, he said: Fulayh related to us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: I met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and I said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is indeed described in the Torah as he is described in the Qur'an: "O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner, and a guardian for the unlettered," "you are My servant and My Messenger, I have named you the one who relies (al-mutawakkil)," [in the printed edition: "I have named you," and what is in the manuscript is retained], "not harsh, nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but pardons and forgives, and We will not take him until through him We set right the crooked community, by their saying: 'There is no god but God,' and We open with it hearts that are veiled, ears that are deaf, and eyes that are blind." 'Ata' said: Then I met Ka'b and asked him about that, and they did not differ by a letter, except that Ka'b said in his language: "hearts veiled (ghulufiya), ears deaf (sumumiya), and eyes blind ('umumiya)." [Note: narration 15225 - 'Uthman ibn 'Umar ibn Faris ibn Luqayt al-'Abdi, trustworthy, a teacher of Ahmad, transmitted by the group, passed as no. 5458. "Fulayh" is Fulayh ibn Sulayman ibn Abi al-Mughira al-Khuzami, trustworthy, transmitted by the group, passed as no. 5090. "Hilal ibn 'Ali ibn Usama al-Madani," who is attributed to his grandfather so it is said "Hilal ibn Usama," trustworthy, passed as no. 1495. See the following narrations.]

15226. Abu Kurayb related to me, he said: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, he said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, he said: 'Ata' related to me, he said: I met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and he mentioned something similar, except that in the words of Ka'b he said: "eyes ('amman) blind ('ummuma), ears deaf (sumuma), and hearts veiled (ghulufa)."

15227. ... He said: Musa related to us, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Salama related to us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abd Allah similarly, except that it lacks the words of Ka'b.

15228. Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding God's words: "whom they find written with them," he said: they find his description, his command, and his prophethood written with them.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This unlettered Prophet commands his followers what is right, which is faith in God and adherence to His obedience in what He commands and forbids; this is "the right" which he commands them with, "and forbids them what is wrong," which is associating partners with God, and refraining from what God has forbidden them. As for His words: "and makes lawful for them the good things," this refers to what the Jahiliyya used to forbid, such as the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila, and the ham [note: see the explanation of "al-tayyibat" previously, 11: 96, note 2, and references there], "and makes unlawful for them the evil things," which is the flesh of swine and usury, and what they used to consider lawful of foods and drinks that God had forbidden, [note: see the explanation of "al-khaba'ith" previously, 11: 96, note 2, and references there], as:

15229. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "and makes unlawful for them the evil things," which is the flesh of swine and usury, and what they used to consider lawful of the forbidden foods that God had forbidden.

* *

As for His words: "and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them," the people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation.

Some of them said: By "isr" is meant the covenant and pact that He had taken from the Children of Israel to act by what is in the Torah.

Mention of those who said this:

15230. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "and relieves them of their burden," he said: their covenant.

15231. ... He said: al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, he said: their covenant.

15232. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

15233. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: "and relieves them of their burden," he said: the covenants they gave from themselves.

15234. ... He said: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Musa ibn Qays, from Mujahid: "and relieves them of their burden," he said: their covenant. [Note: narration 15234 - Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami, passed as no. 6513.]

15235. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them," he says: He relieves them of their covenants and pacts that were taken from them in the Torah and the Gospel.

15236. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them," the covenant God had taken from them concerning what He forbade them. He says: He relieves them of that.

* *

Others said: It means that he relieves from those who follow the Prophet of God (ﷺ) the severity that was upon the Children of Israel in their religion.

Mention of those who said this:

15237. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them," so Muhammad (ﷺ) came with a pardon from Him and an overlooking of it.

15238. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: al-Hammani related to us, he said: Sharik related to us, from Salim, from Sa'id: "and relieves them of their burden," he said: urine and the like, which was made strict upon the Children of Israel.

15239. ... He said: al-Hammani related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, he said: the severity of the work.

15240. Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said regarding His words: "and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them," he said: whoever follows Muhammad and his religion from the People of the Book, the severity that was upon them in their religion is removed from them.

15241. Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, he said: Abu Hurayra said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Is there no hardship upon us in religion that we may commit adultery and steal?" He said: Yes! But the burden that was upon the Children of Israel has been removed from you.

15242. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "and relieves them of their burden," he said: their burden which He placed upon them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these statements, the most appropriate to the truth, is that it be said: The "isr" is the covenant [note: we have explained this with its evidences in a place other than this sufficiently; see the explanation of "isr" previously, 6: 135-138, 560], and the meaning of the sentence is: the unlettered Prophet removes the covenant that God had taken from the Children of Israel, concerning establishing the Torah and acting by what is in it of severe deeds, such as cutting off the skin of urine, and forbidding spoils, and similar deeds that were obligatory upon them, which the ruling of the Qur'an abrogated.

* *

As for "the shackles that were upon them," Ibn Zayd used to say regarding it:

15243. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, from him, regarding His words: "and the shackles that were upon them," he said: "the shackles." He recited: ﴿Their hands are chained﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 64]. He said: those are the shackles. He said: and He called them to believe in the Prophet, so He would remove that from them.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So those who believed in him, honored him, supported him, and followed the light that was sent down with him - those are the successful﴾ (157)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So those who affirmed the unlettered Prophet and acknowledged his prophethood [note: see the explanation of "faith" previously in the lexical indices (amana)] "honored him," meaning: they revered him, glorified him, and protected him from people, [note: see the explanation of "ta'zir" previously, 10: 119-121], as:

15244. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "and honored him," meaning: they protected him and revered him.

15245. Al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Musa ibn Qays related to me, from Mujahid: "and honored him and supported him": "honored him" - they guided his affair rightly, and assisted his Messenger; "and supported him."

* *

As for His words "supported him," meaning: they helped him against the enemies of God and their enemies, by fighting them and waging war against them; "and followed the light that was sent down with him," meaning the Qur'an and Islam [note: see the explanation of "light" previously, 11: 526, note 2, and references there]; "those are the successful," meaning: those who do these deeds by which God, may His praise be majestic, described the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ), are the ones who attain and obtain what they sought and hoped for by their deed. [note: see the explanation of "success" previously, 12: 505, note 5, and references there.]

15246. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, he said: "What they resented" - meaning the Jews - "was only that they envied the Prophet of God." Then God said: "Those who believed in him, honored him and supported him," as for supporting him and honoring him, you have been preceded by it, but your best are those who believed in God and followed the light that was sent down with him.

* *

Qatada means by his words, "What they resented was only that they envied the Prophet of God," that the Jews, for whom Muhammad (ﷺ) with what he brought from God was a mercy upon them had they followed him, because he came with removing the burden and the shackles from them, envy led them to disbelieve in him and to refuse to accept the lightening, because of the prevalence of God's abandonment upon them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 158:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all, He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. So believe in God and His Messenger﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted One says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say", O Muhammad, to all of mankind, "Indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all", not to some of you without others, as was the case with the messengers before me, who were sent to some people and not to others. Whoever among them was sent in that manner, my message is not to some of you without others, but it is to all of you.

His saying "He to whom belongs" is an attribute of the name "God". The meaning of the statement is: Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God, He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, to you.

By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth", He means: He who has authority over the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and the management and disposal of that (see the explanation of "al-mulk" in the earlier lexical indexes under m-l-k) = "There is no deity except Him", meaning: it is not fitting that divinity and worship belong to anyone but Him, may His praise be exalted, rather than all other things, such as rivals and idols, except for the one who has authority over everything and is able to create whatever He wills and bring it to life, and to annihilate it, causing it to die, when He wills = "So believe in God and His Messenger", meaning, may His praise be exalted: Say to them: Affirm the signs of God, He who has this attribute, acknowledge His oneness, and that He is the One to whom divinity and worship belong; and affirm His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, that he is sent to His creation, calling them to His monotheism and obedience.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿the unlettered Prophet who believes in God and His words, and follow him that you may be guided﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying "the unlettered Prophet", it is an attribute of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

* *

I have already explained the meaning of "the Prophet" earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. As for the meaning of His saying "the unlettered" [[(1) See the explanation of "al-nabi" above, 2: 140–142 / 6: 284, 380, and other passages. = And the explanation of "al-ummi" above, p. 163, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

= "who believes in God", meaning: who affirms God and His words.

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying "and His words". [[(2) See the explanation of "al-kalimah" above in the lexical indexes under k-l-m.]]

Some of them said: It means: "and His signs".

Mention of those who said that:

15247 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying "who believes in God and His words": he means His signs.

* *

Others said: Rather, by that He meant Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

15248 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said concerning His saying "who believes in God and His words": he said, Jesus son of Mary.

15149 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "who believes in God and His words", that it is Jesus son of Mary.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that God, may His praise be exalted, commanded His servants to affirm the prophethood of the unlettered Prophet who believes in God and His words. He did not specify the report of his belief in "the words of God" as being about some of them rather than others, but informed them about all the "words". So the truth in this matter is that the statement should be general, for the Messenger of God ﷺ believed in all the words of God, as the apparent meaning of the Book of God indicates.

* *

As for His saying "and follow him that you may be guided": so be guided by him, O mankind, and act upon what He has commanded you to act upon of obedience to God = "that you may be guided", meaning: so that you may be guided, rightly guided, and attain the truth by following him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 159:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses there is a community (ummah) who guide by the truth and by it do justice.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And among the people of Moses," meaning the Children of Israel, "a community," that is, a group [(1) See the explanation of "ummah" above, 12:415, note 3, and the references there.] "who guide by the truth," that is, who are guided by the truth, meaning they remain upright upon it and act by it [(2) See the explanation of "guidance" (hudan) above, in the linguistic indexes, root h-d-y.] "and by it do justice," that is, by the truth they give and take, and they deal justly with themselves, so they do not act unjustly. [(3) See the explanation of "justice" (al-'adl) above, 6:51, and the linguistic indexes, root '-d-l.]

* *

Regarding the description of this community which God mentioned in the verse, a group of scholars have stated opinions, and we will mention those that have reached us.

15250. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Sadaqah Abu al-Hudhayl, from al-Suddi, regarding "And among the people of Moses a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice," he said: "A people between you and them is a river of shuhd." [(1) The report 15250: Sadaqah Abu al-Hudhayl is mentioned by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir (2/2/295), where he says only that he related from al-Suddi and that Ibn 'Uyaynah related from him, with no criticism recorded. He is also mentioned in al-Tahdhib, where Ibn Hajar says: "Sadaqah Abu al-Hudhayl, mentioned earlier in the biography of Sadaqah ibn Abi 'Imran." However, the biography of Sadaqah ibn Abi 'Imran has dropped out of the Tahdhib manuscript, so no mention of him appears in the book. Ibn Abi Hatim does not mention him in his work, neither in a separate entry nor under Sadaqah ibn Abi 'Imran. Ibn Hajar's statement in al-Tahdhib may suggest that the two are one person, but the more likely view is that they are two men, since al-Bukhari gave him a separate entry. The phrase "a river of shuhd" means a river of honey from the rivers of Paradise, of which God, may He be exalted, said in Surah Muhammad (47:15): ﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous are promised: therein are rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey.﴾ Ibn Kathir mentions it with this wording (shuhd) in his tafsir (3:573). In al-Durr al-Manthur (1:136) it reads: "and between them a river of sahl (meaning sand) flowing." Then al-Alusi, in his commentary on this verse (9:75), quoted it as: "and between them a river of sand flowing," and then said: "Ibn al-Khazin weakened this report, and I do not consider it anything, nor do I think you will find a chain of narration to rely upon, even if you sought a tunnel in the earth or a ladder to the sky." Al-Alusi's quotation from al-Suyuti's wording "sahl (meaning sand)" is very corrupt, and the correct reading is that "sahl" is a corruption of "shuhd," which is the correct form, God willing. This is the editing of the text of the report and its interpretation; as for its soundness or weakness, these are beyond the scope of correcting its wording. Reports of this kind, and the one that follows, are not to be relied upon except with a decisive proof to which submission is required. There is no proof in a report that stops at al-Suddi.]

15251. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding his words: "And among the people of Moses a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice," he said: It has reached me that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets, they disbelieved. They were twelve tribes, and one tribe disassociated itself from what they had done, and they made excuse and asked God to separate them from them. So God opened for them a tunnel in the earth, and they travelled through it until they emerged from behind China. They are there, upright, submitting (muslims), facing our qibla. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: That is His words: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land; and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together as a mixed multitude."﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:104]. And "the promise of the Hereafter" is Jesus son of Mary, and they will emerge with him. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: They travelled through the sarab for a year and a half. [(1) The report 15251: Abu Ja'far did not relate this report in his commentary on the verse of Surah al-Isra', and this is a form of abridgement of his tafsir. This may indicate that he considered the report weak, for had it been authentic according to him, he would have mentioned it in his commentary on God's words: "when the promise of the Hereafter comes," that it is Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 160:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes, as nations﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: We divided them, meaning the people of Musa from the Children of Israel. Allah divided them and made them into diverse tribes, twelve tribes.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-asbat" (the tribes) previously, and who they are. [[[[(3) In the manuscript: "yastahkā hādhā al-ta'wīl" (this interpretation is established), and in the printed edition: "yastahkā ʿalā hādhā al-ta'wīl," with the added "ʿalā," because the sentence then has no meaning. What I consider correct is what I have written: "yastakhill," from "al-khalal," which means weakness and corruption; they said "amr mukhtall," meaning corrupt and weak. So Abu Ja'far or someone else derived by analogy from "al-khalal" the form "istakhalla al-shay'," meaning he found it weak and feeble, and found a flaw in it. This is a sound analogy in Arabic, and its meaning is correct, God willing.]] See the explanation of "al-asbat" previously: 2:121, report no. 1047; 3:109-113, 122; 6:569.]]

* *

The grammarians differed concerning the reason the feminine form "al-ithnatay ʿashrah" (twelve) is used, while "al-asbat" is a masculine plural. Some grammarians of Basra said: he intended "ithnatay ʿashrah firqah" (twelve groups), then informed that the groups are "asbat," and did not make the number agree with "asbat."

* *

Some of them would deem this interpretation weak and say: the number does not agree with what is other than what follows it [[(1) In the manuscript: "ʿalā ghayr al-thānī" (with what is other than the second), and in the printed edition changed to "ʿalā ʿayn al-thānī" (with the very second); both are corrupt in meaning, and the correct reading is what I have written. It means: what follows the number, which is "asbat," and this is the apparent sense of the speech. Its estimated form, "twelve groups, asbatan," then omitting "firqah" and its implied presence, requires that the number agree with what follows it, and this confirms the reading of the text as I have given it.]], but rather "al-firaq" (the groups) comes before "al-ithnatay ʿashrah," so that "al-ithnatā ʿashrah" is feminine in agreement with what precedes it, and the sentence reads: "And We divided them into groups, twelve tribes," and the feminine is then correct because of what preceded.

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa said: He only used the feminine "al-ithnatay ʿashrah" while "al-sibt" is masculine, because the speech went to "al-umam" (the nations), so the feminine was given precedence, even though "al-sibt" is masculine. This is like the saying of the poet: [[(2) Al-Nawwah al-Kilabi, a man from the Banu Kilab.]]

And indeed Kilab, these are ten clans (abtun),
and you are free from its ten tribes.

[[(3) Sibawayh 2:174; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:126; al-Insaf: 323; al-ʿAyni (margin of al-Khizanah) 4:484; and al-Lisan (b-t-n); and others. I did not find the remainder of the verse.]]

He took "al-batn" (clan) to mean the tribe and the subdivision, and for this reason "al-batn" was pluralized with the feminine.

* *

Others among the Kufan grammarians said: "al-ithnatā ʿashrah" is feminine only because "al-umam" is masculine in meaning, so the feminine is used because of the masculine "al-umam."

[[(4) This is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:397.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that "al-ithnatay ʿashrah" is feminine to agree with "al-qiṭʿah" (the piece), and the meaning of the speech is: "And We divided them into pieces, twelve," then he translated "al-qiṭaʿ" by "al-asbat." It is not permissible that "al-asbat" be an explanation of "al-ithnatay ʿashrah," since it is plural, because the specification (tafsir, i.e. tamyiz, the accusative of specification) for numbers above ten up to twenty is singular, not plural. [[(1) "Al-tafsir" here means "al-tamyiz," so his saying "mufassarah" means a specification in terms of grammatical case.]] "Al-asbat" is a plural with no singular of the same form, like their saying: "ʿindi ithnatā ʿashrah imra'ah" (I have twelve women), and one does not say "ʿindi ithnatā ʿashrah niswah" (I have twelve women-plural). This shows that "al-asbat" is not a specification of "al-ithnatay ʿashrah," and that the matter is as we have said. [[(2) In the printed edition and manuscript: "fa-fi dhalika anna al-asbat," which is a weak and feeble construction, and I have preferred that what I have written is closer to the correct reading.]]

* *

As for "al-umam," they are the communities, and "al-sibt" among the Children of Israel is like "al-qarn" (a generation/group). [[(3) See the explanation of "al-ummah" previously, p. 172, note 1, and its references there, and the explanation of "al-sibt" previously, p. 174, note 2, and its references there.]]

* *

It was said: They were only divided into tribes because of their disagreement in their religion.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water, "Strike the rock with your staff," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every people knew their drinking place. And We shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails. "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you." And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (7:160)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: "And We revealed to Musa," when We divided the Children of Israel, his people, into twelve groups, and bewildered them in the wilderness, and they asked Musa for water because of thirst and the scarcity of water: "that strike with your staff the rock."

* *

We have already explained the reason his people asked him for water, and explained the meaning of revelation with its evidence. [[(1) See what was previously mentioned, 2:119-122. And the explanation of "al-wahy" (revelation) previously in the indices of language (w-h-y).]]

* *

"And there gushed forth": it flowed and burst out from the rock twelve springs of water. "Every people knew their drinking place": meaning every people from the twelve tribes knew their drinking place, and no tribe would enter upon another in its drinking. "And We shaded them with clouds": sheltering them from the heat of the sun and its harm.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-ghamam" (clouds) earlier, and likewise "al-mann wa al-salwa" (manna and quails). [[(2) See the explanation of the shading by clouds previously, 2:90-91. And the explanation of "al-mann" and "al-salwa" previously, 2:91-101. And the explanation of the rest of the verse, which is its counterpart, previously, 2:101-102.]]

* *

"And We sent down upon them manna and quails" as food for them. "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you": that is, We said to them: Eat of the lawful things with which We have provided you, O people, and We have made it wholesome for you. "And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves": and in the speech there is an omitted element, left unmentioned because what appears makes it unnecessary, and it is: "So they became weary of that and said: We will not be patient with one food, so they exchanged what is lower for what is better." "And they did not wrong Us": that is, they did not bring any diminution to Our dominion and authority by their request for what they asked, and their deeds that they did. "But they were wronging themselves": that is, they diminished their own shares by exchanging the lower for the better and the baser for the superior.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, 'Hittah' (a request for the remission of sins), and enter the gate prostrating; We will forgive you your sins, and We will increase the doers of good."﴾ (7:161)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And recount also, O Muhammad, the error of the deed of these people, their opposition to their Lord, their disobedience to their Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and their substitution of the word they were commanded to say when God said to them: "Dwell in this town," and it is the town of Bayt al-Maqdis [[(1) See the explanation of "al-qaryah" (the town) above, 2:102, 103.]] = "and eat from it," meaning: from its fruits, its grains, and its plants = "wherever you wish," from it, meaning: from wherever you wish within it = "and say, Hittah," meaning: and say, "this act is Hittah," which removes our sins [[(2) See the explanation of "al-hittah" above, 2:105-109.]] = "We will forgive you," meaning: your Lord will cover over for you = "your sins," that have passed from you, so He will pardon you for them and not hold you accountable for them. [[(3) See the explanation of "al-maghfirah" (forgiveness) above in the lexical indices, under (gh-f-r).]] = "We will increase the doers of good," from among you, who are the obedient to God, [[(4) See the explanation of "al-ihsan" (doing good) above in the lexical indices, under (h-s-n).]] in accordance with what I promised you of forgiveness of sins.

* *

We have already mentioned the narrations on all of this, with the differing views of those who differ, and the sound view we hold regarding it has been stated previously, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[(5) See what has passed in the explanation of the similar verse, 2:102-112.]]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿So those who wronged among them substituted a saying other than what had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky for what they used to do wrong﴾ (7:162)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those among them who disbelieved in God changed what God had commanded them to say. When they were told, "Say: *hittah*" (a request for forgiveness), they said, "*ḥinṭah fī shaʿīrah*" (wheat in barley). Their saying this was other than the saying they had been told to say. God says: "So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky," meaning We sent upon them a torment and destroyed them, "for what they used to do wrong," that is, they used to alter what they were commanded, doing the opposite of what God had commanded them to do and saying other than what God had commanded them to say. [[(1) See the interpretation of a similar verse above, 2:112–119.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of *rijz* (punishment) earlier. [[(2) See the explanation of *rijz* above, 2:117–118; 12:521; 13:72.]]

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to defy﴾ (7:163)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Ask them, O Muhammad, these Jews who live near you, about the matter of 'the town that was by the sea,'" meaning it was in the presence of the sea, that is, near the sea and on its shore.

* *

The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) differed about it.

Some said: it is Ayla.

Those who said this:

15252. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is a town called "Ayla," between Madyan and al-Tur.

15253. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, concerning His words: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: We have heard that it is Ayla.

15254. Salam ibn Salim al-Khuzaʿi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbas while the *muṣḥaf* (copy of the Qur'an) was in his lap and he was weeping. I said: What makes you weep, may God make me your ransom? He said: Woe to you, do you know the town that was by the sea? I said: That is Ayla! [[(1) Report 15254: Salam ibn Salim al-Khuzaʿi is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned earlier under nos. 252 and 6529. Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi is mentioned earlier under nos. 4894 and 7831. See this report and its full text below at no. 15271.]]

15255. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is Ayla.

15256. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It is a town on the shore of the sea, between Egypt and Medina, called "Ayla."

15257. Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They are the people of Ayla, the town that was by the sea.

15258. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abu Saʿd narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: Ayla.

* *

Others said: its meaning is the coast of Madyan.

15259. Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," to the end of the verse: It was mentioned to us that it was a town on the coast of the sea, called Ayla.

* *

Others said: it is Maqna.

Those who said this:

15260. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is a town called "Maqna," between Madyan and ʿAynunI. [[(1) ʿAynuni, also written ʿAynuna or ʿAynun, is mentioned by Yaqut in his dictionary under this heading. Al-Bakri mentions it in *Muʿjam mā istaʿjam* under *Ḥabrā* but gives it no separate heading. Yaqut said: It is one of the villages of the Bab al-Maqdis, and it was said: a village beyond al-Buthayna, below the Qulzum, on the edge of Syria. Kuthayyir mentioned it:
"When they were in the darkness of night, boats, like the springs of the springs of Uthal,
They passed through the valleys of al-Buḍayʿ, galloping, through the passes of ʿAynuna, the ridges of Qibal."
Yaqub said: I heard someone say: ʿAyn Anna. Al-Bakri said: It is a village trodden by the route of the Egyptians when they perform the pilgrimage. And Anna is a valley. In a report (Ibn Saʿd 1/2/21–22), the Messenger of God ﷺ wrote for Nuʿaym ibn Aws, brother of Tamim al-Dari, that he had Ḥayrā and ʿAynun in Syria, all its village, its plain and mountain, its water, its fellahin and its cattle, and for his descendants after him, that no one should contest it with him, nor oppress them, and whoever wrongs them and takes anything from them, upon him is the curse of God, the angels and all people. It was written and witnessed. Al-Bakri said in *Muʿjam mā istaʿjam* (420): Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, whenever he passed by it, would not turn aside, saying: I fear that the supplication of the Messenger of God ﷺ may touch me.]]

* *

Others said: it is Madyan.

Those who said this:

15261. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It is a town between Ayla and al-Tur, called "Madyan."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is that it should be said: It is the town that was by the sea. It is possible that it is Ayla, possible that it is Madyan, and possible that it is Maqna, because all of these are by the sea. No report from the Messenger of God ﷺ settles the matter as to which of them it is, and the disagreement concerning it is as I have described. What has passed of things we did not witness cannot be known except through a report that produces certain knowledge, and there is no such report on this. [[(1) In the printed edition: "bi-anna dhalika min ayy" ("that that is from which"). The editor thought it corrected what is in the manuscript and garbled it beyond repair. This expression has occurred many times before; I pointed to it at 1:520 line 16, 2:517 line 15, 3:64 line 7, 6:291 line 6, 8:85–86 note 1. Refer to it there, for the editor altered it in all these places.]]

* *

As for His words: "when they transgressed in the Sabbath," He means its people, who transgressed God's command concerning the Sabbath and went beyond it to what God had forbidden them.

* *

It is said of this: "*ʿadā fulān amrī*" and "*iʿtadā*," meaning he exceeded it. [[(2) See the explanation of *ʿadā* and *iʿtadā* above, 12:36, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Their transgression in the Sabbath was that God had forbidden them the Sabbath, but they used to catch fish on it. [[(1) See the meaning of the Sabbath and their transgression in it above, 2:166–182; 9:361–362.]]

* *

"When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly," he means: when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden to work, "openly," he means appearing and visible on the water from every path and direction, like the open roads, as in:

15262. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Bishr ibn ʿUmara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly," he said: Visible on the water. [[(2) Report 15262: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid al-Zayyat al-Ahwal is "not objectionable" (la ba's bihi), mentioned earlier under no. 137. In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "ʿUthman ibn Saʿd," which is a pure error. Bishr ibn ʿUmara al-Khathʿami is weak, also mentioned under no. 137. This report is part of a long report mentioned earlier under no. 1138 (2:168).]]

15263. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Openly," he said: from every place.

* *

As for His words: "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath," He means: and on the day they did not honor it as they honored the Sabbath, and that is all days other than Saturday. "They did not come to them," meaning the fish. "Thus We tested them for what they used to defy," He means: as We have described to you of trial and testing that we mentioned, by making the fish appear to them on the surface of the water on the day when catching it was forbidden to them, and hiding it from them on the day when catching it was permitted. [[(3) In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-ikhfa'ihā" ("and its hiding," feminine). The context requires what I have adopted.]] "Thus We tested them," meaning We examined them. [[(4) See the explanation of *ibtila'* (testing) in the earlier language indexes (*bala*).]] "For what they used to defy," He means: for their defiance of God's obedience and their departure from it. [[(1) See the explanation of *fisq* (defiance) in the earlier language indexes (*fasaqa*).]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath."

It was recited with a *fatḥah* on the *yāʾ* in ﴿yasbituna﴾, from the speech of one who says: "*sabata fulān yasbutu sabtan wa-subūtan*," when he honored the Sabbath.

* *

It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite it: ﴿wa-yawma lā yusbatūna﴾ with a *ḍammah* on the *yāʾ*, from "*asbata al-qawm yusbitūna*," when they entered upon the Sabbath, as one says "*ajmaʿnā*" (we entered Friday) when a Friday passed us, "*ashharnā*" (we entered the month) when a month passed us, and "*asbatnā*" (we entered the Sabbath) when a Sabbath passed us.

* *

The word "*yawm*" (day) in His words "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath" is in the accusative governed by "they did not come to them," because the meaning of the sentence is: they did not come to them on a day when they did not observe the Sabbath.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿So those who wronged among them substituted a saying other than what had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky for what they used to do wrong﴾ (7:162)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those among them who disbelieved in God changed what God had commanded them to say. When they were told, "Say: *hittah*" (a request for forgiveness), they said, "*ḥinṭah fī shaʿīrah*" (wheat in barley). Their saying this was other than the saying they had been told to say. God says: "So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky," meaning We sent upon them a torment and destroyed them, "for what they used to do wrong," that is, they used to alter what they were commanded, doing the opposite of what God had commanded them to do and saying other than what God had commanded them to say. [[(1) See the interpretation of a similar verse above, 2:112–119.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of *rijz* (punishment) earlier. [[(2) See the explanation of *rijz* above, 2:117–118; 12:521; 13:72.]]

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to defy﴾ (7:163)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Ask them, O Muhammad, these Jews who live near you, about the matter of 'the town that was by the sea,'" meaning it was in the presence of the sea, that is, near the sea and on its shore.

* *

The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) differed about it.

Some said: it is Ayla.

Those who said this:

15252. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is a town called "Ayla," between Madyan and al-Tur.

15253. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, concerning His words: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: We have heard that it is Ayla.

15254. Salam ibn Salim al-Khuzaʿi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbas while the *muṣḥaf* (copy of the Qur'an) was in his lap and he was weeping. I said: What makes you weep, may God make me your ransom? He said: Woe to you, do you know the town that was by the sea? I said: That is Ayla! [[(1) Report 15254: Salam ibn Salim al-Khuzaʿi is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned earlier under nos. 252 and 6529. Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi is mentioned earlier under nos. 4894 and 7831. 15255. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is Ayla.

15256. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It is a town on the shore of the sea, between Egypt and Medina, called "Ayla."

* *

Others said: its meaning is the coast of Madyan.

15259. Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," to the end of the verse: It was mentioned to us that it was a town on the coast of the sea, called Ayla.

* *

Others said: it is Maqna.

Those who said this:

15260. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," he said: It is a town called "Maqna," between Madyan and ʿAynunI. "When they were in the darkness of night, boats, like the springs of the springs of Uthal,
They passed through the valleys of al-Buḍayʿ, galloping, through the passes of ʿAynuna, the ridges of Qibal."
Yaqub said: I heard someone say: ʿAyn Anna. Al-Bakri said: It is a village trodden by the route of the Egyptians when they perform the pilgrimage. And Anna is a valley. In a report (Ibn Saʿd 1/2/21–22), the Messenger of God ﷺ wrote for Nuʿaym ibn Aws, brother of Tamim al-Dari, that he had Ḥayrā and ʿAynun in Syria, all its village, its plain and mountain, its water, its fellahin and its cattle, and for his descendants after him, that no one should contest it with him, nor oppress them, and whoever wrongs them and takes anything from them, upon him is the curse of God, the angels and all people.
