* *

Others said: it is Madyan.

Those who said this:

15261. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It is a town between Ayla and al-Tur, called "Madyan."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is that it should be said: It is the town that was by the sea. It is possible that it is Ayla, possible that it is Madyan, and possible that it is Maqna, because all of these are by the sea. No report from the Messenger of God ﷺ settles the matter as to which of them it is, and the disagreement concerning it is as I have described. What has passed of things we did not witness cannot be known except through a report that produces certain knowledge, and there is no such report on this. [[(1) In the printed edition: "bi-anna dhalika min ayy" ("that that is from which"). The editor thought it corrected what is in the manuscript and garbled it beyond repair. This expression has occurred many times before; I pointed to it at 1:520 line 16, 2:517 line 15, 3:64 line 7, 6:291 line 6, 8:85–86 note 1. Refer to it there, for the editor altered it in all these places.]]

* *

As for His words: "when they transgressed in the Sabbath," He means its people, who transgressed God's command concerning the Sabbath and went beyond it to what God had forbidden them.

* *

It is said of this: "*ʿadā fulān amrī*" and "*iʿtadā*," meaning he exceeded it. [[(2) See the explanation of *ʿadā* and *iʿtadā* above, 12:36, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Their transgression in the Sabbath was that God had forbidden them the Sabbath, but they used to catch fish on it. [[(1) See the meaning of the Sabbath and their transgression in it above, 2:166–182; 9:361–362.]]

* *

"When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly," he means: when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden to work, "openly," he means appearing and visible on the water from every path and direction, like the open roads, as in:

15262. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Bishr ibn ʿUmara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly," he said: Visible on the water. [[(2) Report 15262: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid al-Zayyat al-Ahwal is "not objectionable" (la ba's bihi), mentioned earlier under no. 137. In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "ʿUthman ibn Saʿd," which is a pure error. Bishr ibn ʿUmara al-Khathʿami is weak, also mentioned under no. 137. This report is part of a long report mentioned earlier under no. 1138 (2:168).]]

15263. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Openly," he said: from every place.

* *

As for His words: "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath," He means: and on the day they did not honor it as they honored the Sabbath, and that is all days other than Saturday. "They did not come to them," meaning the fish. "Thus We tested them for what they used to defy," He means: as We have described to you of trial and testing that we mentioned, by making the fish appear to them on the surface of the water on the day when catching it was forbidden to them, and hiding it from them on the day when catching it was permitted. [[(3) In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-ikhfa'ihā" ("and its hiding," feminine). The context requires what I have adopted.]] "Thus We tested them," meaning We examined them. [[(4) See the explanation of *ibtila'* (testing) in the earlier language indexes (*bala*).]] "For what they used to defy," He means: for their defiance of God's obedience and their departure from it. [[(1) See the explanation of *fisq* (defiance) in the earlier language indexes (*fasaqa*).]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath."

It was recited with a *fatḥah* on the *yāʾ* in ﴿yasbituna﴾, from the speech of one who says: "*sabata fulān yasbutu sabtan wa-subūtan*," when he honored the Sabbath.

* *

It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite it: ﴿wa-yawma lā yusbatūna﴾ with a *ḍammah* on the *yāʾ*, from "*asbata al-qawm yusbitūna*," when they entered upon the Sabbath, as one says "*ajmaʿnā*" (we entered Friday) when a Friday passed us, "*ashharnā*" (we entered the month) when a month passed us, and "*asbatnā*" (we entered the Sabbath) when a Sabbath passed us.

* *

The word "*yawm*" (day) in His words "and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath" is in the accusative governed by "they did not come to them," because the meaning of the sentence is: they did not come to them on a day when they did not observe the Sabbath.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 164 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him."﴾ (164)[[(3) See the explanation of the word "ummah" (community) above, p. 176, footnote 3, and the references there.]] The verse was vocalized with "ma'dhiratan" (an excuse) in the accusative case according to our reading in our copy of the Qur'an. The interpretation (tafsir) of Abu Ja'far and his choice in the reading is the nominative "ma'dhiratun," so take note of it.[[]]

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Remember also, O Muhammad, "when a community among them said," a group from among them to a group that was admonishing the transgressors concerning the Sabbath, and forbidding them from disobeying Allah in it, [(2)] "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy," in this world, because of their disobedience to Him, their opposition to His command, and their making lawful what He had forbidden them, "or punish with a severe punishment," in the Hereafter. Those who were forbidding them from disobeying Allah said, in answer to their words, "Our admonishing them is an excuse to your Lord," we are fulfilling His obligation upon us in commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, "and perhaps they will fear Him," meaning: perhaps they will fear Allah and be mindful of Him, turn back to His obedience, repent of their disobedience toward Him, and of their transgression against what He had forbidden them in their violation of the Sabbath, as:

15264 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: "They said, 'An excuse to your Lord,'" meaning: in our anger at their actions. [[The report 15264 has already appeared at length as no. 1139 (2:170).]]

* * *

"And perhaps they will fear Him": that is, that they would desist from what they were doing. [[(2) See the explanation of "ittaqa" (to fear/guard oneself) in the earlier linguistic indexes under (w-q-y).]]

* * *

15265 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "and perhaps they will fear Him": "They would abandon this act in which they were engaged."

* * *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying "They said, 'An excuse.'"[[(3) See the mention of this verse and its grammatical analysis (i'rab) above, 2:107-108.]] The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Kufa and Basra read it as ﴿ma'dhiratun﴾ (with a nominative ending), according to the meaning I have described.

* * *

Some of the people of Kufa read it as ﴿ma'dhiratan﴾ (with an accusative ending), meaning: "As an act of admonition, we admonished them and did that."

* * *

The scholars differed concerning this group who said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy": were they of the saved group or of the doomed group?

Some of them said: They were of the saved group, because they were the ones forbidding the doomed group from transgressing on the Sabbath. [[(1) In the printed edition and the manuscript: "li-annaha kanat min al-nahiyah" (because she was of the forbidding group). The word "min" here has no meaning, and the correct reading is what has been established.]]

Those who said this:

15266 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And when a community among them said, 'Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?'" He said: It is a town on the shore of the sea between Mecca and Medina, called "Aylah." Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day, and the fish would come to them on their Sabbath in abundance along the sea shore. When the Sabbath passed, they could not reach them. They remained in that state for as long as Allah willed. Then a group among them took the fish on their Sabbath day. Another group forbade them and said, "You take them, when Allah has forbidden them to you on your Sabbath day!" They only increased in error and insolence, and another group kept on forbidding them. When this lasted long upon them, a group of those who forbade them said, "Know that these are a people upon whom the punishment has become due,"[[(2) In the printed edition and the manuscript: "ta'lamuna" (you know). The correct reading is "ta'lamu," an imperative verb with a doubled lam, meaning: "Know."]] "why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?" They were more zealous for Allah than the other group. So they said, "An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him." All of them were forbidding. When Allah's anger fell upon them, the two groups who said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy," and those who said, "An excuse to your Lord," were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of disobedience who took the fish, turning them into apes and swine.

15267 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And ask them about the town that was by the sea," up to His saying "On the day they do not keep the Sabbath, they will not come to them." That was because the people of a town by the sea, their fish would come to them on their Sabbath day. He says: When they were on the day of their Sabbath, the fish would come to them in abundance, meaning from every place. But on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, the fish would not come to them. They said: "If we took from these fish on the day they come, it would not suffice us for the other days!" Righteous believers admonished them and forbade them. A group of believers said: "These are a people who have resolved upon a matter from which they will not desist, and Allah will disgrace them and punish them with a severe punishment." The believers said to one another: "An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him." If there is destruction, perhaps we will be saved, and if they desist, it will be a reward for us. Allah had appointed for the Children of Israel a day on which they would worship Him and devote themselves to Him, and it was Monday. The wicked ones transgressed from Monday to Saturday and said, "It is the Sabbath day!" Moses forbade them, and they differed about it. So He imposed the Sabbath upon them, and forbade them to work or transgress on it. A man from among them went to gather firewood, and Moses, peace be upon him, seized him and asked him: "Did anyone command you to do this?" He found that no one had commanded him, so his companions stoned him.

Then some of them said: "An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him."

He said: I do not know whether those who said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy," were saved or not. He said: I kept at him until I informed him that they had been saved, and he clothed me with a garment. [[The report 15269: Mu'adh ibn Hani al-Qaysi is trustworthy. 15270 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse, and then mentioned something similar, except that in his narration he said: "I kept looking at him until he knew that they had been saved."

15271 - Salam ibn Salim al-Khuza'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas while the Qur'an was in his lap, and he was weeping. [[(1) The beginning of this report and another part of it appeared earlier, no. 15254.]]

15272 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: A man narrated to me, from Ikrimah, who said: I came to Ibn Abbas one day while he was weeping, and the Qur'an was in his lap. He said: And it was in "Surat al-A'raf." He said: "Do you know Aylah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "There was a living quarter of Jews. The fish were driven to them on the Sabbath day, then they would sink, and they could not reach them except after great toil and severe hardship. They would come to them on the Sabbath day in abundance, white and fat, as if they were a pregnant she-goat,[[(2) "Al-makhid" is a ewe or other female animal whose birth is near. In the hadith on zakat: "Go to a sheep that has become full of pregnancy (makhad) and fat," meaning its offspring, referring to its fatness and plumpness.]] their backs lying flat on their bellies in their courtyards and dwellings.[[(3) In the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir 3:577: "tantatih" (which has no meaning here). From this comes "iltitah," meaning to roll about, striking the ground with their backs and bellies. Then Satan inspired them, saying: 'You were only forbidden to eat them on the Sabbath day, so take them on it, and eat them on other days!' A group among them said this, and another group among them said: 'Rather, you were forbidden to eat them, take them, and hunt them on the Sabbath day.' So it was like this until the following Friday came. One group went over with their own selves, their children and their women, and another group withdrew to the right and stayed apart, and another group withdrew to the left and remained silent. Those on the right said: 'Woe to you! By Allah, by Allah, we forbid you to expose yourselves to the punishment of Allah!'[[(1) This sentence, "Those on the right said...," is missing from the manuscript and present in the printed edition. Those on the right said: 'An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him!' That is, they will desist. It is more beloved to us that they not be struck or destroyed. If they do not desist, then it is an excuse to your Lord.' They persisted in the sin, and those on the right said: 'You have done it, O enemies of Allah! They said: "You betrayed!" I said: "Indeed!" and often

However, see part of this report with this chain previously, no. 1140.]] His saying: "And when a community among them said, 'Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?' They said, 'An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him.'" The people became three categories: one category refrained from Allah's sanctity and forbade disobedience to Allah; another category refrained from Allah's sanctity out of reverence for Allah; and another category violated the sanctity and fell into sin.

15274 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning Allah's saying: "the town by the sea." He said: The fish were forbidden to them on the Sabbath day, and they would come to them on the Sabbath day in abundance, as a trial with which they were tested, and they would not come to them on other days unless they sought them, which was also a trial, "because they used to defy." So they took them on the Sabbath day, both making them lawful and disobeying. Allah said to them: "Be apes, despised." Except for a group among them who did not transgress and forbade them. Some of them said to others: "Why do you admonish a people..."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 164 (part 2 of 3):

15275. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?"﴾ up to ﴿so that they may fear God﴾: "So that they might give up what they were engaged in." He said: They had been tested by the fish being withheld from them. They used to rest on the Sabbath day and do no work at all on it. When the Sabbath day came, the fish would come to them in throngs, but when it was not the Sabbath day, not a single fish would come. He said: They were a people who had developed a strong craving for fish and suffered a trial because of it. [[(Qaram ila al-lahm), with a kasra on the ra', means a strong desire for meat. (Qaraman), with fatha on both letters, means his desire for it became intense. As for His words (laqu minhu), the pronoun in (minhu) refers back to the verbal noun of (qarimu), that is, the qaram (craving).]] A man among them took a fish, tied a thread to its tail, and tied it to a (khashafa).[[(2) In the printed edition it is (khasfa), which has no meaning. In the manuscript it is undotted, and the correct reading is what I have adopted. (Al-khashfa), with a dotted kha', and (al-hashfa) with an undotted ha' (both with fatha on the kha' and the shin), are stones that grow in the ground like plants, or a soft rock in a flat plain.]] Then he left it in the water. When the sun set on Sunday, he pulled it in by the thread and roasted it. A neighbour of his smelled the scent of fish and said, "O so-and-so, I smell the odour of fish (nun) in your house!" [[(3) (Al-nun): fish and any aquatic creature.]] He said, "No!" The neighbour said, "Then look in your oven," and when he looked, the fish was there. He then told him the whole story, and the neighbour said, "I see that God is going to punish you." When he saw that no punishment came, he (the man) repeated it, and when the next Sabbath came, he took two fish and tied them up. Then a neighbour of his looked in on him, and when he saw him, no punishment came upon him either. They began to hunt fish [[(4) His words (jaʿalu yasidunahu), "they began to hunt it," depart from the preceding singular sequence. I fear that something has fallen out of the text, meaning that some of his neighbours followed him and the matter spread among them, so they began to hunt them...]]. The people of the town became aware of them, and those who forbade wrongdoing forbade them. They became two groups: one group admonished them and restrained them, and another group admonished them but did not restrain them. Those who had admonished and restrained said to those who admonished without restraining: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ The others said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God.﴾ Then God said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, up to His words ﴿for what they used to defy﴾. God said: ﴿So when they persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised."﴾ The people of that town said to them: "You have done an evil deed. Whoever wants to withdraw and purify himself, let him withdraw from these people!" He said: So those people and these people separated within their city, and they built a wall between them, with gates in that wall through which some of them could go out to others. He said: When night came, God struck them with a punishment, and in the morning those believers did not see any of them. They entered upon them and found that they were apes: the man, his wives and his children. They began to enter upon the man, recognising him, and say, "O so-and-so, did we not warn you of God's assaults? Did we not warn you of God's vengeance? We warned you, and we warned you!" He said: There was nothing but weeping! [[(2) In the manuscript it is (fa-laysa illa takakan), which I do not understand. In a report earlier, number 15272, at its end, it reads (fa-tashummu thiyabahu fa-tabki), "he sniffs his clothes and weeps." I have therefore left what is in the printed edition as it is, until the manuscript reading shows a satisfactory sense.]] He said: God only punished those who did wrong, those who persisted in that. He said: As for those who forbade, all of them had forbidden, but some of them were better than others. Then he recited: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment for what they used to defy.﴾
15276. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: al-Mahāribī narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrima, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās recited this verse: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ He said: "I do not know whether the people were saved or destroyed. I kept looking until I knew that they had been saved, and he gave me a garment (ḥulla)."
15277. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ashhab ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz informed me, from Mālik, who said: Ibn Rūmān claimed that His words, ﴿their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, in throngs, but on the days when they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, meant: they would come to them on Saturday, and when evening came they would go away, and none of them would be seen until the next Saturday. So a man among them took a thread and a peg, and tied a fish in the water on the Sabbath day. When they reached the evening of Sunday, he took it and roasted it. The people smelled its scent, came to him and asked him about it, but he denied it. They kept at him until he said to them, "It is only the skin of a fish that we found." When the next Sabbath came, he did the same thing—I do not know, perhaps he said he tied two fish—and when evening came on Sunday, he took it and roasted it. They smelled its scent, came and asked him, and he said to them, "If you wish, do as I do!" They said, "And what did you do?" He told them, and they did what he had done, until it became widespread. They had a city with a suburb (rabaḍ),[[(1) (Al-rabaḍ), with fatha on both letters, is the open ground around a city.]] and they shut its gates. Then they were struck with the transformation that befell them. Their neighbours from around them came in the morning seeking what people seek from them, but they found the city shut against them. They called out but no one answered them, so they climbed over the walls and found that they were apes. The ape began to approach and rub against those who had known him before, drawing near and rubbing against him.
* *
Others said: Rather, the group that said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾ was from the group that perished.
Mention of those who said this:
15278. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Dāwūd ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾, up to ﴿in throngs﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: They invented the Sabbath and were tested by it. The fish were forbidden to them on it, so on the Sabbath day the fish would appear to them, and they would look at them in the sea. When the Sabbath ended, they would go away and not be seen until the next Sabbath. When the Sabbath came, they would come in throngs. They remained as long as God willed them to remain like that. Then a man among them took a fish and pierced its nose [[(1) In the printed edition it is (fa-kharama anfahu), but I have adopted what is in the manuscript, and this is the correct reading and pointing. (Kharaza al-dabba) means he made a hole in the animal's nose and put in it a ring of hair or something else, and (al-khazama), with a kasra on the kha', is the knotted ring.]] and drove a peg for it into the shore, tied it, and left it in the water. When the next day came, he took it, roasted it, and ate it. He did this while they watched and did not object, and none of them forbade him except a small group who forbade him, until the matter appeared in the markets and was done openly. He said: So a group said to those who forbade: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ They said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord﴾, for our anger at their deeds, ﴿and perhaps they will fear God.﴾ ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, up to His words ﴿"Be apes, despised."﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās said: They were in three groups: a third forbade, a third said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾, and a third were the sinners. Only those who had forbidden were saved, and the rest of them perished. One day, those who had forbidden evil woke up in their gatherings, searching for people and not seeing them. They climbed onto their houses (fa-ʿalaw ʿalā duwarihim),[[(2) In the printed edition it is (fa-ʿallaqu ʿalayhim duwarahum), which he tried to correct and got badly wrong. The clear correct reading is what is in the manuscript, as I have given it.]] and they began to say, "Something is going on with the people; look and see what their state is!" They looked into their houses and found the people transformed into apes in their homes. They would recognise a man by his eye, and he was an ape; they would recognise a woman by her eye, and she was an ape. God said: ﴿So We made it an example for those before it and those after it, and an admonition to the God-fearing﴾ [Sūrat al-Baqara: 66].
15279. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, the verse. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Those who forbade were saved, and those who did evil perished. "But I do not know what was done with those who remained silent!"
15280. Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾ He said: They were three groups: the group that admonished, the group that was admonished, and God knows what the third group did—they were those who said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾
= Al-Kalbī said: They were two groups: the group that admonished, and the group that said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾ He said: They were the ones who were admonished.
15281. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: That I should know about those who said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ is dearer to me than what I have been given in exchange!
15282. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, regarding: ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?"﴾: "Hear! God says: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil and seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment﴾. I wish I knew what was done to those who said, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy?﴾"
15283. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Māhān al-Ḥanafī Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding His words, ﴿their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, in throngs, but on the days when they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾: He said: They were in the town on the shore of the sea, and the days were six, from Sunday to Friday. The Jews set aside Saturday and made it a Sabbath for themselves, so God made it a Sabbath for them. It had not been a Sabbath before that, so God confirmed it upon them and tested them with the fish on it. They would come in throngs on Saturday, and they would avoid catching any of them. Then a man among them said, "By God, the Sabbath is not a day that God imposed upon us; we imposed it on ourselves. So, if I were to take some of this fish!" He took a fish, and his neighbour heard of it and feared punishment, so he fled from his house. When he remained for as long as God willed and no punishment befell him, someone else took some too on the Sabbath day. When no punishment came upon them, more and more people took it on the Sabbath, and they made the Sabbath and the night of the Sabbath a festival, drinking wine in it and playing musical instruments. Their best and most righteous said to them: "Woe to you! Stop what you are doing. God is going to destroy you or punish you with a severe punishment. Will you not reason? And do not transgress on the Sabbath!" They refused. The best of them said, "We will set a wall between us and them." They did so. On the night of the Sabbath, they were disturbed by the sounds they heard from them, the voices and the musical instruments. Then, on the night in which they were transformed, their voices fell silent at the beginning of the night. The best of them said, "What has happened to your people, that their voices have fallen silent tonight?" Some of them said, "Perhaps the wine overcame them and they have fallen asleep!" When they woke in the morning, they heard no sound from them. Some said to others, "What is the matter with us that we hear no sound from your people?" They said to a man, "Climb the wall and look at their state." He climbed the wall and saw them swarming over one another, transformed into apes. He said to his people, "Come and look at what your people have come to!" They climbed up and began looking at the man, trying to recognise him, and saying, "O so-and-so, are you so-and-so?" He pointed with his hand to his chest, meaning yes, "for what my hands have earned." [[(1) In the manuscript and the printed edition it is (ayy niʿm), and the good correct reading is what I have adopted.]] [[(2) The report 15283: (Māhān Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī). Al-Bukhārī said: "Māhān Abū Sālim al-Ḥanafī... Some of them said: Māhān Abū Ṣāliḥ, but this is not sound." This has been mentioned earlier under numbers 3226 and 13291, and he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabīr 4/2/67, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/1/434.]]
15284. Yaʿqūb and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to me, both saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Ayyūb, who said: al-Ḥasan recited one day: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day in throngs, but on the days when they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to defy﴾. He said: The fish was forbidden to them on one day and permitted to them on the others. It would come to them on the day God had forbidden to them as though it were a pregnant she-camel,[[(3) In the manuscript it is (ka-annahu al-muḥāṣir), which is undotted; what is in the printed edition seems to be correct. This was mentioned earlier at p. 188 and note 2, where it reads: "they were coming to them... white and fat, as though they were pregnant." I explained there that by al-makhāḍ he meant a ewe or she-camel whose birth was near, and that by this he meant its fatness and plumpness. (Al-mākhiḍ) refers to she-camels that are pregnant, meaning those whose womb is full with young and fat.]] and no one could hold it back. Hardly ever did I see someone who was much concerned with a sin without committing it.[[(1) (Al-ihtimām) here means the desire for it (al-hamm bihi), not the sense of "being concerned" in the sense of grief or sorrow. This is the plain analogical usage: "ihtamma bi-l-amr" meaning "hammahu" (he desired it), but the lexicons of the language do not record it.]] They began to desire it and to hold back, until they seized it and ate the worst meal any people had ever eaten. It left them in disgrace in this world and made them suffer the most severe punishment in the Hereafter![[(2) The use of (qaṭṭ) with something other than negation, that is, in an affirmative statement, is one of the things they denied. It occurs often in speech, and Ibn Mālik drew attention to it in Mushkilāt al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, p. 193, where he said: "In his words, 'we were never more...' (qaṭṭ) is used without a preceding negation, which is something that is hidden from many grammarians, because the usual usage of it is to cover the past time after a negation, as in 'I never did that (qaṭṭ),' but it has come in this report without a negation. It has parallels." See also the following report, number 15285.]] [[(3) His words, (abqāhu khizyan), "it left him in disgrace," make the pronoun agree with (akla), the masculine singular comparative being used with a feminine noun, and this is plain Arabic. This was pointed out previously at 5:488 note 1, 5:557 note 1, 6:395-396 note 1, 7:87 note 4, and report number 14813. In the printed edition it is (athqalahu khizyan), and the correct reading is from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:138. In the manuscript it is (abqā khizyan fi al-dunya wa-ashaddu ʿuqūbatan fi al-ākhira).]] And by God, [a fish that a people took and ate is greater in the sight of God than the killing of a believing man![[(4) This sentence in brackets is in the printed edition but not in the manuscript, nor in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:138. Its text in the manuscript is: "And by God, the believer has greater sanctity." I do not know whether it is an addition from a copy of another manuscript, or was dropped by the copyist of our copy.]] The believer has greater sanctity before God than a fish. But God made the appointed time for that people the Hour, ﴿And the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter﴾ [Sūrat al-Qamar: 46].
15285. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Mūsā, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The fish came to them, rushing into their pools as though they were pregnant she-camels, and by God they ate the worst meal any people ever ate, the worst in punishment in this world and the most severe in torment in the Hereafter![[(5) In the manuscript it is (kaʾannahā al-muḥāṣir), as was mentioned in the preceding report; see p. 196 note 4.]] [[(6) See the earlier note 3.]]
Al-Ḥasan said: And by God, killing a believer is greater than eating fish!

Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 164 (part 3 of 3):

15286 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', who said: "I was sitting in the mosque when an old man came and people sat down around him. They said: 'This is one of the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud!' He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾ [7:163], the verse... He said: When the Sabbath was made forbidden for them, the fish would come on the Sabbath day, feeling safe, and come up, [[(1) In the printed edition: "wa-tajii"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] and they could not touch them. When the Sabbath passed, the fish would go away, and they would hunt as people hunt. When they wanted to transgress on the Sabbath, they hunted. Some of their righteous ones forbade them, but they refused, and the wicked outnumbered them, [[(2) "Kathharahum al-fujjar": that is, they overpowered them by their numbers.]] so the wicked wanted to fight them. Among them were those whom they did not wish to fight, the father of one of them, his brother, or his relative. When they had forbidden them and they refused, the righteous said: 'Then we shall be blamed! We shall place a wall between us and them!' [[(3) In the manuscript: "adanahum, wa-anna naj'alu baynana wa-baynakum hā'iṭan", as it stands, and I have read it as I have written it. In the printed edition, the sentence and its pronouns were altered to read: "idhan nubāyinahum, wa-anna naj'alu baynana wa-baynahum hā'iṭan". The phrase "idhan nuttahamu" means: we shall be accused of what you have done of transgression on the Sabbath, and God will punish us, while we are innocent of what you have done.]] So they did so. When the wicked lost their voices, the righteous said: 'If only you would look at your brothers and what they have done!' So they looked, and behold, they had been transformed into apes, recognising the elderly by their age and the young by their youth, and they began to weep towards them. And this was after Musa (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 165:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a grievous punishment, because they were defiantly disobedient.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: When the group that transgressed on the Sabbath abandoned what God had commanded them regarding the abstention from transgression on it, and neglected what the admonishing group had advised them and reminded them of, [[(1) In the printed edition: "wa-dhakkarathā mā dhakkarathā bihi" (and reminded them what they had reminded them of), which adds to the text what is not needed and departs from the manuscript.]] namely its warning them of God's punishment for their disobedience, and they proceeded to make lawful what God had forbidden them [[(2) See the explanation of "forgetting" (nasiya) in the previous linguistic indexes (nasā).]], God saved those among them who forbade "evil" — meaning, disobedience to God and making lawful what He had made sacred (ḥirmih) [[(3) "Al-ḥirm" (with a kasra and then sukun) means "al-ḥarām" (what is forbidden).]] — "and We seized those who did wrong," meaning: God seized those who transgressed on the Sabbath, for they made lawful on it what God had forbidden of catching and eating fish. So He sent His might upon them and destroyed them with a severe, grievous punishment, because they were opposing the command of God, [[(4) In the printed edition: "bi-mā kānū yafsuqūna yukhālifūna" (because they were defiantly disobedient, opposing). The word "yafsuqūna" was in the manuscript but was struck through, so the editor should rightly have deleted it as he did.]] thereby leaving His obedience for His disobedience, and that is "fisq" (defiant disobedience). [[(5) See the explanation of "fisq" in the previous linguistic indexes (fasaqa).]]

* *

Those interpreters who held the same view as we have stated also said so.

Mention of those who said that:

15287 – Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, regarding His words: "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil," he said: "When they forgot the admonition of the believers to them, who said: 'Why do you admonish a people…'"

15288 – Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā told me, saying: Ḥarmī told us, saying: Shuʿba told me, saying: ʿAmāra informed me, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "We saved those who forbade evil," he said: "I wish I knew what the evil was that they were forbidden from!"

* *

As for His words "bi-ʿadhābin ba'īs" (with a grievous punishment), the readers differed in its recitation.

The common reading of the people of Madina was: ﴿bi-ʿadhābin bīsin﴾ with a kasra on the bāʾ and a light yāʾ, without hamza, on the pattern of "fiʿl".

* *

Some readers of Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿bi-ʿadhābin baʾīsin﴾ on the pattern of "faʿīl", from "al-bu's" (misery), with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, a kasra on the hamza, and its lengthening.

* *

Some Meccans likewise recited it in the same way, except that they put a kasra on the bāʾ: ﴿bi-ʿadhābin biʾīsin﴾ on the pattern of "fiʿīl".

* *

Some Kufans recited it: ﴿bayʾisin﴾ with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, a sukun on the yāʾ, and a kasra on the hamza after it, on the pattern of "fayʿil".

* *

This is anomalous according to the grammarians, because "fayʿil", when it is not from the roots with yāʾ and wāw, has fatḥa on its middle letter in the eloquent speech of the Arabs, like their saying of its counterpart from the sound roots: "ṣayqal" and "nayrab". The middle letter is only given a kasra in roots with yāʾ and wāw, as in their saying "sayyid" and "mayyit". Some of them have recited the verse of Imru' al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindī:

Both of them were a chief, a bayʾis (courageous), who strikes the helmet on the day of combat.

With a kasra on the ʿayn of "fayʿil", and that is the hamza of "bayʾis". Perhaps the one who recited it thus recited it according to this [form]. [[(1) Tafsir Abi Hayyan 4: 413.]]

* *

It is also mentioned from another Kufan that he recited it: ﴿bayʾasin﴾, similar to the reading we mentioned before this, with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, a sukun on the yāʾ, and a fatḥa on the hamza after the yāʾ, on the pattern of "fayʿal" like "ṣayqal".

* *

It is reported from some Basrans that he recited it: ﴿baʾisin﴾ with a fatḥa on the bāʾ and a kasra on the hamza, on the pattern of "faʿil", as Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:

Would that I could meet Ruqayya in seclusion, free from any misery (bāʾis).

[[(1) His Diwan: 386; al-Khizāna 3: 587; al-ʿAynī (in the margin of al-Khizāna) 4: 379. The narration in al-Khizāna is "min ghayri mā anas" (free from what is intimate), and its commentator explained it, which in my view is an effort of the author of al-Khizāna, and the verse is a corrupted text whose correct form is what is in al-Ṭabarī. As for al-ʿAynī, he wrote "min ghayri mā yabs" (with yāʾ then bāʾ), which is undoubtedly a mistake, and likewise in the Diwan as quoted from it. The correct version is what Abu Ja'far explained.]]

* *

It is reported from another of them that he recited: ﴿bi'sa﴾ with a kasra on the bāʾ and a fatḥa on the sīn, meaning: "how wretched is the punishment."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these readings in my view is the reading of the one who recited ﴿baʾīsin﴾ with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, a kasra on the hamza and its lengthening, on the pattern of "faʿīl", as Dhu al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī said:

Enraged at me, and you do not see in them any trace of me, grievous (baʾīsan)…

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would inflict on them the worst torment﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "wa-idh ta'adhdhana" (and when [your Lord] proclaimed), God, may His praise be exalted, means: Remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord proclaimed (ta'adhdhana, from adhdhana) and made known. [[(1) In the printed edition it read: "idh adhdhana rabbuka fa-a'lam" (when your Lord proclaimed and made known), and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

This is the form *tafa''ala* from *al-iidhan* (proclamation), as al-A'sha, Maymun ibn Qays, said:

"Today my neighbours have proclaimed their departure with the *khufuf*, having cut the rope of a familiar, beloved companion."

[[(2) His Diwan, p. 211, the opening of a long qasida of his. In the printed Diwan it reads "bi-khufufi" (with my khufuf), which is an error of reading; the correct form, as in the manuscript copy of his Diwan, is "bi-khufuf". *Al-khufuf* is the verbal noun of the saying "khaffa al-qawm 'an manzilihim khufufan," meaning they departed, or hastened in departing. In the Prophet's ﷺ sermon during his illness he said: "O people, the khufuf of one who is about to leave has drawn near to me from among you," meaning the approach of departure, warning of his death ﷺ.]]

By His saying "adhina" he means: informed/made known. We have explained this with its evidence in another place. [[(3) See the explanation of "al-idhn" above, 11:215, note 2, and the references there.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (7:167)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is swift in His punishment toward whoever deserves punishment from Him for his disbelief in Him and his disobedience. "And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful": that is, He is one who pardons the sins of whoever repents of his sins, turns back and returns to obedience, covering them with His pardon; "Merciful" to him, so that He does not punish him for his offence after his repentance from it, because He accepts repentance and overlooks the slip. [[(2) See the explanation of "swift in punishment," "Forgiving," and "Merciful" above in the lexical indices (s-r-') (gh-f-r) and (r-h-m).]]

Commentary on the words of Allah: ﴿And We divided them into communities upon the earth; among them are the righteous, and among them are those below that; and We tested them with good times and bad, that they might return﴾ (7:168).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We dispersed the Children of Israel upon the earth [(1) See the explanation of "qatta'a" (to cut up, divide) earlier, p. 164.] — "umaman" means: groups scattered and separated [(2) See the explanation of "umma" (community, nation) earlier, p. 184, note 3, and the references there.] — as related:

15311 — Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "And We divided them upon the earth into communities," that he said: In every land they entered, there were people of the Jews. [(3) Report 15311: Ishaq ibn Isma'il is Abu Yazid Habawayh; see what preceded, no. 15221, and the commentary there.]

15312 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And We divided them upon the earth into communities," that he said: They are Jews.

* *

As for His words, "among them are the righteous," meaning: among these people whom Allah described from the Children of Israel are "the righteous," meaning: those who believe in Allah and His messengers. "And among them are those below that," meaning: below the righteous. Allah, majestic is His praise, described them as being so before their apostasy from their religion and before their disbelief in their Lord, and that was before 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was sent among them.

* *

As for His words, "And We tested them with good times and bad, that they might return," He says: We tested them with ease of living, comfort and tranquility in this world, and abundance of provision — and these are the "good times" which He mentioned — and by "bad times" He means hardship in living, austerity therein, and calamities and misfortunes in their wealth [(1) See the explanation of "ibtila'" (testing) in the language indexes earlier under (b-l-w).] [(2) See the explanation of "hasanat" (good deeds, good things) in the language indexes earlier under (h-s-n).] [(3) See the explanation of "sayyi'at" (bad deeds, evils) in the language indexes earlier under (s-w-').] — "that they might return," He says: that they might return to obedience to their Lord, turn to it penitently, and repent of His disobedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 169:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then there succeeded them an evil successor who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower world and saying, "It will be forgiven us." And if goods like it came to them, they would take them.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: "Then there succeeded after those people whose characteristics He described" [[(3) See the explanation of "khalf" (successor) above, p. 122, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = "khalf," meaning an evil successor. He says: there came after them and in their place, and they were replaced by them, a replacement of evil.

* *

It is said of this: "He is a khalf of truth" (a good successor) and "khalf of evil" (an evil successor). Most of its use in praise is with a fatha on the "lam," and in blame with a sukun, though it may be vocalized in blame and be sukun in praise. Among its use with sukun in praise is the verse of Hassan:

"For us is the first step toward You, and our successor follows our first in the obedience of God."

[[(4) His Diwan: 254; Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 283; Lisan (khalf). It will come in the tafsir 11: 59 (Bulaq), from a poem in which he wept for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh on the day of Banu Qurayza and for men of the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ among the martyrs. His words "the first step" mean the precedence of the Ansar in Islam. The Sirah narrates "in the religion of God, a follower."]] I think that when it is directed to corruption, it is derived from their saying "khalafa al-laban" (the milk became sour), when it turns sour from being left a long time in the waterskin until it spoils, as if the corrupt man is likened to it. It may also be that from it comes their saying "khalafa fam al-sa'im" (the fasting person's mouth changed), when his breath changes. As for the sukun of the "lam" in blame, it is the saying of Labid:

"Gone are those in whose shelter one lived, and I remain in a khalf like the hide of a mangy camel."

[[(2) His Diwan, poem 8; Lisan (khalf); and many others. He elegises Arbad, his companion and cousin, saying:
"Cut off your grief, may you have no father, and go, and join your noble absent kin..."
"Gone are those..."
"They devour through malice and treachery, and whoever speaks is blamed even if he does not clamour..."
"O Arbad of goodness, whose ancestry is noble, you left me walking with a broken horn..."
"Indeed the calamity, there is no calamity like it, the loss of every brother like the light of a star."
"Al-mughalla" is extreme enmity and slander against one you oppose, and "al-qarn al-a'dab" is the broken horn, meaning that its edge has been dulled by Arbad's death.]]

* *

It was said: the khalf mentioned by God in this verse, who succeeded those before them, are the Christians.

Those who said this:

15313 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words "Then there succeeded them a successor": he said: the Christians.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my judgment, is to say: God, exalted is He, only described that He made as successors the people whose stories He related in the verses that preceded, an evil, bad successor. He did not mention to us in His Book that they were Christians, and their story resembles the story of the Jews more than the story of the Christians. Moreover, what precedes this is a report about the Children of Israel, and what follows is likewise, so what lies between them is more likely to be a report about them, since there is no evidence in the verse to turn the report away from them to others, nor has any evidence come that would make it necessary to hold that view.

* *

The meaning of the statement, then, is: "There came after them a replacement of evil, who inherited the Book of God and were taught it, and neglected to act upon it, opposing its judgment. They accepted bribes in God's judgment, taking bribes in it from the goods of this immediate, 'lower' (al-adna) life" [[(2) See the explanation of "the goods of the world" above, 9: 71.]] — meaning by "lower" (al-adna): the nearer as opposed to the farther hereafter [[(3) See the explanation of "al-adna" above, 2: 131.]] — "and they say, when they do so: God will forgive us our sins, wishing vain things upon God, as He, exalted is His praise, said of them: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, 'This is from God,' to trade it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 79] = "And if goods like it come to them, they would take them": meaning, if a sinful, forbidden bribe like it came to them afterward, they would take it, consider it lawful, and not refrain from it. Exalted is His praise, He informs that they are people persisting in their sins, and not people of repentance or turning back.

* *

What the people of interpretation said agrees with what we have said, though their expressions differ.

And if goods like it come to them, they would take them": he said: the sins.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they should not say of God except the truth? And they studied what is in it. And the Last Abode is better for those who are righteous. Will you not reason?﴾ (7:169)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: "Was it not taken" from these bribe-takers in their judgments, who say, "God will forgive us for doing this," when they are rebuked for it, "the covenant of the Book" — which is God's taking of covenants from the Children of Israel to establish the Torah and act by what is in it. So He, exalted is His praise, says to those whose story is related in this verse, rebuking them for their opposition to His command and their breaking of His covenant and pact: Did God not take from them the covenant of His Book, that they not say of God except the truth, and not attribute to Him except what He sent down to His messenger Musa ﷺ in the Torah, and that they not lie about Him? As:

15327 — al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Was it not taken from them the covenant of the Book, that they should not say of God except the truth?" He said: regarding what they claim of God, forgiveness of their sins, which they continually return to and do not repent of.

* *

As for His words "and they studied what is in it," it is joined to His words "inherited the Book," and its meaning: "Then there succeeded them a successor who inherited the Book" and "studied what is in it." By His words "and they studied what is in it," He means: they read what is in it. He says: they inherited the Book, knew what is in it and studied it, yet neglected it, abandoned acting upon it, and opposed God's covenant to them in that, as:

15328 — Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "and they studied what is in it": he said: they taught it, they taught what is in the Book God mentioned, and he recited: ﴿by what you used to teach of the Book and by what you used to study﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 79].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "And the Last Abode is better for those who are righteous": He, exalted is His praise, says: what is in the Last Abode, that is, what is in the return with God, of what He has prepared for His friends and those who act by what He sent down in His Book and guard its limits, "is better for those who fear God," and fear His punishment, so they watch over His command and prohibition and obey Him in all that in their worldly life. "Will you not reason?" [[(1) Abu Ja'far's reading is "a-fa-la ya'qilun" with the ya', and his interpretation followed it, so I have left it here as he explained it, though I placed the verse previously in the script of our Qur'an and our reading. Abu Ja'far did not point out this reading.]] He means: will not those who take the goods of this lower life in their judgments, and say, "It will be forgiven us," reason that what is with God in the Last Abode is better for the righteous who judge justly among people than this small good which they hasten to seize in this world, in opposition to God's command and judging people with injustice?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 170:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who hold fast to the Scripture and establish prayer – We do not allow the reward of the righteous to be lost﴾ (170)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The readers (qira'at, the recognized modes of reciting the Qur'an) differed concerning the recitation of this.

Some of them recited ﴿يُمْسِكُونَ﴾ with the **mim** lightened and unvowelled, from "amsaka yumsiku" (أمْسك يمسك).

* *

Others recited it ﴿يُمَسِّكُونَ﴾ with the **mim** vowelled with a fatha and the **sin** doubled, from "massaka yumassiku" (مَسَّك يُمَسِّك).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By this is meant: those who act upon what is in the Book of God, ﴿and establish prayer﴾, observing its limits and not neglecting its times, ﴿We do not allow the reward of the righteous to be lost.﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever among My creatures does that, I will not allow the reward of his righteous deed to be lost, as:

15329 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning ﴿Those who hold fast to the Scripture﴾: "The Scripture of God which Moses, peace be upon him, brought."

15330 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said concerning His words ﴿Those who hold fast to the Scripture﴾: "from the Jews or the Christians" ﴿We do not allow the reward of the righteous to be lost.﴾

The exposition of His words: ﴿And [remember] when We uprooted the mountain above them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them: "Take what We have given you with strength, and remember what is in it, that you may be mindful [of God]."﴾ (7:171)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Remember, O Muhammad, when We uprooted the mountain, lifted it and raised it above the Children of Israel, as though it were a cloud of shade, and We said to them: "Take what We have given you with strength," [meaning] from Our obligations, and what We have imposed upon you of the rulings of Our Book. So accept it, act upon it diligently in performing it, without negligence or laxity [[(1) See the explanation of "with strength" above, 1:160, 161, 356, 357, and the other indexes of language under the root (q-w-y).]] = "and remember what is in it," meaning what is in Our Book of covenants and pledges which We took from you to act upon what is in it = "that you may be mindful," meaning: so that you may be mindful of your Lord, fearing His punishment for abandoning action upon it when you recall the pledges taken from you concerning it.

* *

Those of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said.

Those who said that:

15331. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And when We uprooted the mountain above them as though it were a canopy," Moses said to them: "Take what We have given you with strength," meaning: by acting upon the Book, or else the mountain will fall upon you and destroy you! They said: "Rather, we will take what God has given us with strength!" Then they broke [their covenant] after that.

15332. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And when We uprooted the mountain above them as though it were a canopy." This is His words: ﴿And We raised the mount above them for their covenant﴾ (4:154). He said: "Take what We have given you with strength," or else I will send it down upon you.

15333. Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed I know the most of God's creation as to why the Jews prostrate with the side of their faces: when the mountain was raised above them, they prostrated, and began looking at the mountain fearing it would fall upon them. He said: So that was a prostration God was pleased with, and they made it a sunnah. [[(1) The report 15333: Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti, a teacher of Abu Ja'far; I have not found a biography for him, and he appeared under numbers 7211 and 9788. Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani al-Wasiti, who appeared under number 7211. Dawud is Dawud ibn Abi Hind. 'Amir is al-Sha'bi.]]

15334. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Amir, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

15335. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And when We uprooted the mountain above them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them: Take what We have given you with strength," meaning: with earnestness = "and remember what is in it, that you may be mindful." [He said:] a mountain which God plucked from its root and then placed above their heads, and said: "You will surely take My command, or I will drop it upon you!"

15336. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "And when We uprooted the mountain," he said: as the butter is churned [[(2) In the printed edition: "as the rabadha is churned," which in the manuscript is undotted, and its dotting is greatly mistaken. Nataq al-zubda means shaking a waterskin to dislodge its butter.]] = Ibn Jurayj said: They refused the Torah, to accept it or to believe in it = "Take what We have given you with strength." He said: He says: You will surely believe in the Torah and surely accept it, or it will fall upon you.

15337. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: This is the Book of God; will you accept it with what is in it? For in it is the clarification of what He has made lawful for you and what He has made unlawful for you, what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you! They said: Recite to us what is in it, and if its obligations are light and its limits are easy, we will accept it! He said: Accept it with what is in it! They said: No, not until we know what is in it, how its limits and obligations are! They returned to Moses repeatedly, so God revealed to the mountain, and it was uprooted and rose into the sky, until it was between their heads and the sky. Moses said to them: Do you not see what my Lord says? "If you do not accept the Torah with what is in it, I will surely drop this mountain upon you." He said: al-Hasan al-Basri related to me, saying: When they looked at the mountain, every man fell prostrate upon his left brow, and looked with his right eye toward the mountain, out of fear that it would fall upon him. Therefore no Jew on earth prostrates except upon his left brow; they say: this is the prostration by which punishment was lifted from us. = Abu Bakr said: When he spread the tablets, in which was the Book of God that he wrote with his own hand, no mountain, tree or stone remained on the face of the earth without trembling. Today there is no Jew on the face of the earth, young or old, upon whom the Torah is recited without trembling and shaking his head at it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning the meaning of His words: "nataqna" (We uprooted).

Some of the Basran [grammarians] [[(1) He is Abu 'Ubayda, as will be clear to you from the following takhrij.]] said the meaning of "nataqna" is "raised," and cited the verse of al-'Ajjaj:

*He lifts the saddle-pads of the pack-saddle (yantuq aqtad al-shalil) lifting [them] (nataqa)*

and said: He means by his words "yantuq," he lifts it from his back. And by the saying of another: [[(1) He is Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj.]]

*And they lifted our dreams, the heavy ones (wa nataqu ahlamana al-athaqila)*

[[(2) Diwan: 40; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1:232, from verses describing his camel, its swiftness and the severity of its march. "Al-shalil" is the cloth or felt of hair or wool placed on the camel's rump behind the saddle. "Al-aqtad" is the plural of "qatad" (with two fatha), the wood of the saddle. In the printed edition it read "al-sulail," following the manuscript, which is undotted. Diwan of Ru'ba 122, Majaz al-Qur'an 1:232, and Lisan (n-t-q), from a rajaz poem in praise of his people, then in praise of Sulayman ibn 'Ali. In mentioning his people he said: "The people, if you distinguish them into groups... all of them seek our means... they have tested our noble natures... and they lifted our heavy dreams... so the people have seen no equal to us... more honored in might and mightier in wisdom." "Al-athaqil" is the plural of "al-athqal" meaning heavier than all other people's dreams, as one says "al-akabir," "al-asaghir," "al-amathil."]]

It has been related from the proponent of this view another statement [[(3) Meaning Abu 'Ubayda also; I have not found it elsewhere in what has been printed of Majaz al-Qur'an.]]: that the origin of "al-nataq" and "al-nutuq" is that everything you uproot from its place and throw away; from it one says: "nataqtu nataqan." He said: For this reason a woman who bears many children is called "natiq," [[(4) In the printed edition and the manuscript: "a woman who is great (kabira)," which is incorrect; the copyist dropped what I have placed between the brackets, and the correct reading is what I have given.]] because she throws out her children with throwing, and he cited the verse of al-Nabigha:

*They did not deprive them of good nourishment, and their mother was filled upon you by a birth-giving male-bearer (dahaqat 'alayka binatiqin madhkar)* [[(5) Diwan 50; Lisan (d-h-q) and (n-t-q), from his ode which he composed concerning Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Khuwaylid, when he met al-Nabigha at 'Ukaz, and advised him to urge his people Banu Dhubyan to abandon their alliance with Banu Asad. Al-Nabigha refused treachery, so Zur'a threatened and warned him. When it reached him, he denounced and satirized him, and praised Banu Asad, saying at the beginning of his poem: "I was informed of Zur'a, and foolishness is by its name, bringing me strange poems." Then he says, mentioning the Ghadiriyyun of Banu Asad, allies of Banu Dhubyan: "The Ghadiriyyun who carried their banner in a march toward a dwelling place... they walk with them, dark-colored camels whose saddles seem like clots of blood poured on the backs of stallions..." ... "a host around which the open land is bounded, leaving the hills like deserts..." ... "They were not deprived..." He describes them in the last verse as blessed, with ease of living, and that their mothers lived in the best livelihood, so their children multiplied. His words "dahaqat": when a woman bears her children one after another, it is said "dahaqat." "Madhkar": one who bears males. The version of the Diwan and others reads "taf'hat 'alayka," meaning she overflowed with her child and prevailed, as water overflows, covers what is around it and drowns it.]]

* *

Another said: its meaning in this place is: We raised it. He said: They say "nataqani al-sayr," meaning it moved me. He said: They say "ma nataqa bi-rijlihi la yarkud" (he did not move with his leg, he does not kick). "Al-nataq" is the rider's mount tossing him when it gallops with him and tires him until he is out of breath; that is "al-nataq" and "al-nutuq," and "nataqatni al-dabba" (the mount tossed me), and "nataqat al-mar'a tantuqu nutuqan" (the woman bore many children).

* *

Some of the Kufans said: "nataqna al-jabal" means: We suspended the mountain above them and raised it, we lift it up lifting (nantuquhu natqan). "Imra'a mintaq" means a woman with many children. He said: I heard "akhadha al-jirab, fa-nataqa ma fihi" (he took the bag and shook out what was in it), when he scattered what was in it. [[In the printed edition: "wa nataqa" with a waw, which I have adopted from the manuscript.]] [[Abu Ja'far did not explain "al-zill" (the shade); see its explanation above, 4:261, 262.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, Verse 172 (Part 1 of 5)

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"﴾ (7:172)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Remember, O Muhammad, your Lord when He brought forth the offspring of Adam from the loins of their fathers, established them in His Oneness, and made some of them bear witness against others to their acknowledgment of that and their affirmation of it." [[An earlier narration on the interpretation of this verse, numbered 10855, was not mentioned here. It appears in Abu Ja'far's abridgement, which preceded on the previous page.]] As follows:

15338 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "God took the covenant from the back of Adam at Na'man [i.e., 'Arafa], and He brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him like specks (dharr). Then He spoke to them face to face (qablan), and said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we testify...' " up to "...what the falsifiers did" (Qur'an 7:173). [[The narration 15338: this report of Ibn 'Abbas, from the hadith of Kulthum ibn Jabr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, was transmitted by Abu Ja'far through five chains: this one, and 15339–15341, then 15350. This first one is the only one traced to the Prophet (marfu', i.e., attributed to the Prophet); all the others stop at Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf, i.e., attributed to a Companion).
Abu Ja'far transmitted it with this chain as marfu' in the History (Tarikh) 1:67.
Ahmad transmitted it as marfu' in his Musnad, number 2455, through the route of Husayn ibn Muhammad, which is the route of Abu Ja'far.
al-Hakim also transmitted it as marfu' in al-Mustadrak 1:27, through Ibrahim ibn Marzuq al-Basri, from Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, from Jarir ibn Hazim, with the same wording, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it. Muslim relied on Kulthum ibn Jabr as a narrator." al-Dhahabi agreed. He then narrated it again in al-Mustadrak 2:544 through al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwarudhi, from Jarir ibn Hazim, and declared it sound, and al-Dhahabi agreed.
al-Haythami also mentioned it as marfu' in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:52 and 7:188–189, and said: "Ahmad transmitted it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."
As for those who transmitted it as mawquf, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) transmitted it through the following chains: 15339–15341 and 15350. Ibn Sa'd also transmitted it in al-Tabaqat 1/1/8, through Ibn 'Ulayyah from Kulthum, and through Hammad ibn Zayd from Kulthum.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3/584–585, and in his History 1:90. He spent a long time discussing its defects and made the large number of narrators of the mawquf version a reason to reject the marfu' transmission. On page 985 (sic) he said that he had shown it to be mawquf and not marfu'. My brother, al-Sayyid Ahmad, in the commentary on the Musnad, said: "It seems Ibn Kathir wanted to defect the marfu' by the mawquf, but this is not a defect, and the raising (to the Prophet) is an addition from a trustworthy narrator, so it is accepted and sound." He also said: "Its chain is sound."
Then consult the takhrij (sourcing) of the following narrations. The narrators of this report are: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, who is Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Qayzak ibn Habib al-Tusi, the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy. He appeared under numbers 3883, 5493, 8870. Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Bahram al-Tamimi, who is also called "Husayn the teacher" and "Husayn the tutor." The group (of major compilers) narrated from him. Appeared under number 2340. Kulthum ibn Jabr ibn Mu'ammal al-Dili, a trustworthy narrator of the junior Successors (tabi'un), appeared under numbers 2861, 2866, 6240. Na'man is a valley of Hudhayl, beyond 'Arafa, two nights from 'Arafa, and it is Na'man al-Arak, which often appears in their poetry.]]

15339 - Amran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Kulthum ibn Jabr narrated to us, saying: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾. He said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about it, and he said: 'Your Lord wiped the back of Adam, and every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection came out at this Na'man' (and he gestured with his hand), 'and He took their covenants and made them testify concerning themselves: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes﴾." [[The narration 15339: Amran ibn Musa ibn Hayyan al-Laythi al-Qazzaz al-Saffar, the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, appeared under numbers 2154, 6589, 6591, 8683. 'Abd al-Warith is 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id ibn Dhakwan, one of the eminent Imams, appeared under numbers 2154, 6589, 6591, 6819, and elsewhere. Abu Ja'far transmitted it in his History 1:67, as mawquf also, and its chain is sound. Ibn Kathir referred to it in his Tafsir 3:585. In the printed edition here it read "bi-Na'man hadha" (at this Na'man), and I have adopted what is in the manuscript and the History, which is the correct reading. See the note on number 15338.
* *
Notice: His saying ﴿dhurriyyatahum﴾ (their descendants) is one of the two readings, and it is our reading. In the other reading it is ﴿dhurriyyatahum﴾ in the plural. Abu Ja'far did not mention this reading. In the manuscript, "dhurriyyatahum" (singular) occurs frequently, and in some reports it is "dhurriyyatahum" (plural). But the editor placed "dhurriyyatahum" (plural) throughout all the reports, so I changed that and followed the manuscript. Wherever it is written in the singular, I keep it so, and wherever it is written in the plural, I keep it so and did not change it.]]

15340 - Ibn Wakī' and Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Kulthum ibn Jabr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify"﴾, he said: "Your Lord wiped the back of Adam, and every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection came out at this Na'man which is beyond 'Arafa, and He took their covenant: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we testify﴾." The wording is that of the narration of Ya'qub. [[The narration 15340: Ibn 'Ulayyah is Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Asadi, the well-known Imam, who has appeared many times before. This is the second of the mawquf narrations on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Ja'far narrated it with this chain in his History 1:67, and Ibn Sa'd narrated it through this same route in al-Tabaqat 1/1/8 with this wording. Sound chain. See the note on 15338.]]

15341 - Ya'qub also narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'a ibn Kulthum narrated, from his father, in this narration: ﴿They said: Yes, we testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"﴾. [[The narration 15341: Ibn Sa'd transmitted it in al-Tabaqat 1/1/8, and limited it to the words of the Exalted: "on the Day of Resurrection." See the preceding notes.]]

15342 - 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Amran ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first thing God caused Adam to descend upon was Bad-hana, a land in India, [[In the printed edition: "Bad-Jani, a land in India," with a jim. I have adopted what is in the manuscript at this point, and in the History of al-Tabari 1:60. In this same report: "Badhana'," the land of India, with a hamza at the end, as if it were from "al-Dahna'," which is the whole wasteland and... This is not correct, as you will see. This word will come in report 15347, where the printed edition also has "Bad-Jani," with a jim, which is a change by the editor. As for the manuscript, it has "Badhana." Ibn Sa'd narrated this report in al-Tabaqat 1/1/5, and in it: "He created Adam from a land called Dahna'," with a ha and a hamza, and then similarly in 1/1/8, where it says: "God created Adam at Badhana'." A great confusion has occurred regarding the name of this place and its location, which is worth detailing here.
1. It is stated in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, from Ibn Ishaq: "Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out, when he turned back from al-Ta'if, to Dahna, until he alighted at al-Ji'rana, along with those people who were with him, and with him from Hawazin were many captives." Similarly in the History of al-Tabari 3:134, from Ibn Ishaq.
This is a place which, without doubt, is in the Arabian Peninsula. al-Bakri mentioned it in Mu'jam ma Asta'jam (pp. 545–546) and did not confuse it with anything else. He vocalized it with a fatha on the dal, a sukun on the unpointed ha, and a fatha on the nun, in the pattern "fa'la." Yaqut in his Mu'jam vocalized it likewise, then said: "It is also transmitted with the short and long vowel." al-Bakri, in defining it, said: "A place on the sea-coast." Then he returned and mentioned the report of Ibn Ishaq in his Sirah, then said: "So it occurs in the book of the Sirah with the nun, and al-Tabari also mentioned it that way, and there is no sea-coast there. I think he meant: 'He passed by Dahi,' which was mentioned earlier. Were it not that it is not precisely defined for us, the doubt would be removed" (with a fatha on the dal, a sukun on the ha, followed by a ya). Thus al-Bakri mentioned it in his Mu'jam (p. 347) and said: "A place, mentioned by Abu Bakr," without further explanation. As for Yaqut, he said of "Dahna": "It is one of the districts of al-Ta'if," and did not mention the entry for "Dahi" which al-Bakri mentioned.
My view is that al-Bakri took his statement "a place on the sea-coast" from some commentator on poetry, for he recited the verse of Rabi'a ibn Jahdar al-Hudhali al-Lihyani:
"Had he been a man I deceived, I would have deceived him, / but he is a fish in Dahna, I struggle (with him)."
"I say to him, that I might oppose his trickery: / 'Behind you, fill your flock of wild sheep.'"
So the commentator on the poem seems to have made it a place on the sea-coast because of his phrase "a fish in Dahna I struggle," but that is not necessary, unless "Dahna" is a different place from the one mentioned in the Sirah.
He also recited from al-Asma'i: "And a companion of mine in Dahna, whatever man... that I killed, and you are the valiant knight!"
Whatever the case, it is a place in the lands of the Arabs, beyond doubt, and it is far removed from the other "Dahna," as you will see below.
2. As for the other "Dahna," mentioned in this report, it is described in it as "in the land of India." al-Bakri mentioned it under the entry (Washam): 1364, saying: "Ibn Ishaq said: The people of knowledge mention that the descent-place of Adam and Eve was upon a mountain called Washam, in the land of India, and it is today in the middle among its villages, between al-Dahanj and al-Mandal." al-Tabari also mentioned it in his History 1:60, and in it: "As for the People of the Torah, they said: Adam was caused to descend in India, upon a mountain called Wasam, near a valley called Buhayl, between al-Dahanj and al-Mandal, two towns in the land of India." This is the text of Ibn Ishaq as he narrated it with his chain. So the reports in which mention is made of the descent or creation of Adam and in which occurs "Dahna," without specifying its location, are clarified by these reports, which mention this and show that it is in the land of India.
