"Dahna" with an unpointed ha is "Dahanj" in the reports I mentioned before, arabicized. Thus in the sources it appears as "Dahna" with an unpointed ha. But the transmitters of lexicographical books related to us in the report of Ibn 'Abbas: "God wiped the back of Adam at Dajna'," which is the name of a place, and is also transmitted with an unpointed ha. This is what the author of Lisan al-'Arab mentioned under (dajn), then under (dahn), and said: "It is between al-Ta'if and Makkah." This is the first confusion. In fact, in this report it is a place in India, but the one "between al-Ta'if and Makkah" is the Arabic "Dahna" which we mentioned first.
The author of the Qamus said: "Dajni, with a damma or kasra, and it may be lengthened, is a land from which Adam (peace be upon him) was created, or it is with an unpointed ha." Then he mentioned it under (dahn) and said: "Dahna, in (d-j-n)," meaning that it is the same, with a damma on the dal.
al-Zabidi in Taj al-'Arus commented and said: "Its mention has come in the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq, regarding the departure of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from al-Ta'if, at Dajna'. And it has come in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: 'God created Adam from Dajna', then wiped his back at Na'man al-Arak.' And the wiping of his back was after his coming out of Paradise, by agreement of the narrations." All of this he mentioned with the jim. He too confused the two places: the place in the Sirah and the place of Adam's creation or descent. The confusion arose by his following al-Suhayli in al-Rawd al-Anf 2:305. The undoubted cause of this confusion is the mention of "Na'man al-Arak" in the report about the creation of Adam, and "Na'man al-Arak" is in the land of the Arabs. So whoever has not gathered the reports on the creation said that "Dahna" is in the land of the Arabs, and did not consider what came in the other version of the report, that it is in the land of India.
Moreover, I think that "Dahna" and "Dajna'," with short and long vowel, is an arabicization of "Dahanj" which has been mentioned, and it is the land which is in India. As for the one in the lands of the Arabs, it is "Dahna" with an unpointed ha, and nothing else. This is sufficient, God willing, in verifying this word.]] Then God wiped his back, and brought out from it every soul that He would create until the Hour arises. Then He took their covenant: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were unaware of this.'"﴾ [[The narration 15342: 'Amr is 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, who has appeared many times before. Amran ibn 'Uyayna is the brother of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, the well-known Imam. Ibn Ma'in and Abu Zur'a said: "Good in narration (salih al-hadith)." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "His hadith is not used as evidence, for he brings unusual reports (manakir)." al-'Uqayli said: "There is error in his hadith." It has appeared under numbers 4189 and 10580. Abu Ja'far narrated this report in abridged form in his History 1:60, and Ibn Sa'd in abridged form 1/1/5. It will come under number 15343, through the narration of Waki', from Amran, from 'Ata', and there is no mention in it of "Dahna." It also comes through other chains, numbers 15346 and 15347, from other than Amran, from 'Ata'.]]

15343 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Amran ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Adam was caused to descend when he was caused to descend, and God wiped his back and brought forth from it every soul which He would create until the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes﴾. Then he recited: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and the pen dried up from that day with what would come to be until the Day of Resurrection." [[The narration 15343: This is another route of the earlier report. Abu Ja'far transmitted it through this route in his History 1:67. See the preceding note.]]

15344 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, he said: "When God created Adam, He took his offspring from his back like specks (dharr), and then He grasped with two handfuls, and said to the People of the Right: 'Enter Paradise in peace,' and said to the others: 'Enter the Fire, and I do not care.'" [[The narration 15344: This report and the one which follows it were transmitted through two routes. The first was transmitted by Abu Ja'far in his History 1:67. Yahya ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi al-Nahshali, whom Ahmad and others declared trustworthy, while Ibn Ma'in and others declared weak. Appeared under numbers 300, 6317, 9035, 14201. Habib ibn Abi Thabit is Habib ibn Qays ibn Nayyar, trustworthy, narrated by the group (of major compilers), appeared under numbers 9012, 9035, 10423, and elsewhere. The meaning of this report is recorded in the musnads of a group of Companions, but I did not find it in this wording from Ibn 'Abbas except in this place and in the History of al-Tabari. See the following note.]]

15345 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "God wiped the back of Adam, and brought forth from it every good one in His right hand, and brought forth every wicked one in the other." [[The narration 15345: This is another route of the earlier report, without its wording. Al-Ajurri transmitted it in Kitab al-Shari'a pp. 211–212, through 'Ali ibn Mushir from al-A'mash, without this wording. In the manuscript it reads: "every wicked one in the Hereafter."]]

15346 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Shurayk, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "God wiped the back of Adam, and brought forth from it every soul which He would create until the Day of Resurrection." [[The narration 15346: See what preceded, numbers 15342 and 15343, the report of 'Ata' from Sa'id, without this wording. This is a report of sound chain, and it will come through another route in the one that follows.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 2 of 5):**

15347. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from ʿAta, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾." He said: When God created Adam, He wiped his back with *Dahna* [[In the printed edition it reads "Bad Jinа" with a jim; I have adopted what is in the manuscript. For the discussion of this, see p. 225, note 1.]], and He brought forth from his back every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: "﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: '﴿Yes, we testify﹄." He said: "They will be seen on that day, when the pen has dried over what will occur until the Day of Resurrection." [[Report 15347: another chain for the earlier report. ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays al-Razi al-Azraq is trustworthy (thiqa), though he erred slightly in narration. Previously cited under nos. 6887, 9346, and elsewhere.
Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) also related this report in *al-Tarikh* 1/68, and Ibn Saʿd related it in *al-Tabaqat* 1/1/8, through Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad, from ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib, with much the same wording, and at its end: "Saʿid said: 'They will consider that the covenant was taken on that day.'" Al-Suyuti attributed it in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:141 to Ibn al-Mundhir alone. The phrase "yuraw" (with a dammah on the yaʾ and a fathah on the raʾ, in the passive voice) means: they assume and estimate this.]]

15348. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAli ibn Badhima, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When God created Adam, peace be upon him, He took his covenant, wiped his back, and brought forth his descendants like the *dharr* (tiny ants/motes) [[Dharr: the smallest visible particles or tiny ants.]], and He recorded their terms (of life), their provisions, and their afflictions. = "﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.'﴾" [[Report 15348: Abu Jaʿfar related this report by two chains, this one and the one that follows. Al-Masʿudi is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, previously cited under nos. 2156, 2729, 2937, 5563, and elsewhere. He is trustworthy, but he became confused in his later years and his memory changed. Whatever the early shaykhs narrated from him is sound. Waki''s hearing from al-Masʿudi is an early one. ʿAli ibn Badhima al-Jazari is trustworthy, and there is some criticism of him that is not serious; previously cited under no. 629 and elsewhere. Al-Suyuti cited this report in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:141 and attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

15349. ...He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAli ibn Badhima, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾." He said: When God created Adam, He took his covenant that He is his Lord, and He recorded his term and his afflictions. He brought forth his descendants like the *dharr*, took their covenant, and recorded their terms, their provisions, and their afflictions. [[Report 15349: Yazid ibn Harun al-Sulami is one of the well-known memorizing scholars and leading authorities, cited many times. Yazid ibn Harun narrated confused reports from al-Masʿudi after his memory had changed, as I mentioned in the earlier note.]]

15350. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Rabiʿa ibn Kulthum ibn Jabr, from his father, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves﴾." He said: God wiped the back of Adam, peace be upon him, while he was in *Batn Nuʿman* [[Batn Nuʿman: a valley beside ʿArafat.]], =a valley beside ʿArafat=, and He brought forth his descendants from his back like the *dharr*. Then He made them testify concerning themselves: "﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾" They said: "Yes, we testify." [[Report 15350: This is another chain for the earlier reports 15338–15341, whose takhrij was given there.]]

15351. ...He said: My father narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Jamra al-Duba'i, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God brought forth the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, from his back like the *dharr*, while he was in *adhay* of water [[Adhay al-ma': the layers of water that the wind raises from its surface, not the waves. It also means strong waves, which is the more common meaning. The intended meaning in this report is the first one. The printed edition has "adha" without the madd, which is not correct. The manuscript has "adna," which is a clear error.]]. [[Report 15351: Abu Hilal is Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Rasibi, trustworthy though subject to criticism. Ibn ʿAdi said, after mentioning reports of his that are all or mostly not preserved: "He has other narrations besides what I mentioned, and some of his narrations are not agreed upon by the trustworthy transmitters, yet his hadith is written down." Previously cited under nos. 2996, 4681, and 13967.
Abu Hamza al-Dubaʿi is Nasr ibn ʿImran ibn ʿIsam al-Dubaʿi, trustworthy and reliable, previously cited under nos. 5995 and 6228. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Abu Hamza," which is a pure error.
This report was cited by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* 3:585, and al-Suyuti cited it in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:141, attributing it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Manda in *Kitab al-Radd ʿala al-Jahmiyya*, and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

15352. ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Damra ibn Rabiʿa narrated to us, saying: Abu Masʿud narrated to us, from Juwaybir, who said: A son of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim died, when he was six days old. He said: "O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, uncover his face and untie his knot, for my son will be questioned and examined!" I did what he had instructed me. When I had finished, I said: "May God have mercy on you, about what will your son be questioned? Who will question him?" He said: "He will be questioned about the covenant he affirmed in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him." I said: "O Abu al-Qasim [[Abu al-Qasim: a kunya of the Prophet ﷺ, though here it is used of the addressee (al-Dahhak)? Translated as addressed.]], what is this covenant he affirmed in the loins of Adam?" He said: "Ibn ʿAbbas told me that God wiped the loins of Adam and brought forth from them every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection, and took their covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them their provisions. The Hour will not come until those who were given the covenant that day are born. So whoever of them reaches the later covenant and fulfills it, the first covenant benefits him. Whoever reaches the later covenant and does not fulfill it, the first covenant does not benefit him. And whoever dies young, before reaching the later covenant, dies upon the first covenant, upon the *fitra* (natural disposition)." [[In the manuscript, the text from the beginning of "then He guaranteed for them" up to "the Hour arrives" has been omitted; it is present in Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* and *al-Durr al-Manthur*. In the printed edition, from "and He guaranteed" to "in his loins" has been omitted.]] [[Report 15352: ʿAli ibn Sahl al-Ramli is the shaykh of al-Tabari, cited many times. Damra ibn Rabiʿa al-Filastini is trustworthy, previously cited under nos. 7134, 12868, and 13650. Abu Masʿud, who narrated from Juwaybir, I fear may be Saʿid ibn Iyas al-Jurayri, but I have not verified this. Juwaybir is a nickname; it is said his name is Jabir ibn Saʿid. He has been cited many times, and in this report his name is explicitly stated as Jabir. If Juwaybir is a nickname, then it is a diminutive of Jabir. This report was cited by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* 3:585, and by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:143.]]

15353. Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me, that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan narrated to them, from al-Aswad ibn Sarie of the Banu Saʿd, who said: I went on four military campaigns with the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: The people attacked the offspring after they had killed the combatants. This reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it upset him greatly. Then he said: "What is wrong with people who attack offspring?" A man said: "O Messenger of God, are they not the children of polytheists?" He said: "Your best are the children of polytheists! Indeed, every soul that is born is born upon the *fitra*, and it remains so until its tongue speaks for it, and then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian." = al-Hasan said: "By God, God has said this in His Book," [[In the printed edition: "By God, God has said," I do not know where that addition came from.]] and he recited: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾." [[Report 15353: al-Sarri ibn Yahya ibn Iyas al-Shaybani, Abu al-Haytham, is trustworthy and firm. He narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri; he is biographically recorded in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Kabir* 2/2/176, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/283.
Al-Aswad ibn Sarie ibn Hamiri ibn ʿUbada al-Tamimi is a Companion. He was a well-known poet and the first to give sermons (qass) in the mosque of Basra. He is the one who said in his sermon about the dead: "If you escape from it, you escape from a great calamity; and if not, I do not think you will escape." (*al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin* 1:467; *Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shuʿara* 151, note 6). He is biographically recorded in *al-Isaba*, *Usd al-Ghaba*, Ibn Saʿd 7/1/28, *al-Istiʿab* 44, Ibn Qutayba's *al-Maʿarif* 276, al-Bukhari's *al-Kabir* 1/1/445, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/129, and others.
This report was narrated by this chain by Ahmad in his *Musnad* 4:24, with slight differences in wording; Ibn Saʿd in abridged form in *al-Tabaqat* 7/1/28; al-Bukhari in abridged form in *al-Tarikh* 1/1/445; and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in *al-Istiʿab* in a longer form similar to it, 44. Ibn Hajar mentioned it in *al-Isaba* in his biography and said: "Ibn Hibban and Ibn al-Sakan narrated it through al-Sarri." Ahmad narrated it in his *Musnad* 3:435 through Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib, from Aban ibn Yazid, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, in abridged form, then he narrated after it through Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, in similar form. Then he narrated it in 4:24 through Saʿid, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, and the report clarifies that this occurred in a military expedition (sariya) that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent on the day of Hunayn. al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* 2:123 through Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib, then through Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, in similar form to what Ahmad narrated, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it in *al-Sunan al-Kubra* 9:77, through Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan. He also narrated it in *al-Sunan* 9:130, through Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib, from Aban ibn Yazid, from Qatada. al-Haythami mentioned it in *Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid* 5:316, then said: "Ahmad narrated it with several chains, and al-Tabarani in *al-Kabir* and *al-Awsat* likewise... and some of Ahmad's chains have narrators who are the narrators of the Sahih." Ibn Kathir cited it in his *Tafsir* 3:584 and said: "It was recorded by al-Nasa'i in his *Sunan* through the hadith of Hushaym, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, who said: 'al-Aswad ibn Sarie narrated to me,' and he mentioned it, but did not mention the statement of al-Hasan al-Basri, and he abbreviated the verse at that point."]]

15354. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyiba narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Saʿid ibn al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak =and from Mansur, from Mujahid=, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾": "They were taken from his back as a comb is drawn through the hair from the head. Then He said to them: '﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾' They said: '﴿Yes, we testify.﴾' The angels said: 'We testify that you will say on the Day of Resurrection: "We were indeed unaware of this."'" [[Report 15354: Abu Jaʿfar related it through three chains. The first is traced to the Prophet ﷺ (marfuʿ), and the other two are traced to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr (mawquf). There are two chains for this report: "Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Ajlah" and "Sufyan, from Mansur." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid al-Jurjani is a shaykh of Abu Jaʿfar. I have not found a biography for him, but he narrated from him in *al-Tarikh* 3:207, from Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba as well, and then in *al-Muntakhab min Dhayl al-Mudhayyal* (*al-Tarikh*: 13), pp. 48, 60. Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba is Ahmad ibn ʿIsa ibn Sulayman al-Jurjani, judge of Qumis. Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written down." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in *al-Thiqat*, and Ibn ʿAdi said: "He narrated hadiths most of which are strange." He is biographically recorded in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Khulasa* 7, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/64. The name "Tayba" is vocalized with a ẓa' in *al-Khulasa*, but in other sources with a ṭa' (unmarked dot). "Sufyan ibn Saʿid" is al-Thawri, and in the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Sufyan, from Saʿid," which is a plain error; al-Thawri narrated directly from al-Ajlah without an intermediary, *al-Kabir* 1/2/68. "Al-Ajlah" is al-Ajlah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hujayya al-Kindi, previously cited under nos. 5384 and 10857. He is subject to criticism, but Ibn ʿAdi judged him trustworthy. This report was cited in the marfuʿ form by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:142, and he added its attribution to Ibn Manda in *Kitab al-Radd ʿala al-Jahmiyya*. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his *Tafsir* 3:586, 589, and weakened its marfuʿ form, explaining that its mawquf form is sounder. Al-Tabari's statement about it will come later on p. 250: "I do not know it to be sound, because the trustworthy narrators whose memory and mastery are relied upon narrated this hadith from al-Thawri and halted it at ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr; they did not raise it, nor did they mention in the hadith this phrase that Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba attributed to him."]]

15355. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, regarding His saying: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾," He said: He took them as a comb takes [hair] from the head. [[Report 15355: This report and the one that follows are the two authentic mawquf reports. See the earlier note.]]

15356. Ibn Wakiʿ and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾," He said: He took them as a comb takes [hair] from the head. Ibn Humayd said: "As the comb is drawn." [[Report 15356: It is mawquf on ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, sound in its chain, like the earlier ones. In the manuscript it reads "kama yu'akhadh al-mashtu" once more without the bāʾ, and the correct form seems to be that of the printed edition, which is how it appears in *al-Durr al-Manthur*. See the earlier note. These three reports were cited by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* 3:586, 589, and al-Suyuti cited them in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:141 as mawquf, attributing them to Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Lalakai in *al-Sunna*, though he shortened their attribution to Ibn Jarir.]]

15357. Ibrahim ibn Saʿid al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn ʿUbada and Saʿd ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was asked about this verse: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins﴾," and ʿUmar said: "I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'God created Adam, then wiped his back with His right hand, [[In the printed edition: "wiped his back," I have adopted what is in the manuscript and *al-Tarikh*.]] and brought forth from it offspring, and said: "I created these for Paradise, and they will act by the deeds of the people of Paradise." Then He wiped his back and brought forth from it offspring, and said: "I created these for the Fire, and they will act by the deeds of the people of the Fire."' A man said: 'O Messenger of God, then what is the point of deeds?' He said: 'When God creates a servant for Paradise, He makes him act by the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies upon the deeds of one of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him into Paradise. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He makes him act by the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies upon the deeds of one of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him into the Fire.'" [[Report 15357: Ibrahim ibn Saʿid al-Jawhari al-Tabari is the shaykh of al-Tabari, cited many times. Saʿd ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Jaʿfar al-Ansari is trustworthy, though some have criticized him. Previously cited under nos. 3959 and 9225. His weakness does not harm this chain, because Rawh ibn ʿUbada is trustworthy beyond doubt and is the main source for this report in all the books.
Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa al-Jazari is trustworthy, previously cited under nos. 4964 and 8396.
ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab is trustworthy and reliable; the group (of compilers) narrated from him. Previously cited under no. 14685.]]

And (Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani) is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i, one who met the Companions). It is said that he did not hear from Umar, and between them is (Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah al-Azdi), as will come in the following report. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 4/1/276. I do not know why Ibn Abi Hatim omitted him in his book, or whether he fell out of his biographies. Abu Ja'far narrated this report with this chain in his history 1:67, with slight variation in its wording. Malik narrated it in the Muwatta, 898. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad, no. 311. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 4:312, no. 4703. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 1:27 and said: "This hadith is sound according to the conditions of both of them, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi objected to him, saying: "It contains an interruption (irsal)." Then al-Hakim returned and narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:324, 544 and said: "This hadith meets the condition of Muslim, though he did not record it." This contradicts what he said at first. More surprising is that al-Dhahabi agreed with him in these two places and did not object that it contains an interruption!! This is strange! Al-Ajurri narrated it in Kitab al-Shari'ah, 170. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in al-Taqassi, 54, and said: "There are two defects (illah) in the chain of this hadith, which I have explained in my book al-Tamhid." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir and said: "This is a good hadith. Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from Umar. Some have mentioned a man between Muslim ibn Yasar and Umar in this chain." After writing what preceded, I found that the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned the report in Shifa al-Alil, 1029, quoting what Ibn Abd al-Barr said in al-Tamhid, and he said: "al-Hakim said: 'This hadith meets the condition of Muslim,' and it is not as he said; rather it is a broken (munqati') hadith. Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) said: It is a broken hadith, for this Muslim ibn Yasar did not meet Umar ibn al-Khattab; between them is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah. This is if it is correct that the one who narrated it from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah mentioned Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, since he is no more reliable than Malik, nor one who is used as evidence when he contradicts Malik. Moreover, Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah and Muslim ibn Yasar are both unknown, not recognized as bearers of knowledge or transmitters of hadith. This is not Muslim ibn Yasar the worshipful Basran; rather he is an unknown Medinan man." Then he cited from the history of Ibn Abi Khaythamah: "I read to Yahya ibn Ma'in this hadith of Malik, and he wrote with his own hand against Muslim ibn Yasar: 'not known.'" Abu Umar said: "This hadith, although its chain is defective, its meaning from the Prophet (ﷺ) has been narrated through many routes," and then he listed the names of the Companions from whom it was narrated. Ibn Kathir took it up in his Tafsir 3:586 and in his history 1:89, 90, and he said after quoting at-Tirmidhi: "So said Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah. Abu Hatim added Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah between them. What Abu Hatim said, then Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan from Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, from Baqiyyah, from Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, who said: 'I was with Umar...'" And the Hafiz ad-Daraqutni said: "Umar ibn Ju'thum was followed by Yazid ibn Sinan Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, and their statement is more correct than the statement of Malik." Ibn Kathir said: "It is apparent that Malik deliberately dropped Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, because he did not know Nu'aym's condition and did not recognize him, for he is unknown except in this hadith. Likewise he omits the mention of a group whom he does not approve of, and for this reason he often transmits raised (marfu') reports as mursal and cuts off many connected (mawsul) ones." See the commentary on the following report.

**15358.** Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa narrated to us, from Baqiyyah, from Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi, who said: Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah narrated to me, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muslim ibn Yasar, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, from Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording.

[[15358 – Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa ibn Bahlul al-Qurashi, a memorizer, truthful, with some criticism of him; it is said he was among those who practised tadlis (concealment) of the type called tadlis al-taswiyah (levelling the chain). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/246, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/104. Baqiyyah is Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, who has passed several times. Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, and is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/101. In the manuscript it was "Umar ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi," which is an error; in the printed edition it was "Umar ibn Ju'thum," which is also an error. Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah al-Azdi: al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention any criticism of him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/96, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/460. This report was narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 4/2/96, 97, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, who heard his father, who heard Zayd, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah al-Azdi, in similar wording but abridged. Abu Dawud narrated it in the Sunan 4:313, no. 4704, by the route of Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, from Baqiyyah, but he did not mention its wording, and he said: "The hadith of Malik is more complete." See the mention of this connected narration in the commentary on the report above.]]

**15359.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Ammarah, from Abu Muhammad, a man from Medina, [[In the printed edition: "a man from Medina." I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] who said: I asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about the words of Him (Exalted): ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾. He said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about it as you asked me, and he said: "Allah created Adam with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit. Then He seated him and wiped his back with His right hand, and brought forth a seed, and said: 'This seed I have created for Paradise.' Then He wiped his back with His other hand, and both His hands are right hands, and said: 'This seed I have created for the Fire, and they will work whatever work You wish. Then I will seal for them with the worst of their deeds, and enter them into the Fire.'"

[[Report 15359 – Ammarah is Ammarah ibn Umayr al-Taymi; the authors of the six books narrated from him. He has passed under nos. 3294 and 5789. Abu Muhammad, a man of Medina: I have not found any information about him in any of the books. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated this report in al-Tamhid (appended to al-Taqassi), 302, with this same chain and wording, except that it has: "Then I will seal for them with the most evil of their deeds." As-Suyuti took it up in ad-Durr al-Manthur 1:142, and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.]]

**15360.** al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾. He said: Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, then brought forth his offspring from his loins like ants (dharr). He said to them: "Who is your Lord?" They said: "Allah is our Lord." Then He returned them to his loins, until every one whose covenant He had taken is born, neither increased nor decreased among them, until the Hour rises.

[[Report 15360 – This is a chain that circulates in tafsir; its explanation has passed in reports nos. 186 and 187. As-Suyuti took it up in ad-Durr al-Manthur 1:141, attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim, and to al-Lalika'i in as-Sunnah.]]

**15361.** Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾, … up to His words: ﴿They said: "Yes, we testify."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back and brought forth all his offspring in the form of ants. He made them speak, and they spoke, and He made them testify against themselves. He put light with some of them. He said to Adam: "These are your offspring; I take their covenant: that I am their Lord, so that they do not associate anything with Me, and their provision is upon Me." Adam said: "Who is this one with the light with him?" He said: "He is David." He said: "O Lord, how many years have You decreed for him?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "How many have You decreed for me?" He said: "A thousand years. And I have decreed for every person among them how long he will live and how long he will remain." He said: "O Lord, increase it for him." He said: "This is a written decree, so give him from your life, if you wish." He said: "Yes." The pen had dried over the term of all the rest of the children of Adam, so forty years were written for him from Adam's term, and his term became a hundred years. When he had lived nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came to him. When Adam saw him he said: "What is it with you?" He said: "You have completed your term." Adam said: "I have lived only nine hundred and sixty years, and forty years remain." He said: "When he said that to the Angel, the Angel said: 'My Lord has informed me of it.'" He said: "Return to your Lord and ask Him!" So the Angel returned to his Lord and said: "What is it with you?" He said: "O Lord, I came back to You because of what I knew of Your honouring him." Allah said: "Go back and inform him that I have given his son David forty years."

[[Report 15361 – This is a chain that circulates in tafsir; its weakness has been explained in the commentary on no. 305.]]

**15362.** al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah, blessed and exalted, struck His right shoulder, and every created soul destined for Paradise came out, white and pure, and He said: "These are the people of Paradise." Then He struck His left shoulder, and every created soul destined for the Fire came out, black, and He said: "These are the people of the Fire." Then He took their covenants of faith and recognition of Him and of His command, and of belief in Him and in His command, from all the children of Adam, and He made them testify against themselves. They believed, affirmed, recognized and acknowledged. It has reached me that He brought them out upon His palm like grains of mustard. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: When Allah brought them out, He said: "O servants of Allah, answer Allah!" "Al-ijabah" (response) means obedience. They said: "We obey; O Allah, we obey; O Allah, we respond (labbayk)!" He said: So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was given it in the rites of Hajj: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk" (Here I am, O Allah, here I am). He said: He struck the back of Adam when He created him. He said: Ibn Abbas also said: Allah created Adam, then brought forth his offspring from his back like ants, and spoke to them, then returned them to his loins. So there is no one but who has spoken and said: "My Lord is Allah." He said: Every creature that is created will exist until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the natural disposition (fitrah) upon which He created people. Ibn Jurayj said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The covenant was taken from them at Nu'man (Nu'man is beyond Arafat), "that they would say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of this﴾," concerning the covenant that was taken from them.

[[Report 15362 – al-Zubayr ibn Musa ibn Maynaa al-Makki is trustworthy; he has passed under no. 8649. This report was narrated by al-Ajurri in Kitab al-Shari'ah, abridged, 212, by the route of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa. As-Suyuti took it up in ad-Durr al-Manthur 1:144, attributing it only to Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

**15363.** al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: He gathered them all together on that day, everything that would exist until the Day of Resurrection. Then He questioned them and took their covenant: ﴿And He made them testify against themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed, we were unaware of this." Or lest you should say: "Only our fathers associated partners before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ He said: "I call upon the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call upon your father Adam to witness against you, that you would not say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We did not know of this!' Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you My Books!" They said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord but You and no god but You." So on that day they acknowledged obedience to Him, and their father Adam was raised above them, and he looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "O Lord, why did You not make them equal!" He said: "I wish to be thanked." He said: On that day among them were the prophets, peace be upon them, like lamps. And He singled out the prophets with another covenant. Allah said: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary, and We took from them a firm covenant﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 7]. And it is He, may His mention be exalted, who says: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no change in the creation of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 30]. And concerning that He said: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 56], meaning: We took his covenant along with the earlier warners. And of this is His saying: ﴿And We found most of them unfaithful to covenant; indeed, We found most of them defiant﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 102], [and His saying, exalted be He] [[This addition in parentheses is from other references; it is not in the manuscript or the printed edition.]] ﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾ [Surah Yunus: 74]. He said: He knew, on the day they acknowledged it, who would believe and who would deny.

[[Report 15363 – A sound chain, similar to what has passed many times. This report was narrated by Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal in his additions to his father's Musnad (5:135), from his shaykh Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Rabbali, from al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, abridged. al-Haythami took it up in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:25 and said: "Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it from his shaykh Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Rabbali, who is unknown (mastur), and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." al-Hakim narrated it in full in al-Mustadrak 2:323 by the route of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Abu Ja'far Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Mahan, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and said: "This hadith is sound in its chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. al-Ajurri narrated it in Kitab al-Shari'ah, 207, by the route of Hakkam ibn Muslim al-Razi, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in al-Tamhid (appended to al-Taqassi), 307, by the route of Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Salih, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, which is the route of al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3:588 and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh in their tafsirs. As-Suyuti took it up in ad-Durr al-Manthur 1:142, adding its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mandah in Kitab al-Radd ala al-Jahmiyyah, al-Lalika'i, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma wa al-Sifat, and Ibn Asakir in his history.]]

**15364.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify against themselves: "Am I not your Lord?"﴾ He said: He brought them out from the back of Adam, and gave Adam a lifespan of a thousand years. He said: They were presented to Adam, and he saw a man from his offspring with a light, which pleased him. He asked about him, and it was said: "He is David; his lifespan has been set at sixty years!" So he gave him forty years from his own lifespan. When Adam was near death, he began to dispute with them over the forty years. It was said to him: "You gave them to David!" He said: So he began to dispute with them.

**15365.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾. He said: He brought out his offspring from his back like ants, and presented them to Adam by their names, the names of their fathers, and their terms! He said: Then the spirit of David was presented to him in a shining light. He said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is from your offspring, a prophet and a successor." He said: "How long is his life?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "Add to him forty years from my life." He said: "And the pens were moist, flowing." So forty years were recorded for David. The lifespan of Adam, peace be upon him, was a thousand years. When he had completed it, except for the forty years, the Angel of Death was sent to him, and said: "O Adam, I have been commanded to take you." He said: "Has not forty years of my life remained?" He said: So the Angel of Death returned to his Lord and said: "Adam claims forty years of his life!" He said: "Inform Adam that he gave them to his son David, and the pens were moist!" So they were recorded for David.

**15366.** Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, in similar wording.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 4 of 5):

15367 -.... He said: Ibn Fudayl and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAtaʾ, regarding ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾: "He brought them out from the back of Adam until He took the covenant from them, then He returned them into his loins."

15368 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Nadr ibn ʿArabi, regarding ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾: "He brought them out from the back of Adam until He took the covenant from them, then He returned them into his loins."

15369 -.... He said: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Abu Bistam, from al-Dahhak, who said: "When God created His creation for Adam, peace be upon him [[(1) This is an unusual expression, but it is thus in the manuscript and the printed edition.]] He said: He created them and made them testify concerning themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.'" [[The report 15369: "Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd" is, in my estimation, Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Abi Umayya al-Tanafisi, who has passed as no. 405, 9155, 11418. "Abu Bistam" is Muqatil ibn Hayyan al-Balkhi, who has passed as no. 3842.]]

15370 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Farj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾: "Ibn ʿAbbas said: God created Adam, then He brought forth his descendants from his back. God spoke to them and made them speak, and said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' Then He returned them into his loins. So there is no creature except that he has spoken and said: 'My Lord is God.' And the Hour will not come until there is born the one who was on that day a witness over himself."

15371 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Talha narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes."﴾ And that is when He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 83], and that is when He says: ﴿Then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [Surah al-Anʿam: 149], meaning: the day He took the covenant from them, then He presented them to Adam, peace be upon him. [[(1) The report 15371: "ʿAmr ibn Talha" is ʿAmr ibn Hammad ibn Talha al-Qannad, one of the most frequently recurring men in tafsir, who has passed as no. 168. In the printed edition, here and in the following report, it was "ʿUmar ibn Talha," which is a clear error. This report is part of a long report that Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr narrated in al-Tamhid (appended to Kitab al-Taqassi): 303, 304, with its chain from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Sanjar, from ʿAmr ibn Hammad, from Nasr ibn Nasr al-Hamadhani, from al-Suddi, from his companions. ʿAmr said: his companions were Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, and from Murra al-Hamadhani, from Ibn Masʿud, and from some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Suyuti extracted it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:141, at length, and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Tamhid. See the following report, no. 15373.]]

15372 - He said: ʿUmar narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: "God brought Adam out of Paradise, and he had not descended from the heaven. Then He wiped the right side of his back, and brought forth from it his descendants like the form of ants, white, like pearls. He said to them: 'Enter Paradise by My mercy!' Then He wiped the left side of his back, and brought forth from it, like the form of ants, black, and He said: 'Enter the Fire, and I do not care!' That is when He says: 'The companions of the right and the companions of the left.' Then He took the covenant from them, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes.﴾ So a group obeyed Him willingly, and a group obeyed Him unwillingly, out of dissimulation (taqiyya)." [[(1) In the printed edition: "He brought forth from it descendants, white, like pearls, like the form of ants." This agrees with what Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr narrated, but I affirm what is in the manuscript. As for what Abu Jaʿfar narrated in the History, it is: "He brought forth from it descendants like the form of ants, white like pearls," in the plural "white." In the printed edition: "He brought forth from it a black descendant like the form of ants," which agrees with Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's al-Tamhid, but I affirm what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what Abu Jaʿfar narrated in the History.]] [[The report 15372: this report, mentioned earlier, is in Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's al-Tamhid (appended to Kitab al-Taqassi: 303, 304) at length, and Ibn Jarir narrated it in his History in abbreviated form with this wording: 1:68.]]

15373 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a similar manner, but he added after his saying "and a group [obeyed] out of dissimulation" the words: "So He and the angels said: 'We testify, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed, we were unaware of this. Or you say: Indeed our fathers associated partners with God before, and we were descendants after them.'" Therefore there is no one on earth among the children of Adam except that he knows that his Lord is God, and there is no polytheist except that he says to his son: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community﴾ — and "community" means religion — ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 23]. That is when God says: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes."﴾ And that is when He says: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 83], and that is when He says: ﴿Then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [Surah al-Anʿam: 149], meaning: the day He took the covenant from them. [[The report 15373: this report is part of the two preceding reports, 15371 and 15372, as I believe. See their takhrij above. However, the opening of this report does not appear in any of the sources.]]

15374 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbi, regarding ﴿from their loins, their descendants﴾: "God wiped over the loins of Adam and brought forth from his loins his descendants until the Day of Resurrection, and He took their covenant that He is their Lord. They gave Him that, and you will not ask any unbeliever or anyone else: 'Who is your Lord?' except that he says: 'God.'" And al-Hasan said the same. [[The report 15374: al-Suyuti extracted this report in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:141, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, attributing it to ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir. It is evident that it is from the tafsir of al-Kalbi, with his chain from Ibn ʿAbbas.]]

15375 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAli ibn Husayn, that he used to practice ʿazl, [[(1) In the printed edition: "he used to say and interpret," which is words without meaning; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. ʿAzl is that a man withdraws his semen from the woman, that is, removes it from her womb when he has intercourse with her, so that she does not conceive.]] and he interpreted this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾. [[The report 15375: al-Suyuti extracted it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:144, and increased its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba.]]

15376 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn ʿUbayda narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, regarding His saying ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾: "The spirits acknowledged before their bodies were created." [[The report 15376: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr narrated it in al-Tamhid (appended to Kitab al-Taqassi: 301) by way of Qasim ibn Asbagh, from Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, from Rawh ibn ʿUbada, from Musa ibn ʿUbayda. Al-Suyuti extracted it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:140 and increased its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba.]]

15377 - Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Zubaydi narrated to me, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nasri, from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim: that a man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, are deeds begun, or has the decree already been decided?" [[In another narration: "or has the decree already passed."]] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God took the descendants of Adam from their loins, then made them testify concerning themselves, then He scattered them in His palm [[His saying: "He scattered them in His palm": He spread them out separated and dispersed. Its origin is from "the striker scattered the arrows," when he shuffled them and struck with them, so they fell dispersed and scattered. This wording has come in the report of Ibn ʿAbbas: "God brought forth the descendants of Adam from his back, and scattered them as the arrow is scattered," which means striking with it and shuffling it in gambling. It has come in al-Tabarani's narration of this report (Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7:186): "then He scattered them in His palms, or His palm."]], then He said: 'These are in Paradise, and these are in the Fire.' So the people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire."

[[The report 15377: Abu Jaʿfar narrated it by four chains: this one, and the following one up to no. 15380. It is a report that the early scholars declared to have a disturbed chain (mudtarib). Its disturbance is from aspects which I will explain later, God willing, at this point.

"Ahmad ibn al-Faraj ibn Sulayman al-Kindi al-Himsi," Abu ʿUtba, known as al-Hijazi. He entered Baghdad more than once, and narrated there from Baqiyya ibn al-Walid and others. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ibn Jarir, al-Husayn ibn Ismaʿil al-Mahamili, and others narrated from him. Ibn Abi Hatim wrote from him and said: "His standing with us is truthfulness." Ibn ʿAdi said: "Muhammad ibn ʿAwf al-Ta'i used to weaken him, yet despite his weakness his hadith was written." Muhammad ibn ʿAwf al-Ta'i said: "al-Hijazi is a liar... there is nothing in his hadith from Baqiyya ibn al-Walid from al-Zubaydi that has a source. He is the most lying of God's creatures in it. They are only hadiths that came to him on the back of a sheet of paper from the book of a hadith-collector, the beginning of which was written: 'Yazid ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated to us, saying: Baqiyya narrated to us,'" and then he attacked him with other things. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: "He errs, and he is well known by his kunya." Nevertheless, this report, which Abu Jaʿfar narrated from him, Abu Jaʿfar narrated after him from Muhammad ibn ʿAwf al-Ta'i and others, so what was said about him does not harm it. He is biographically listed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/67, Tarikh Baghdad 4: 339-341, and he has passed as no. 6899, narrated from Baqiyya ibn al-Walid, but he was not biographically treated there.

"Baqiyya ibn al-Walid al-Himsi" is trustworthy; they spoke about him because of his tadlis (concealing sources). When he states hearing explicitly, his narration is sound, and he has done so in this report, but he did not state it in the following one. He has passed as nos. 153, 5563, 6521, 6899, 9224, and others.

"al-Zubaydi" is Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn ʿAmir al-Zubaydi al-Himsi, trustworthy; the two Sheikhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him. He has passed as nos. 6656, 6899.

"Rashid ibn Saʿd al-Muqri al-Habarani al-Himsi": Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy. Ahmad said: "There is no harm in him." al-Daraqutni said: "He is considered when he does not narrate from one who is abandoned." Ibn Hazm alone deemed him weak. Rashid ibn Saʿd lost his eye on the day of Siffin, and he died in the year 108. He is biographically listed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Saʿd 7/2/162, al-Kabir 2/1/266, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/483, Mizan al-Iʿtidal 1: 331, and Mukhtasar Tarikh Ibn ʿAsakir 5: 289.

From the narration of Rashid ibn Saʿd the disturbance in the chain of the report begins, and in ascribing some of its narrators, and the variation in its wording. These are the chains that have reached me, which I have collected with a note of the place of each chain:

1 - al-Zubaydi, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nasri, from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim = al-Tabari: 15377-15379 / al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/191, 192 / Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, in "Shifa al-ʿAlil" of Ibn al-Qayyim: 10 / Ibn Kathir 3: 588.

2 - al-Zubaydi, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nasri, from Hisham ibn Hakim = al-Ajurri in al-Shariʿa: 172.

3 - Muʿawiya ibn Salih, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, from Hisham ibn Hakim = al-Tabari: 15380.

4 - Muʿawiya ibn Salih, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ)" = Ibn Saʿd 1/1/9 then 7/2/135 = Musnad 4: 186 / al-Mustadrak 1: 31 / Usd al-Ghaba 3: 319 / al-Isaba 4: 179, in the biography of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada.

5 - al-Zubaydi, ... from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, from his father, and Hisham ibn Hakim = al-Isaba 4: 179, without the full chain being clarified, but it is from Rashid ibn Saʿd without doubt.

So the first three chains and the fifth chain have the report from Hisham ibn Hakim or from Qatada al-Nasri. al-Zubaydi differed regarding Rashid ibn Saʿd: once he said, "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, from his father, from Hisham," and once he said, "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, from Hisham," omitting "from his father." As for Muʿawiya ibn Salih, he differed regarding Rashid ibn Saʿd: once he said, "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada from Hisham ibn Hakim," like the second chain of al-Zubaydi, and once he said, "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

Ibn Hajar said: "al-Bukhari found a defect in the hadith, saying that ʿAbd al-Rahman only narrated it from Hisham ibn Hakim. Thus Muʿawiya ibn Salih and others narrated it from Rashid ibn Saʿd. Muʿawiya once said that ʿAbd al-Rahman said 'I heard,' and that is an error. It was narrated by al-Zubaydi from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, from his father, and Hisham ibn Hakim. It has also been said from al-Zubaydi: ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Hisham" (al-Isaba 4: 179).

As for the second disagreement about ascribing some of its narrators, the chain that came in the first and second chains is "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nasri." Then in the fourth chain came "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami," and in the biography of the Companion "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami" it is not mentioned that he is called "al-Nasri." This will become clear in the discussion below concerning the narrators of the chain.

As for the third disagreement, it is in the wording. The wording that Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari narrated here under no. 15377 was narrated in a similar form by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 4/2/191, 192, al-Ajurri in al-Shariʿa: 172, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (Shifa al-ʿAlil: 10), Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7: 186, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 143, and he increased its attribution to al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma wa al-Sifat, all of them from Hisham ibn Hakim.

Al-Haythami said in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid, mentioning this report with its wording, from Hisham ibn Hakim, then said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani. In it is Baqiyya ibn al-Walid, who is weak, and his hadith is improved by many corroborations. The chain of al-Tabarani is good."

As for the second wording: it is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'God, the Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, then took the creation from his back, and said: These are in Paradise and I do not care, and these are in the Fire and I do not care.' A speaker said: 'O Messenger of God, then on what should we act?' He said: 'On the places of destiny.'"

With this wording and similar to it from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Salami the Companion, it was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad 4: 186, Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 1/1/9 then 7/2/135, then Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa al-Taʿdil 2/2/276, then al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1: 31, Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7: 186, al-Isaba 4: 179, Taʿjil al-Manfaʿa: 255, 256, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 144, 145, attributing it to Ibn Saʿd and Ahmad. al-Hakim said in al-Mustadrak: "This is a sound hadith; the two Sheikhs agreed on relying on its narrators all the way to the Companions. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qatada is from the Banu Salama, a Companion. Both of them relied on Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he has no narrator other than Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi. Likewise al-Bukhari relied on the hadith of Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla, and he has no narrator other than Hafs ibn ʿAsim." al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

As for al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid, he said: "Ahmad narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy," meaning the fourth chain that we mentioned, with the second wording.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 5 of 5):

Next, we come to the discussion of ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah)). In the first and second chains he is ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī)), who narrates from his father, from Hishām, the hadith with the first wording. It does not appear from his chain that he was a Companion (ṣaḥābī). If he was a Companion, then he is a Companion narrating from a Companion, from a Companion, which is strange and rare. If what al-Bukhārī said is correct, that the narrator is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from Hishām, and that his saying "from his father" is an addition, then this is a Companion narrating from a Companion. It is possible that ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī)) was a Successor (tābiʿī). However, no one has shown that ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī)) is other than ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Sulamī)), and ((al-Sulamī)) was a Companion, as appears in the text of the fourth chain. Biographies of the Companion ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Sulamī)) are given by Ibn Saʿd (7/2/135), then Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/2/276), who said afterward: ((He narrated from Hishām ibn Ḥakīm; Rāshid ibn Saʿd narrated from him)). Also in al-Istīʿāb (398), Usd al-Ghābah (3:319), Taʿjīl al-Manfaʿah (255), and al-Iṣābah (4:179). None of them mentioned that this al-Sulamī is called al-Naṣrī. This too is strange.

Furthermore, they gave biographies of his father ((Qatādah al-Naṣrī)) in al-Kabīr (4/1/185), where he said: ((He heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm; his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from him)), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (3/2/135), who said the same. As for ((Qatādah al-Sulamī)), neither of the two sources mentions him; rather, his mention appears in the biography of ((Hishām ibn Ḥakīm)) in al-Tahdhīb and al-Iṣābah. This is also strange.

The nisbah ((al-Sulamī)) is vocalized in the manuscripts of Ibn Saʿd and others with a ḍammah on the sīn and a fatḥah on the lām, attributing him to ((Sulaym ibn Manṣūr ibn ʿIkrimah ibn Khaṣafah ibn Qays ʿAylān)). As for al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak, he specified that he is from ((Banū Salamah)) (with a fatḥah on the sīn and a kasrah on the lām), and the nisbah to them is ((al-Salamī)) (with two fatḥahs), and they are from the Anṣār. Whether it is this or that, I do not know how one from this or that group could be ((Naṣrī)). The ((al-Naṣrī)), in my view, is attributed to ((Naṣr ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Bakr ibn Hawāzin ibn Manṣūr ibn ʿIkrimah)), and they are paternal cousins of ((Sulaym ibn Manṣūr)). It is possible that ((ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah)) was from the Banū ((Sulaym ibn Manṣūr)), who joined his paternal cousins ((Naṣr ibn Muʿāwiyah)) and was therefore attributed to them as well. But I have no proof of this, just as I did not find proof for what al-Ḥākim said in al-Mustadrak.

I have gone on at length in explaining this confusion, so that I might pin it down to some degree. And after all of this, the meaning of the hadith is sound, transmitted from a group of Companions through chains that do not contain this confusion. It is an ancient confusion, as the scholars have stated, as I quoted just above.

15378 - Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf al-Ṭāʾī narrated to me, saying: Ḥaywah and Yazīd narrated to us, both saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from al-Zubaydī, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī, from his father, from Hishām ibn Ḥakīm, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

[[The report 15378: "Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf ibn Sufyān al-Ṭāʾī", a teacher of Abū Jaʿfar, a trustworthy memorizer among the narrators from Aḥmad, passed as no. 5445.
"Ḥaywah" is "Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī", a trustworthy jurist and scholar, passed as nos. 2891, 3179. "Yazīd" is "Yazīd ibn Hārūn", one of the memorizers, passed many times. This chain is the same as the earlier report.]]

15379 - [ʿAbd Allāh ibn] Aḥmad ibn Shabawayh narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Zubaydī, saying: Rāshid ibn Saʿd narrated to us, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah narrated to him, that his father narrated to him, that Hishām ibn Ḥakīm narrated to him, that he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned the like of it.

[[The report 15379: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Shabwayh" (written in the printed and manuscript editions as "Shabūyah"), is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-Marwazī", a teacher of Abū Jaʿfar, one of the imams of hadith, passed many times, including nos. 1909, 4612, 4923. In the printed and manuscript editions it read "Ḥadathanī Aḥmad ibn Shabūyah", which is an error without doubt, so I added "ʿAbd Allāh ibn" between the brackets, first because "ʿAbd Allāh" is the teacher of Abū Jaʿfar from whom he narrates, and second because his father "Aḥmad ibn Shabūyah" died in the year 230, and Abū Jaʿfar did not live to narrate from him. "Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm" is "Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Ḥimṣī al-Zubaydī", also called "Isḥāq ibn Zubayriq" or "Ibn Zubayriq", trustworthy, though criticized out of envy. Biographized in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr (1/1/380), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/1/209). "ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Zubaydī al-Ḥimṣī" was mentioned by Ibn Ḥibbān in al-Thiqāt, and al-Dhahabī said: "His uprightness is not known." Biographized in al-Tahdhīb, Ibn Abī Ḥātim (3/1/226), and Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl (2:284). "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim al-Ashʿarī al-Waḥāẓī" was judged trustworthy by Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Dāraqutnī. Biographized in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/2/76). In the manuscript and printed editions it read "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim", which is an error without doubt.]]

15380 - Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah, from Hishām ibn Ḥakīm, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar.

[[The report 15380: "Abū Ṣāliḥ" is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Miṣrī", scribe of al-Layth ibn Saʿd. Trustworthy, though criticized. Passed many times; see no. 186. "Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥimṣī", trustworthy, passed many times; see no. 186, and see after all of this the comment on no. 15377.]]

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: There is disagreement concerning His saying: ﴿Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware"﴾. Al-Suddī said: It is a report from Allah about Himself and His angels: that He, glorified is His praise, said, He and His angels, when the children of Adam acknowledged His lordship, when He said to them: "Am I not your Lord?" And they said: [[In the manuscript: "when it was said to them"]] "Yes" (in the printed edition: "They said, 'Yes'", set as it stands in the verse).

So the interpretation of the statement according to this interpretation is: "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes.'" Then Allah and His angels said: We testify against you by your acknowledgment that Allah is your Lord, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware." The report from him to this effect has been mentioned previously, and the other report transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr from the Prophet (ﷺ) with the like of that. [[See the report of al-Suddī no. 15373, and the report of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: 15354.]]

* *

Others said: That is a report from Allah about the saying of some of the children of Adam to others, when Allah made some of them testify against others. They said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves﴾ is that some of them made others testify by their acknowledgment of that. The report to this effect has also been mentioned from those who said it before.

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two views is what is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), if it is sound, though I do not know it to be sound. This is because the trustworthy narrators on whose memory and precision one relies narrated this hadith from al-Thawrī, and they halted it at ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, and did not raise it, and they did not mention in the hadith this phrase which Aḥmad ibn Abī Ṭayyibah mentioned from him. [[See what has preceded in the comment on no. 15354.]] And if that is not sound from him, then the apparent meaning indicates that it is a report from Allah about the saying of the children of Adam to one another, because He, glorified is His praise, said: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify"﴾. So it is as if it were said: Those who testified against those who acknowledged, when they acknowledged and said, "Yes," said: "We testify against you to what you acknowledged against yourselves, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were of this unaware.'"

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Or you should say, "Only our fathers associated partners with God before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: "We bear witness against you, O you who acknowledge that God is your Lord, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: 'Indeed, we were unaware of this, [we did not know that]; indeed, we did not know it and were heedless of it.'" Or you should say: ﴿Only our fathers associated partners with God before, and we were offspring after them﴾, [meaning] we followed their path. ﴿Will You destroy us﴾ for the associating of partners by those of our fathers who associated, and our following of their path, in ignorance on our part of the truth? And by His words ﴿for what the falsifiers did﴾ He means: for what those who falsified, in their claim of a god other than God, did.

* *

The reciters differed concerning the reading of this. Some of the Meccan and Basran reciters read "أَنْ يَقُولُوا" (an yaqūlū) with the yāʾ, meaning: "We bear witness, lest they say," in the manner of reporting about an absent party.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read ﴿an taqūlū﴾ with the tāʾ, in the manner of address from the witnesses to those witnessed against.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that both are two readings, sound in meaning and agreeing in interpretation, even though their wording differs, because the Arabs do this in reported speech, as God said: ﴿Surely you will make it clear to the people﴾ and ﴿surely they will make it clear﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 187]. We have already explained similar cases earlier, in a way that makes repeating them unnecessary. [[See what has passed in the indexes on Arabic linguistic and grammatical topics and others.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And thus do We detail the signs, that they may perhaps return﴾ (7:174)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as We have detailed for your people, O Muhammad, the verses of this surah, and clarified in them what We did to the nations before your people, [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) above, p. 106, note 5, and the references there. And the explanation of "ayah" (sign) above in the language indexes, under (ayy).]] and what We brought down upon them of punishments because of their disbelief and their associating others in worship with Me, so too do We detail other signs and make them clear to your people, so that they may be restrained and deterred, and turn back to obeying Me, repent of their polytheism and disbelief, and return to faith and to acknowledging My oneness, devoting obedience to Me alone and abandoning the worship of anything other than Me.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off, so Satan pursued him, and he became one of the misguided﴾ (7:175)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And recite," O Muhammad, to your people, "the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs," meaning his news and his story. [[See the explanation of "talā" (to recite) above, 12:215, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "naba'" (report) above, p. 7, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It is said that the signs of God which He gave to the one to whom God gave them were the Greatest Name of God, and it was said they were prophethood.

* *

The exegetes differed concerning him.

Some of them said: He was a man from the Children of Israel. [[See the account of Bal'am ibn Ba'ur in Tarikh al-Tabari, 1:226–228.]]

Those who said this:

15381. Ḥumayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, concerning this verse: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: It is Bal'am.

15382. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, the like of it.

15383. ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, who said: He is Bal'am ibn Abar.

15384. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾. He said: A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Abar.

15385. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Ibn Mahdī, and Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, that he said concerning this verse, and he mentioned the like of it, but he did not say "ibn Abar."

15386. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Abar.

15387. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is Bal'am ibn Bāʿir.

15388. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾ up to ﴿so he became one of the misguided﴾. He is Bal'am ibn Abar.

15389. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, the like of it, except that he said "Ibn Abur," with a ḍammah on the "bāʾ."

15390. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants, called Bal'am.

15391. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: Bal'ām ibn Bāʿir, from the Children of Israel.

15392. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Abu Saʿd narrated to us, who said: I heard Mujāhid say, and he mentioned the like of it.

15393. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kathīr informed me that he heard Mujāhid say, and he mentioned the like of it.

15394. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said concerning the one whom ﴿We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾: He is Bal'ām.

15395. And Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said: He is Bal'am.

15396. ... He said: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said: He is Bal'am.

15397. Ḥumayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: He is Bal'ām.

15398. al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Mujāhid, who said: He is Bal'am.

15399. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Mughīrah, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is Bal'am. =

And the Thaqīf said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[This sentence, "And the Thaqīf said…", was omitted from the printed edition, but it is present in the manuscript. I do not know whether it is the words of Abu Ja'far, the words of Ibn ʿAbbās, or the words of one of the narrators of Ibn ʿAbbās's report. The more likely view is that it is the statement of one of the transmitters of the report.]]

* *

Others said: This Bal'am was from the people of Yemen.

Those who said this:

15400. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man called Bal'am, from the people of Yemen.

* *

Others said: He was from the Canaanites.

Those who said this:

15401. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants, called Bal'am.

* *

Others said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

Those who said this:

15402. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Ghuṭayf ibn Abi Sufyān, from Yaʿqūb and Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said concerning this verse: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[(2) The report 15402: Saʿīd ibn al-Sāʾib ibn Yasār al-Thaqafī al-Ṭāʾifī; Saʿīd ibn Abi Ḥafṣ, a trustworthy transmitter; some of them counted him among the Abdāl (the holy substitutes), and his tears never dried. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 2/1/439, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 2/1/30. Ghuṭayf ibn Abi Sufyān al-Ṭāʾifī, or Ghuḍayf, was a trustworthy Successor.
