He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb (under Ghuḍayf), al-Kabīr 4/1/106 (Ghuṭayf), and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 3/2/55 (Ghuḍayf). In the printed edition it was "Ghuḍayf," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī was a trustworthy Successor, biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/2/84, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 4/1/454.]]

15403. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah informed us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said: He is your companion, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[The report 15403: Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-ʿĀmirī al-Ṭāʾifī, passed as 2858, 11527, 11529. Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī passed in the previous report. This is why ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said "he is your companion," because he was a Thaqafī like him.]]

15404. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, both saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, the like of it.

15405. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abi Thābit, from a man, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr: ﴿But he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15406. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, who said: I heard Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd say: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr say concerning this verse: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is your companion, meaning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15407. ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from a man, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15408. ... He said: Yazīd narrated to us, from Sharīk, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Faḍālah, or Ibn Faḍālah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: He is Umayyah.

15409. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, who said: They discussed in the Great Mosque of Damascus this verse: ﴿but he sloughed them off﴾. Some of them said: It was revealed concerning Bal'am ibn Bāʿūrāʾ. Others said: It was revealed concerning the monk. [[The "monk" is Abu ʿĀmir the monk, ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Ṣayfī of Mālik ibn al-Nuʿmān. In the pre-Islamic period he was called "the monk," but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) named him "Abu ʿĀmir the Corrupt." His account is well known in the biographical literature.]] Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ came out to them, and they said: Concerning whom was this revealed? He said: It was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt al-Thaqafī.

15410. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. Qatādah said: He is in doubt about it; some of them say: Bal'am, and some say: Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the signs which he had been given, of which He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿We gave him Our signs﴾.

Some of them said: They were the Greatest Name of God.

Those who said this:

15411. Mūsā narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When the forty years had ended, which are the years of which God said: ﴿It is forbidden to them for forty years﴾ [Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 26], God sent Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet, and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants, and they pledged allegiance to him and affirmed him. A man from the Children of Israel called "Bal'am" set out, who was a scholar who knew the hidden Greatest Name, and he disbelieved and came to the tyrants, and said: Do not fear the Children of Israel, for when you go out to fight them I will invoke a curse upon them, and they will perish! He had among them what he wished of the world, except that from the greatness of their women he could not approach them, [[In the printed edition it reads "the women, their greatness," differing from the manuscript, and this corrupts it. What is meant is the great size of the women of the tyrants, who are described as having bodies whose measure none knows but God.]] so he would have intercourse with a she-ass of his. [[al-Atān: the female donkey.]] And he is the one of whom God says: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾, that is: he gained insight, [[In the printed edition: "he was disengaged"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript. As for in the history: "he saw," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] but he sloughed them off, up to His saying: ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾. [[The report 15411: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his history, 1:227–228, and it will come in full as 15423.]]

15412. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾. He said: He is a man called "Bal'am," who knew the Greatest Name of God.

15413. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He would not ask God for anything except that He gave it to him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the signs which he had been given were a book from the books of God.

Those who said this:

15414. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Ḥamzah, from Jābir, from Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Among the Children of Israel there was Bal'am ibn Bāʿir, who was given a book. [[The report 15414: It will come at length as 15432.]]

Others said: Rather, he had been given prophethood.

Those who said this:

15415. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Abu Saʿd narrated to us, from another — al-Ḥārith said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: meaning from someone other than himself — from Mujāhid, who said: He was a prophet among the Children of Israel, meaning Bal'am, who was given prophethood, but his people bribed him to keep silent, so he did, and he left them as they were.

15416. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, that he was asked about the verse: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾, and he related from Sayyār that he was a man called "Bal'ām," who had been given prophethood, and whose supplication was answered. [[The report 15416: It will come in full as 15420.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to recite to his people the report of a man whom God had given His proofs and evidences, which are "the signs."

It has already been shown, in what has passed, that the meaning of "the signs" is proofs and indications, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "ayah" in the language indexes above, under (ayy).]]

It is permissible that the one to whom God gave this was Bal'am, and it is permissible that it was Umayyah. Likewise, if "the signs" means the proof which is part of the books of God that He sent down to one of His prophets, then the one whom God mentions in this verse, and whom He means by it, learned it; so it is permissible that the one who was given it was Bal'am, and it is permissible that it was Umayyah, for Umayyah had, it is said, read from the books of the People of the Book.

But if it means a book which God sent down to the one whom He commanded the Prophet of God (ﷺ) to recite to his people, or the Greatest Name, or prophethood, then it is not permissible that Umayyah is meant by it, for the community does not differ that he had not been given any of these things, and no report indicates which of these is meant, and which of the two men is meant, in a way that would establish proof, nor does reason offer any indication as to which of them is meant by which. [[(1) Context: "and no report indicates which of these is meant, and which of the two men is meant… nor does reason offer any indication as to which of these is meant by which." See the explanation of "ayy dhālika min ayy" above, p. 182, note 1, and the references there. In the printed edition and manuscript it read "on that the meaning by it is from which," and the correct reading is what I have adopted.]] So the correct position is to say about it what God said, and to affirm the outward sense of the revelation as it came from God.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But he sloughed them off﴾, it means: he went out from the signs which God had given him, and disowned them.

The exegetes said something similar to this.

Those who said this:

15417. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When Mūsā (peace be upon him) arrived… [[In the manuscript there is a blank after "peace be upon him," and in the margin the letter (ṭ) indicating an error.]] — meaning the tyrants — and those with him, Bal'am, meaning him, was approached by his paternal cousins and his people, who said: Mūsā is a fierce man, and with him are many soldiers, and if he prevails over us he will destroy us. Invoke God to turn Mūsā and those with him away from us. He said: If I invoke God to turn Mūsā and those with him away, I will lose my world and my hereafter! They kept at him until he invoked a curse against them, and God stripped him of what he had been upon. That is His saying: ﴿But he sloughed them off, so Satan pursued him, and he became one of the misguided﴾. [[In the printed edition the second "he came to him" is omitted.]]

15418. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: God had given him His signs, but he abandoned them.

15419. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿But he sloughed them off﴾, he said: knowledge was taken from him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, it means: he made him a follower of his own, who obeyed his command in disobedience to God, and opposed the command of his Lord in disobedience to Satan and in obedience to the All-Merciful.

* *

"And His words ﴿so he became of those who go astray﴾ mean: he became among those who perish, because of his straying and his opposition to his Lord's command, and his obedience to Satan. [[See the explanation of "ghawa" (to go astray) in what has preceded: 5:416 / 12:333 / 13:114.]]"

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And thus do We detail the signs, that they may perhaps return﴾ (7:174)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as We have detailed for your people, O Muhammad, the verses of this surah, and clarified in them what We did to the nations before your people, [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) above, p. 106, note 5, and the references there. And the explanation of "ayah" (sign) above in the language indexes, under (ayy).]] and what We brought down upon them of punishments because of their disbelief and their associating others in worship with Me, so too do We detail other signs and make them clear to your people, so that they may be restrained and deterred, and turn back to obeying Me, repent of their polytheism and disbelief, and return to faith and to acknowledging My oneness, devoting obedience to Me alone and abandoning the worship of anything other than Me.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off, so Satan pursued him, and he became one of the misguided﴾ (7:175)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And recite," O Muhammad, to your people, "the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs," meaning his news and his story. [[See the explanation of "talā" (to recite) above, 12:215, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "naba'" (report) above, p. 7, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It is said that the signs of God which He gave to the one to whom God gave them were the Greatest Name of God, and it was said they were prophethood.

* *

The exegetes differed concerning him.

Some of them said: He was a man from the Children of Israel. [[See the account of Bal'am ibn Ba'ur in Tarikh al-Tabari, 1:226–228.]]

Those who said this:

15381. Ḥumayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, concerning this verse: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: It is Bal'am.

15382. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, the like of it.

15383. ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, who said: He is Bal'am ibn Abar.

15384. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾. He said: A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Abar.

15385. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Ibn Mahdī, and Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from ʿAbdullāh, that he said concerning this verse, and he mentioned the like of it, but he did not say "ibn Abar."

15386. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am ibn Abar.

15387. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is Bal'am ibn Bāʿir.

15388. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾ up to ﴿so he became one of the misguided﴾. He is Bal'am ibn Abar.

15389. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Manṣūr, from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, from Ibn Masʿūd, the like of it, except that he said "Ibn Abur," with a ḍammah on the "bāʾ."

15390. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants, called Bal'am.

15391. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: Bal'ām ibn Bāʿir, from the Children of Israel.

15392. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Abu Saʿd narrated to us, who said: I heard Mujāhid say, and he mentioned the like of it.

15393. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kathīr informed me that he heard Mujāhid say, and he mentioned the like of it.

15394. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said concerning the one whom ﴿We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾: He is Bal'ām.

15395. And Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said: He is Bal'am.

15396. ... He said: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, who said: He is Bal'am.

15397. Ḥumayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: He is Bal'ām.

15398. al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Mujāhid, who said: He is Bal'am.

15399. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Mughīrah, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is Bal'am. =

And the Thaqīf said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[This sentence, "And the Thaqīf said…", was omitted from the printed edition, but it is present in the manuscript. I do not know whether it is the words of Abu Ja'far, the words of Ibn ʿAbbās, or the words of one of the narrators of Ibn ʿAbbās's report. The more likely view is that it is the statement of one of the transmitters of the report.]]

* *

Others said: This Bal'am was from the people of Yemen.

Those who said this:

15400. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man called Bal'am, from the people of Yemen.

* *

Others said: He was from the Canaanites.

Those who said this:

15401. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants, called Bal'am.

* *

Others said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

Those who said this:

15402. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Ghuṭayf ibn Abi Sufyān, from Yaʿqūb and Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said concerning this verse: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[(2) The report 15402: Saʿīd ibn al-Sāʾib ibn Yasār al-Thaqafī al-Ṭāʾifī; Saʿīd ibn Abi Ḥafṣ, a trustworthy transmitter; some of them counted him among the Abdāl (the holy substitutes), and his tears never dried. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 2/1/439, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 2/1/30. Ghuṭayf ibn Abi Sufyān al-Ṭāʾifī, or Ghuḍayf, was a trustworthy Successor. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb (under Ghuḍayf), al-Kabīr 4/1/106 (Ghuṭayf), and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 3/2/55 (Ghuḍayf). In the printed edition it was "Ghuḍayf," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī was a trustworthy Successor, biographically recorded in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/2/84, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim 4/1/454.]]

15403. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdī narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah informed us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said: He is your companion, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. [[The report 15403: Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-ʿĀmirī al-Ṭāʾifī, passed as 2858, 11527, 11529. Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī passed in the previous report. This is why ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said "he is your companion," because he was a Thaqafī like him.]]

15404. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, both saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, the like of it.

15405. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abi Thābit, from a man, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr: ﴿But he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15406. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, who said: I heard Nāfiʿ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd say: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr say concerning this verse: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is your companion, meaning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15407. ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from a man, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

15408. ... He said: Yazīd narrated to us, from Sharīk, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Faḍālah, or Ibn Faḍālah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: He is Umayyah.

15409. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, who said: They discussed in the Great Mosque of Damascus this verse: ﴿but he sloughed them off﴾. Some of them said: It was revealed concerning Bal'am ibn Bāʿūrāʾ. Others said: It was revealed concerning the monk. [[The "monk" is Abu ʿĀmir the monk, ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Ṣayfī of Mālik ibn al-Nuʿmān. In the pre-Islamic period he was called "the monk," but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) named him "Abu ʿĀmir the Corrupt." His account is well known in the biographical literature.]] Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ came out to them, and they said: Concerning whom was this revealed? He said: It was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt al-Thaqafī.

15410. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī: ﴿the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt. Qatādah said: He is in doubt about it; some of them say: Bal'am, and some say: Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the signs which he had been given, of which He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿We gave him Our signs﴾.

Some of them said: They were the Greatest Name of God.

Those who said this:

15411. Mūsā narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When the forty years had ended, which are the years of which God said: ﴿It is forbidden to them for forty years﴾ [Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 26], God sent Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet, and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants, and they pledged allegiance to him and affirmed him. A man from the Children of Israel called "Bal'am" set out, who was a scholar who knew the hidden Greatest Name, and he disbelieved and came to the tyrants, and said: Do not fear the Children of Israel, for when you go out to fight them I will invoke a curse upon them, and they will perish! He had among them what he wished of the world, except that from the greatness of their women he could not approach them, [[In the printed edition it reads "the women, their greatness," differing from the manuscript, and this corrupts it. What is meant is the great size of the women of the tyrants, who are described as having bodies whose measure none knows but God.]] so he would have intercourse with a she-ass of his. [[al-Atān: the female donkey.]] And he is the one of whom God says: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾, that is: he gained insight, [[In the printed edition: "he was disengaged"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript. As for in the history: "he saw," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] but he sloughed them off, up to His saying: ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾. [[The report 15411: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his history, 1:227–228, and it will come in full as 15423.]]

15412. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾. He said: He is a man called "Bal'am," who knew the Greatest Name of God.

15413. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾. He said: He would not ask God for anything except that He gave it to him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the signs which he had been given were a book from the books of God.

Those who said this:

15414. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Ḥamzah, from Jābir, from Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Among the Children of Israel there was Bal'am ibn Bāʿir, who was given a book. [[The report 15414: It will come at length as 15432.]]

Others said: Rather, he had been given prophethood.

Those who said this:

15415. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Abu Saʿd narrated to us, from another — al-Ḥārith said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: meaning from someone other than himself — from Mujāhid, who said: He was a prophet among the Children of Israel, meaning Bal'am, who was given prophethood, but his people bribed him to keep silent, so he did, and he left them as they were.

15416. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, that he was asked about the verse: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he sloughed them off﴾, and he related from Sayyār that he was a man called "Bal'ām," who had been given prophethood, and whose supplication was answered. [[The report 15416: It will come in full as 15420.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to recite to his people the report of a man whom God had given His proofs and evidences, which are "the signs."

It has already been shown, in what has passed, that the meaning of "the signs" is proofs and indications, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "ayah" in the language indexes above, under (ayy).]]

It is permissible that the one to whom God gave this was Bal'am, and it is permissible that it was Umayyah. Likewise, if "the signs" means the proof which is part of the books of God that He sent down to one of His prophets, then the one whom God mentions in this verse, and whom He means by it, learned it; so it is permissible that the one who was given it was Bal'am, and it is permissible that it was Umayyah, for Umayyah had, it is said, read from the books of the People of the Book.

But if it means a book which God sent down to the one whom He commanded the Prophet of God (ﷺ) to recite to his people, or the Greatest Name, or prophethood, then it is not permissible that Umayyah is meant by it, for the community does not differ that he had not been given any of these things, and no report indicates which of these is meant, and which of the two men is meant, in a way that would establish proof, nor does reason offer any indication as to which of them is meant by which. [[(1) Context: "and no report indicates which of these is meant, and which of the two men is meant… nor does reason offer any indication as to which of these is meant by which." See the explanation of "ayy dhālika min ayy" above, p. 182, note 1, and the references there. In the printed edition and manuscript it read "on that the meaning by it is from which," and the correct reading is what I have adopted.]] So the correct position is to say about it what God said, and to affirm the outward sense of the revelation as it came from God.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But he sloughed them off﴾, it means: he went out from the signs which God had given him, and disowned them.

The exegetes said something similar to this.

Those who said this:

15417. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When Mūsā (peace be upon him) arrived… [[In the manuscript there is a blank after "peace be upon him," and in the margin the letter (ṭ) indicating an error.]] — meaning the tyrants — and those with him, Bal'am, meaning him, was approached by his paternal cousins and his people, who said: Mūsā is a fierce man, and with him are many soldiers, and if he prevails over us he will destroy us. Invoke God to turn Mūsā and those with him away from us. He said: If I invoke God to turn Mūsā and those with him away, I will lose my world and my hereafter! They kept at him until he invoked a curse against them, and God stripped him of what he had been upon. That is His saying: ﴿But he sloughed them off, so Satan pursued him, and he became one of the misguided﴾. [[In the printed edition the second "he came to him" is omitted.]]

15418. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: God had given him His signs, but he abandoned them.

15419. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿But he sloughed them off﴾, he said: knowledge was taken from him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, it means: he made him a follower of his own, who obeyed his command in disobedience to God, and opposed the command of his Lord in disobedience to Satan and in obedience to the All-Merciful.

* *

"And His words ﴿so he became of those who go astray﴾ mean: he became among those who perish, because of his straying and his opposition to his Lord's command, and his obedience to Satan. [[See the explanation of "ghawa" (to go astray) in what has preceded: 5:416 / 12:333 / 13:114.]]"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 176 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: And had We willed, We would have elevated this one to whom We gave Our verses, by means of Our verses that We gave him. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾, meaning: he settled into the life of this world on earth and inclined toward it, and preferred its pleasures and desires over the Hereafter. ﴿And followed his own desire﴾, and abandoned the obedience of God and opposed His command.

* * *

The account of this man whose story God describes in this verse, though the scholars differ regarding his story and his affair, is as follows:

15420 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father: that he was asked about the verse: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our verses, but he withdrew from them﴾. He related from Sayyar that he was a man called Bal'am, who had been given prophethood and whose supplications were answered [[See the previous report no. 15416.]]. He said: Moses came with the Children of Israel, intending the land in which Bal'am was (or he said: al-Sham). He said: The people were struck with great terror of him. He said: They came to Bal'am and said: Invoke God against this man and his army! He said: Until I consult my Lord (or until I consult [[The second reading "uw'amir" with the hamza is the eloquent form; the first, "uwamir" with the waw without hamza, is not eloquent but occurs in this report. See the following note.]]). He said: So he consulted (about the supplication against them), and it was said to him: Do not invoke against them, for they are My servants, and their prophet is among them! He said: So he said to his people: I have consulted my Lord about invoking against them, and I have been forbidden. He said: They presented him with a gift, and he accepted it. Then they returned to him and said: Invoke against them! He said: Until I consult! So he consulted, but nothing was returned to him. [[The editor has garbled this sentence with additions, alterations and omissions. The manuscript gives "uwamir" and "wamar" with waw, as elsewhere. As for his saying "lam yahur ilayhi shay'", it means nothing returned to him: "haara ilayhi yahuru hawran" means he returned to it, whence "hawara" (to converse) and the expressions "ahara 'alayhi jawabuhu", "ahrtu lahu jawaban", and "ma ahara bi-kalimah".]] He said: So he said: I have consulted, but nothing has been returned to me! They said: If your Lord disliked your invoking against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time. He said: So he began to invoke against them, but whenever he sought to invoke, what came to his tongue was supplication against his own people; and when he wished to invoke that victory be granted to his people, he invoked that victory be granted to Moses and his army (or something like that, God willing). He said: They said: We see you invoking only against us! He said: Nothing comes to my tongue but this, and if I invoked against him it would not be answered for me. But I will direct you to a matter in which their destruction may lie: God hates fornication, and if they fall into fornication they will perish, and I hope God will destroy them. So bring out the women, and let them meet them, for they are travelling people, and perhaps they will commit fornication and perish. He said: They did so, and brought out the women to meet them. [[In the printed edition: "li-tastaqbilahum", with the fa' and nun dropped; the manuscript reads "tastaqbilahum".]] He said: The king had a daughter, and he described her greatness, which only God knows! He said: Her father, or Bal'am, said: Do not let yourself be taken except by Moses! He said: And they fell into fornication. He said: The chief of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her and sought her for himself. He said: She said: I will not yield myself except to Moses! He said: He said: My rank is such and such, and my condition is such and such! He said: She sent to her father asking his advice, and he said to her: Yield to him! [[In the printed edition: "makkinih", differing from the manuscript.]] He said: Then a man of the sons of Aaron came with a spear and thrust through both of them. He said: God strengthened him with power, and he skewered them together and raised them on his spear. [[The manuscript omits "wa-rafa'ahuma"; the printed edition and Ibn Kathir have it, which is correct.]] He said: The people saw them (or as he narrated). He said: God sent the plague upon them. He said: Seventy thousand of them died. He said: Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar told me that Bal'am rode his she-donkey until he came to al-Fulul (or he said: a path between al-Fulul [[In the printed edition and Ibn Kathir: "al-Mu'lawla" (or "tariqan min al-Mu'lawla"), which has no meaning. The manuscript has "al-'Ulul" and "bayna al-'Ulul"; I have corrected the reading as given, because when Moses' army was struck by the punishment and seventy thousand of them perished, those who remained became "fulul" (fugitives). This is what I prefer.]]), and he began striking her, and she would not advance. He said: She stood against him and said: Why do you strike me? Do you not see what is before you! He said: Behold, Satan was before him. He said: So he dismounted and prostrated to him. God said: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our verses, but he withdrew from them, so Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾. He said: Sayyar related this to me, and I do not know whether something from the report of someone else has entered into it. [[Report 15420: al-Mu'tamir is al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, the well-known imam, mentioned many times before. His father is Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, known as al-Taymi, whose kunya is Abu al-Mu'tamir, mentioned many times before. The Sayyar from whom he narrated is Sayyar ibn Salamah, Abu al-Minhal al-Riyahi, the well-known reliable narrator, mentioned under no. 5478. This report is related by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 3:595, 596, and by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 3:147, in abridged form.]]

15421 - Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: And a report reached me from a man of the People of the Book who related: that Moses asked God to seal him (i.e., make him unable to repent) and to make him one of the people of the Fire. He said: God did so. He said: It was reported to me that Moses killed him afterwards.

15422 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Salim Abi al-Nadr, that he related: that when Moses halted in the land of the Canaanites in the land of al-Sham [and Bal'am was in Ba'ilah, a village of the villages of al-Balqa'. When Moses descended with the Children of Israel at that place] [[The words in parentheses are from Tarikh al-Tabari.]], the people of Bal'am came to Bal'am and said to him: O Bal'am, this is Moses son of 'Imran with the Children of Israel; he has come to drive us from our lands and kill us, and the Children of Israel will inhabit it and settle in it; we are your people, and we have no dwelling place, and you are a man whose supplication is answered, so go out and invoke God against them! [[The printed edition has "wa-ad'u" with waw; the manuscript and the Tarikh read as given.]] He said: Woe to you! The Prophet of God is with him, with the angels and the believers; how can I go to invoke against them, when I know what I know of God!? They said: We have no dwelling place! They kept at him, softening him and humbling themselves before him, until they tempted him and he was tempted. He mounted his she-donkey heading toward the mountain overlooking the army of the Children of Israel, which is Mount Husban. [[The printed edition has "Hassan"; the manuscript has it undotted, and I have followed the form found in the Tarikh, which vocalizes it there; I found no mention of it in the geographical dictionaries.]] When she had gone not far, she knelt down with him, so he dismounted and struck her until she was exhausted, then she stood and he mounted her, but she did not go far before she knelt again with him. He did the same to her, she stood and he mounted, but she did not go far before she knelt with him. He struck her until she was exhausted, and God permitted her, and she spoke to him as a proof against him, saying: Woe to you, O Bal'am! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me turning me from this direction? Are you going to the Prophet of God and the believers to invoke against them! He did not desist from striking her, so God released her when he did that to her. He said: She went on until she brought him up over the top of Mount Husban above the army of Moses and the Children of Israel. He began invoking against them, but he invoked against them nothing except that his tongue was turned to his own people, and he invoked for his people nothing good except that his tongue was turned to the Children of Israel. He said: His people said to him: Do you know, O Bal'am, what you are doing? You are invoking for them, and invoking against us! He said: This is what I cannot control; this is a thing God has overcome. He said: And his tongue hung out and fell upon his chest [[To hang out the tongue means to come out of the mouth, become slack, and fall upon the chin like a dog's tongue. In another report about Bal'am: "God cursed him, and his tongue hung out, so its tip fell upon his chest, and it remained so."]]. He said to them: Now the world and the Hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but cunning and trickery. I will scheme against you and devise: beautify the women, give them merchandise, then send them to the army to sell it there, and command them that no woman refuse herself to a man who desires her, for if one of them commits fornication, you will be relieved of them! They did so; when the women entered the army, a woman of the Canaanites named "Kasbi daughter of Sur", the chief of her people, passed by a man of the great men of the Children of Israel, [[In Tarikh: "the chief of her people and of her father's kin, those of them who were in Midian; he was their leader, passing by a man ..."]] and he was Zimri ibn Shalum, chief of the tribe of Simeon son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham. He went to her, took her hand when her beauty pleased him, and brought her until he stood with her before Moses, peace be upon him, and said: I suppose you will say that she is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, she is forbidden to you; do not approach her! He said: By God, we will not obey you in this! [[The printed edition has "la uti'uka"; the manuscript and Tarikh read as given.]] So he entered with her into his tent and lay with her. God sent the plague among the Children of Israel. Phinehas ibn al-'Ayzar ibn Aaron, the companion of Moses' affair, was a man given stature in creation and strength in seizing, and he had been absent when Zimri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel, [[In the manuscript and Tarikh: "yahus" with the unpointed ha', from the saying "you left so-and-so raiding the tribe of so-and-so", meaning moving among them, seeking among them and trampling them. And "the wolf raids the sheep", moving through them and scattering them. In the printed edition: "yajus" with jim.]] and he was informed of the matter, so he took his spear. It was entirely of iron. Then he entered upon them in the tent while they were lying together, [[In Tarikh: "upon them, the tent"]] and he pierced them both with his spear, then he went out carrying them both aloft toward the sky, the spear grasped in his forearm, leaning with his elbow on his side, and supporting the spear against his jaws [[In Tarikh and the manuscript: "his beard"; the printed edition's reading is correct, as the later mention of the Children of Israel giving the "lihan" (jaws) of Phinehas' descendants shows.]] = and he was the eldest son of al-'Ayzar, and he began saying: O God, thus do We deal with whoever disobeys You! The plague was lifted, and those who died of the plague among the Children of Israel were counted, from the time Zimri struck the woman until Phinehas killed him, and they were found to have lost seventy thousand [[Another account, from the one who minimized, says: twenty thousand]] in one hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel give the sons of Phinehas ibn al-'Ayzar ibn Aaron from every sacrifice they slaughter the qibah, the forearm, and the jaws [[In the printed edition: "al-fushshah"; I have followed the manuscript and Tarikh. "Al-qibah" (with kasra on the qaf and fatha on the ba' lightly) is from the stomach, and "al-hafth" (fatha then kasra) is the stomach with folds; the other "qibah" lies beside it and has no folds.]] because he leaned with the spear on his side, took it with his forearm, and supported it against his jaws = and the firstborn of all their wealth and their persons, because he was the firstborn of al-'Ayzar. Concerning Bal'am ibn Ba'ura, God revealed to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our verses, but he withdrew from them﴾, meaning Bal'am, ﴿so Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾. [[Report 15422: related by Ibn Jarir in his Tarikh, 1:226, 227.]]

15423 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: A man of the Children of Israel called Bal'am set out and came to the tyrants and said: Do not fear the Children of Israel; when you go out to fight them, I will invoke against them and they will perish [[The words "fa-yuhlikun" (and they will perish) are missing from the manuscript and the printed edition, but are present in report 15411 above and in Tarikh.]]. Yusha' went out to fight the tyrants among the people, and Bal'am went out with the tyrants on his she-ass, wanting to curse the Children of Israel. Whenever he wished to invoke against the Children of Israel, he invoked against the tyrants, and the tyrants said: You are only invoking against us! He would say: I only intended the Children of Israel. When he reached the gate of the city, an angel seized the tail of the she-ass and held her back; he kept urging her, but she did not move. When he struck her repeatedly, she spoke and said: You have intercourse with me by night and ride me by day? Woe to you! Had I been able to go out, I would have gone out, but this angel is holding me back. And concerning Bal'am God says: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our verses﴾ .. the verse. [[Report 15423: passed as no. 15411, and it is in Tarikh, 1:227, 228.]]

15424 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: a man who heard 'Ikrimah narrated to me, saying: A woman of them said: Show me Moses, and I will tempt him! He said: So she perfumed herself, and passed by a man who resembled Moses, and she lay with him. Then Ibn Harun was brought the news, so he took a sword and thrust it into his male organ until he pulled it out, and pulled it out from her private part [[In the printed edition, "wa-akhrajahu" (and pulled it out) is omitted, though it is in the manuscript. Even so, I am uncertain about the whole phrase. Had it said "from her rear", the sense would be somewhat more sound and the image somewhat clearer.]]; then he raised them both until the people saw them, and he knew that it was not Moses. So the family of Aaron was preferred in the offering over the family of Moses by the shoulder-blade, the upper arm and the thigh [[The printed edition has "bi-akt[af] wa-al-'adud", and the manuscript "bi-al-kitab"; the likely correct reading is "al-katd", the junction of the shoulder blades. God knows which is right.]]. He said: He is the one to whom We gave Our verses, but he withdrew from them, meaning Bal'am.

* * *

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: We would have elevated him by his knowledge of them.

Those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 176 (part 2 of 2):

15425 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾: He would have been raised by Allah, the Exalted, through his knowledge.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: We would have removed from him the state into which he fell of disbelieving in Allah through Our signs.
Those who said this:
15426 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾: We would have repelled it from him. [[In the printed edition: "lraf'anā 'anhu bihā" (we would have raised from him thereby). I do not know where that came from; I have kept what is in the manuscript. And "lidafa'nā" is with a dal.]]
15427 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾: We would have repelled it from him. [[In the printed edition: "lar'afanā 'anhu" (we would have raised from him). I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations concerning this is to say: Allah has made the statement general by His saying ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾, that if He had willed, He would have raised him by His signs which He had given him. "Raising" encompasses many meanings: among them, raising in rank with Him; among them, raising in the honour and nobility of this world; and among them, raising in fine remembrance and lofty praise. It is permissible that Allah meant all of that: that if He had willed, He would have raised him, granting him all of it, by enabling him to act upon His signs which He had given him. Since that is permissible, the correct view is that none of it be restricted, since there is no indication of its specificity from any report or from reason. As for His saying ﴿thereby﴾, Ibn Zayd said regarding it what we have said.
15428 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾: "by those signs." As for His saying ﴿but he inclined toward the earth﴾, the people of interpretation said regarding it something similar to what we have said.
Those who said this:
15429 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿but he inclined toward the earth﴾, meaning: he settled toward the earth.
15430 - ... He said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿but he inclined toward the earth﴾, he said: he leaned toward the earth.
15431 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "akhlada": he dwelt.
15432 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the Children of Israel there was Balam ibn Ba'ur, who was given a Scripture, but he inclined toward the desires, pleasures and wealth of the earth, and he did not benefit from what the Scripture brought. [[The report: 15432 - It has passed in abridged form under no. 15414.]]
15433 - Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire﴾: As for ﴿inclined toward the earth﴾: he followed the world and settled in it. Abu Ja'far said: The original sense of "al-ikhlad" in the speech of the Arabs is: delay and remaining. It is said of it: "akhlada fulan bil-makan" (so-and-so remained at the place) if he stayed in it; and "akhlada nafsahu ila al-makan" (he made himself incline to the place) if he came to it from another place. [[This last explanation you will not find in any dictionary of the language, so verify it.]] From the same root is the verse of Zuhayr:
"To whom do these abodes belong, which you have passed by at al-Fadfad, like writing on the stone-bed of the watercourse that endures?" [[His Diwan: 268, and al-Lisan (kh-l-d), the opening line of his ode concerning Sinan ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri. In the printed edition it read "ghashitaha bil-gharqad" (the fadfad is a place with roughness and elevation, or it is level land), and "al-wahy" means writing. And his saying "hajar al-masil" (the stone-bed of the watercourse) because it is the hardest of stones, so writing on it lasts longer, and the flood strikes it because of its endurance, so it takes from it, and the writing fades. He likened the traces of the abodes to the remaining writing on a rock that the flood visits, which wipes away the freshness of what was written on it.]]
meaning: the one who remains. From the same is the saying of Malik ibn Nuwayra:
"Among the sons of a tribe of the tribes of Malik and Amr ibn Yarbu', who remained and so dwelt [akhladu]." [[Al-Asmaiyyat: 323, from his ode composed on the day of Mukhattat, and before it, which is the beginning of the poem: "Unless I have met on the day of Mukhattat, then the riders have informed of what I was trying to ..."; "He came to me with the men of good whom I met, the steadfast, and a company around him supporting..."; "They called out to Ammar when they turned aside, and met Quraysh and informed them, then they went to their aid."]]
* *
Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say that the meaning of His saying "akhlada" is: he clung, lagged and delayed. And "al-mukhlad" also refers to one whose white hair comes late among men; and among animals, it is one whose incisors remain until its quadrangular teeth emerge. [[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda 1: 233 / then Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 399.]]
* *
As for His saying ﴿and followed his desire﴾, Ibn Zayd said in its interpretation [[In the printed edition: "Kana Ibn Zayd qala..." which is very poor and did not read the manuscript well.]] the following:
15434 - Yunus narrated to me, with it, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and followed his desire﴾: "His desire was with the people."
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾
Abu Ja'far said: Allah, His remembrance be exalted, says: So the example of this one to whom We gave Our signs but who withdrew from them is like the dog that pants, whether you chase it or leave it.
* *
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the cause for which Allah made his example like the example of the dog.
Some of them said: He likened him to it in panting, because of his abandonment of acting upon the Book of Allah and His signs which He had given him, and his turning away from the admonitions of Allah, which is the turning away of one whom Allah has not given any of that. So He, may His praise be exalted, said about him: since his case was equal, whether he was admonished by the signs of Allah which He gave him or not admonished, in that he does not heed them and does not abandon disbelief in Him, so his example is like the example of the dog whose case is equal in its panting, whether it is chased or not chased, since it never abandons panting in any state.
Those who said this:
15435 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants﴾, he said: You chase him away; he is the example of one who reads the Book and does not act by it.
15436 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants﴾, he said: You chase him with your mount and your foot, "he pants." He said: He is like the one who reads the Book and does not act by what is in it. Ibn Jurayj said: The dog is one whose heart is cut off, having no heart; if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. He said: He is like one who abandons guidance, having no heart; rather his heart is cut off. [[The word "munqati'" was dropped from the manuscript, and it is in all other sources as in the printed edition.]]
15437 - Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from some of them: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾: that is the disbeliever; he is astray whether you admonish him or do not admonish him. [[The report: 15437 - "Ibn Abd al-A'la" is Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la. "Ibn Thawr" is Muhammad ibn Thawr; in the printed edition and the manuscript it read "Ibn Tawba", which is an undoubted error, rather this is an abridgment of the chain that has passed many times, ending with no. 15410; and it seems he means by "from some of them": al-Kalbi, and that is why he disliked it.]]
15438 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog﴾: if wisdom is carried to him, he does not carry it; and if he is left, he does not gain guidance to good; like the dog, if it is lying down it pants, and if it is chased it pants.
15439 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah gave him His signs, but he left them, so Allah made his example like the example of the dog: "if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants."
15440 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him﴾, the verse: This is a parable Allah struck for one to whom guidance was presented, but he refused to accept it and left it. He said: al-Hasan used to say: he is the hypocrite. ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire. So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.﴾ He said: This is the example of the disbeliever whose heart is dead.
* *
Others said: Allah, His praise be exalted, only likened him to the dog because he used to pant as the dog pants.
Those who said this:
15441 - Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾: Balam used to pant as the dog pants. As for "tahmil 'alayhi" (you chase him): it means you rush upon him.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of those who said: it is an example for his abandonment of acting upon the signs of Allah which He gave him, and its meaning is: whether he is admonished or not admonished, he does not abandon what he is upon of opposing the command of his Lord, just as the dog, whether it is chased and driven away or left and not driven away, does not give up panting in either of its states.
We said that this is the more correct of the two views because of the indication of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾, so He made that the example of those who deny His signs. We know that panting is not in the nature of every denier, for whom it is written that he abandon returning from his denial of the signs of Allah; and that this is only an example which Allah struck for them. So it was known by that that it is an example for the one whom Allah described in this verse, just as it is an example for all the deniers of the signs of Allah. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "min takdhib" (from the denial); what I have adopted is more probable to me in its context.]] [[The context: "annahu lilladhi wasafa Allahu sifatahu ... mathal": the predicate of "anna".]]
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories, that they might reflect﴾ (176)
Abu Ja'far said: Allah, His remembrance be exalted, says: This example which I have struck for this one to whom We gave Our signs but who withdrew from them is the example of the people who denied Our proofs, Our indications and Our evidences, and they followed in that the path of this one who withdrew from Our signs which We gave him, in his abandonment of acting upon what We had given him of those things.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿So relate the stories﴾, He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So relate, O Muhammad, this account which I have related to you [[In the printed edition: "alladhi qasasatuhu" (which I related); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] = of the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, and the reports of the nations whose reports I informed you of in this surah, and I related to you their news and the news of their likes, [[In the printed edition: "wa qasasta nabā'ihim" (and you related their news), differing from the manuscript, like the earlier note.]] and what punishment from Us befell them, and what vengeance from Us descended upon them when they denied Our messengers = to your people from Quraysh, and to those before you from the Jews of the Children of Israel, that they might reflect upon that, and take heed, and turn in repentance to Our obedience, lest there befall them the like of what befell those before them of vengeances and exemplary punishments, and that the Jews of the Children of Israel may ponder it, and thus know the reality of your matter and the soundness of your prophethood, since the news of "the one to whom We gave Our signs" was among their hidden knowledge and secret reports, which none knows except their rabbis and those who read and studied the books among them. And in your knowledge of that, while you are an unlettered one who does not write, nor read, nor study books, nor sat with the people of knowledge, is a clear proof for you against them that you are truly a messenger of Allah, and that you did not know what you know of that, and your state being what it is, except by revelation from heaven. [[See the explanation of "al-qasas" above, p. 7, note 1, and the references there.]]
* *
Abu al-Nadr used to say something similar to that.
15442 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Salim Abi al-Nadr: ﴿So relate the stories that they might reflect﴾, meaning: the Children of Israel, since you have brought them news of what was among them which they concealed from you; "that they might reflect," so they would know that no one brought this news of what passed among them except a prophet to whom the news of heaven comes.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 177:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and were wronging themselves﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Evil is the example of the people who denied the proofs and evidences of God, and so rejected them, and who were diminishing their own share of them and depriving themselves of their benefits, by denying them and no other.

* *

It has been said: "Sa'a mathalan" (evil is the example) is from "al-su'" (evil), [[In the printed edition: "from the evil," but in the manuscript it is undotted, and the correct reading is what has been established.]] meaning: "bi'sa mathalan" (wretched is the example) [[of speech. See the explanation of "sa'a" above, 8:138, 358; 9:101, 205; 10:465. The grammarians consider "sa'a" a rigid verb that functions like "ni'ma" and "bi'sa."]] = [the example of the people], [[What is between the parentheses is an addition without which the sentence is not complete; but the copyist confused this sentence severely, omitting from his words later, "but righteousness is the righteousness of one who believes," the word "birr" (righteousness), so the sentence became corrupted.]] = and "the people" was placed in the position of "the example," and "the example" was omitted, since its meaning was understood from the context, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who believes in God﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 177]; for its meaning is: "But righteousness is the righteousness of one who believes in God." We have explained parallels to this in other places, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the note above numbered 2, then 3:338, 339; 10:313, and the indexes of the linguistic and grammatical discussions and others in the preceding volumes, under the chapter on omissions.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 178:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leaves astray, those are the losers.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, may He be exalted, means: guidance and leading astray are in the hand of Allah. "The one guided" is the one who travels the path of truth, who rides the clear road (al-mahajjah) in his religion, whom Allah has guided to that, granting him success in attaining it. The one who is astray is the one whom Allah has forsaken, so He does not grant him success in obedience to Him. Whomever Allah does that to is "the loser," meaning the one who is ruined.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "loss" (al-khasarah), "guidance" (al-hidayah), and "misguidance" (al-dalalah) in more than one place in this book, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[See the explanation of these terms in the language indexes under (hadha), (khasar), (dalal).]]

**Commentary on His words: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind."

* *

It is said of this: Allah created His creation, *dhara'a* (to create, bring forth) them, *yadhra'uhum*, *dharʼan*. [[See the explanation of *dhara'a* (ذرأ) above, 12:130-131, and there is additional material on its sources there.]]

* *

The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation of meaning) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

15443. Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾, he said: "From what We created." [[(1) The report 15443: in the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi," and "Ali ibn al-Husayn" appears. I followed what preceded it under number 10258, for it agrees with what is in Tarikh al-Tabari. I noted there that I had not found a biography for him, and I showed the places where he narrated from him in the History. An error occurred there: what is in the chain is "Ali ibn al-Hasan," and I wrote in the margin and the commentary "Ali ibn al-Husayn," and did likewise in the indexes. That should be corrected. Another error occurred in the indexes: I wrote the number (10285), and its correct form is (10258).]]

15444. ... Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell﴾, he said: "We created."

15445. ... He said: Zakariyya narrated to us, from Attab ibn Bashir, from Ali ibn Badhayma, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The children of fornication are among those whom Allah created for Hell."

15446. He said: Zakariyya ibn Adi and Uthman al-Ahwal narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiya, from al-Hasan ibn Amr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ishaq, from a companion of his in al-Ta'if, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah created for Hell what He created, the child of fornication was among those He created for Hell." [[The report 15446: Zakariyya ibn Adi ibn Zurayq al-Taymi, the teacher of Abu Kurayb, who is the narrator of the report, a trustworthy and eminent authority, appeared under number 1566.

Uthman al-Ahwal, the teacher of Abu Kurayb, is Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Qurashi, al-Zayyat al-Ahwal al-Tayyib al-Sa'igh. He appeared under numbers 137 and 11547.

Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari, the memorizer and trustworthy authority, appeared under numbers 1222, 3322, 3842, and 7685. Al-Hasan ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi al-Tamimi, trustworthy, whom al-Bukhari included in his Sahih, appeared under number 3765. Mu'awiya ibn Ishaq ibn Talha al-Taymi, a trustworthy Successor, appeared under number 3226. This chain is weak, because of the unknown identity of the one from whom Mu'awiya ibn Ishaq narrated, namely "a companion of his in al-Ta'if." Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:147, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

15447. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell﴾, he said: "We created."

15448. Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell﴾, "We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind."

15449. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell﴾, "We created."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance is exalted, and He said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾, because His knowledge of them is absolute: that they will go to it by their disbelief in their Lord.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, its meaning is: for these whom Allah created for Hell out of His creation there are hearts with which they do not reflect upon the signs of Allah, and with which they do not ponder His proofs of His oneness, and with which they do not draw lessons from His arguments presented through His messengers, [[See the explanation of *fiqh* (understanding) above, 11:572, note 2, and the references there.]] so that they would know the oneness of their Lord and recognize the truth of the prophethood of their prophets. Our Lord, exalted is His remembrance, described them as: "they do not understand with them," because of their turning away from the truth, their abandonment of contemplating the soundness of [the prophethood of] the messengers, [[In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "the soundness of guidance (rushd)," which has no meaning. I deduced the correct reading from the context of his commentary, and I added "prophethood (nubuwwa)" in the brackets to make the sentence complete.]] and the length of their disbelief. Likewise His words: ﴿And they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ mean: and for them are eyes with which they do not look upon the signs and proofs of Allah, so that they would contemplate them and reflect upon them, and thereby know the soundness of what their messengers call them to, and the corruption of what they persist in, namely associating partners with Allah and denying His messengers. So Allah described them, through their abandonment of using these faculties in the truth, as not seeing with them. [[In the printed edition: "that they do not see," and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]]

Likewise His words: ﴿And they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ mean the verses of the Book of Allah, so that they would draw lessons from them and reflect upon them, but they turn away from them, saying: (Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that perhaps you will prevail) [Surah Fussilat: 26]. This is similar to Allah's description of them elsewhere, with His words: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not reason﴾ [Surah al-Baqara: 171]. The Arabs say this of one who abandons using some of his limbs for what they are fit for, and from it is the verse of Miskin al-Darimi:

*I am blind when my neighbour goes out,*
*until the curtain conceals my neighbour;*
*and deaf to what was between us,*
*my hearing—though there is no deafness in my hearing.*

[[Amali al-Murtada 1:43-44, and again 474, from a qasida that he narrated and explained; Khizanat al-Adab 1:468. The correct version of the first verse is: "my neighbour's veil," because before it is: "It does not harm my neighbour, when I am his neighbour, that his house has no curtain." The second hemistich is: "my hearing, and I have no deafness," without iqwa'.]]

So he described himself, through his abandonment of looking and listening, as blind and deaf. From it is also the saying of another: [[He is Abdullah ibn Murra al-Ijli.]]

*And the ugly speech of the base I have turned a deaf ear to,*
*though if I wished, I could hear it well.*

[[Hamasa of al-Buhturi: 172. I forgot where I read it outside the Hamasa. What is in al-Buhturi's Hamasa is: "and the ugly speech (awra' al-kalam)," while in the manuscript it was: "awra' al-lu'am" (the ugly of the foolish), and it seems the correct reading is what is in the Hamasa.

"Al-awra'" is an ugly word, or one that goes astray out of ignorance without reason or right guidance. Among the finest things said on this is the saying of Hatim al-Ta'i, or al-A'war al-Shanni:

*An ugly word came to me from a brother, and I returned it*
*with its two eyes unharmed, seeking an excuse.*

*Had I, when he said it, said the like of it,*
*and not pardoned it, it would have left a rancour between us.*

*So I turned away from him, and waited for him a day,*
*perhaps a day would reveal a matter to one who waits.*

*I said to him: Return to brotherhood between us!*
*and I did not take what was of his ignorance as a moon [i.e., as a worthy matter].*

*I would uproot a lizard hidden in his heart,*
*and trim the nails that he let grow long in digging.*

And a sudden outburst I restrained myself from it,*
*while the ribs were filled with anger.*

[[In the printed edition: "though I was built of sinew," which is corrupt meaning, different from the manuscript, which had "and the ribs were torn from anger (nataqat min al-ghadab)," undotted, so he did not understand it and produced what makes no sense. In al-Buhturi's Hamasa: "when it was filled (idha tiqat)," with a kasra under the ta' and a fatha on the qaf, which has no meaning.

"Al-badira" is the error and the slips that come from a person when he becomes angry and heated, whether in action or speech.

"Wazza'a al-nafs 'an al-shay'" means to restrain it and hold it back. "Tia'a al-rajul" means he became full of anger and rage. "Al-ta'aq" is the intensity of fullness to the point that there is no room for more.]]

This is common in the speech and poetry of the Arabs. The people of *ta'wil* have said the same as what we have said about this.

* *

Mention of those who said that:

15450. Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'd narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, he said: "They do not understand with them anything of the matter of the Hereafter"; ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾, "the guidance"; ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾, "the truth." Then He made them like the cattle, equal, then He made them worse than cattle, and said: ﴿Nay, they are more astray﴾. Then He informed that they are the heedless. [[In the manuscript: "then He made them like cattle, then He made them equal, worse than cattle." The publisher dropped the word "equal," but I have restored it in its exact place.]]

* *

Commentary on His words: ﴿Those are like cattle; nay, they are more astray. Those are the heedless﴾ [7:179]

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Those are like cattle﴾, He means that these whom He created for Hell are like cattle, which are beasts that do not comprehend what is said to them, and do not understand what they see of what is suitable and what is not suitable, and do not reason with their hearts between good and evil, so that they distinguish between them. Allah therefore likened them to cattle, since they do not remember with their eyes the proofs of His, nor reflect upon what they hear of the verses of His Book. Then He said: ﴿Nay, they are more astray﴾, meaning: these disbelievers whom He created for Hell are further removed from the truth and more bound to the path of falsehood than the beasts, [[See the explanation of *dalal* (going astray) above, in the lexical indexes under the root (d-l-l).]] because beasts have no choice or discernment, so that they might choose and distinguish. They are rather subjugated, and yet they flee from harms and seek for themselves the more suitable nourishment. As for those whose description Allah gave in this verse, despite what they have been given of understanding and intellect that distinguish between benefits and harms, they abandon what contains the welfare of their worldly life and their Hereafter, and seek what contains their harm. So the beasts are more guided than them, and they are more astray, as our Lord, exalted is His remembrance, described them.

And His words: ﴿Those are the heedless﴾ mean: these whose description I have given, are the people who have been heedless—meaning, through inattention—[[See the explanation of *ghafl* (heedlessness) above, p. 115, note 1, and the references there.]] of My signs and My proofs, and have abandoned contemplating them, drawing lessons from them, and reasoning from what they indicate about the oneness of their Lord. They are not the beasts, whom their Lord has made known to what He subjected them to.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 180:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾ (7:180)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names﴾, and they are, as Ibn 'Abbas said:

15451 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾. Among His names are "al-'Aziz" (the Mighty) and "al-Jabbar" (the Compeller), and all His names are beautiful.

15452 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them all will enter Paradise." [[Report 15452: Hisham ibn Hassan al-Qurdusi is trustworthy. The whole group of compilers related from him. He has passed under numbers 2827, 7287, 9837, 10258. This is a sound chain. Al-Bukhari related it through Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (Fath al-Bari 5: 262 / 11: 180-194). Ibn Hajar explained it in exhaustive detail.

Muslim related it in his Sahih, through a route similar to al-Bukhari's, and then through Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah (Muslim 17: 4, 5).

Ahmad related it in his Musnad through several routes, numbers 7493, 7612, 8131, 9509, 10486, 10539, 10696. See its takhrij there.

Some of its routes contain the addition: "Indeed Allah is odd (witr) and loves the odd," or "He is odd and loves the odd."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, it refers to the polytheists. [[See the explanation of "dhara" (leave) in the earlier linguistic indices, under (wadhara).]]

* *

Their deviation (ilhad) concerning the names of Allah consisted in diverting them from what they are, so they named their gods and idols by them, and they added to them and subtracted from them. They named one of them "al-Lat," deriving it from the name of Allah, which is "Allah," and they named another "al-'Uzza," deriving it from the name of Allah, which is "al-'Aziz."

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:
