15453 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. He said: The deviation of the deviators was that they called "al-Lat" by one of the names of Allah.

15454 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. He said: They derived "al-'Uzza" from "al-'Aziz," and they derived "al-Lat" from "Allah."

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿yulhidun﴾ (deviate).

Some of them said: they deny.

Those who said so:

15455 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. He said: Ilhad is denial (takdhib).

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: they associate partners (with Allah).

Those who said so:

15456 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Abu Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿yulhidun﴾. He said: They associate partners. [[Report 15456: "Ibn Thawr" is Muhammad ibn Thawr al-San'ani. He has passed in the chain many times, the last under number 15437, where I corrected another error there. Then what will come: 15459. In the printed edition and the manuscript here it reads "Abu Thawr related to us," which is a pure error.]]

* *

The root of "ilhad" in the speech of the Arabs is: turning away from the intended course, deviating from it, and turning aside. It is then used for anything crooked and not straight. For this reason the niche in the side of a grave is called "lahd," because it lies to one side of it and not in its middle. From it one says: "alhada fulan yulhidu ilhadan," and "lahada yalhadu lahdan and luhudan." [[(2) The second verbal noun "luhud" is rarely found in the lexicons, so I have noted it.]] It is related from al-Kisa'i that he distinguished between "ilhad" and "lahd," saying that "ilhad" is turning away from the intended course, and "lahd" is leaning toward a thing. He used to read every occurrence in the Qur'an as ﴿yulhidun﴾ with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the ḥā', except the one in Surat al-Nahl, which he read as "yalhadun" with a fatha on the yā' and the ḥā'. [[The verse of Surat al-Nahl is 16:103, in al-Kisa'i's reading: "the tongue of the one to whom they lean is foreign." This is the common reading of the people of Kufa, as Ibn Jarir said later in his tafsir (14: 120, Bulaq). He did not single out al-Kisa'i there, because he differed from them on the reading of the letter in other places.] He claimed that it means leaning.

As for the rest of the people who know the speech of the Arabs, they hold that the two have one meaning, and that they are two dialects that came in one letter with one meaning.

* *

The readers differed in reading it. The majority of the readers of Madinah, some of the Basrans and the Kufans read ﴿yulhidun﴾, with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the ḥā', from "alhada yulhidu," throughout the Qur'an.

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa read "yalhadun," with a fatha on the yā' and the ḥā', from "lahada yalhadu."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that they are two dialects with one meaning, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is right. However, I prefer the reading with a damma on the yā', following the dialect of those who say "alhada," because it is the better known and more eloquent of the two dialects.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say, concerning His saying ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, that it is abrogated (mansukh).

15457 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾: These are the people of disbelief, and it has been abrogated; fighting abrogated it.

* *

= There is no sense in what Ibn Zayd said about it, that it is abrogated, because His saying ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾ is not a command from Allah to His Prophet (ﷺ) to leave the polytheists alone in saying that, until He permits him to fight them. Rather, it is a threat from Allah to those who deviate concerning His names, and a warning from Him to them, as He said in another place: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon know﴾ (15:3), and the verse that follows it, and as in His saying: ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them, and so that they may enjoy themselves; they will soon know﴾ (29:66). It is a speech that comes in the form of a command with the meaning of warning and threat. Its meaning is: Give respite, O Muhammad, to those who deviate concerning the names of Allah, until a term which they will reach. [[In the printed edition: "an tumhil" (that you give respite). It did not read the manuscript well.]] Then they will be recompensed, when the term of Allah that He set for them comes upon them, for the deeds they used to do before that: disbelief in Allah, deviation concerning His names, and denial of His Messenger. [[In the printed edition: "alladhi ajjalahu ilayhim" (which He set for them). It changed the pronouns and thereby ruined the sense.]]

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Among the creatures We created is "a community" (ummah), meaning a group [see the explanation of "ummah" earlier, p. 208, note 2, and the references there] "who guide" (yahdūn), meaning they are guided by the truth [see the explanation of "guidance" (hudā) earlier in the lexical indexes, under h-d-y] "and by it do justice" (wa-bihi ya'dilūn), meaning: they judge and deal equitably with people by the truth [see the explanation of "justice" ('adl) earlier, p. 172, note 3, and the references there], as Ibn Jurayj said:

15458 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿A community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "This is my community!" He said: They take, give, and judge by the truth.

15459 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾ ... [These dots were placed because the report is incomplete; either something fell from the copyist's text, or it is a separate chain for the report that follows.]

15460 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾. It has reached us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say when reciting it: "This is for you, and the people before you were given the like of it: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾" [Surah al-A'raf: 159].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 182:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And those who deny Our signs - We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ (7:182)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And those who denied Our proofs and signs, rejecting them and not being admonished by them, We will give them respite with their delusion and make their evil deeds appear fair to them, [[Abu Ja'far unexpectedly dropped the plural pronoun in favor of a singular pronoun, which is very strange. However, it is so in the manuscript and the printed edition. I have left it as it is, because I think that Abu Ja'far was sometimes absorbed by what he wanted to write, so that his thought would sometimes turn from one side of the sentence to another. Something like this has occurred in some places elsewhere, as I have indicated. This is useful in knowing the composition of authors and what befalls them while they write. For this reason I did not change it, in order to preserve the characteristics of what Abu Ja'far wrote. I consider it unlikely that this is from the copyist, because the sentence is too long for a copyist to omit in its transmission to such a degree, or to introduce all this change into all its pronouns. Then see what will come at p. 338, note 2.]] until he thinks that, in his denial of God's signs, he is a doer of good to himself, and until he reaches the limit of the respite that was written for him. Then He will seize him for his evil deeds and requite him with the punishment He has prepared for him. That is God's "istidraj" (gradual leading) of him.

* *

The root of "istidraj" is the deception of the one being led on by the kindness of the one who leads him on [istadrajahu], [[What is between the brackets is missing from the manuscript and the printed edition, and the context requires it, as you see.]] where the one being led on sees that the one leading him on is good to him, until he drops him into something hateful.

* *

We have already explained the manner of God's doing this to the people of disbelief in Him in an earlier place, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[I have lost track of its location and have not found it.]]

**The exegesis of His words: ﴿And I give them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾ (7:183)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And I defer these who denied Our signs." [The root of *al-imla'* (granting respite) comes from their saying: "a long period (*mali*) passed over him," and *malawa* and *mulawa* (with kasra, damma and fatha) "of time" (*min al-dahr*).] [[There is no doubt that something has fallen out of Abu Ja'far's words. I completed it by inference from Abu 'Ubayda's *Majaz al-Qur'an* 1:234, and I have placed it in brackets. You will see later that the discussion in these paragraphs is disjointed, and I do not know whether this is from the copyist or from Abu Ja'far, so I have separated some of it from other parts. Note this separation between consecutive passages, with explanatory text, as you see. In the printed edition it read *mala'a* (a sheet), and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] It means a period of time, and from it one says: "I waited for you a long while (*malyan*)." [[See the explanation of *al-imla'* above, 7:421–422.]]

* *

The sense of the passage: (And I defer ... so that they may reach ...) [[the context is "and I defer ..."]] so that they may reach, through their disobedience to their Lord, the measure that He has decreed for them of punishment and torment, and then He will take them to Himself.

* *

﴿Indeed My plan﴾.

* *

*Al-kayd* is *al-makr* (deception, scheming). [[See the explanation of *al-kayd* above, 7:156 and 8:547.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿*matin*﴾, it means: strong and firm. From it is the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

*'Adalna 'udul al-nas wa aqbah yabtali / afanina min ulhub shadd mumatin*

[[The verse appears in the printed edition as: "'Adalna 'udul al-nas wa aqbah yabtali / aqas min al-harab shadd mumatin," and in the manuscript as: "'Adalna 'udul al-nas dhamh sala / ... sadd mumatin," unpointed except where I pointed it.

I do not know what the first half means. As for the reading of the second half, its correct reading is certainly what I have given, and it describes she-camels or horses. *Al-afanin* is the plural of *afnun*, meaning mixed running from the gait of a horse or a camel. One says: "The horse ran with various kinds of running (*afanin*)," and "the horse varied its running (*aftana*)." *Al-ulhub* means that the horse exerts itself in its running and blazes, until it raises dust; one says: "the ulhub intensified" and "the horse blazed (*alhaba*), its running was ablaze." *Al-shadd* means running. One says: "the horse and other animals ran in a run, a shadd, and intensified," that is, hastened and ran a strong run. I have left the first half as it is until I find a source that corrects it.]]

That is, a strong, lasting course that does not stop.

[[In the manuscript: "meaning a strong *sabab* (cause)," and what is in the printed edition is close to the correct meaning.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do they not reflect? There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner﴾ (7:184)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Have not these people who denied Our signs reflected with their minds, reasoned, and known that Our Messenger whom We sent to them has no madness (jinnah) and no derangement (khabal), and that what he calls them to is the sound opinion (al-ra'y al-sahih), the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim), and the manifest truth (al-haqq al-mubin)? [In the printed edition it reads: "it is the sound and upright religion", differing from the manuscript, and I added what is between the brackets as an inference from the context.] It is said that this verse was revealed [in the printed edition: "So this verse was revealed"; in the manuscript: "And when it was revealed"; I judged the correct reading to be what I have recorded, though I am uncertain whether the text has a lacuna.] as follows:

15461 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was on al-Safa [the printed edition, the manuscript and Ibn Kathir all read "was on al-Safa"; I think the correct reading is "stood on al-Safa", as in all other reports on the commentary of the verse in Surah al-Shu'ara' 26:214, see Tafsir al-Tabari 19:73-76, Bulaq edition], and he called the Quraysh, going through them clan by clan (fakhidhan fakhidhan): "O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so!" [Fakhdh (clan) of the man: Banu so-and-so; he called them clan by clan. The "fakhdh" is a division of groups and tribes. It is said: the "sha'b" (people), then the "qabilah" (tribe), then the "fasilah" (sub-clan), then the "‘imarah" (household), then the "batn" (lineage), then the "fakhdh" (thigh-clan).] He warned them of the might of Allah and the days of Allah's punishment. One of them said: "Your companion here is surely a madman! He spent the night crying out until morning" [or: "until he reached the morning"]. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Do they not reflect? There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿he is only a clear warner﴾, the meaning is: he is only a warner who warns you of Allah's punishment for your disbelief in Him, if you do not turn back in faith to Him. [In the printed edition: "munadhdhirakum"; I have kept the reading of the manuscript.] [See the explanation of "nadhir" above, 11:369, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

As for His words ﴿clear﴾, the meaning is: he has made clear to you, O people, his warning of the punishment of Allah for your disbelief in Him. [See the explanation of "mubin" in the language indices above under (b-y-n).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 185:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth, and at what things Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has drawn near? So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these deniers of the signs of Allah not looked at the kingdom and sovereignty of Allah in the heavens and on the earth, [[See the explanation of "al-malakut" above, 11:470.]] and at what He, may His praise be exalted, has created of any thing in them, so that they might reflect upon that and take warning from it, and know that it belongs to One who has no equal and no like, and is of the action of the One for whom worship and pure religion alone are fitting; so that they would believe in Him, affirm His Messenger, turn in obedience to Him, cast off the rivals and idols, and beware that their terms may have drawn near, so that they perish in their disbelief and come to the punishment of Allah and His painful retribution. [[See the explanation of "al-ajal" above, p. 73, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾, he says: So in what warning and admonition, and what frightening, after the warning and admonition of Muhammad ﷺ and his admonition which he brought to them from Allah in the verses of His Book, will they believe, if they do not believe in this Book which Muhammad ﷺ brought to them from Allah, exalted is He? [[See the explanation of "al-hadith" above, 8:592, 593.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 186:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him, and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the turning away of these people who denied Our signs, neglecting to reflect upon the proofs of Allah and to think about them, is due to Allah's leading them astray. Had Allah guided them, they would have taken heed and reflected, and so they would have perceived their right guidance. But Allah has led them astray, so they do not perceive right guidance nor follow the path. And whomever He leads astray from righteous guidance, there is none to guide him to it. Allah leaves them in their continued excess in their disbelief and their rebellion in their polytheism, wandering back and forth, so that they deserve the end that Allah has decreed for them of His punishment and His painful retribution. [[See the explanation of "al-dalal" (misguidance) and "al-huda" (guidance) in the earlier lexical indices under (ḍ-l-l) and (h-d-y). = The explanation of "yadharu" (leaves) earlier, p. 36, footnote 2, and the references there. = The explanation of "al-tughyan" (transgression) earlier, p. 12: 46, footnote 2, and the references there. = The explanation of "al-ʿamah" (blind wandering) earlier, 1: 309–311 / 12: 46.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord; none but He will reveal it at its time﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding those meant by His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the people of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Quraysh, who had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it.

Those who said this:

15462 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, who said: Quraysh said to Muhammad ﷺ: "Indeed there is kinship between us and you, so disclose to us when the Hour will come!" Then Allah said: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it﴾. [[The report: 15462 - it will come under number 15481.]]

* *

Others said: it refers to a group of Jews.

Those who said this:

15463 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Saʿid ibn Jubayr or ʿIkrimah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Jabal ibn Abi Qushayr and Shamwil ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Muhammad, tell us when the Hour will come, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know when it is?" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿but most people do not know﴾. [[The report: 15463 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 218, continuing the earlier report no. 12216.]]

15464 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: The Prophet ﷺ would not cease mentioning the matter of the Hour until this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be?﴾. [[The report: 15464 - Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid al-Ahmasi is trustworthy and reliable, mentioned under numbers 5694, 5777, 12280. Tariq ibn Shihab al-Ahmasi saw the Prophet ﷺ and narrated from him as a mursal report; mentioned several times under numbers 9744, 11682, 12073, 12075, 12085. In the printed and manuscript editions it read "Mukhariq ibn Shihab", which is a plain error; the correct form is from Ibn Kathir. This report was cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3: 609, where he said: "al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of ʿIsa ibn Yunus, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with it. This is a good, strong chain."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter is to say: a group of people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Hour, and Allah revealed this verse. It is possible that they were from Quraysh, and it is possible that they were from the Jews; we have no report that permits us to affirm definitively which of these it was.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse is: Do the people who ask you about the Hour ask ﴿when will its arrival be?﴾ That is, when will it be established?

* *

The meaning of "ayyan" (when) in the speech of the Arabs is "matā" (when), and from it is the saying of the rajiz (rhyming poet): [[I do not know who said it.]]
"When will my need be fulfilled, when? Do you not see its success is at its time?"
[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbaydah 1: 234; Lisan al-ʿArab (ayn). And "ibban al-shay'" is its time and its appointed season in which it is suitable or occurs.]]

* *

The meaning of His saying: ﴿its arrival (mursaha)﴾ is its establishment, from the speaker's saying: "Allah anchored it, so it is mursat (anchored)," and "the people anchored it" when they held it back, and "it anchored itself, yarsu rusuwwan."

* *

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

15465 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be?﴾, he said: when will it be established?

* *

15466 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be?﴾: when will it be established?

* *

Others said: the meaning is: its termination (muntahaha). This is close in meaning to those who said: its establishment, because its ending is its reaching its time. We have already explained that the root of this is holding back and standing still.

Those who said this:

15467 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its arrival be?﴾, he means: its termination.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord; none but He will reveal it at its time﴾, it is a command from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to answer his questioners about the Hour that none knows the time of its establishment except Allah, who knows the unseen, and that He does not manifest it at its time, nor does anyone other than Him, may His remembrance be exalted, know it, as:

15468 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord; none but He will reveal it at its time﴾, he says: its knowledge is with Allah; He reveals it at its time, and none knows that except Allah.

15469 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Lā yujalliha﴾ (will not reveal it): he brings it.

15470 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿Lā yujalliha﴾, he said: none but He brings it.

15471 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Lā yujalliha li-waqtiha illā huwa﴾, he says: none but He sends it at its time.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 187:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth; it will not come to you except suddenly﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: the Hour is heavy upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth in that they cannot know its time and its coming, because it is hidden from them and God has reserved knowledge of it to Himself.

Those who said this:

15472 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: it is hidden in the heavens and the earth, so no one knows when it will rise, neither an angel brought near nor a messenger prophet.

15473 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us = and al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us = all of them, from Ma'mar, from some of the people of interpretation: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: its knowledge is heavy upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth, that they do not know it.

* * *

Others said: The meaning is: its coming is great (or grievous) to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

Those who said this:

15474 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us = and al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us = all of them, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: when it comes, it is heavy upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth. He says: it is grievous to them.

15475 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: when it comes, the sky will split, the stars will scatter, the sun will be folded up, the mountains will be set in motion, and what God said will happen; that is its weight.

15476 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: some people said regarding "thaqulat": it became great.

* * *

Others said: The meaning of His words ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾ is: upon the heavens and the earth.

Those who said this:

15477 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., upon the heavens and the earth.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The view most correct in my opinion is the view of the one who said: the meaning is: the Hour is heavy in the heavens and the earth upon their inhabitants, that they should know its time and its rising; because God has concealed that from His creation, and has not let any of them know it. This is because God informed of it after His words: ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with my Lord; none but He will reveal it at its time﴾, and then informed after it that it will not come except suddenly. So the more fitting is that what lies between these also be a report about the concealment of its knowledge from creation, since what came before it and what came after it are both like that.

* * *

As for His words ﴿it will not come to you except suddenly﴾, He says: the Hour will not come except unexpectedly, you will not perceive its coming, [[See the explanation of "al-baghta" previously: 11:325, 360, 368 / 12:576.]] as:

15478 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿it will not come to you except suddenly﴾, he says: its rising will surprise them, it will come upon them in heedlessness.

15479 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿it will not come to you except suddenly﴾, God decreed that it will not come to you except suddenly. He said: it was related to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ used to say: the Hour will rush upon people while a man is mending his pool, and a man is watering his livestock, and a man is displaying his goods in the market, and a man is lowering his scale and raising it.

* * *

The explanation of His words: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it. Say: its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know (187)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: these people ask you about the Hour as though you were eager (hafiy) about it.

* * *

[The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿hafiyy 'anha﴾.] [[The addition between brackets is required by Abu Ja'far's method in his tafsir.]]

Some of them said: They ask you about it as though you were eager for them. And they said: the meaning of "'anha" is inverted (al-taqdim), though it is placed after.

Those who said this:

15480 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he says: as though there were affection between you and them, as though you were a friend to them. Ibn 'Abbas said: when the people asked Muhammad ﷺ about the Hour, they asked him in the manner of a people who think Muhammad is eager for them, so God revealed to him: its knowledge is only with Him; He has reserved its knowledge, and has not let any angel or messenger know it.

15481 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah said: the Quraysh said to Muhammad ﷺ: there is kinship between us and you, so disclose to us when the Hour is! Then God said: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾. [[The report 15481 was previously given as no. 15462.]]

15482 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, i.e., eager for them. He said: the Quraysh said: O Muhammad, disclose to us the knowledge of the Hour, because of the kinship between us and you = because of our kinship to you.

15483 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, and Hani' ibn Sa'id, from Hajjaj, from Khusayf, from Mujahid and 'Ikrimah: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: eager for them when they ask you.

15484 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: near to them, and concealing from them = he said: and Abu Malik said: as though you were eager for them, so you tell them. [[Report 15484: I do not know who "Abu Malik" is in this report.]]

15485 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, as though you were a friend to them.

* * *

Others said: rather, the meaning is: as though you had made the question about it urgent so that you know it.

Those who said this:

15486 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾, you were pressed by the question about it until you knew it.

15487 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Sa'd related to us, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: you were pressed by the question about it until you knew its time.

15488 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: al-Maharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: as though you knew it.

15489 - ... he said: Hamid ibn Nuh related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: as though you knew it. [[Report 15489: "Jabir ibn Nuh", previously given as 5694, 9863; in the printed edition "Hamid ibn Nuh", in the manuscript it is poorly written, and this is its correct form.]]

15490 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to me, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he says: they ask you about the Hour, as though you had knowledge of it = ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾.

15491 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from some of them: ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾, as though you knew it.

15492 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾, he said: as though you knew it. He also said: He concealed its knowledge from His creation. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour﴾ [Surah Luqman: 34] until he finished the surah.

15493 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿They ask you as though you were eager about it﴾, he says: as though their questioning of you pleases you = ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with God﴾.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾, he says: gentle toward it. [[This sentence, which I have set apart, is certainly not part of Ibn 'Abbas's report above, which is why I separated them. I still fear that something may have fallen from the copyist before this sentence, since what Abu Ja'far mentioned is only two views, not three, and this last sentence relates to the first view and seems to be an explanation of it.]]

* * *

Those who took this view directed the interpretation of His words ﴿as though you were eager about it﴾ toward "eager with it" (hafiyy biha), and said: the Arabs say: "I took pains with him in the question" (tahaffaytu lahu fi al-mas'alah) and "I took pains about him" (tahaffaytu 'anhu). They said: that is why it is said: "We came to so-and-so to ask about him," meaning to ask concerning him.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views in this matter is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: as though you were eager in the question about it, so you know it.

If someone says: how is it said ﴿hafiyy 'anha﴾ and not "hafiyy biha", if that is the intended meaning of the speech?

It is said: this was said in this way because al-hafawah (eagerness) occurs in the question, and it is cheerfulness toward the one questioned at the time of asking, and frequent asking about him. The verb "to ask" is connected with "'an" at one time and with "ba'" at another; one says "sa'altu 'anhu" and "sa'altu bihi." So when "hafiyy" was placed in the position of the asking, it was connected with the more common of the two particles with which "to ask" is connected, namely "'an," as the poet said: [[He is al-Mu'attal al-Hudhali.]]

su'āla ḥafiyyin 'an akhīhi ka'annahu / bi-dhikratihi wasnānu aw mutawāsin

[[From a long qasida in Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 3:45. With this reading which Abu Ja'far narrated, "su'al hafiyy", the poem's context is disrupted. Its reading in his diwan: ... Its correct reading is "su'ala al-ghaniyy 'an akhihi" (the question of one who is indifferent about his brother)...]]

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with God﴾, its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you about the time of the Hour and its coming: I have no knowledge of that, and no one has knowledge of it except [with] God, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth [[In the printed edition: "and none knows it except God", which is not good; I have kept what is in the manuscript and added in brackets what the context requires.]] = ﴿but most people do not know﴾, meaning: but most people do not know that none knows it except God, rather they suppose that knowledge of it exists with some of His creation.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Say, "I possess no power to bring benefit to myself or to ward off harm, except as Allah wills. And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much of good, and no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you about the Hour, "When will it arrive?" ﴿I possess no power to bring benefit to myself or to ward off harm﴾, meaning: I am not able to bring benefit to myself or to repel a harm that befalls me, except what Allah wills that I should possess of that, by strengthening me to it and helping me. ﴿And if I knew the unseen﴾, meaning: if I knew what is to occur of what has not yet happened. ﴿I would have acquired much of good﴾, meaning: I would have prepared much good. [See the explanation of "malaka" (possess) above, 10:147, 187, 317.] [See the explanation of "al-ghayb" (the unseen) above, 11:464, note 2, and the references there.] [See the explanation of "istakthara" (acquire much) above, 12:115.]

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed concerning the meaning of "the good" (al-khayr) which Allah intended by His saying: ﴿I would have acquired much of good﴾. [See the explanation of "al-khayr" (good) above, 2:505 / 7:91.] Some of them said: The meaning of that is: I would have acquired much of righteous deeds.

Those who said this:

15494. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, saying: Ibn Juraij said, concerning His saying: ﴿Say, "I possess no power to bring benefit to myself or to ward off harm"﴾, he said: "guidance and misguidance." ﴿If I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much of good﴾, he said: "knowing the unseen" means when I will die; "I would have acquired much of righteous deeds."

15495. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

15496. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much of good, and no harm would have touched me﴾, he said: "I would have avoided whatever evil might occur and guarded against it."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "If I knew the unseen" I would have prepared for the year of drought in advance of the year of plenty, and I would have known high prices from low prices, and I would have made provision for it during the cheap times.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and no harm would have touched me﴾, it means: no harm would have afflicted me. ﴿I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾, meaning: I am only a messenger of Allah, sent by Him to you, to warn of His punishment whoever among you disobeys Him and opposes His command, and to give good tidings of His reward and honor to whoever among you believes in Him and obeys Him. [See the explanation of "nadhir" (warner) above, p. 290, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "bashir" (bringer of good tidings) above, 11:369, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to a people who believe﴾, it means: those who affirm that I am Allah's messenger, and acknowledge the truth of what I have brought them from Him. [In the printed edition: "bihaqqiyyat ma ji'tahum bihi" (the truth of what I brought them), and the correct reading is from the manuscript; he changed it in hundreds of places. See what has passed, p. 113, note 1, and the references there. And "al-haqiqa" (the reality), is a verbal noun, meaning truthfulness and right, as I have previously stated.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 189:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her. And when he covered her, she carried a light burden and passed on with it. But when she became heavy, they both invoked Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a good (child), we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul﴾, meaning by the single soul: Adam. [[See the explanation of "a single soul" above, 7: 513, 514.]] As related:

15497 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿created you from a single soul﴾, he said: Adam, peace be upon him. [[Report 15497 - already passed as no. 8402.]]

15498 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul﴾, from Adam.

* *

And by His words: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾: and made from the single soul, which is Adam, its mate Hawwa' (Eve). [[See the explanation of "made" (ja'ala) in the lexical indexes above under (ja'ala).]] As related:

15499 - Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾: Hawwa', who was made from one of his ribs, so that he might dwell in tranquility with her.

* *

And by His words: ﴿that he might dwell in tranquility with her﴾: that he might take refuge with her for the fulfilment of his need and his pleasure.

* *

And by His words: ﴿And when he covered her﴾: when he covered her to fulfil his need of her, and he fulfilled his need of her, ﴿she carried a light burden﴾. There is an omission in the speech, left out because what is apparent indicates what is omitted, and that is His words: ﴿when he covered her, she carried﴾. The speech in full is: when he covered her [and fulfilled his need of her] she carried.

* *

As for His words: ﴿she carried a light burden﴾, by "lightness of the burden" is meant the water which Hawwa' carried in her womb from Adam; it was a light burden, and likewise a woman's carrying of a man's water is light for her.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and passed on with it﴾, it means: she continued with the water, standing and sitting, and completed the pregnancy, as related:

15500 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Abu 'Umayr, from Ayyub, who said: I asked al-Hasan about His words: ﴿she carried a light burden and passed on with it﴾, and he said: If you were an Arab man, would you know what it is? It is only: "fa-istamarrat bihi" (she continued with it). [[Report 15500: Abu 'Umayr is al-Harith ibn 'Umayr al-Basri, a trustworthy narrator spoken of concerning his memory, biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/2/83. Ayyub is al-Sakhtiyani, Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/409, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/255.]]

15501 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when he covered her, she carried a light burden and passed on with it﴾: its carrying became apparent.

15502 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿passed on with it﴾, he said: its carrying continued.

15503 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿she carried a light burden﴾, he said: it was the drop (nutfah). And His words: ﴿and passed on with it﴾, he means: she continued with it.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: she doubted about it.

Those who said so:

15504 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿passed on with it﴾, he said: she doubted, whether she was pregnant or not?

* *

And by His words: ﴿But when she became heavy﴾: when what was in her womb of the pregnancy, which had been light, became heavy, and her delivery drew near.

* *

It is said from this: "Such-and-such a woman became heavy" when she became burdened with her pregnancy, just as it is said: "Such-and-such a man became rich in dates" (atmara) when he came to have dates. As related:

15505 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿But when she became heavy﴾: the child grew large in her womb.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: ﴿they both invoked Allah, their Lord﴾: that is, Adam and Hawwa' called upon their Lord and said: "O our Lord," "If You give us a good (child), we will surely be among the thankful."

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "good" (salih) which Adam and Hawwa', peace be upon them, swore that if He gave them a good (child) in Hawwa's pregnancy, they would surely be among the thankful.

Some of them said: it is that the child be a boy.

Those who said so:

15506 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words: ﴿If You give us a good (child)﴾, he said: a boy.

* *

Others said: rather, it is that the newborn be a complete human being like them, and not an animal.

Those who said so:

15507 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Jubayr al-Jushami, from Abu al-Bakhtari, regarding His words: ﴿If You give us a good (child), we will surely be among the thankful﴾, he said: they feared that it would be something other than a human being. [[Report 15507: Zayd ibn Jubayr al-Ta'i, trustworthy, related by the group, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/356, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/558. In the printed edition it read "al-Hashmi", unpointed as in the manuscript; the correct reading is what is given here.]]

15508 - ... He said: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: they feared that it would not be a human being.

15509 - ... He said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, who said: When Adam's wife became pregnant and heavy, they both feared that it would be an animal, so they called upon their Lord: ﴿If You give us a good (child)﴾, the verse.

15510 - ... He said: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they feared that it would be an animal.

15511 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When Adam and Hawwa' descended, desire was cast into his soul, and he had intercourse with her; no sooner had he had intercourse with her than she conceived, and no sooner had she conceived than her child stirred in her womb. She said: "What is this?" Then Iblis came to her and said [to her: "You have conceived, and you will give birth!" She said: "What will I bear?" He said]: "Do you not see on the earth only a she-camel, or a cow, or a ewe, or a she-goat, or some of that? [It will come out of your nose, or your ear, or your eye]." She said: "By God, nothing of mine but would be too narrow for that!" He said: "Then obey me and name him 'Abd al-Harith' [and his name among the angels was al-Harith], and you will bear a likeness of you both, like you!" She said: So she mentioned that to Adam, peace be upon him, and he said: "He is our companion whom you know!" [In the printed edition: "he is our companion who has expelled us from the Garden", while in the manuscript: "who has fa-mata", with a mark of "ta" between "qad" and "fa-mata" and a note in the margin "thus". I have followed the text of al-Durr al-Manthur.] Then he died. Then she conceived another, and he came to her and said: "Obey me and name him 'Abd al-Harith' — and his name among the angels was al-Harith — or else you will bear a she-camel, or a cow, or a ewe, or a she-goat, or you will kill him, for it was I who killed the first!" She mentioned that to Adam, and he seemed not to dislike it, so she named him "Abd al-Harith." That is His words: ﴿If You give us a good (child)﴾, meaning: a likeness of us, like us. ﴿Then when He gave them a good (child)﴾, he said: a likeness of them, like them. [[Report 15511: these are false reports, as I have pointed out several times.]]

15512 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿But when she became heavy﴾: the child grew large in her womb. Iblis came to her, frightened her, and said to her: "How do you know what is in your belly? Perhaps it is a dog, or a pig, or a donkey! And how do you know where it will come out? From your back, so that it kills you, or from your front, or your belly will split and it will kill you?" So at that point they invoked Allah, their Lord: ﴿If You give us a good (child)﴾, meaning: a likeness of us, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful.﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is that it should be said: Allah informed about Adam and Hawwa' that they invoked Allah, their Lord, concerning Hawwa's pregnancy, and swore that if He gave them what was in Hawwa's womb as a good (child), they would surely be among those thankful to Allah.

"Good" (salih) may comprise many meanings: among them, "good" in soundness of creation, among them "good" in religion, and among them "good" in intellect and management.

Since that is so, and there is no report from the Messenger that establishes a proof that it refers to some meanings of "good" rather than others, nor is there any indication of it in reason, it must be taken in its general sense as Allah made it general, so it is said: they both said, ﴿If You give us a good (child)﴾, in all the meanings of "good".

* *

As for the meaning of His words: ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾, it is: we will surely be among those who thank You for the child You have granted us, a good one.

**The Commentary on His Words (exalted is He): ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. But exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ (7:190)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: when Allah granted them a righteous child, as they had asked, they made partners for Him in what He had given them and provided for them.

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed concerning the "partners" that they made in what they were given of the child.

Some of them said: they made partners for Him in the name.

Those who said this:

15513. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah ibn Jundub, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: Hawwa' (Eve) had no child who survived, so she vowed that if a child of hers survived, she would name him "ʿAbd al-Harith." A child survived to her, and she named him "ʿAbd al-Harith." [[In the printed edition: "from the inspiration of Satan," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the sources.]] That was only from the inspiration of Satan.

[[The narration 15513: "ʿAbd al-Samad" is ʿAbd al-Samad ibn ʿAbd al-Warith, who has passed many times. ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim al-ʿAbdi: Ahmad and others declared him trustworthy, but he said: "He narrates from Qatadah unusual reports, and he contradicts." Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written down but not used as evidence." Ibn ʿAdi said: "He narrates from Qatadah things that are not corroborated, and his hadith specifically from Qatadah is disturbed." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: "He errs and contradicts." Then he mentioned him among the weak and said: "He was among those who transmit alone from Qatadah in ways that do not resemble his other hadith. I do not favour using him as proof when he transmits alone. As for what the trustworthy narrate, if someone takes it into account, I see no harm in it." al-Daraqutni said: "Weak (layyin), to be abandoned." He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/98, and Mizan al-iʿtidal 2:248.

This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 5:11, with a different wording. Al-Hakim narrated it with this wording in al-Mustadrak 2:545 and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. al-Tirmidhi included it in his tafsir of the verse and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. We only know it from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim, from Qatadah. Some of them narrated it from ʿAbd al-Samad without raising it (to the Prophet)."

Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir 3:611-612 and gave it defects in three respects:
First: ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim is not used as evidence.
Second: it was also narrated as the words of Samurah himself, not raised to the Prophet.
Third: al-Hasan himself explained the verse differently. Abu Ja'far mentioned some reports from him with their chains, numbers 15526-15528. Then Ibn Kathir said: "These are sound chains from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, that he explained the verse in that way, and it is among the best of the tafsirs and the most fitting meaning for the verse. If this hadith had been preserved from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his view, neither he nor anyone else would have turned away from it, especially given his piety and scrupulousness. This shows you that it is a report stopping at the Companion. It is possible that he received it from some of the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, such as Kaʿb or Wahb ibn Munabbih and others, as will be explained later, if Allah wills. However, we are cleared of the responsibility of the raised (marfuʿ) report. And Allah knows best."

I say: You will see that Abu Ja'far preferred that the one meant by this is Adam and Hawwa', saying: "Because of the consensus of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon this." But the consensus of the people of ta'wil on such a matter does not stand... The first point: the verse is problematic, since it attributes shirk to Adam, whom his Lord chose, by the text of the Book of Allah. Abu Ja'far wanted to escape this, and he claimed (p. 315) that the account about Adam and Hawwa' ended at His words "they made partners for Him in what He had given them," and then His words "exalted is Allah above what they associate" were resumed, meaning above what the pagan Arabs associate with idols. This is a very weak way out.

The second point: such a problematic matter concerning Adam and Hawwa', and the attribution of shirk to them, is not decided except by a proof that must be accepted, either from the text of the Book or a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There is no such report except this weak report whose weakness we have shown, that it is from the narration of ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim from Qatadah. His narration from Qatadah is disturbed, and it contradicts what is narrated from al-Hasan, that by the verse he meant some of the people of other religions and the polytheists.

This view has been rejected by a group of exegetes, such as Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, and al-Fakhr al-Razi (3:243-345). al-Zamakhshari tried to refute it in his tafsir but did not succeed, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munayyir criticised him in al-Insaf. There are many others besides these.

But after all this, we find that the explanation of the wording of the verse, and its agreement with the correct meaning that the scholars adopted in clearing our father Adam, peace be upon him, of shirk, and in holding that the verse does not refer to our father Adam and our mother Hawwa', has remained obscure, and no one has provided a sound clarification of it. I would have liked to be able to clarify it in this place, but I found the matter too difficult to discuss in a commentary of this kind.]]

15514. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Maʿmar narrated to us, from his father, who said: Abu al-ʿAla' narrated to us, from Samurah ibn Jundub, that he reported that Adam, peace be upon him, named his son "ʿAbd al-Harith."

15515. ... He said: al-Maʿmar narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu al-ʿAla' ibn al-Shikhkhir, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: Adam named his son "ʿAbd al-Harith."

[[The narrations 15514 and 15515: "Abu al-ʿAla' ibn al-Shikhkhir" is named after his grandfather. He is Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir al-ʿAmiri, a devout and trustworthy Successor, who used to read the Qur'an from the codex until he fainted, so his brother Mutarrif would say to him: "Set aside your codex for the rest of the day." Biographied in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Saʿd 7/1/113, al-Kabir 4/2/345, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/274.]]

15516. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Hawwa' used to bear children to Adam, and she would make them worship Allah, naming them "ʿUbayd Allah," "ʿAbd Allah," and similar names, but they would be struck by death. Then Iblis came to her and to Adam, and said: "If you were to name him by other than what you name him, he would live!" So she bore him a man, and he named him "ʿAbd al-Harith." Concerning this Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul﴾, to His words ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾, to the end of the verse.

15517. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words about Adam: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul﴾, to His words ﴿so she carried it lightly, and she passed on with it﴾, [and it was uncertain whether she had conceived or not]. ﴿So when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah their Lord: "If You give us a righteous child…"﴾, the verse. Then Satan came to them and said: "Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know what will happen? Will it be an animal or not?" And he adorned falsehood for them. ﴿Indeed, he is an obvious enemy.﴾ Before that she had borne two children who died. So Satan said to them: "If you do not name him after me, he will not come out sound, and he will die as the first two died!" So they named their child "ʿAbd al-Harith." That is His words: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾, the verse.

15518. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: When his first child was born to him, Iblis came to him and said: "I will advise you sincerely concerning this child of yours. Name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" Adam said: "I seek refuge in Allah from obeying you!" [Ibn ʿAbbas said: His name in heaven was "al-Harith."] Adam said: "I seek refuge in Allah from obeying you. I obeyed you concerning eating from the tree, and you expelled me from the Garden, so I will not obey you." So the child died. Then another child was born to him after that, and he said: "Obey me, or he will die as the first one died!" He disobeyed him, and the child died. Then Iblis said: "I will not stop killing them until you name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'." He kept at him until he named him "ʿAbd al-Harith." That is His words: ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾. He made him a partner in obedience, not in worship, and he did not associate others with Allah, but he obeyed him.

15519. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Harun, who said: al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit informed us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Neither Adam nor Hawwa' associated (partners). They had no child survive, and Satan came to them and said: "If it pleases you that a child should live for you, name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" That is His words: ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾. [[Narration 15519: In the printed edition the chain read "Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Harun." I do not know where the word "Salamah" came from! In the manuscript there is a blank space at this point, reading: "Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: ……, from Harun." I placed dots in the place of the blank. In the manuscript, after "ʿIkrimah" and before "said," there is a bracketed mark, and in the margin before the blank and beside this mark there is the letter (ṭ) and then beside it the letter (alif) with three dots. All this indicates doubt and error.
"Harun" is the grammarian al-Aʿwar, Harun ibn Musa al-Azdi, the reciter, a trustworthy narrator, who has passed at no. 4985 and 11693.
"al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit" is trustworthy, also passed at no. 4985 and 11693.
Abu Ja'far's chain in both places, in the narration of al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit from ʿIkrimah, is: "al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Harun al-Nahwi narrated to us, saying: al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah." I fear that the chain of Ibn Humayd and his report dropped out of the tafsir here, and then a chain came after it, which is Abu Ja'far's earlier chain: "al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Harun…" to the end of the chain. And Allah knows best.]]

15520. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Then when he covered her, she carried a light burden﴾. He said: Adam, peace be upon him, had no child who did not die. So Satan came to him and said: "If it pleases you that this child should live, name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" He did so. He said: So they made a partner in the name, but they did not make a partner in worship.

15521. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾: It was mentioned to us that they had no child who survived, so Satan came to them and said to them: "Name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" This was from the inspiration of Satan and his command. It was a partnership in obedience, not a partnership in worship.

15522. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them. But exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾. He said: Adam and his wife had no child who survived. Satan said to them: "When a child is born to you, name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" They did so and obeyed him. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾, the verse.

15523. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿When she became heavy, they both called upon Allah their Lord…﴾, to His words ﴿But exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾. He said: When Hawwa' conceived the first child she bore, when she became heavy, Iblis came to her before she gave birth and said: "O Hawwa', what is this in your belly?" She said: "I do not know." He said: "From where will it come out? From your nose, or your eye, or your ear?" She said: "I do not know." He said: "Do you see, if it comes out sound, will you obey me in what I command you?" [[In the printed edition: "Will you obey me," and the correct good reading is from the manuscript.]] She said: "Yes." He said: "Name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" [Iblis had been called al-Harith.] She said: "Yes." Then after that she said to Adam: "A comer came to me in a dream and said such and such to me." He said: "That is Satan, so beware of him, for he is our enemy who expelled us from the Garden!" Then Iblis came to her and repeated it to her, and she said: "Yes." When she gave birth to him, Allah brought him out sound, and she named him "ʿAbd al-Harith." That is His words: ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them, but exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾.

15524. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir and Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: It was said to him: Did Adam associate? He said: I seek refuge in Allah from claiming that Adam associated. But when Hawwa' became heavy, Iblis came to her and said: "From where will this come out, from your nose, or your eye, or your mouth?" He discouraged her, then said: "Do you see, if it comes out sound"—Ibn Fudayl added: "it will not harm you or kill you"—"will you obey me?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'!" She did so. Jarir added: "So his partnership was only in the name." [[In the printed edition: "shirkah" with a ta' at the end, and the correct reading is what I have given.]]

15525. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: She gave birth to a boy (meaning Hawwa') and Iblis came to them and said: "Name him 'my servant' or I will kill him!" Adam, peace be upon him, said to him: "I have obeyed you and you expelled me from the Garden!" He refused to obey him, so he named him "ʿAbd al-Rahman," and Allah gave Iblis power over him, and he killed him. She then conceived another; when she bore him, he said to her: "Name him 'my servant' or I will kill him!" Adam said to him: "I have obeyed you, and you expelled me from the Garden!" He refused, so he named him "Salih," and he killed him. When it was the third, he said to them both: "If you overcome me, then name him 'ʿAbd al-Harith'." [[In the printed edition: "If you are overcome, then name him," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] And that was the name of Iblis. Iblis was named so when he despaired (abalasa). So they submitted (ʿanaw) [[In the printed edition: "fa-fa'alu" ("they did"), which is a clear error. If it were correct it would say "fa-fa'ala" (he and she did). The manuscript's unpointed writing is what I have given, and its correct reading is what I have read. It is said: "ʿanā lahu yaʿnū," when one submits to him and obeys him.]], and that is when Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾, meaning in the naming.

* *

Others said: Rather, what is meant by this is a man and a woman from among the disbelievers of the children of Adam, who made partners for Allah from the gods and idols when He gave them the child they were granted. They said: The meaning of the speech is: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find rest in her. Then when he covered her, she carried a light burden, and when she became heavy﴾: that is, this disbelieving man, ﴿you two called upon Allah your Lord.﴾ They said: This is a case in which the speech began in the form of address, then returned to the report about the absent party, as it is said: ﴿He it is who conveys you through the land and the sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them with a good wind﴾ [Surah Yunus: 22]. We have already shown parallels to this with their evidences before. [[See what has passed: 1:154 / 3:304, 305 / 6:238, 464 / 8:447 / 11:264.]]

Those who said this:

15526. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾: He said: This was in some of the people of other religions, and it was not in Adam.

15527. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said: By this is meant the offspring of Adam, those among them who associated after him. He meant by His words: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them.﴾

15528. Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: They are the Jews and the Christians. Allah gave them children, and they made them Jews and Christians. [[The reports 15526-15528: see the comment on the earlier report no. 10013.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion of the one who said: By His words ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾ is meant the partnership in the name, not in worship, and that the one meant by this is Adam and Hawwa', because of the consensus of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon this.

* *

If someone says: Then what do you say, given that the matter is as you have described in the interpretation of this verse, and that the one meant by it is Adam and Hawwa', concerning His words ﴿exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾? Is it a disdain from Allah that He should have a partner in names, or in worship? If you say "in names," this is refuted by His words: ﴿Do they associate that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ And if you say "in worship," it will be said to you: Did Adam associate someone else in the worship of God's servants?

It is said to him: The matter in His words ﴿exalted is He above what they associate﴾ is not what you suppose. Rather, the meaning is: exalted is Allah above what the pagan Arabs associate with Him, the worshippers of idols. As for the report about Adam and Hawwa', it ended at His words ﴿they made partners for Him in what He had given them﴾, and then His words ﴿exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾ were resumed. [[See the comment on the report no. 155130.]] As:

Al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾, said: This is a separation from the story of Adam, specifically concerning the gods of the Arabs.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿shuraka'﴾ (partners).

The majority of the reciters of Madina, some of the Meccans, and some of the Kufans recited it as "jaʿalā lahu shirkan" with a kasra on the shin, meaning "partnership" (sharika). [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 400.]

Some of the Meccans, the majority of the Kufan reciters, and some of the Basran reciters recited it as ﴿jaʿalā lahu shurakāʾa﴾ with a damma on the shin, meaning the plural of "partner" (sharik).

Abu Ja'far said: This second recitation is the more correct of the two readings, because if the reading with a kasra on the shin were sound, the statement would have to be: "When He gave them a righteous child, they assigned to another a partnership in it." This is because Adam and Hawwa' did not believe that their child came from Iblis's gift, and then assign to Allah a share in it by naming him "servant of Allah." Rather, there is no doubt that they believed their child came from the provision and gift of Allah, and then they named him "servant of al-Harith," thereby assigning to Iblis a share in him by the name.

So if the reading of those who recite "shirkan" were correct, it would necessarily follow what we have said: that the statement would be "they assigned to another a share in it." The revelation of God's words ﴿jaʿalā lahu﴾ clarifies that the correct reading is ﴿shurakāʾ﴾ with a damma on the shin, as I explained earlier.

* *

If someone says: Adam and Hawwa' named their son "servant of al-Harith," and "al-Harith" is singular, while His words ﴿shurakāʾ﴾ are plural. How then does He, may His praise be exalted, describe them as having "made for Him partners," when they only associated one?

It is said: We have already shown earlier that the Arabs express a report about one person in the form of a report about a group, when they do not intend a specific individual or name him, as in His words ﴿Those to whom the people said: Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 173], whereas the one who said that was a single person, and the report was expressed in the form of a report about a group because he was not specifically intended. This is widespread in the speech and poetry of the Arabs.

* *

As for His words ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾, it is a declaration of Allah, blessed and exalted, of His own transcendence and magnification above what the wrongdoers say, and the gods and idols they claim alongside Him, as:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾: He said: It is "al-Inkaf"; He humbled Himself, may He be mighty and majestic — meaning He magnified Himself — and the angels humbled themselves to Him and glorified Him.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, saying: I heard Sadaqa narrate from al-Suddi, who said: This is from the connected and the separated: His words ﴿they assigned to Him partners in what He gave them﴾ concern the matter of Adam and Hawwa'; then Allah, blessed and exalted, said ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾, meaning above what the polytheists associate, and He did not mean the two of them.

[At this point the tenth part of our manuscript ends. At its end is the following text: "The tenth part of the book al-Bayan is complete, by the praise and help of Allah, His good success and His bounty. May Allah bless Muhammad. Next in the eleventh, God willing, is the discussion of His words: ﴿Do they associate with Him what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾. The copying was completed in the month of Jumada al-Ula, in the year 715 AH. May Allah forgive its scribe and its author, and whoever wrote it for him, and all Muslims. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds." Then the eleventh part of the manuscript begins: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. My Lord, make it easy and help."]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 191:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Do they associate with Him those that create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance. He says: Do they associate in the worship of God, worshipping alongside Him ﴿those that create nothing﴾, while He creates them and brings them into being? Pure worship belongs only to the Creator, not to the created.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

15532 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Adam and Eve had a child, and they named him "Abd Allah" (Servant of God). Iblis came to them and said: "What did you two name your son, O Adam and O Eve?" He said: Before that, they had had a child, and they named him "Abd Allah," but he died. So they said: "We named him 'Abd Allah.'" Iblis said: "Do you think that God will leave His servant with you? No, by God, He will surely take him away just as He took the other! But let me direct you to a name that will remain with you as long as you live: name him 'Abd Shams' (Servant of the Sun)!" He said: That is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿Do they associate with Him those that create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ Does the sun create anything, that it should have a servant? It is only created! The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "He deceived them twice: he deceived them in the Garden, and he deceived them on earth."

[[The report from the Messenger of God ﷺ I have not found. In al-Durr al-Manthur 3:152: "The Messenger of God ﷺ said: He deceived them twice. Zayd said: He deceived them in the Garden, and he deceived them on earth."]]

* *

It has also been said: ﴿and they themselves are created﴾: here the pronoun for them is put in the form of the pronoun for the sons of Adam, [[The "pronoun" (al-mukanna) here means the pronoun.]] and ﴿those that﴾ is expressed with "ma" rather than "man," in the manner of speaking about non-human beings, because what they used to worship was only a stone, wood, or copper, or some of the things about which one speaks with "ma" and not "man." Therefore it is said "ma," then it is said "wa-hum" (and they), and their pronoun is expressed in the manner of the pronoun for the sons of Adam, because the reference to them is made in the manner of the idolaters' veneration of them, similar to the reference to people's veneration of one another.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves﴾ [7:192]

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do these polytheists associate in worship with God that which creates nothing of God's creation, and which cannot help them if God intends harm for them or sends down punishment upon them, and which is not able, if He intends harm for it, to help itself or to ward off harm from itself? The worshipper worships only that which he worships in order to obtain benefit from it or to ward off harm from himself by it. Yet their gods, which they worship and associate in worship with God, neither benefit them nor harm them; rather, they cannot bring benefit to themselves nor ward off harm from themselves. So how could they be [able to bring] benefit to others than themselves, or to ward off harm from others, any more than from themselves? He, blessed and exalted, marvels at His creatures at the great error of those who associate with God others in their worship.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 193:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says, describing Him and mentioning the defect of what these polytheists associate with their worship of their Lord: Among its attributes is that you, O people, if you call them to the straight path and the correct, upright way, they will not follow you, because they do not understand anything, so as to leave the paths that deviate from the moderate course and take up what is straight and upright.

* *

Allah, exalted is His praise, intended by describing their gods with this attribute to alert them to the magnitude of their error and the ugliness of their choice. He, exalted is His praise, says: How, then, will one guide you to right guidance when, if he is called to right guidance and it is made known to him, he does not recognize it, and does not understand right guidance from error, and it is the same for him whether his caller calls him to right guidance or remains silent, because he does not understand his call, does not hear his voice, and does not comprehend what is said to him? He says: How, then, is one whose attribute is this worshipped, or how could the magnitude of the ignorance of the one who takes as a god what has this attribute be disguised? Rather, the Lord who is worshipped is the one who benefits those who worship Him, harms those who disobey Him, helps His friend, forsakes His enemy, guides to right guidance those who obey Him, and hears the supplication of those who call upon Him.

* *

It has been said: ﴿It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾.
