Here he conjoined "silent" (ṣāmitūn), which is a noun, to "you called them" (ʾadaʿawtumūhum), which is a past-tense verb, and did not say "am ṣamamtum" (or have you been silent), as in the verse of the poet, whose composer I have not identified:

It is the same for you whether the departure (al-nafr) or you spent a night with the people of the domes of Numayr ibn ʿAmir.

And it is recited: "am anta bāʾitun" (or are you one who spends the night).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 194:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah are servants like you, so call upon them and let them respond to you, if you are truthful.﴾ (7:194)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says to these polytheists, worshippers of idols, rebuking them for their worship of idols that neither harm them nor benefit them: ﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke﴾, O polytheists, as gods, ﴿besides Allah﴾, and worship, as shirk (association of partners with God) and disbelief in Allah on your part, ﴿are servants like you﴾, meaning: they are possessions of your Lord, just as you are His possessions. ﴿So if you are truthful﴾ that they can harm and benefit, and that they deserve worship from you because of their benefit to you, then let them respond to your call when you call upon them. [[See the explanation of "response" (al-istijabah) in what has preceded: 3:483, 484 / 7:486-488 / 11:341.]] If they do not respond to you, because they do not hear your supplication, then be certain that they neither benefit nor harm; for harm and benefit only come from one who, when asked, hears the request of the one who asks and gives and bestows favour, and who, when complained to about something, hears, so that he harms the one who deserves punishment and benefits the one who does not deserve harm.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Have they feet with which they walk, or have they hands with which they strike, or have they eyes with which they see, or have they ears with which they hear?﴾ ﴿Say: Call upon your associates, then scheme against me, and give me no respite.﴾ (7:195)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty God says to those who worshipped idols besides Him, making them aware of the ignorance in which they persist: Do your idols, O people, have ﴿feet with which they walk﴾, so that they run with you and for you in your needs, and move about for your benefit? ﴿Or have they hands with which they strike﴾, so that they repel for you and support you with them when someone intends you harm or evil? ﴿Or have they eyes with which they see﴾, so that they inform you of what they have witnessed and seen of things hidden from you that you do not see? ﴿Or have they ears with which they hear﴾, so that they tell you what they have heard, apart from you, of what you have not heard?

He, may His praise be exalted, says: If your gods that you worship have none of these instruments I have mentioned, and what is honoured is only honoured for the benefits hoped from it, which reach it through some of these meanings in your view, then what is the reason for your worshipping your idols, when they are empty of all these things by which benefit is obtained and harm is averted?

As for His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon your associates, then scheme against me﴾, [Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worship idols: Call upon your associates whom you have made partners with God in worship] ﴿then scheme against me﴾, [[This phrase enclosed in parentheses I have inferred from the context of the verse and the interpretation. It is evident that it has dropped out from the copyist's text, and that the statement does not hold without it, or without something that stands in its place.]] you and they [[In the printed edition: "you and them", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. See also the explanation of "kayd" (scheming) earlier, p. 288, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿and give me no respite﴾ [[See the explanation of "inzar" (respite) earlier, 12:331, note 1, and the references there.]], meaning: do not delay in scheming and plotting, but hasten to it. By this, may His praise be exalted, He informs him that they will not harm him, that He has protected him from them, and He makes the unbelievers aware of the powerlessness of their idols to support those who would wish their allies harm.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 196–197:

The exposition of His saying: ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous.﴾ (7:196)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists among the worshippers of idols: "Indeed, my protector (walī)," meaning my helper, supporter and backer against you [[See the explanation of "al-walī" in the earlier linguistic indexes under (w-l-y).]], is ﴿Allah, who sent down the Book﴾ to me with the truth, and He is the One who takes charge of those among His creation whose deeds are upright through their obedience.

* *

The exposition of His saying: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ (7:197)

Abu Ja'far said: This is also a command from Allah, mighty and majestic is His praise, to His Prophet to say to the polytheists. His remembrance, exalted is He, says to him: [[In the printed edition: "bi-qawlihi ta'ala" (with His saying, exalted is He); in the manuscript it is similar but unpointed; the correct reading is "yaqulu lahu" (says to him).]] Say to them: Indeed Allah is my helper and supporter, while those you invoke, O polytheists, besides Allah, from among the deities, cannot help you, and nor can they, despite their inability to help you, help themselves. So which of these two is more deserving of worship and more worthy of divinity? Is it the One who supports His protégé and protects Himself from whomever wills Him harm, or the one who cannot support his protégé and is unable to protect himself from whoever wills and seeks to harm him?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 196–197:

The exposition of His saying: ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous.﴾ (7:196)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists among the worshippers of idols: "Indeed, my protector (walī)," meaning my helper, supporter and backer against you [[See the explanation of "al-walī" in the earlier linguistic indexes under (w-l-y).]], is ﴿Allah, who sent down the Book﴾ to me with the truth, and He is the One who takes charge of those among His creation whose deeds are upright through their obedience.

* *

The exposition of His saying: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ (7:197)

Abu Ja'far said: This is also a command from Allah, mighty and majestic is His praise, to His Prophet to say to the polytheists. His remembrance, exalted is He, says to him: [[In the printed edition: "bi-qawlihi ta'ala" (with His saying, exalted is He); in the manuscript it is similar but unpointed; the correct reading is "yaqulu lahu" (says to him).]] Say to them: Indeed Allah is my helper and supporter, while those you invoke, O polytheists, besides Allah, from among the deities, cannot help you, and nor can they, despite their inability to help you, help themselves. So which of these two is more deserving of worship and more worthy of divinity? Is it the One who supports His protégé and protects Himself from whomever wills Him harm, or the one who cannot support his protégé and is unable to protect himself from whoever wills and seeks to harm him?

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear; and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to the polytheists: And if you call, O polytheists, your gods to guidance, which is uprightness and rectitude, ﴿they will not hear﴾, meaning they will not hear your call; ﴿and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see﴾.

* * *

This is an address from God to His Prophet ﷺ. He says: And you see, O Muhammad, their gods looking at you, yet they do not see. That is why He used the singular. [[Meaning: the address was first to the polytheists collectively, when He said "And if you call them," then He said "and you see them" in the singular, addressing the Messenger of God ﷺ.]] Had the Prophet ﷺ been commanded to address the polytheists, He would have said: "And you see them looking at you." [[In the manuscript: "And you see them looking at you..." and after "at you" there is a blank space about the size of one word. What is in the printed edition is close to correct.]]

* * *

It has been related from al-Suddi concerning this:

15533 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear; and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see﴾, he said: "These are the polytheists."

* * *

The statement of al-Suddi may imply that by his words "these are the polytheists" he meant God's saying ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear﴾. Mujahid also said concerning this:

15534 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see﴾: "What you call them to guidance." It seems Mujahid directed the meaning of the statement toward this: "And you see the polytheists looking at you, yet they do not see." This is a valid reading, but the speech is in the context of informing about the gods, so the description fits them better.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What is the meaning of His saying ﴿and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see﴾? Is it permissible for a thing to look at another thing without seeing it?

It is said: The Arabs say of a thing that faces or is opposite another thing: "It looks toward such-and-such," and it is said: "The dwelling of so-and-so looks toward my dwelling," when it faces it. It is reported from them: "When you come to such-and-such a place, and the mountain looks at you [fa-nazara ilayka al-jabal], take right or left." I was told on the authority of Abu Ubayd, who said: al-Kisa'i said: "The wall looks at you" when it is near you, where you can see it. From this is the words of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

When you look at the lands of Bani Tamim with an eye, or the lands of Bani Subah,

We shot them with every hard, full-breasted [arrow], and with young men of the morning and the evening.

I do not know what "Bani Habib" is. As for "Bani Subah," they are in Dabba, and it is apparent that other Arabs also have a "Bani Subah." See al-Ishtiqaq: 122. The version in Abu Zayd's Nawadir is "When the lands of Bani Habib..." with "with an eye or the lands of Bani Subah." The version of al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Faris is "the lands of Bani Numayr." I do not know which is correct until the poet and those to whom it is attributed are known. Al-Zamakhshari, before citing the poem, said: "The land looked [nazarat] with one eye or two eyes," when it appeared on land where livestock graze, without full growth. Ibn Faris said: when the plant sprouts. All of this is taken figuratively, as a metaphor and a comparison.

He means: its plants and herbage face and are opposite each other.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement is: And you see, O Muhammad, the gods of these polytheists who worship idols, facing you and opposite you, yet they do not see you, for they have no sight. It was said "And you see them" and not "And you see it" because they are images fashioned in the likeness of the sons of Adam, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 199:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, and enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ (199)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its interpretation is: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾ from the dispositions of people, which is what is easy and does not burden them. [(1) See the explanation of "al-'afw" above, 4: 337 - 343.]

Those who said this:

15535 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, he said: from the dispositions of people and their deeds, without probing (bi-ghayr tahassus). [(2) In the manuscript here, and in the next report, number 15539, it is "tahassis" with a yā', and I do not know what it is. "Tahassasa al-shay'" means to search for and seek something, as if he means exhaustive seeking; what comes later at number 15542 supports this.]

15536 - Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, he said: the forgiveness of people's dispositions and the forgiveness of their affairs.

15537 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad related to me, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, ... the verse. 'Urwah said: God commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take forgiveness from the dispositions of people. [(1) The report 15537: al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 229) by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Barrad, from Abu Usamah, from Hisham, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. See what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said about it.]

15538 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: God did not send down this verse except concerning the dispositions of people: ﴿Hold to forgiveness and enjoin what is right﴾, the verse. [(2) The report 15538: "Hisham ibn 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr" is trustworthy (thiqah), well known, and has passed several times. His father "'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr" narrates from his brother "'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr." In the printed edition here it was "'an Abi al-Zubayr," which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.

This is a sound report, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 299), and it will come later as number 15541, with a different chain.]

15539 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached me from Mujahid: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾: from the dispositions of people and their deeds, without probing. [See the earlier note, p. 326, no. 2.]

15540 - ... He said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, he said: from the dispositions of people; by God, I will take it from them as long as you keep company. [The report 15540: "Ibn al-Zubayr" is 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr; in the manuscript and the printed edition here it was "Abi al-Zubayr," which is an error we have corrected above.]

15541 - ... He said: 'Ubaydah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Ibn al-Zubayr [in the printed edition here "from Abi al-Zubayr," which is an error as I have already noted], who said: God only sent down: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, from the dispositions of people.

15542 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, he said: from the dispositions of people and their deeds, without probing, or spying (tajassus), Abu 'Asim doubted. [The "tajassus" is like "tahassus," with slight difference; see what passed on p. 326, note 2.]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: take forgiveness from the wealth of people, which is the surplus. They said: He was commanded with that before the obligation of zakat was revealed, and when zakat was revealed, it was abrogated (nusikha).

Those who said this:

15543 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾, meaning: take what is left over to you from their wealth, and whatever they bring you of something, take it. This was before Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) was revealed with the obligations of alms and their details, and where the alms reached.

15544 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾. As for "al-'afw": it is the surplus of wealth; zakat abrogated it.

15545 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾: take what is left over from their wealth. And this was before the obligatory charity was revealed.

* *

Others said: Rather, that is a command from God to His Prophet ﷺ to pardon the polytheists and to abandon harshness toward them, before fighting them was made obligatory upon him.

Those who said this:

15546 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾: He commanded him, so he turned away from them for ten years in Mecca. He said: Then He commanded him to be harsh toward them, to sit for them at every lookout, to besiege them, then He said: ﴿But if they repent and establish prayer﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 5, 11], the verse, all of it. And he recited: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 73 / Surat al-Tahrim: 9]. He said: And He commanded the believers to be harsh with them, saying: ﴿O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you, and let them find harshness in you﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 123], after He had commanded them to pardon. And he recited the saying of God: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾ [Surat al-Jathiyah: 14]. Then He did not accept from them after that except Islam or death, so this verse abrogated the forgiveness. [Another report passed under number 4175, which mentions this verse and its interpretation on that basis from Ibn 'Abbas.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: take forgiveness from the dispositions of people, and abandon harshness toward them; and he said: the Prophet of God ﷺ was commanded with that concerning the polytheists.

We only said that this is more correct because God, majestic is His praise, followed that with teaching His Prophet ﷺ to argue with the polytheists in speech, which is His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon your associates, then plot against me and give me no respite﴾, and He followed it with His saying: ﴿Whereas their brethren extend them in error, then they do not desist. And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: why have you not chosen it?﴾. So what lies between these is, by being part of His disciplining of His Prophet ﷺ in his dealings with them, more fitting and more correct than the objection that it concerns his command to take alms from the Muslims.

* *

If someone says: Is it then abrogated?

It is said: We have no evidence that it is abrogated, since it was possible that it be [the case that] — even though God sent it down to His Prophet ﷺ in regard to his acquaintance with ten of the polytheists who had not been commanded to fight them — it is intended as the disciplining of the Prophet of God and the Muslims all together in dealing with people, and commanding them to take the forgiveness of their dispositions. So it would be, though it was sent down concerning them, an instruction from God for His creation regarding the attribute of dealing with one another; [if] it is not obligatory to employ harshness and severity toward some of them. [If] it becomes obligatory to employ that toward them, the obligatory is employed. So His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness﴾ is a command to take it as long as nothing other than forgiveness is obligatory; if something other than it becomes obligatory, the obligatory is taken, and what is not obligatory too when that is possible. Therefore the verse is not judged to be abrogated, for what we have explained about its counterparts in more than one place in our books. [See Abu Ja'far's discussion of "naskh" in the indexes of the earlier volumes.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its interpretation.

Some of them said, with what:

15547 - Al-Hasan ibn al-Zabarqan al-Nakha'i narrated to me, saying: Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to me, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from a man whom he named, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, and enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: O Jibril, what is this? He said: I do not know until I ask the knowledgeable one! He said: Then Jibril said: O Muhammad, God commands you to join the one who cuts you off, to give to the one who withholds from you, and to pardon the one who wronged you. [The report 15547: "al-Hasan ibn al-Zabarqan al-Nakha'i" is the teacher of al-Tabari, passed under number 2995. The man not named in this report is "Ummi ibn Rabi'ah," who comes in the following report.]

15548 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Ummay, who said: When God sent down to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, and enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Prophet ﷺ said: What is this, O Jibril? He said: God commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join the one who cut you off. [The report 15548: "Sufyan" is Ibn 'Uyaynah. "Ummay" is "Ummay ibn Rabi'ah al-Muradi al-Sayrafi," who heard al-Sha'bi, 'Ata', and Tawus. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Shari k narrated from him. Trustworthy (thiqah). Biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 6: 254, al-Kabir 1/2/67, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/347. In the manuscript above "Ummi" there was a mark (ṭ) indicating an error, and in the margin (kadha); but the copyist did not know the name, so it became unclear to him. In the printed edition it was made "Ubayy," as also in Ibn Kathir 3: 618; the correct reading is what is adopted here. This report was related by "Ummi ibn Rabi'ah" from al-Sha'bi, as is apparent from the versions of the report in Ibn Kathir and al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 153.]

* *

Others said, with what:

15549 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾, he says: with what is known (al-ma'ruf).

15550 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾, he said: As for "al-'urf": it is "al-ma'ruf."

15551 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾, that is: what is known (al-ma'ruf).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is to say: God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to command people with "al-'urf," which is "al-ma'ruf" in the speech of the Arabs, a verbal noun in the sense of "al-ma'ruf."

* *

It is said: "I gave him 'urfan, and 'arifan, and 'arifatan," all of which have the meaning of "al-ma'ruf." [The word "'arifan" I did not find in the lexicons, and it is correct, I believe. See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" above, p. 165, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

So when the meaning of "al-'urf" is that, then from "al-ma'ruf" is maintaining ties of kinship with the one who cut them, giving to the one who withheld, and pardoning the one who wronged. Every act God has commanded or recommended is from "al-'urf." God did not single out from that one meaning over another; so the truth concerning it is to say: God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to command His servants with all of "al-ma'ruf," not with some of its meanings to the exclusion of others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, it is a command from God, exalted is He, to His Prophet ﷺ to turn away from the one who is ignorant. [See the explanation of "al-i'rad" above, 12: 32, note 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-jahl" above, 2: 183 / 8: 89-92 / 11: 339, 340, 393, 394.] And that, though it is a command from God to His Prophet, is a disciplining by Him, great is His mention, of His creation to bear with those who wronged them or transgressed against them; [meaning that "al-jahl" here means folly, rebellion, and aggression, not the "ignorance" that is the opposite of knowledge and recognition.] not by turning away from the one who is ignorant of the obligation owed to him regarding God's right, nor by overlooking the one who disbelieved in God and was ignorant of His oneness, and who is at war with the Muslims.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

15552 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, and enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, he said: These are dispositions which God commanded His Prophet ﷺ with, and guided him to.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 200:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ (7:200)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you﴾, He means: if Satan provokes you to anger, an anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant and drives you to repay them. ﴿Then seek refuge in Allah﴾, meaning: then seek Allah's protection from his prompting [[See the explanation of "al-isti'adhah" (seeking refuge) earlier: 1/111 and 6/326.]] ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing﴾, meaning: indeed Allah, whom you seek refuge in from Satan's prompting, is ﴿Hearing﴾ of the ignorant person's foolishness towards you, and of your seeking refuge in Him from his prompting, and of other speech of His creatures, nothing of which is hidden from Him. ﴿Knowing﴾ of what removes the prompting of Satan from you, and of other matters concerning His creation. [[See the explanation of "Hearing" (sami') and "Knowing" (alim) earlier, in the language indexes under the roots (s-m-' ) and (' -l-m).]] As related:

15553 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Take what is given freely, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then what about anger, O Lord?" He said: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

15554 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ He said: "Allah knew that this enemy is strong and defiant."

* *

The root of "nazgh" (نزغ, prompting/provocation) is corruption. It is said: "Satan incited discord (nazgh) among the people" when he corrupted their relations and set some of them against others. From it one says "nazagha yanzughu" and "naghaza yanghuzu."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, remember [Him], and then they are seeing [clearly]﴾ [7:201]

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Indeed, those who fear [Allah]﴾ — [they are] those among His creation who fear Him, so they fear His punishment, by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobediences — ﴿when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-massu" (touching) earlier, p. 303, note 1, and the references there.]] — meaning: when a fit of madness (lamam) from Satan befalls them, from anger or something else that turns them away from the obligation of Allah's right over them, they remember the punishment of Allah and His reward, His promise and His threat, and they see the truth and act upon it, and they turn to obeying Allah in what He has enjoined upon them, and they abandon obeying Satan in it. [[In the printed edition: "idha alamma bihim tayf" (when a phantom befell them), which misreads the manuscript, so it was replaced by what was in it.]]

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying "ṭayf."

The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa recited it: ﴿ṭā'if﴾, on the pattern of "fā'il."

* *

And some of the Meccan, Basran and Kufan readers recited: "ṭayfun min ash-shaytan." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an lil-Qurra' 1:402.]]

* *

The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning the distinction between "al-ṭā'if" and "al-ṭayf."

Some of the Basrans said: "al-ṭā'if" and "al-ṭayf" are the same, and it is that which is like a phantom or a thing that visits you. [[Abu Ja'far attributed this to the Basrans, and it is in Lisan al-Arab (ṭwf), attributed to al-Farra', who was a Kufan, and I did not find it in the printed Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]] He said: It is permissible that "al-ṭayf" be a lightened form of "ṭayyif," like "mayt" and "mayyit."

* *

Some of the Kufans said: "al-ṭā'if" is what circles you of the whisperings of Satan. As for "al-ṭayf," it is only from lamam (madness) and touching.

* *

Another of them said: "al-ṭayf" is lamam, and "al-ṭā'if" is everything that circles around a person.

* *

It is reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he used to say: "al-ṭayf" is whispering (waswasa).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations in my view is the recitation of the one who recites ﴿ṭā'ifun min ash-shaytan﴾, because the people of interpretation interpreted it to mean anger and a slip that comes from the one who circles around. When that is its meaning, it becomes known — since "al-ṭayf" is in fact a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker "ṭāfa yaṭīfu" — that it is a report from Allah about what touches those who fear Him from Satan, and what touches them is only what circles around them of its causes, such as anger and whispering. Satan only circles around the son of Adam in order to make him slip from obedience to his Lord, or to whisper to him. Whispering and causing slips is the "ṭā'if min ash-shaytan." [[From his saying: "As for al-ṭayf" to the end of the second paragraph ending with a line of poetry, I have no doubt that it was placed in the wrong position, for he says afterwards: "and he says: I have not heard in that," and this speaker is undoubtedly other than Abu Ja'far, and I could not determine his place among the earlier statements, so I left it where it was and separated it. Its proper place was before his saying: "Abu Ja'far said: And the more correct of the two recitations..."]]

* *

As for "al-ṭayf," it is indeed the phantom, and it is a verbal noun from "ṭāfa yaṭīfu," and he says: I have not heard "ṭāfa yaṭīfu" in that [meaning "al-ṭā'if"], and he interprets it as meaning "al-mayt" (the dead), which is from the root with waw. [[His saying: "I have not heard in that ṭāfa yaṭīfu," meaning in "al-ṭā'if."]]

* *

The Basrans and some of the Kufans related from the Arabs by hearing: "ṭāfa yaṭīfu," and "ṭift uṭīfu," and they recited in support of that: [[This is the exact text of Abu 'Ubayda's words in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:237, to the end.]] Ka'b ibn Zuhayr:

Annā alamma bika al-khayālu yaṭīfu / wa-maṭāfuhu laka dhikratun wa-shu'ūfu [[From his Diwan: 113; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1:237; and Lisan (ṭyf) (shf), from a long qasida of his. "Shu'ūf" is a verbal noun from their saying "sha'afahu hubb fulānatin," when it burns his heart, and he finds the pleasure of the anguish in its burning, and in the loss of his reason so that he understands nothing but love.]]

* *

As for the interpretation, they differed concerning its meaning.

Some of them said: that "al-ṭā'if" is anger.

Those who said that:

15556 - Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id: ﴿when an impulse touches them﴾ he said: and "al-ṭayf" is anger.

15557 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "when an impulse from Satan touches them," he said: it is anger. [[I left what is in the narrations as it came in the manuscript: "ṭā'if" once and "ṭayf" another time, and they are two recitations of the verse as preceded before.]]

15558 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Juraj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, he said: anger.

15559 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "when a ṭayf from Satan touches them, they remember," he said: it is anger.

15560 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "ṭā'if min ash-shaytan," he said: anger.

* *

Others said: it is the passing thought (lamma) and slip from Satan.

Those who said that:

15561 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Indeed, those who fear [Allah], when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember," and "al-ṭā'if" is a passing thought from Satan — ﴿then they are seeing﴾.

15562 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them," he says: a prick (nazgh) from Satan — ﴿they remember﴾.

15563 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember﴾, he says: when they slip, they repent.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These two interpretations are close in meaning, for "anger" is from the enticement of Satan, and "lamma" (passing thought) from sin is also from him, and all of that is from the circling of Satan. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "wa-kāna dhālika" (and that was), and the correct reading is what I have established.]] Since that is the case, there is no basis for restricting its meaning to one sense rather than another; rather the correct view is that it is general, as His exalted praise made it general, so it is said: Indeed, those who fear Allah, when some occurrence from the causes of Satan befalls them, whatever that occurrence is, they remember the command of Allah and turn to His command.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then they are seeing﴾, it means: then they are seeing the guidance of Allah, His clarification, and His obedience in it, so they desist from what the impulse of Satan calls them to. As [is narrated]:

15564 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿then they are seeing﴾, he says: then they are desisting from disobedience, holding to the command of Allah, disobeying Satan.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 202:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And the brothers of the devils, the devils draw them on further into error." [[See the explanation of "al-ghayy" (error) earlier, p. 261, note 1, and the references there.]] By His words ﴿yamuddunahum﴾ (draw them on), He means: they increase them. ﴿Thumma la yuqsirun﴾ (then they do not hold back) means: they do not fall short of what those who are God-fearing fall short of when a passing thought from Satan touches them. [[In the printed edition: "then they do not hold back from what those who fear God hold back from." I have retained what is in the manuscript, and Abu Hayyan mentions something similar in his tafsir (4:451), saying: "then they do not diminish from their being aided and their misguidance." Therefore I have left the manuscript reading as it is, though I am uncertain of its soundness.]]

This is only a report from God about the two groups of faith and disbelief: that the group of faith and the people of God-consciousness, when Satan causes them to slip, remember the greatness of God and His punishment, so His awe restrains them from His disobedience and returns them to repentance and turning back to God from what had been a lapse on their part. And that the group of disbelievers, Satan increases them in their error when they commit an act of disobedience to God, and the fear of God does not restrain them, nor does the fear of returning to Him stop them from persisting in it and adding to it. So they are always increasing in committing sin, and Satan always increases them; the human does not fall short of any of the committing of abominations, nor does Satan cease from his extension of it. [[This is how al-Tabari did it: he gave the pronouns in the singular after the plural, and this recurs in many places in his tafsir; the closest of them is what I pointed out on p. 286, note 2.]] As:

15564 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾: He said: The humans do not hold back from the evil deeds they do, and the devils do not refrain from them.

15565 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾. He said: They are the jinn, who inspire their allies among mankind. ﴿And they do not hold back﴾: they do not tire.

15566 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error﴾: the brothers of the devils from among the polytheists; the devil draws them on into error. ﴿And they do not hold back﴾.

15567 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: ﴿And their brothers﴾ are from the jinn, who draw their brothers from mankind on [further]. ﴿And they do not hold back﴾: he says, the human does not hold back. He said: "al-madd" (drawing on) is increase, meaning the people of polytheism; he says: the people of polytheism do not hold back as those who are God-conscious hold back; they do not repent (la yar'awun), faith does not restrain them. [[In the printed edition, in place of "la yar'awun" there is a different reading; the manuscript has "la yar'awun", and the correct reading is what I have given. "Ir'awwa 'an al-qabih" means: to feel remorse, then turn away from it and desist.]] Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: ﴿And their brothers﴾ are from the devils; ﴿draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾: as ignorance, they draw on the people of polytheism. Ibn Jurayj said: [And] ﴿Indeed, We have created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 179]. He said: These are mankind. God says: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error﴾.

15568 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾, he said: the brothers of the devils; the devils draw them on into error. ﴿And they do not hold back﴾.

15569 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And their brothers﴾ are from the devils. ﴿Draw them on further into error﴾, as ignorance.

* *

Some of them interpreted His words ﴿thumma la yuqsirun﴾ (then they do not hold back) to mean: nor do the devils cease in their extension of their brothers into error.

Those who said this:

15570 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And their brothers draw them on further into error, and they do not hold back﴾: from them, and they do not show mercy to them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown which of the two interpretations is more correct to us. We chose what we chose in this matter for the reason we have explained: because God, in the verse before it, described the people of faith in Him and their restraint from His disobedience and from what He dislikes, moving toward His love when they remember His greatness; then He followed that with the report about the brothers of the devils and their commission of His disobedience. So it was more fitting to describe them by their persistence in it, since it came directly after the report about the believers' restraint from it.

* *

As for His words ﴿yamuddunahum﴾ (draw them on), the readers differed in its recitation.

Some of the Medinan readers recited it as "yumiddunahum," with a damma on the ya' from "amadadtu."

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited it as ﴿yamuddunahum﴾, with a fatha on the ya' from "maddtu."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is ﴿yamuddunahum﴾ with a fatha on the ya', because what the devils draw their brothers among the polytheists on is only an increase of the same kind as what is drawn on, and when what is drawn on is of the same kind, the Arabic usage is "maddtu," not "amadtu." [[See the explanation of "madd" and "amadd" earlier, 1:306–308 / 7:181.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿yuqsirun﴾ (they hold back), the readers follow the dialect of one who says "aqsartu uqsir." The Arabs have two usages in this: "qasara 'an al-shay'" and "aqsara 'anhu." [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:402, where he corrected the error, for he vowelled "qasara" with a damma on the sad, whereas the correct form is a fatha, with no other correct form.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 203:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why do you not choose one?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: And when you, O Muhammad, do not bring these polytheists a sign from God, ﴿they say: "Why do you not choose one?"﴾ That is, they say: "Why do you not select it and pick it out?"

[See the explanation of "lawla" (why not) above, 11:356, note 2, and the references there.] This is from the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 179], meaning: He selects and chooses. We have already explained this in its places, with its evidence. [See the explanation of "ijtaba" (to choose) above, 7:437 / 11:512, 513.]

* *

Then the interpreters differed in the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning is: "Why do you not fabricate it on your own account and invent it?" That is, "Why do you not choose it by invention?" As the Arabs say: "So-and-so chose this matter and selected it by invention." [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:402, and the commentary there. This is a very strange meaning of "ikhtiyar" (choosing), about which I have doubts, unless he intended that the Arabs say in their figurative speech "he chose the thing by invention", all of which means "he invented it", not that "ikhtara" means "iktalaqa" (invented). Although the author of Lisan al-Arab followed the later saying of al-Farra' after p. 343: "It is permissible in Arabic speech to say: 'He chose for you the thing, selected it and improvised it'."]

Those who said this:

15571 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why do you not choose one?"﴾ That is: "Why do you not bring it to us from your own self?" This is the saying of the disbelievers of Quraysh.

15572 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why do you not choose one?"﴾ They said: "Why do you not improvise it!" [("Iqtada'a al-kalam iqtida'an" means he improvised the speech without preparation or prior arrangement. It is said: "This is improvised poetry, and an improvised book."] They said: "You bring it out of yourself."

15573 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say: "Why do you not choose one?"﴾ They said: "Why do you not fabricate it, bringing it from your own self?"

15574 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Why do you not choose it?﴾ He says: "Why do you not receive it?" And at another time he said: "Why do you not originate it and create it?"

15575 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿They say: "Why do you not choose it?"﴾ He says: "Why do you not originate it?"

15576 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Why do you not choose it?﴾ He said: "Why do you not bring it from your own self!"

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Why do you not take it from your Lord and accept it from Him?" [In the printed and manuscript texts, at this place and the one following it in the report: "taqabbaltaha" (accepted it), and in the report after that: "talaqqaytaha" (received it); in the manuscript and print, and I hope the latter is the correct reading, as was mentioned in no. 15574, although the former is permissible.]

Those who said this:

15577 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Why do you not choose it?﴾ He says: "Why do you not accept it from God!"

15578 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Why do you not choose it?﴾ He says: "Why do you not receive it from your Lord!"

15579 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Why do you not choose it?﴾ He says: "Why do you not take it yourself and bring it from heaven?"

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said its meaning is: "Why do you not originate it from your own self!" due to the indication of God's saying: ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This is insights from your Lord"﴾, which clarifies that God only commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to answer them by informing about himself that he only follows what his Lord sends down to him and reveals to him, not that he originates speech from his own self and creates it and then calls people to it.

* *

It is related from al-Farra' that he used to say: "Ijtabaytu al-kalam" and "iktalaqtuhu" and "irtajaltuhu": when you fabricate it from your own self. [See what has passed above, p. 341, note 2.]

15580 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us from him.

* *

Abu Ubayda said: Abu Zayd used to say: The Arabs only say that for speech that a man initiates, which he had not prepared beforehand in his mind. Abu Ubayd said: "Ikhtara'tuhu" is similar to that.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿This is insights from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ (203)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you when you do not bring them a sign: "Why do you not originate it from your own self!": That is not for me, and it is not permissible for me to do it, because God only commanded me to follow what is revealed to me from Him. I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord, for I am His servant, to His command I submit, and Him I obey. [See the explanation of "al-ittiba'" (following) and "al-wahy" (revelation) in the language indices above, under the roots (t-b-') and (w-h-y).] ﴿This is insights from your Lord﴾, that is: this Qur'an and the revelation that I recite to you, ﴿insights from your Lord﴾, that is: proofs against you and clarification for you from your Lord.

* *

Its singular is "basirah", as His exalted saying: ﴿This is insights for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾ [Surah al-Jathiyah: 20]. [See the explanation of "basirah" above, 12:23, 24.]

* *

"This" is mentioned in the singular in His saying: ﴿This is insights from your Lord﴾ only because, as I described, it refers to the Qur'an and the revelation.

* *

His saying: ﴿And guidance﴾, that is: a clarification that guides the believers to the straight path. ﴿And mercy﴾, by which God shows mercy to His believing servants, rescuing them by it from error and destruction. ﴿For a people who believe﴾, that is: it is insights from God, guidance and mercy for whoever believes, that is, for whoever affirms that the Qur'an is the revelation and inspiration of God and acts upon what is in it, as opposed to whoever denies it, rejects it and disbelieves in it. [See the explanation of "al-huda" (guidance), "al-rahmah" (mercy) and "al-iman" (faith) in the language indices above, under the roots (h-d-y), (r-h-m), (a-m-n).] Rather, it is blindness and disgrace upon those who do not believe in it. [In the print edition it reads "ghamm" and in the manuscript "amm" without dots, and this is the correct reading, due to God's saying in Surah Fussilat 44, describing the Qur'an: "And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness upon them."]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 7, Verse 204**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy﴾ (7:204).

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God says to the believers in Him, who affirm His Book, for whom the Qur'an is guidance and mercy: ﴿When it is recited﴾, to you, O believers, ﴿the Qur'an, then listen to it﴾, meaning: give it your ears, so that you may understand its verses and take heed of its admonitions [[See the explanation of "istama'a" (listen) in the earlier linguistic indices under (s-m-‘).]] = ﴿and be silent﴾ to it, so that you may comprehend and reflect upon it, and do not engage in idle talk during it, so that you do not comprehend it = ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾, meaning: that your Lord may show you mercy by your heeding its admonitions, your taking lessons from its warnings, and your acting upon the obligations that your Lord has made clear to you in it.

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the circumstance in which God commanded listening to and silence for the reciter of the Qur'an when he recites.

Some of them said: This refers to the situation of the worshipper in prayer behind an imam whom he follows, who hears the imam's recitation; he must listen to his recitation. They said: This verse was revealed concerning this.

He said: Then the Qur'an came down: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾. [[The report 15581: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash is a well-known trustworthy narrator, mentioned several times before. ʿAsim is ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, also known as ʿAsim ibn Bahdala, a trustworthy narrator mentioned before. al-Musayyab ibn Rafiʿ al-Asadi is a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi) who did not meet Ibn Masʿud; he was mentioned under nos. 128 and 6175. It is coordinated with what precedes it, as if he said: and that there is no time in which silence is required for the one who hears it from its reciter.]] The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has been authenticated with what we have mentioned of his saying: "When the imam recites, then be silent." Therefore silence behind him for his recitation is obligatory upon the one who follows him as a listener to his recitation, by the general apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾ (7:205)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And remember﴾, O listener who attends silently to the Qur'an when it is recited in prayer or in a sermon. [[Ibn Kathir refuted what al-Tabari held in his tafsir (commentary) of this verse, saying: "Ibn Jarir claimed, and before him ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, that it means commanding the listener to the Qur'an, while he is listening, to remember in this manner. This is far-fetched and contradicts the silence that is commanded. Moreover, the meaning of that in prayer is as previously mentioned, or in prayer and sermon. It is known that silence at that time is better than remembrance by the tongue, whether quietly or aloud. What these two said has not been followed by anyone. Rather, the meaning is an exhortation to frequent remembrance by the worshippers in the mornings and evenings, lest they be among the heedless." Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3: 626, 627. What he said is the pure truth, God willing.]] ﴿Your Lord within yourself﴾, he says: take admonition from what is in the verses of the Qur'an, reflect upon it, and remember your return to Him when you hear it. ﴿Humbly﴾, he says: do that in humility before God and submission to Him. [[See the explanation of "tadarru'" (humble supplication) above, 13: 572, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And in fear﴾, he says: and in fear of God, that He may punish you for any shortcoming on your part in admonishing yourself and reflecting upon it, and for heedlessness of the limits that God has made clear in it. [[See the explanation of "khawf" (fear) above, 9: 123, footnote 3, and the references there.]] ﴿And without loudness of speech﴾, he says: and supplicating to God with the tongue in secrecy, not aloud. [[See the explanation of "jahr" (loudness) above, 2: 80 / 9: 344, 358 / 11: 368.]] He says: let the remembrance of God, while you listen to the Qur'an, be in supplication if you supplicate, not loud, but in a quiet speech, as:

15621 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from his father, from Hayyan ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, regarding His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, he said: "God says: when My servant remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and when My servant remembers Me alone, I remember him alone; and when he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better and more honourable gathering than theirs." [[The report 15621: "Ibn al-Taymi" is Maʿmar ibn Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, and his father is Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, both of whom have been mentioned many times before. "Hayyan ibn ʿUmar al-Qaysi al-Jurayri" is trustworthy, of few narrations; he narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Samura, Ibn ʿAbbas, Samura ibn Jundab and others. Sulayman al-Taymi, Saʿid al-Jurayri and Qatadah narrated from him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Saʿd 7/1/137, 165, al-Kabir 2/1/50, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/244. "ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr ibn Qatada al-Jundaʿi" was the storyteller of the people of Mecca, a trustworthy Successor and one of the great Successors, mentioned under numbers 9180, 9181, 9189 and others.]]

15622 – al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾, he said: One is commanded to humble supplication in prayer and submission, and raising the voice, calling out and shouting in supplication is disliked.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾, it means at the early hours and the evening times.

* *

As for "al-Asal" (evenings), it is a plural, and the grammarians differed concerning it.

Some of them said: It is the plural of "asil" (late afternoon), just as "al-Aymān" is the plural of "yamīn" (right hand), and "al-Asrār" is the plural of "sarīr". [[The "sarīr" whose plural is "asrār" is the "sarir" of the truffle (kam'a), which is what is on it of dust, peels and mud; the truffle has no roots, but it has "asrar".]]

* *

Others among them said: It is the plural of "asul", and "asul" is the plural of "asil". [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu ʿUbayda 1: 239.]]

* *

Others among them said: It is the plural of "asl" and "asil". He said: If you wish, you may make "al-asul" a plural of "al-asil", and if you wish, you may make it singular. He said: The Arabs say: "al-asul has drawn near", treating it as singular.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is more correct in this matter, namely that it is permissible for it to be the plural of "asil" and "asul", because both may be pluralised as "af'al". As for "al-Asal", it is, as is said in the speech of the Arabs, what lies between the afternoon prayer (ʿasr) and sunset (maghrib).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not be among the heedless﴾, He says: Do not be among those who are frivolous when the Qur'an is recited, regarding its admonitions and lessons and what is in it of wonders, but reflect upon it and understand it, and let your heart be pervaded by the remembrance of God, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "bi-dhikr Allah" (with the remembrance of God), and the context requires what has been affirmed.]] and humility before Him, and fear of God's power over you, if you are heedless of that.

15623 – Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾, he said: in the early hours and the evening = ﴿and do not be among the heedless﴾.

15624 – al-Harith told me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, saying: Maʿruf ibn Wasil al-Saʿdi told us, saying: I heard Abu Wa'il say to his servant at sunset: Have we reached the asr (late afternoon) yet? [[Report 15624: "Maʿruf ibn Wasil al-Saʿdi" was known as "Abu Badl" or "Abu Yazid", trustworthy. He was the imam of the mosque of the sons of ʿAmr ibn Saʿid ibn Tamim, leading them for sixty years, and he never erred in prayer, because it concerned him. He narrated from Abu Wa'il, Ibrahim al-Taymi, al-Nakhaʿi, al-Shaʿbi and others. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Saʿd 6: 248, al-Kabir 4/2/30, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/410.

"Abu Wa'il" is "Shaqiq ibn Salama al-Asadi", who met the Prophet (ﷺ) but did not see him, an authority in Arabic. His saying "aṣala" means he entered the time of al-asil (late afternoon).]]

15625 – al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said, regarding His saying: ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾: "al-Ghuduw" is the end of dawn, the dawn prayer = ﴿and the evenings﴾ is the end of the afternoon, the afternoon prayer. He said: All of that has a time, the beginning of dawn and its end. And this is like His saying in Surat Al ʿImran: ﴿And remember your Lord much, and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning﴾ [Surat Al ʿImran: 41]. It is said: "al-ʿAshiyy" is the inclining of the sun until it sets, and "al-Ibkar" is the beginning of dawn. [[The end of this report has passed as number 7024, by another route.]]

15626 – Ibn Wakiʿ told us, saying: my father told us, from Muhammad ibn Sharik, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who was asked about [the dawn prayer, and he said: It is indeed in the Book of God, and no one stands upon it] ..... Then he recited: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and His name be remembered therein; exalting Him therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾, the verse [Surat al-Nur: 36]. [[Report 15626: "Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Makki" is trustworthy, passed as number 10260, biographied in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Saʿd 5: 360, al-Kabir 1/1/112, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/284. The report came thus in the manuscript, as it is in the printed edition, and I almost certainly hold that it is an error and distortion, and there is a lacuna in it; but I did not find the report with its chain, so I did not change it. I found the text of the report without a chain in al-Durr al-Manthur 5: 52, concerning the forenoon prayer (salat al-duha), not the dawn prayer, and that is the correct version, God willing. He said:

(Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The forenoon prayer is indeed in the Qur'an, and none can penetrate its meaning except one who penetrates deeply, in His saying: "In houses which God has permitted to be raised and His name be remembered therein; exalting Him therein in the mornings and the evenings." This is the correct wording. But I placed what was in the manuscript and the printed edition between brackets, because I did not find the report with its chain. I placed dots in place of the lacuna. Then I completed the verse to its end as well.)]]

15627 – Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾, up to His saying: ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾: God commanded His remembrance and forbade heedlessness. As for "al-ghuduw" (mornings): the dawn prayer; and "al-asal" (evenings): the afternoon. [[Report 15627: The manuscript and the printed edition had: "... Yazid told us, saying, Suwayd told us, saying, Saʿid told us ..." It added in the chain "Suwayd told us", and that is a clear error. The scribe wrote "Yazid" and then wrote "Suwayd" and added it to the chain. This chain recurs in the tafsir, its last occurrence being number 15598.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 206:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says: Do not be arrogant, O listener who attends to the Qur'an, toward the worship of your Lord, and remember Him when the Qur'an is recited, humbly and fearfully, and without loud speech. For indeed those who are with your Lord, from among His angels, do not act arrogantly toward humbling themselves before Him and submitting to Him, and that is "worship" ('ibadah). [[See the explanation of "worship" in the earlier language indexes, under the root ('-b-d).]] ﴿And they exalt Him﴾: that is, they magnify their Lord by their humility before Him and their worship [[See the explanation of "glorification" (tasbih) in the earlier sections, 1: 474-476 / 6: 391, and the root (s-b-h) in the language indexes.]] ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾: that is, they pray to Him, and this is their prostration. [[See the explanation of "prostration" (sujud) in the earlier language indexes, under the root (s-j-d).]] So you too, pray to Him and magnify Him with worship, as those among His angels who are with Him do.

* *

End of the commentary on Surah al-A'raf. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."]]
